## The remaining pointer and length parameters to spans (Patella-Modern issue #69)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 5, 2026. These are the parameters #59 and #60 left (their "Not done" lists): the
pointer and length pairs, and the buffers passed without a size, now take `patella::TSpan` (src/compat/span.h).
Two parameters stay, and why is given below.

- **What takes spans** (high). Script.h: `TReadBinaryFile::readBytes(TSpan<uint8>)`,
  `TWriteBinaryFile::writeBytes(TSpan<const uint8>)`. Status.h: `CheckClipboardText(TSpan<const char>)` (the copied
  characters, which need no NUL). Utils.h: `CopyString(TSpan<char> DestinationBytes, const char *Source)` (the
  original's Destination and Size) and `FormatNumber(int, TSpan<char>)`. Network.h:
  `GetErrorMessage(TSpan<char, ERROR_MESSAGE_SIZE>, int, int)`. graphics.h: `DrawOutfit(..., TSpan<const int, 4>
  Colors, ...)` (TCreature's and TOutfitIcon's `std::array<int, 4>`; outfit 0 reads only Colors[0], as before).
- **The macros' text** (high). As in #59, each body defines the original's parameters as locals from the span, under
  the names the assertions' text uses: CopyString's `Destination` and `Size` (`TASSERT(124, Destination!=NULL)`),
  FormatNumber's `Buffer` (467), GetErrorMessage's `Message` (544), readBytes' `Buffer` and `Count` (line 664's error
  names Count), writeBytes' and CheckClipboardText's own. The int is `static_cast<int>(size())`, so a null span fails
  the same assertion and a size above INT_MAX is the original's negative size. macrocheck 7ad3e31 issue-69: 2,108
  calls, 0 differences.
- **Fixed extents for the two that the golden tests fake by address** (high). GetErrorMessage (mainfrm_tests.cpp,
  commworld.cpp) and DrawOutfit (the content windows, dialog elements and dialogs tests) are replaced, on our side and
  in the image, by one fake with the original's signature (`char *`, `int *`). A fixed-extent span holds only the
  pointer and is trivially copyable (`IsSpanLayout`, asserted next to each declaration), so MSVC x86 pushes it as the
  pointer's stack word and MSVC x64 passes it in the pointer's register: the fakes need no change, and the sizes are
  the ones the callers always had (new char[1024]; the four colours). A dynamic span is two words on x86 (the
  pointer's and the int's places) but goes through a stack temporary on x64, so CheckClipboardText, also faked by
  address (0x4ea370), gets a second fake for our side that takes the span and calls the first
  (dialogelements_tests.cpp, dialogs_tests.cpp: `FakeOurCheckClipboardText`; the image keeps the old one, the logs
  are the same). SetSymmetricKey and CreateNewChannelDialog keep their signatures (#59, #60).
- **FormatNumber writes no further than its span** (high). The text is built in a local `TFixedString<14>` (10
  digits, 3 commas, the NUL) and copied into the caller's buffer with `TStringBuffer::Assign`. The original wrote
  nothing after the final NUL (the digits' NUL moves right with each comma), so the caller's bytes are the original's
  wherever the result fits: every caller's buffer holds 14 (ContentWindows' `TFixedString<20>`, the tests' 16, 32 and
  64). Where it does not, which overflowed in the original, the text is cut (#57's contract), and an empty span is
  not written. New unit test: tests/unit/core_utils_test.cpp's "the original's buffer and size as spans".
- **Kept** (high). `CompareStrings(const char *s1, const char *s2, int Count)`: Count limits a comparison of two C
  strings and -1 means no limit; it is not the size of a buffer (the callers pass -1 or a token's length).
  `ShortenString(char *Text, int MaxLength)`: MaxLength is the length the text is cut to (a font's fitting length),
  and the buffer is the text's own (strlen(Text) + 1, longer than MaxLength). Neither is a pointer and length pair;
  a span would describe a buffer neither function has (Utils.h says so). TrimString (`char *Destination`, no size)
  was not in the issue: its callers' buffers hold Source (#57).
- **The callers** (high). A TFixedString destination is `.Chars` (the array converts to the span with its N, which is
  the count the original passed: 30, 50, 20, 100, MAX_IDENT_LENGTH, HOTKEY_LENGTH); the ignore and white lists' 29 is
  `TSpan<char>(Name.Chars).first(29)`; a pointer and a computed count (the console's selected text, TFormattedText's
  pieces, the clipboard's ranges, readString's and writeString's lengths, the automap block's two tables) is
  `TSpan<T>(Pointer, static_cast<std::size_t>(Count))`; GetErrorMessage's seven callers wrap their new char[1024] in
  `TSpan<char, ERROR_MESSAGE_SIZE>(Message, ERROR_MESSAGE_SIZE)`. Same pointers and counts, so the same bytes.
- **Tests** (high). Forced: tests/golden's core, errors and script tests pass the original's arguments through
  golden_test.h's `OriginalSpan` (CopyString with a null pointer and 3, FormatNumber with a null pointer, readBytes
  with a null pointer and 2); network_tests.cpp's table of our functions takes a lambda for GetErrorMessage (also
  called with NULL); the CheckClipboardText fakes above. tests_core gains one case: 35/337 to 36/352 on Windows and
  with mingw-w64, 35/340 to 36/355 on Linux; Clang's ASan and UBSan run is clean.
- **The images** (high). pecompare of 7ad3e31 and issue-69, built at the same path, with the functions' sizes from
  both PDBs: no function added or removed in either, no text of .rdata changed. The oracle resizes 20 functions,
  .text +0x2b0: the callers that build the spans (CopyString's in AddAutomapMark, AddTalkFilter, InitPreferences,
  TAutomapWindow::MouseHover, the context menu entry's constructor, TEditMarkDialog::HandleEvent, the ignore list
  dialog's HandleEvent and LeftButtonUp, the talk buffers' and TTalkLine's constructors, GetSelectedText; readBytes'
  and writeBytes' in LoadAutomapBlock and SaveAutomapBlock; CheckClipboardText's in TEditLine::HandleEvent;
  FormatNumber's in TSkillsWindowBody::Draw; DrawOutfit's in TBattleWindowBody::Draw and TOutfitIcon::Draw),
  FormatNumber's new body and DrawOutfit (the stand-in's operator[]). CopyString, readBytes, writeBytes,
  CheckClipboardText and GetErrorMessage keep their sizes on x86 (a dynamic span is the pointer's and the int's
  words, a fixed one the pointer's). x64 resizes 51 (.text +0x2c0, .rdata +0x1b0 of unwind and EH data): those
  callers and their catch funclets, the bodies of CopyString, CheckClipboardText, readBytes, writeBytes, readString,
  CopyToClipboard, GetErrorMessage and TFormattedText::Arrange (the span through a temporary), the ignore list
  dialog's constructor and its unwind funclets (CopyString's first(29)), and FormatNumber, whose one unwind funclet
  is renumbered (dtor$20 to dtor$10). GetErrorMessage's callers are unchanged on both (the fixed span is the
  pointer).
- **Proof** (high). difftest 16,848,752, sysinctest 67, communicationtest 1,134,513, vlong 3,201, 0 failures
  (`oracle-x86 --fresh`, and again recording the branch's corpus); golden_runner 16,461,713 replayed, 1,521,619
  retired, 0 not ported, 0 failures in windows-x64 and windows-x64-debug. tools/patch_client.py and

## The main window's background during a live resize (Patella-Modern issue #71)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 5, 2026, from the owner's report (build\manual-test\Patella.exe on the intro
screen: while the border is dragged larger, the new area shows stretched stripes of old pixels; whole again when the
mouse is released) and live runs of Tibia.exe and of main's and the branch's x64 Patella.exe. notes/vulkan.md, "The
main window's background during a live resize (issue #71)" has the facts.

- **The cause** (high). While Windows runs its modal size loop (the border held), the message loop is the system's:
  CPlayerApp::OnIdle, which draws the frames (Control.cpp ProcessEvents), never runs, only WM_TIMER's TimerEvent,
  which draws nothing. The device's window (issue #52) keeps its size until the next frame's Fit, so the part a
  larger window uncovers is the main window's own client area. Its class has no background brush (Player.cpp
  InitInstance, as the original's) and CMainFrame handles neither WM_ERASEBKGND nor WM_PAINT, so nothing paints it:
  the compositor shows what is left in the window's surface, the stripes of the report (each size step's edge).
- **What Tibia.exe does** (high for the stripes, medium for the rest). The same: the same class, the same message
  map, no frame during the loop. A live run (build\logs\issue-71\scripts\resize_repro.py: the window on the intro
  screen, the bottom-right border pressed and dragged 700x450 with simulated mouse input, so the system's own size
  loop runs, screenshots during and after) shows the same stripes in the uncovered area with its DirectX 9 and its
  OpenGL engine. Its picture itself is not visible on this machine's desktop tonight (the monitor is off, the display
  falls back to 1024x768, Direct3D 9 and OpenGL content shows white, as in issue #18's screenshots), so what it shows
  after the release could not be seen; by the code it is the next frame of OnIdle, over the whole client area, as
  the x64 client's.
- **The change** (high). The uncovered area is filled black. TPresentWindows (src/vulkan/PresentWindow.cpp)
  subclasses the main window from its first Open to Close or the main window's WM_NCDESTROY (SetWindowSubclass,
  comctl32): on WM_ERASEBKGND it fills the client area outside the device windows (the current one and a retired one
  that still shows its last frame) black and returns 1. The resize's invalidation brings the erase (CS_HREDRAW and
  CS_VREDRAW), and the modal loop dispatches WM_PAINT, so each size step is filled at once. The device windows
  themselves keep their size and their last picture during the loop, as the original's picture stays where it was.
- **Why so, and not otherwise** (high). Nothing reconstructed changes: Player.cpp's class, MainFrm.cpp's message map
  and the oracle stay as they are, and the fill lives where #52 put the x64 client's own windows. Drawing frames
  during the loop (a timer between WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE and WM_EXITSIZEMOVE) would run the client's drawing and its
  side effects at times the original never does; fitting the device window during the loop would show the old
  swapchain image stretched by the compositor on the GPUs, and on the CPU driver (GDI) the old picture at its old
  size with the rest of the device window unpainted: neither clean. Black:
  no picture rather than an invented one, and a stock brush (no GDI object to keep).
- **A deliberate on-screen difference from Tibia.exe** (high). During a live resize Tibia.exe's uncovered area shows
  stripes of old pixels, the x64 client's is black. Also black, where it showed whatever the compositor had: the
  client area when no device window exists (a failed CreateSurfaces) while the main window erases. Nothing the
  comparisons see changes: the frames are the engine's own images, read back (the frame dumps, the reference
  compare), the test mode moves no border, and no packet or file depends on the window's painting.
- **Checked** (high). tests_vulkan's new case "the main window's area the device windows do not cover is filled
  black (issue #71)": a hidden main window of the client's class style, the erase sent with a memory DC of white
  pixels: before any device window and after Close the class's own erase (nothing, 0); with a device window the
  uncovered part black and the window's part untouched through 8 size steps without a Fit (the device window keeps
  its size), the fitted window, a retired window and the next one over a larger window, no device window at all
  (all black); the main window's end takes the subclass with it, and a new main window gets it again. Live, with
  main's and the branch's Patella.exe (PATELLA_VULKAN=cpu, whose picture the monitor-off desktop shows, and gpu):
  stripes before, black after; with the CPU driver the whole picture after the release in both.
- **The image** (high). pecompare of main 3de8059 and issue-71's x64 Release Patella.exe, built at the same path,
  function by function through .pdata (13,299 and 13,301 functions): TPresentWindows' destructor (93 to 138 bytes,
  Close's Unsubclass inlined) and Open (175 to 269, Subclass inlined) change, ExcludeChild (170) and ParentProc (267,
  FillUncovered and Unsubclass inlined) are new; everything else only moves (.text +0x260, the references to what
  moved; .rdata +0x4e, the new functions' unwind data and the import; .pdata two entries; .reloc +8). One import
  more: COMCTL32.dll, ordinals 410, 412 and 413 (SetWindowSubclass, RemoveWindowSubclass, DefSubclassProc), which
  Tibia.exe imports too (InitCommonControls); the Rich header has one entry more, which moves the PE header 8 bytes.
  No text of .rdata changed but the DLL's name. The oracle is not built from these files (cmake/Vulkan.cmake is the
  x64 client's).

## Each golden run in a temporary folder of its own (Patella-Modern issue #66)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 5, 2026. Found in #26: golden runners of different worktrees shared the user's
TEMP (ConsoleWindow's SaveChannel file in %TEMP%\consolewindow, Errors' scripts in %TEMP%\errortest, the data files in
%TEMP%\golden-data, Preferences' %TEMP%\tibia-difftest-cfg, the map, objects and script folders); two at once gave
748 failures in SaveChannel, alone 0.

- **The runner's run folder** (high). tests/golden/runner.cpp's TRunFolder: once the corpus is found, the runner
  creates `golden-run-<process id>-<n>` below the TEMP it was started with (the first n whose folder does not exist
  yet), sets TEMP and TMP to it with _putenv_s (the C runtime's copy and the process environment: getenv,
  GetTempPathA, std::filesystem::temp_directory_path and tmpfile all see it) and makes it the current directory. At
  the end (the static object's destructor: a return from main and the tests' exit(1) alike) the previous directory
  again and the folder removed with remove_all; a failure to remove it is printed to stderr. A relative corpus path
  is made absolute before the change of directory. Not removed: a run ended by _exit (the Debug library's check,
  exit code 3) or a crash; the next run takes another name. No src/ change and no test change: every path the tests
  and the code under test write is below TEMP, GetTempPath or the current directory, so the redirect reaches all of
  them, and the recorded values hold no TEMP path (Errors' replaces its folder with "%TEMP%\errortest"; the recording's
  TEMP was build\oracle-x86\tmp\golden-difftest already, not the runner's). Considered: changing each test's folder
  name (seven files, each with its own spelling, and a new writer would have to remember it); a folder per test
  (the tests share TEMP across a run in the oracle too).
- **The recording side** (high). golden_corpus ran each test program with TEMP and TMP set to a fixed
  build\oracle-x86\tmp\golden-<test>, never cleaned (Errors' written.bin and written.txt stayed). Now each runs
  through cmake/RunGoldenRecord.cmake: `golden-<test>-<time with microseconds>-<6 random hex digits>` below
  build\oracle-x86\tmp, the program's TEMP, TMP and working directory, removed afterwards; the program's exit code is
  the script's. The oracle's CTest tests keep their fixed folders (build\oracle-x86\tmp\<test>, oracle_test_environment):
  each build tree has its own, and one CTest run starts each test once. Recording twice at once in one build tree stays
  unsupported: both write the one corpus.
- **The proof as a test** (high). CTest test `golden_concurrent` (tests/golden/concurrent.py, the windows-x64 presets'
  Python): two golden_runner processes over the same corpus started together, their output in
  golden-concurrent-1.log and -2.log next to the runner; it passes when both exit 0 and neither's
  `golden-run-<pid>-*` is left below TEMP; 77 (skipped) when both have no corpus, as `golden` (hosted CI). It runs as
  long as one golden run (both run at once) and in CTest next to `golden`, a third runner at once, which is what it
  tests. windows-x64, -debug and -asan(-debug) have 14 CTest tests now; windows-x64-gcc and Linux build no runner.
- **Not done** (found). The fixed folders that runners before #66 left in %TEMP% (errortest, consolewindow,
  golden-data, tibia-difftest-cfg, ...) are not removed by anything: no run uses them any more; deleting them is the
  user's.

## patch_client.py on the Debug builds: InitServerList's loop store (Patella-Modern issue #73)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 5, 2026. Found in #70: `reference.py compare --exe
build\windows-x64-asan\Debug\PatellaTest.exe` stopped before any client started (exit 2), because tools/patch_client.py
found none of the four `mov dword ptr [Servers[i].Port], 7171` stores. The plain windows-x64-debug images fail the same
way (Patella.exe and PatellaTest.exe, today's and the build of November 3): without optimization InitServerList keeps
its loop, `call std::array::operator[]; add rax, 64h; ...; mov dword ptr [rax], 1C03h` (`c7 00 03 1c 00 00`), under ASan
after the shadow check of the address. No src/ change.

- **The loop store through the PDB** (high). When the structural search finds none of the four stores (and only
  then), the PDB's function InitServerList (dbghelp: its RVA and size, the new `Pdb.function_symbol` of
  tools/client_state.py; an image whose PDB has none keeps today's error) must hold exactly one `mov dword ptr [<register
  based address>], 7171` (C7 /0, a memory operand that is neither absolute nor RIP-relative, its SIB byte and
  displacement decoded from the ModRM, a REX prefix allowed, an operand-size prefix not), and its immediate must be the
  function's only occurrence of the bytes 03 1c 00 00. That one immediate is patched (it sets the port of all four
  servers); the check after writing finds it again with the new port. Anything else stays an error. Any count of the
  four stores other than zero takes the old path unchanged, so every image patched before is patched byte for byte the
  same. Considered: a byte pattern for the whole loop (it changes with ASan, /RTC1 and /JMC); the PDB's line records of
  `Servers[i].Port = 7171` (tied to src/Network.cpp's line numbers); decoding every instruction of the function (a
  disassembler: a dependency the plan does not name).
- **The self-test** (high). `--self-test` covers the new form: the ASan Debug code's `mov rax, [rsp+38h]; mov dword ptr
  [rax], 7171`, the addressing forms [reg+disp8], [reg+disp32], [rsp+disp8] (SIB), [index*4+disp32] (SIB without a
  base) and a REX prefix; not matched: the absolute or RIP-relative form, `mov ecx, 7171`, C7 /1, a register destination,
  a 16-bit store, another immediate; a function with no store, two stores or the bytes once more is refused.
- **Proof** (high). main's patch_client.py (4d1b8bd) and the branch's on Tibia.exe, the oracle-x86 Release Patella.exe,
  windows-x64 Release Patella.exe and PatellaTest.exe, windows-x64-asan Release Patella.exe and PatellaTest.exe, each
  with `--host 127.0.0.1 --port 7271 --rsa tibia.pem`, with `--host --port 7271` and with `--host` alone: the outputs are
  identical byte for byte. The Debug images (windows-x64-debug and windows-x64-asan-debug, Patella.exe and
  PatellaTest.exe): `--host` alone identical; with `--port`, main refused them and the branch patches the one immediate
  (69 bytes changed). `python -I tools/reference.py compare --exe build\windows-x64-asan\Debug\PatellaTest.exe --out
  build\reference-compare-asan-debug`: all 8 sessions match their recordings, no ASan finding.
- **Not done** (found). `--rsa` refuses every Debug image: "the RSA modulus: expected one occurrence, found 2".
  src/Communication.cpp passes CipSoft's modulus as two literals (the login and the game connection's
  TRSA::SetPublicKey); Release builds pool identical strings (/GF with /O), Debug builds keep both. reference.py does not
  use `--rsa` (the replay takes each connection's XTEA key), compare_traffic.py and testmode_check.py do (Release
  clients). Patching both copies is a change of its own.

## The live checks on a hidden desktop (Patella-Modern issue #56): a second session instead; --hidden experimental

Found by Claude Opus 5.5, November 5, 2026, on branch issue-56 (not merged). The owner decided on November 4 that the
live checks run on a hidden Windows desktop. tools/desktop.py does that: before main, each live check
(reference.py compare and record, testmode_check.py, compare_traffic.py, compare_files.py, compare_rendering.py,
compare_network.py) runs itself again on a new desktop (CreateDesktopW in its own window station,
STARTUPINFO.lpDesktop, the same standard handles) in a job of its own. Every process it starts inherits that
desktop, and nothing appears on the user's screen. (Since the decision below only with `--hidden`; the first
version hid every run and had `--visible` for the old behaviour.) Arguments that start no
client (--self-test, --check-only, --compare-only, --list, list, --check-route, -h) stay in the process. After the
run, any process of the job still running is ended, except the test server and its console host, which are
named. `python -I tools/desktop.py --self-test` checks the mechanism: the child's window is on its own desktop, and
the user's EnumWindows does not see it. ctypes only, as the other tools.

The mechanism works. The clients do not behave on that desktop as they do on the user's, so the issue's criterion
("the same results as on the visible desktop") is not met. Three Windows behaviours of a desktop that is not the
input desktop cause it (high: each one seen in the runs and in a small program):

- **GDI into a window not yet shown fails.** BitBlt into a window that has not been shown fails with error 6 on a
  new desktop. On the user's desktop the same call succeeds without drawing anything. Showing another window first
  changes nothing. The client draws its first frame (CPlayerApp::InitInstance, Redraw(false)) before ShowWindow,
  and lavapipe's present (Mesa's Win32 WSI, a BitBlt into the window) returns VK_ERROR_MEMORY_MAP_FAILED (-5).
  TRenderer::Present throws, InitControl's catch calls ExitControl, which then crashes (0xC0000005: the original's
  path; corrected by issue #83: FatalError's ShowWindow on a null main window crashes, after InitInstance's first
  Redraw, and Tibia.exe's catch (...) caught it; "A fatal error before the main window is set"). Every PatellaTest.exe and Patella.exe run on the CPU driver (PATELLA_VULKAN=cpu: reference.py compare's
  and testmode_check.py's default, compare_rendering.py's vulkan-cpu) ends this way after 1 s. On a GPU
  (PATELLA_VULKAN=gpu) the Vulkan engine presents and runs.
- **DirectDraw and Direct3D 9 do not start; OpenGL does.** Tibia.exe and the oracle's Patella.exe with Engine = 0
  (DirectX 5) or Engine = 2 (DirectX 9) draw every frame through OpenGL there (patcap.dll: "the frames came from
  OpenGL SwapBuffers"), and write `Engine = 1` to Tibia.cfg and `Graphic Engine: 1` to error.txt. Engine = 1
  (OpenGL) runs as on the user's desktop. Tibia.exe's DirectX 9 frames are the reference of every Vulkan
  comparison (plan D7), and Tibia.exe is CipSoft's, so this cannot change in the client.
- **GetCursorPos fails** ("the input desktop must be the current desktop"). The client polls it in OnIdle
  (Player.cpp) into an uninitialised POINT and feeds the result to MouseMove. Under patcap.dll (compare_rendering.py,
  reference.py record) the hook returns a fixed point, so nothing changes there. The clients of compare_traffic.py,
  compare_files.py and compare_network.py run without it, and the posted clicks then miss: compare_traffic.py's
  "trade request" never reaches the server (no TTradeOffers window), compare_files.py's walk never opens its mark
  dialog, and its report run does not close within 20 s of WM_CLOSE. In the test mode, PATELLA_GET_CURSOR_POS goes
  to the real GetCursorPos unless the script has `cursor`.

What runs on the hidden desktop with the same results (tonight's runs, `build\logs\issue-56` of the worktree):
PatellaTest.exe on a GPU (reference.py compare --sessions traffic --vulkan gpu: every check equal, hidden and
visible), the OpenGL engine of both 32-bit clients under patcap.dll (compare_rendering.py --engines gl: identical
but for the frame-rate mask), and compare_network.py (0 of 51 scenarios differ, 4 variable). compare_network.py
passes because both clients fall back to OpenGL the same way and none of its scenarios uses the cursor, not because
the run matches the user's desktop.

Choices for the owner (not taken here; the issue says tools only, and each of these changes something else):

1. **A second interactive session**: run the checks in a session of their own, either a separate local Windows
   user through fast user switching or a Remote Desktop session to this machine (notes/reconstruction.md
   "Checking" already says this for the self-hosted runner). That session's desktop is an input desktop, so
   DirectDraw, Direct3D 9, GDI and GetCursorPos behave as on the user's desktop, and none of the user's input
   reaches it. Needs no code; a manual set-up.
2. **Hidden for what works, visible for the rest**: keep tools/desktop.py, but hide only the runs that do not need
   DirectDraw, Direct3D 9, the CPU driver's first present or the real cursor. That leaves PatellaTest.exe on a
   GPU, and compare_rendering.py's gl engine. The reference compare would then run on the GPU, whose frames are not
   the CPU driver's (the exact frames of notes/vulkan.md); one session matched tonight, the rest was not checked.
3. **Client changes so that the test build runs hidden** (src/, so stopped here): the Vulkan engine skips the
   present while the main window is not visible (on the user's desktop such a present shows nothing anyway), and
   the test mode's GetCursorPosition returns a fixed point outside the window when GetCursorPos fails. With both,
   reference.py compare and testmode_check.py should run hidden on the CPU driver (not tried). Tibia.exe's DirectX
   runs (compare_traffic.py, compare_files.py, compare_rendering.py's dx5, dx9, vulkan and vulkan-cpu, reference.py
   record) would still need the visible desktop or choice 1.

**The owner's decision (November 5, 2026): choice 1, no client change.** The live checks that need isolation run in
a second interactive session; every tool runs on the desktop of the session that starts it, exactly as before
tools/desktop.py, unless `--hidden` is given (branch issue-56b; `--visible` is gone, not kept as a no-op: it never
reached main). `--hidden` stays as an experimental switch, its help and tools/desktop.py's text list what fails on
the hidden desktop (the three behaviours above) and what does not (PatellaTest.exe on a GPU, the OpenGL engine,
compare_network.py). notes/reconstruction.md, "Checking", "The live checks in a second session", says how to set
the session up and what Windows does to it, with the sources; in short (Windows 11 Pro, a client edition):

- Only one session is connected at a time (a workstation lets one user at a time use its desktop): switching to
  the checks' user, or a Remote Desktop logon, disconnects the user's own session, and Remote Desktop to this
  computer itself does not change that. The second session keeps the user's windows and input apart from the
  checks; it does not let the user work in their own session while they run. That needs Windows Server or
  Windows Enterprise multi-session, or the user off the machine.
- A locked or disconnected session's Default desktop is not an input desktop (Microsoft Learn, "Desktops": one input
  desktop per interactive window station; Winlogon on Ctrl+Alt+Del and UAC). Its programs keep running, but under
  the conditions the hidden desktop showed: the checks' session must stay connected and unlocked for the run.
  GUI test vendors (SmartBear) say GUI tests fail once the Remote Desktop window is closed, and keep the session's
  GUI with `tscon <id> /dest:console`, which on a client edition disconnects the user's own session; a minimized
  Remote Desktop window stops the session's drawing unless the connecting computer sets
  `RemoteDesktop_SuppressWhenMinimized` (third-party documentation).
- Not tried on this machine: no second user or Remote Desktop session was set up (the owner's set-up). What a
  Remote Desktop session does to DirectDraw, Direct3D 9 and the Vulkan device (its display adapter is the remote
  one; the real GPU only through the policy "Use hardware graphics adapters for all Remote Desktop Services
  sessions", reported on by default on Windows 11) is open; fast user switching gives the console's display and
  GPU, the closest to the user's own desktop.

Found, not done (issues of their own): ExitControl's null dereference after InitControl's catch (above: a failing
first present crashes the client with 0xC0000005 instead of ending it cleanly; the original's path, a src/ change),
and the two flakes of the visible runs (compare_files.py's report run that did not close within 20 s of WM_CLOSE,
rerun once; compare_rendering.py's dx9 run with two packets swapped in the oracle's replay, rerun once). And, in
issue-56b's runs on the user's desktop: two trolls attack the test character in the temple of the test server's
world, so its Ctrl+L logout is refused, and testmode_check.py (the client does not close within 180 s of the
script's quit) and compare_traffic.py's live half ("still connected to the game server 10 s after Ctrl+L") fail,
with main's tools too; the test server's world, not the tools.

## The error report removed: error.txt, the report dialog, packet 0xE8 (Patella-Modern issue #74, D2)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 5, 2026; M5's first issue (decision D2, notes/modernization-plan.md 7 M5). The
crash report had one consumer chain: Player.cpp's HandleException appended a report to error.txt (the version, the
exception's origin, ctime, the Windows version, the engine, Control.cpp's last ten packet types, MainFrm.cpp's last
packet header and the player's position, the message), ReadErrorFile read it back at the next start into Status.cpp's
report list, event 0x2a (posted by InitInstance) opened the error report dialog, and event 0x2b (posted on entering the
game) sent each report as packet 0xE8 and deleted the file. The game server only logs 0xE8
(gameserver/src/game/receiving.cc CErrorFileEntry).

- **Removed** (high). CPlayerApp::ReadErrorFile (0x4da140) and HandleException's file; Status.cpp's TErrorReport,
  its vector (0x71c648), ClearErrorReports, AddErrorReport, SetErrorReportDate, AddErrorReportText,
  SetErrorReportComment, GetNumberOfErrorReports, GetErrorReportTitle/Date/Text/Comment (0x4e7bb0-0x4e7ed0) and
  DeleteErrorFile (0x4e7380), and ExitStatus's call of ClearErrorReports; Dialogs.cpp's CreateErrorReportDialog (line
  631) and TErrorReportDialog (constructor, KeyPress, HandleEvent: lines 4053-4084); Control.cpp's SendErrorReports
  (line 392), OutputControlErrorInformations (0x445900) and events 0x2a and 0x2b (ProcessEvents' cases, InitInstance's
  and ReceivePackets' posts); Communication.cpp's SendDebugReport (line 969, packet 0xE8); CMainFrame::
  OutputErrorInformations (0x4a8360); the texts 117 and 118 of src/Text.h (the dialog's). 6 TEND calls went with their
  functions (macrocheck: 2,108 calls, 6 deleted, no other difference); no TASSERT/TERROR/TEND argument was rewritten.
  tools/lines.py (only in the decompilation workspace, never in the repository since November 2) is dropped from
  tools/decompilation.ps1 and .gitignore; compare_files.py's sessions error-login and report and their reference
  recordings (reference.py, reference_record.py) are gone.
- **Kept** (high). An unrecoverable error still ends the client through FatalError: the connection shut down, the
  display mode restored, the window hidden, the "Tibia Error - Debug Assertion" box (MB_ICONHAND), exit(1). New:
  FatalError writes "<caption>: <text>" to stderr before the box, and HandleException writes "Debug Assertion 7.72
  <message>" (the exception's message: "<file> <line>: <kind> ..." with the values and the expression) before it, one
  fwrite each, failures ignored (a GUI client's stderr is valid only when redirected). HandleProgramError's box goes to
  stderr the same way. TBEGIN/TEND stay (issue #78), and so do the data the report printed, LastPacketTypes and
  PacketHeader (written, no longer read: the developer log of issue #77 can use them) and GetCurrentEngine (no caller
  in the client now). TextCriticalError stays entry 116, with the first sentence of the original's text only.
- **The box's text** (high). The original's second sentence ("A detailed error report has been written to the error
  file which you are asked to submit at your next login.") would now be false; the box keeps the caption and the first
  sentence. Considered: the exception's message in the box (new user-visible text the plan does not ask for); the
  original's text unchanged (it points the user to a file that does not exist).
- **No layout change** (high). Only functions, one global vector and a class of its own went; no structure the oracle
  freezes changed (CPlayerApp loses two non-virtual members, SkinProperties keeps the dialog's fields Data14E0-Data1518,
  set by InitSkinProperties and unread). The oracle builds the same sources.

## The error paths compared by outcome only (Patella-Modern issue #76)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 5, 2026; M5's second issue (notes/modernization-plan.md, 7 M5: "difftest (until
M6) and the golden corpus compare the error paths by outcome only"), before #78 (TBEGIN/TEND removed) and #79 (TASSERT
to PATELLA_ASSERT), which change the texts and the lines. No src/ change.

- **The comparison** (high). Every exception comparison of difftest, communicationtest and the golden runner goes
  through tests/golden/golden_eh.cpp's CompareThrown (the error rounds' TErrorRound::Compare, errors_tests.cpp's
  Compare, commworld.cpp's CompareRun). It now makes one check per call: TThrown's `==`, the kind (nothing,
  TMyException, PROGRAM_ERROR, another type), the thrown type's decorated name and a PROGRAM_ERROR's value. A
  TMyException's message and origin (file names, line numbers, the stringized expressions, the values, the TEND
  levels) are not compared. Until now the per-call check compared them too, with every "<file> <line>" pair
  replaced, and each pair had a check of its own (issue #35: our line must be the original's). Those line-pair
  checks are gone: under #78 their number follows the TEND levels, so no form of them stays meaningful. Considered:
  keeping a check per pair that compares only the file names (it would still depend on the TEND levels), and keeping
  the per-call check on the message without its lines (#78 and #79 change the message itself). EH_LINEMAP, EH_LINES,
  ER_LINES and ThrownLineMap went with them; errors_tests.cpp's Relative (the work directory in the script errors'
  messages, which differs between recording and replay) too: no text is compared now. TThrown keeps Message and
  Origin for the failure reports only (ours, and the original's in the oracle).
- **What stays a text** (high). Errors' TestMyException compares TMyException's two constructors (4,000 checks: the
  class's formatting for random files, lines, names and values), not a site's text: a changed assertion does not
  reach it. #79, which shrinks TMyException, changes or retires it. HandleException's check compares our stderr with
  our own message ("Debug Assertion 7.72 " + GetMessage()), HandleProgramError's FatalError text and caption with the
  original's (the fake's texts), and FatalError's caption and text as #74 left them: no site text is in them.
  VerifyOurSideAssertion (the oracle's check that the runner's OurSideAssertion throws what our TComponent::SetSize
  throws) compares by outcome too.
- **The corpus** (high). golden::OutputThrown records the kind, the value and the type name, no message or origin;
  GOLDEN_FORMAT 1 to 2, so a corpus of before says "format 1, the runner reads format 2; record the corpus again".
  Recorded again (880 MB).
- **macrocheck and the rule retired** (high). With nothing comparing the texts, plan 4.2's stringized-expression rule
  (no change to a TASSERT*/TERROR*/TEND* argument until M5) and build\issue-8\tools\macrocheck.py (never in the
  repository; it imported tidy.py's parser) are retired, dated November 5, 2026: notes/modernization-plan.md 4.2,
  CLAUDE.md, notes/reconstruction.md "Checking", .clang-tidy's and .clang-format's comments. tools/tidy.py's guard
  existed only for that rule: protected_spans, the revert of fixes inside those arguments, the separate count and -v
  are gone, and every finding counts. .clang-format's WhitespaceSensitiveMacros stays: the arguments are still

## The built-in patcher removed: packets 0x1e, 0x1f, 0x20, Patch.exe (Patella-Modern issue #75, D9)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 5, 2026; M5, decision D9 (notes/modernization-plan.md, 11). A login server could
send a patch at any login (the client's first packet carries the data files' signatures): 0x1e (a difference patch of a
file) or 0x1f (a whole file) with the file number and size, then 0x20 blocks. ReceivePatchBlock wrote the result next to
the file (Script.cpp ApplyPatch, ApplyFullPatch: Tibia.da_, Tibia.sp_, Tibia.pi_, Patch.ex_, and Tibia.exe's as
Tibia.bak), events 0x41-0x44 moved it into place (InstallPatch), 0x45-0x47 reloaded the data files, and after a
Tibia.exe patch the client showed "Updating", closed (event 0x48, CloseProgram) and CPlayerApp::Run started patch.exe
(`_execl`): any server could replace the client's files and have a program run. The test server sends no patch (its
binary has no patch path; its sources are not on this machine).

- **Removed** (high). Communication.cpp's ReceivePatch (0x40a9c0), ReceiveWholeFile (0x40ae70), ReceivePatchBlock
  (0x40b290), CancelPatch (0x40bac0) and the transfer's state (PatchData, PatchWholeFile, PatchDataCount, PatchDataSize,
  PatchFileNumber, 0x5c4344-0x5c4357); Script.cpp's ApplyPatch (0x4e3100), ApplyFullPatch (0x4e3500) and InstallPatch
  (0x4e3610); Dialogs.cpp's TUpdateDialog (constructor, Draw, HandleEvent) and CreateUpdateDialog, and Text.h's texts
  74-76 (its "Downloading ..." texts); Control.cpp's events 0x29 (the update dialog), 0x40 (wait for the login
  connection's end; with it the goto to the shared exit block 0x44a2f5 that #42 kept), 0x41-0x48, CloseCallback
  (0x5c4534) and InitWindow's CloseProgram parameter; MainFrm.cpp's CloseProgram (0x4a8940); Player.cpp's RunPatch and
  Run's `_execl("patch.exe")`; compat/msvc.h's and msvc_portable.h's MsvcExecl (with <process.h> and <unistd.h>, which
  only it needed). compare_files.py's sessions patch and patch-exe, their recording in reference_record.py and the
  reference sessions patch and patch-exe of reference.py (a reference set may still hold them, unused, as error-login
  and report since #74).
- **The end of the login** (high). The three packets go to one new function, Communication.cpp's ReceiveUpdateRequest:
  it reads and drops everything the server sent (GetNextCommand until it returns -1: the patch's header or block, the
  packets after it in the frame and in the frames already received, so that none of it reaches the game server's table
  once the connection state is 0), posts the login error dialog's event (event 1, "Sorry") with "This server wants to
  update the client", disconnects and sets the connection state 0, as ReceiveLoginError does with the server's text. No
  HandleEvents after it (the original's showed the update dialog during a transfer). Considered: a dialog of its own
  ("Update refused"; new user interface the plan does not ask for); reading only the packet's own fields (the next
  bytes of the frame would then be read as game packets in state 0 and a crafted frame could end the client with a
  fatal error); the message in the message of the day's dialog (it is not an error).
- **Kept, with no caller in the client now** (high). HandleEvents, ReloadObjects, ReloadSprites, ReloadPictures,
  ClearMemoryCache, SetProgress and GetProgress, Network.cpp's GetBytes, TProgressBar::SetComplete and FileExists: their
  tests stay, the linker drops them from the images (below); as #74 kept GetCurrentEngine. MESSAGE_STARTPATCHER (72,
  Status.h: AddMessage's range check) stays the original's. SkinProperties keeps the update dialog's fields (Data104C,
  Data1050, Data1054, Data1074), set by InitSkinProperties and unread. InitCommunication stays, empty (it only cleared
  PatchData), so that InitControl's calls are the original's.
- **The layouts** (high). CPlayerApp loses RunPatch (+0xa1): padding now, the size the original's (CWinApp and two
  flags padded to 4); Player.h asserts `sizeof(CPlayerApp) == sizeof(CWinApp) + 4` in the oracle build
  (PATELLA_ORIGINAL_LAYOUT). No other structure changes; TUpdateDialog was a class of its own. Text.h's copies shrink by
  three pointers, as #74's did by two.
- **#67** (high). The crash of #67 (a block of a zero-sized patch divided by zero in ReceivePatchBlock, which the x64
  client's /EHsc catch (...) does not catch) is gone with the code: ReceiveUpdateRequest divides by nothing. Checked by
  the golden corpus's TestUpdateRequests (51 rounds of a zero-sized patch and its empty block, in the oracle and the
  three x64 runners) and by PatellaTest.exe on a crafted session (below). #67's second part, the list of other catch
  (...) blocks that relied on catching hardware exceptions, is not done here; #67 stays open.

## The 30-character ignore names and the 128-character buddy descriptions (Patella-Modern issue #85)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 5, 2026. A regression of #57 (5b98b20), found in #75: TIgnoreListDialog kept a
name of 30 characters, the most the lists' edit line takes (TFontListBox's TEditLine of 30), as 29. The original's
`strcpy(IgnoreEntries(Selection).Name, Name)` (and the white list's, in Add 709/712 and Delete 710/713) wrote the 30
characters and put the NUL into the next byte, TIgnoreEntry::Permanent, which the next statement sets; #57's
`Name.Assign(Name)` kept N - 1 characters, the rule for a text that does not fit its buffer, though this one never left
its structure.

- **The fix: strcpy's bytes within the structure** (high). `TIgnoreEntry::AssignName` writes the text and its NUL
  through a TStringBuffer over the whole entry (31 bytes: Name and Permanent; `offsetof(TIgnoreEntry, Name) == 0` is
  asserted with the layout), so the entry's bytes are the original's for every name the edit line gives; the four
  calls use it. Same size, no layout change (a non-virtual member function). The readers are unchanged: they read the
  entry as the original did, so a 30-character entry with Permanent set reads on into the next entry (its "\x01" and
  the next name) in both, as the original's dialog showed after a Delete; that is the original's behaviour, kept, and
  the Dialogs checks below compare it.
- **The other #57 conversions** (high). Every write of 5b98b20 and a7e13c6 (and the TFixedStrings of #60, which added
  no write) was checked for the same off-by-one, a source that can be exactly N characters for a buffer of N:
  - **The same bug, fixed**: Preferences.cpp's Tibia.cfg reader, `Buddies(n).Description.Assign(Description)`. The
    description is read without a limit; the original's strcpy kept one of 128 characters whole (NUL in
    TBuddy::Notify, which the reader sets next) and up to 131 its characters went into Notify and the padding (the
    entry is 0x8c bytes, Description at 0x08); #57 cut at 127. `TBuddy::AssignDescriptionRead` writes over
    Description, Notify and the padding (132 bytes), the original's bytes up to 131 characters; 132 or more, which
    the original wrote past the entry (undefined), is cut at 131. SetBuddy keeps Description.Assign (it asserts
    strlen<128).
  - **Asserted before the write, cannot reach N**: TServer::Address (<100), TBuddyEntry::Name, TContainer::Name,
    TOffer::Name, TCharacter::Name and World (<30), the hotkeys (<HOTKEY_LENGTH), SetBuddy's description (<128),
    TEffect::Text (<10 in 12), the sprite and picture file names (<PATH_MAX), the status message
    (<STATUSMESSAGE_LENGTH), TTextButton::Text (<50), TDialog::Caption (<100).
  - **Bounded below N by their source**: THotkeyDialog::Texts (256) from its TEditLine of 255 or GetHotkey; the
    battle list's MouseOverText (32), the shortened names (32, 40), the VIP list's MouseOverText (36), the context
    menus' copies (30) and lines (50: "Revoke " + 29 + "'s Invitation" is 49), the talkbox's first line (40: 29 + "
    whispers:" is 39), the console's prefix, file name and message (100, 1024, 100), the report title (220), the
    skill names (100), all from names of at most 29 characters (GetString(..., 30), asserted elsewhere); the formats
    of numbers, the packet types, the map file names (12 in 16), the time stamps (6 in 8), the account number (11 in
    12), the IP address (15 in 16), GetErrorMessage (about 300 in 1024), the text dialog's descriptions (fixed texts
    in 255), the Script file names ("Tibia.cfg" and the data file names in 1024).
  - **Sized by their allocation**: the talk lines, list box lines, labels, captions, help, report and MotD copies,
    TrimString, the ignore and exemption texts.
  None was unclear, so none was left for the user.
- **The checks** (high). tests/golden/dialogs_tests.cpp, LongIgnoreNames: four rounds of the ignore list dialog after
  the error round, on their own random numbers (seed 85, the seed saved and set again: no other round's inputs move),
  for the ignore and the white list, with the permanent box clear and set: Add, the long clipboard text pasted over
  "new entry" (cut to 30 characters), Add (entry written by 709/712), the first line selected and deleted (710/713;
  the list rebuilt from the entries, the long one among them), the long line selected and deleted (its 30 characters
  written by 710/713), OK; the creator, each step's log and dump, the destructor's log. 80 checks, printed apart
  ("Dialogs: 80 checks of ignore and white list names of 30 characters"). tests/golden/preferences_tests.cpp, after
  the 400 random rounds: one Tibia.cfg with buddies of descriptions of 127 (Notify yes), 128, 129 and 131 characters
  (Notify no: with yes the original reads on past Notify into padding whose bytes are each side's own), CheckLists and
  the saved file compared; 179 checks, no random numbers. Proof: with the four Assign calls and the reader's Assign
  put back (the tests kept), difftest fails 21 checks (Dialogs 16: Add the long name, the selections and deletes
  after it, in the ignore and white list rounds; PreferencesFile 5: GetBuddyDescription(2), (3), (4), the saved
  file, and ExitPreferences' file); with the fix 0 (build\logs\issue-85\proof-difftest.log). With the permanent
  box set the rebuilt line is the long name, "\x01" and the next entry's "new entry" (the read past Permanent above),
  the same on both sides; deleting it writes its first 30 characters (the original's strcpy wrote the 40 on into the
  next entry, whose bytes were those characters already, so the entries end the same).
- **The counts** (high). `python -I tools/build.py oracle-x86`: difftest 16,459,078 to 16,459,337 (+259: Dialogs +80,
  PreferencesFile +179; every other test's count unchanged, Dialogs' main rounds 93,396 and errors 173,967 as on
  main), sysinctest 67, communicationtest 856,621, vlongtest 3,201, 0 failures, CTest 4/4. The golden corpus recorded
  again from the branch: 15,803,203 replayed + 1,512,822 retired = 17,316,025 (+259 replayed), 0 failures, golden and
  golden_concurrent pass on windows-x64, windows-x64-debug and windows-x64-asan (no ASan finding).
- **The images** (high). Main and the branch built at the same path, function by function through the PDBs
  (build\issue-85\funcs.py and funcs2.py, never committed: the rel32 operands of call, jmp and jcc and the base
  relocations masked; on x64 also 32-bit words moved by the code shift). Both images: TFixedString<128>::Assign gone

  InitPreferences the same size with the bound 127 to 131. Nothing else differs.

## Tests in parallel, golden_concurrent only in Release (Patella-Modern issue #84)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 5, 2026. The owner asked to speed up the tests: CTest ran each preset's tests one
after another, and in Debug and under ASan golden_concurrent (two runners at once, #66) was the longest test. Build and
test configuration only (CMakePresets.json, tests/golden/CMakeLists.txt, cmake/OracleX86.cmake); no src/ change, no test
checks anything else.

- **CTest in parallel** (high). Every test preset has `execution.jobs` 16 (CMakePresets.json; an integer: presets have no
  "all processors"). 16 starts all 14 tests of windows-x64 at once on this machine and only oversubscribes short unit
  tests on a smaller one (hosted CI: no corpus, so golden and golden_concurrent are skipped there). golden and
  golden_concurrent (COST 1000), difftest (1000) and communicationtest (500) start first while CTest has no timing
  data of its own yet; golden_concurrent counts as two (PROCESSORS 2). Output: with verbosity verbose CTest prefixes
  every line with the test's number, so each test's counts can still be found in the log. Considered: `jobs` per preset
  (the presets have 4 to 14 tests; one value is enough); CTEST_PARALLEL_LEVEL in the environment (not the presets').
- **Nothing shares a folder** (high). Checked every add_test. The oracle's four (difftest, sysinctest,
  communicationtest, vlongtest) have a TEMP and TMP of their own since build.cmd (oracle_test_environment,
  build\oracle-x86\tmp\<test>); every path their tests write is below TEMP or GetTempPath, or below a directory they

## TBEGIN/TEND deleted, file by file (Patella-Modern issue #78)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 5, 2026; M5 (notes/modernization-plan.md, 7 M5), after #74 (the error report,
TBEGIN/TEND's only consumer, removed) and #76 (difftest and the golden corpus compare the error paths by outcome only).
`TBEGIN`/`TEND*` (src/common.h) wrapped most function bodies in a try block whose handlers passed a PROGRAM_ERROR
through, wrapped a TMyException with the TEND's line and values (text only, which #76 no longer compares) and turned
anything else (`catch (...)`) into a TMyException "unknown exception occurred". Deleting a TEND therefore changes an
exception's kind only where something other than a TMyException or a PROGRAM_ERROR passed through it: a C++ exception
of another type (std::bad_alloc, std::bad_array_new_length, TRSA's `const char *`, an MFC exception), or, where the
build uses /EHa (the oracle's difftest, sysinctest and communicationtest), a structured exception (the x64 client and
the oracle's Patella.exe build with /EHsc, whose `catch (...)` never caught one; #67).

### The plan (high)

One merged branch per part (issue-78a, issue-78b, ...), the subsystems of notes/ownership.md section 2 grouped by size,
the least entangled first; the TBEGIN counts are main 01937c5's (`git grep -c -E '^\s*TBEGIN\s*$' -- src`: 1,130 try
blocks; the ~1,161 of `git grep -c TBEGIN` count comments too).

| Part | Subsystems | Files (TBEGIN) | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (issue-78a) | Files, buffers and portable code; Objects and the map; the small ones | Script.cpp 6, Inventory.cpp 4, Player.cpp 3, Status.cpp 1, Objects.cpp 61, Map.cpp 47, Creatures.cpp 31 | 153 |
| 2 | Graphics, the GUI core, the main window and the map, the frame | graphics.cpp 43, GUI.cpp 39, MainWindow.cpp 27, MapWindow.cpp 40, MainFrm.cpp 32 | 181 |
| 3 | Talk, the console, context menus | Talk.cpp 64, ConsoleWindow.cpp 71, ContextMenus.cpp 33 | 168 |
| 4 | Content windows, sub-windows and the side panel | ContentWindows.cpp 137, DialogWindow.cpp 40 | 177 |
| 5 | Dialog elements | DialogElements.cpp 141 | 141 |
| 6 | Dialogs | Dialogs.cpp 129 | 129 |
| 7 | Communication and the network, Control; the macros | Communication.cpp 125, Network.cpp 30, Control.cpp 26; then TBEGIN, TEND_HANDLERS, TEND, TEND1, TEND2 out of src/common.h and the comments that name them (Objects.h, TestHooks.h, compat/print.h, Utils.cpp, .clang-format's WhitespaceSensitiveMacros) | 181 |

Communication, Network and Control come last: they hold the inner handlers that really handle errors (the encryption
failures, TRSA's `const char *`, the connection's errors, Control's engine change) and Control's conversions, and every
other subsystem calls into them or is called from their event loop. Each part, for the kind changes: list every handler
that catches a TMyException by type (`catch (TMyException &)`, not `catch (...)`) and whose try block reaches a function
of the part; for each, the third-type sources in the part's functions (new/new[] and their sizes, the standard
library, TRSA, MFC) that no remaining TEND or `catch (...)` converts any more on the way. Where the size or the type comes
from input (a file, a packet), keep the conversion at that boundary; where only an exhausted heap reaches it, record it.
Then the top-level handlers (CPlayerApp::InitInstance and Run: every type to a TMyException, HandleException, the "Tibia
Error - Debug Assertion" box, exit code 1) end the client as before.

Mechanical deletion: the TBEGIN and TEND lines go, nothing else in the bodies changes (the blocks sit at the body's own
indentation, so clang-format moves nothing). The functions' comments keep the original's catch lines and try blocks as
line evidence; each file's header says they are the original's. A variable declared only for a TEND1's value stays.

### Part 1 (issue-78a): Script, Inventory, Player, Status, Objects, Map, Creatures

- **Deleted** (high). 153 TBEGIN/TEND pairs in 152 functions: Script.cpp 6 (TReadBinaryFile readWord, readQuad,
  readString; TWriteBinaryFile writeWord, writeQuad, writeString), Inventory.cpp 4, Player.cpp 3 (InitInstance's two
  around `new CMainFrame` and Redraw, OnIdle), Status.cpp 1 (CheckClipboardText), Objects.cpp 61, Map.cpp 47,
  Creatures.cpp 31. Every block was the rest of its function's body at the body's indentation, except Player.cpp's
  two single statements (no declaration in them), so no variable's scope or lifetime changed and clang-format moves
  nothing. The other subsystem files of the part have none: Utils.cpp, Container.h, vlong.cpp and sysinc.cpp never had
  one (the "TBEGIN" in Utils.cpp, TestHooks.h and compat/print.h are comments, and Objects.h's names MapWindow's
  TEND1; part 7 rewrites them with the macros).
- **Kept** (high). Every handler of these files that handles an error: Player.cpp's FatalError steps, WriteToStderr,
  `SurfaceInitInstance`'s `catch (...)` to PROGRAM_ERROR 12, InitInstance's and Run's top-level handlers (each type
  to its TERROR, HandleProgramError, HandleException); Map.cpp's LoadAutomapBlock and SaveAutomapBlock (an unreadable
  or unwritable automap file is reported in the console and the block emptied or counted saved) and FindPath's
  handler (its search state into the message); Objects.cpp's InitObjects (below). TASSERT*/TERROR* stay (#79).
- **The kinds** (high). The handlers that catch a TMyException by type and reach a function of this part:
  InitObjects (LoadObjects), LoadAutomapBlock and SaveAutomapBlock (TReadBinaryFile/TWriteBinaryFile's readQuad,
  readString, writeQuad, writeString), graphics.cpp's four loaders (readWord, readQuad), Map.cpp's FindPath (the
  field queries), MapWindow.cpp's light (GetObjectFlag), Preferences.cpp's two (only TReadScriptFile/TWriteScriptFile,
  not changed here). The third-type
  sources in this part's functions: `new`/`new[]` (readString's Length+1 of at most 65,536 bytes, CheckClipboardText's
  two copies of the clipboard text, LoadObjects' four tables and LoadProperties' sprite table, Container.h's growth,
  Map.cpp's std::stringstream in two error messages) and Player.cpp's `new CMainFrame`; readWord, readQuad,
  writeWord, writeQuad, writeString and GetObjectFlag allocate nothing. Three cases:
  - **LoadProperties' sprite table** (kept at the boundary). `new uint16[Count]`, Count the product of seven bytes of
    Tibia.dat: a damaged file can make it negative (std::bad_array_new_length) or too large (std::bad_alloc). Before,
    LoadProperties' and LoadObjects' TENDs made it a TMyException and InitObjects PROGRAM_ERROR 1 ("Tibia.dat" could not
    be loaded, HandleProgramError's box); without them it would have passed InitObjects' `catch (TMyException &)` and
    ended in HandleException's "Tibia Error - Debug Assertion" box, a different box for the same damaged file.
    InitObjects now catches everything (`catch (...)`; LoadObjects throws no PROGRAM_ERROR), so the outcome is the
    original's in every build. The only change of a handler in this part.
  - **An exhausted heap in readString under LoadAutomapBlock** (recorded, not kept). Before, std::bad_alloc in

    now it reaches the top-level handlers and the client ends with the "Tibia Error" box. The size is at most 65,536

    end every type in the same box (HandleException; caption "Tibia Error - Debug Assertion", TextCriticalError, exit
    code 1). Only the fork's stderr line names a different message.
  Structured exceptions: the x64 client and the oracle's Patella.exe build with /EHsc, whose `catch (...)` never caught
  one, so nothing changes there; difftest, sysinctest and communicationtest build with /EHa, and none of their

## The developer log and the fatal-error path (Patella-Modern issue #77, D16)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 5, 2026; M5 (notes/modernization-plan.md, 7 M5 "Kept", decision D16). Since #74
the fatal path wrote its texts to stderr through Player.cpp's WriteToStderr, and the diagnostics error.txt had held
(LastPacketTypes, PacketHeader, GetCurrentEngine, the player's position) were written but never read. Both now go
through a small log of our own.

- **The log** (high). src/log/Log.h, header only, so every target that compiles Player.cpp has it without a new
  source on its list (the client, the test build, golden_runner, the oracle's Patella.exe, difftest, mfc_shim_check):
  `patella::log::TLog` with a level, a console (a function given each whole line: `WriteToStderr` by default, the C
  library's stderr in one fwrite, then fflush) and an optional file (a TFile opened for appending, binary, so '\n'
  line ends on every platform), each line flushed at once (the fatal path's next step may end the process). The
  client's log is `patella::log::Log()`; `Error`, `Warn`, `Info`, `Debug` (members and free functions) format with
  std::format's language: std::format where the library has it, compat/format.h's stand-in on the oracle's C++17 and in
  tests_unit_cxx26_standin, as compat/print.h and TFile::Print do (TFixedString arguments as their text). A line is
  "[<level>] <message>\n" (a message keeps its own line breaks: the exception messages and HandleProgramError's text
  have them). Nothing throws: a message that cannot be formatted (the stand-in's TFormatError, std::bad_alloc) is
  dropped, a failed write ignored (a GUI client's stderr is valid only when redirected). A mutex guards the console and
  the file, the level is an atomic. No library, no dependency, nothing sent anywhere. Considered: a FILE * console
  (tools/banned_calls.py bans FILE outside src/types/File.h, issue #64; the function pointer also lets the unit tests
  capture the lines); a timestamp per line (not needed for the fatal path, and the stand-in has no chrono formatting).
- **The levels** (high). error, warn, info, debug (TLevel, in that order; a line is written when its level is the
  log's or more severe). Default info. error: FatalError's "<caption>: <text>" and HandleException's "Debug Assertion
  7.72 <message>" (the #74 stderr texts, now with the prefix), and the Debug stack trace. warn: a Patella.ini value that
  cannot be used. info: nothing yet (the default level, so stderr stays as it was apart from the prefix). debug: the
  settings read at the start, and the fatal diagnostics below.
- **Patella.ini** (high; D12). Two keys, read once at the start by InitInstance (x64 client only, `#if
  defined(PATELLA_VULKAN)`, like the device choice), never written by the client: `LogLevel` (error, warn, info, debug,
  without regard to case; another value is a warn line and the level stays) and `LogFile` (a file the lines are
  appended to as well, created where it does not exist, relative to the working directory; none without the key or
  with an empty value; one that cannot be opened is a warn line). src/log/LogSettings.cpp, in patella_core (and
  compiled into the client again, as Settings.cpp is), tested by tests_core. Without Patella.ini or the keys nothing
  changes: no file appears (tier A: no new file by default).
- **At the debug level: error.txt's diagnostics** (high). HandleException, after the message, writes what its report
  held until #74 besides the version, origin, time and Windows version: "Graphic engine: <GetCurrentEngine()>", "Last
  packet types: 255 108 ..." (Control.cpp's new GetLastPacketTypes: the ring in error.txt's order, the newest first,
  three digits each), "Last packet: 001 000 ..." (MainFrm.cpp's PacketHeader, when any byte is set, as
  OutputErrorInformations printed it) and "Player position: [x,y,z]" (GetCreature(GetPlayerID()), in the game). Each
  part is left out where it throws. The failed check itself is the message at the error level. Not done above debug:
  the work runs only when the level is debug.
- **The fatal path** (high; M5 "Kept"). FatalError writes its line at the error level, then, in Debug builds
  (`!defined(NDEBUG)`) only, the caller's stack as one error line ("Stack trace:" and std::stacktrace's to_string;
  where the library has none, a line that says so) and `BreakIfDebugged`: IsDebuggerPresent and DebugBreak on Windows
  (kernel32's, declared without <windows.h>), the TracerPid of /proc/self/status and SIGTRAP on Linux, nothing
  elsewhere; without a debugger nothing happens and the box follows. Then, unchanged, the connection shut down, the
  display mode restored, the window hidden, the box, exit(1). std::stacktrace by compiler: MSVC 19.51 yes (the Debug
  test build's trace names FatalError, HandleException, Run's catch, AfxWinMain); GCC 16.2 on Linux yes (in
  libstdc++exp, which patella_target_language already links for contract_assert); Clang 22.1 on Linux with Debian's
  libstdc++ 14 yes, with libstdc++exp, linked by patella_target_language when a check program links (cmake/Warnings.cmake,
  PATELLA_CLANG_STDCXXEXP); a libc++ has no __cpp_lib_stacktrace, the check fails and the fallback line is written;
  mingw-w64 GCC 16.2 no (its libstdc++ has no backtrace for Windows: __cpp_lib_stacktrace undefined), so the fallback;
  the oracle's /std:c++17 no. C++26's std::breakpoint_if_debugging was considered: GCC 16 has it only in libstdc++exp,
  MSVC and Clang's libstdc++ 14 not at all.
- **oracle-x86** (high). The log works there too, at its defaults: Patella.ini is never read (Settings.cpp and
  LogSettings.cpp are not in the oracle; the call is the x64 client's), so the level is info and the lines go to
  stderr only. difftest compares no stderr with the original (Tibia.exe wrote error.txt); its Errors test (and the
  golden corpus's) compares our HandleException's stderr with the text it expects, now "[error] Debug Assertion 7.72
  <message>\n" (tests/golden/errors_tests.cpp; FatalError itself is faked there, so neither the box line nor the stack
  trace is written). The debug diagnostics never run in the tests (info level), and difftest gets a stub
  GetLastPacketTypes (tools/difftest/playertest.cpp: Control.cpp is not linked there). No layout changes; no check
  count changes.

### The tests

  the lines, the levels written, the formats through both paths, the file (appended, flushed per line, a folder
  refused), the client's log, the stack trace, the debugger break); tests/unit/core_log_settings_test.cpp in tests_core
  (4 cases: the defaults, LogLevel, LogFile, LoadSettings from a Patella.ini in the working directory). tests_unit 57 to

- **The counts** (high). `python -I tools/build.py oracle-x86`: difftest 16,459,337, sysinctest 67, communicationtest

- **The fatal path, live** (high). PatellaTest.exe on the reference error session (the forced unrecoverable error:
