## The thread census counts after lavapipe's threads have ended (Patella-Modern issue #87)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026. Seen in #78 part 5: windows-x64-asan's tests_vulkan failed one check
of issue #53's handle census ("switching to and from the CPU driver leaves no handles of ours"), the per-device
count of ended rasterizer threads: 21 and then 27 where every device leaves 24. tests/vulkan only; no src/ change.

- **Why the count moved** (high). On Windows, Mesa 26.2.5's `lp_rast_destroy` (lp_rast.c, lines 1334-1350) waits
  on each rasterizer thread's `work_done` semaphore, which the thread posts just before it returns. It does not
  wait for the thread to end (it never joins it on Windows; notes/vulkan.md, "Handles the drivers leave (issue
  #53)"). So right after a CPU driver device is destroyed, some of its threads may still be exiting. The census
  counted their handles as handles of live threads, and the next census counted them as ended, in the next device's
  share. The sum stays the same (21 + 27 = 2 × 24). It shows under ASan because ASan's thread exit is slower, and
  more often under load.
- **The fix: count once the threads have ended** (high). Each census in the rounds is now taken through `Settled`.
  `Settled` looks for handles that are new since the previous census, are of live threads, and whose thread started
  in vulkan_lvp.dll (or in the ASan runtime; issue #70). It waits on those handles (WaitForSingleObject; the census
  already queries their start address), then takes the census again. It stops when no such thread is left, or after
  30 s in all. A handle value can be reused, so "new" means not the same handle of the same live thread.
  `TakeCensus` now also records the start address of live threads. Every check keeps its exact numbers and its
  purpose: the same number of rasterizer threads for every device, at most LP_MAX_THREADS, all started in the
  driver, and that number times the devices in all. A thread that does not end within the timeout stays live, and
  those checks then count it. Considered and not taken:
  - a bound instead of equality: it would lose the "same for every device" check, which is what catches a device
    that leaves more threads;
  - polling the count until it is stable: slower, and "stable" is itself a timing guess;
  - checking only the total over all devices: it would also lose the per-device check.
- **The log** (high). The census line also prints how many threads a census found still ending (summed over the
  censuses), so the logs show whether the wait did anything.
- **Not yet seen working** (November 6, 2026). In the 52 runs after the fix (20 windows-x64, 20 windows-x64-asan, 12
  under three concurrent ASan loops), no census found a thread still ending, so the wait never ran. The fix follows
  from Mesa's source (lp_rast.c, lp_rast_destroy) and the sum-preserving counts (21 + 27 = 2 x 24), but is untested
  against the failure itself; the census line's "still ending" count will show it when it happens.

## patch_client.py --rsa on the Debug builds: the modulus's two copies (Patella-Modern issue #82)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026. Found in #73: `tools/patch_client.py --rsa` refused every Debug image
("the RSA modulus: expected one occurrence, found 2"), so compare_traffic.py and testmode_check.py, which patch in the
server's key, could not use a Debug client. src/Communication.cpp passes CipSoft's modulus to TRSA::SetPublicKey twice,
as two identical literals (the login connection, line 110, and the game connection, line 170). Tibia.exe and every
Release build pool identical strings (/GF, which /O1 and /O2 imply), so the image holds one copy, referenced twice; the Debug
builds do not pool, so they hold two copies, each referenced once (windows-x64-debug Patella.exe: 0xce6250 and
0xce65f0 in the file). No src/ change.

- **Both copies, each referenced by code** (high). The copies are found as the 309 digits with a NUL before and after
  (a lookahead and lookbehind, so two copies with one NUL between them are both found). One copy is patched as
  before. Two are patched only when the code references each of them: on x86 its absolute address in a code section,
  on x64 a RIP-relative disp32 after a ModRM byte with mod 00 and r/m 101 (first_reference's test) whose target is
  inside the copy. Both get the same text, NUL-padded to the old length, so the image's layout and size stay the same.
  Any other count (zero, three or more), or two copies of which one is not referenced, stays an error. The check after
  writing reads each copy back as the new modulus. The new scan (`literal_references`) reads the code with
  struct.iter_unpack per alignment: about 8 s on a 19 MB Debug image. Considered: telling Debug from the PDB (the
  issue's suggestion; a PDB does not say whether strings were pooled, and the references say directly which copies
  the client reads); patching any number of copies (a stray copy elsewhere would be patched unseen); one literal in
  src/ (a src/ change, while #79 rewrites src/; and Patella.ini's key, D8 for M8, will remove the patching anyway).
- **The self-test** (high). `--self-test` builds made-up PE32 and PE32+ images (a code and a data section, the four
  login server names, the modulus copies, `push imm32` or `lea rcx, [rip+disp32]` references into the middle of
  each copy) and runs patch, verify and check on them: one copy referenced twice, and two copies each referenced
  twice, are patched (each copy to the same 308-digit text and its NUL padding); two copies with only the first, only
  the second or neither referenced, and three copies, are refused. It also checks that a disp32 after a ModRM other
  than mod 00 r/m 101 is no reference.
- **Proof** (high). main's patch_client.py (c9c4833) and the branch's, with `--host 127.0.0.1 --rsa
  C:/Tibia/gameserver/tibia.pem` and with `--port 7271` added, on Tibia.exe, the oracle-x86 Release Patella.exe, and
  windows-x64 and windows-x64-asan Release Patella.exe and PatellaTest.exe: the outputs are identical byte for byte
  (344 bytes changed, 348 with the port). The Debug images (windows-x64-debug and windows-x64-asan-debug, Patella.exe
  and PatellaTest.exe): main refused them, the branch patches both copies (620 bytes changed, 621 with the port), the
  same size, every changed byte in a patched range, both copies equal to the Release image's patched text. Logs:
  build\logs\issue-82 of the branch's worktree.
- **Live proof** (high). `python -I tools/testmode_check.py --exe build/windows-x64/Debug/PatellaTest.exe --runs 2
  --timeout 600 --out build/testmode/issue-82` (the client patched with the server's key by testmode_check.py itself):
  both runs log in (login and game connection, account 772001), walk four steps, talk and log out (opcodes
  login-login game-login a0 65 66 67 68 96 14); a (client packets), b (raw frames), c (driver logs), d (Tibia.cfg),
  f (the packet log against the proxy's decrypted recording), g (frames) and h (keys) pass. Exit code 1, from e
  alone: see the next point.
- **Found, not done** (high). With a Debug PatellaTest.exe, check e (the state dumps against client_state.py's reading
  from outside) differs only in "gui": the client's dump lists 9 to 50 windows, client_state.py's reading 1 to 3 (the
  root, then a modal TDialog where the client has TStartWindow and TBorder). Every other key of the six dumps is the
  same. client_state.py's walk of the window tree does not follow the Debug image's (tools/client_state.py, not the
  RSA patch: the packets show the session as the Release client plays it). An issue of its own.

## TASSERT* to PATELLA_ASSERT (Patella-Modern issue #79)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026; M5 (notes/modernization-plan.md, 7 M5: "`TASSERT*` becomes
`PATELLA_ASSERT(expr)`"), after #76 (outcome-only comparison) and #78 (TBEGIN/TEND deleted).

- **contract_assert is not used** (high). The plan named `contract_assert` (and `pre(...)`) on GCC 16. What a failed
  assertion throws must stay a TMyException: difftest and the golden corpus compare the kind (#76), and the original
  throws one. A contract assertion with the default semantic "enforce" ends the program after the violation handler
  returns; only a replaceable violation handler that throws gives an exception. Tried on GCC 16.2.0 in the Linux image
  (`g++ -std=c++26`, `-lstdc++exp`, a `handle_contract_violation` that throws; build\issue-79 scratch, never
  committed): (1) a throwing handler does propagate out of `contract_assert` under enforce and observe, and out of a
  noexcept function it terminates, as a throw does; but (2) `-fcontract-evaluation-semantic=ignore` compiles the check
  out (the predicate was not evaluated, nothing thrown) and `quick_enforce` terminates without calling the handler:
  a compiler flag decides whether an assertion on a packet is checked at all; (3) the handler is one for the whole
  program, so CONTRACT_ASSERT (compat/cxx26.h, TStaticVector's preconditions, which must terminate: its
  RunContractViolation tests) would throw a TMyException too; (4) GCC 16.2's `std::contracts::contract_violation`
  has no `evaluation_exception()` and reports `detection_mode::predicate_false` also when the predicate threw, so a
  predicate's own exception (a PROGRAM_ERROR, say) could not be passed on unchanged: its kind would change; (5) the
  standard lets a contract predicate be evaluated more than once, or its side effects be elided (P2900, the repeated
  evaluation of contract assertions), where TASSERT evaluated it exactly once; and (6) locals are const inside a
  contract predicate. Sources: GCC 16.2's `<contracts>` (/usr/local/include/c++/16.2.0/contracts in the image),
  `g++ --help=c++` (the -fcontract-* options), compat/cxx26.h's notes on GCC's handler. So PATELLA_ASSERT is the same
  function-based check on every compiler; `pre(...)` is not used either (the same handler).
- **The macro** (high). src/compat/assertion.h (not cxx26.h: the oracle-x86 build compiles common.h with /std:c++17,
  and cxx26.h's stand-ins need C++23; the header is C++17-clean like compat/span.h). `PATELLA_ASSERT(Expression)` and
  `PATELLA_ASSERT_VALUES(Expression, Value1[, Value2])`: an expression of type void, `(!(Expression) ?
  patella::AssertionFailed(#Expression, PATELLA_SOURCE_LOCATION()) : void())`, so it is one statement anywhere (no
  dangling else); the expression is evaluated once with `!` as TASSERT did, the values only when it fails (in an
  unspecified order, as TASSERT2's arguments), each `static_cast<int>` as TASSERT1/2's `(int)` cast. The failure
  functions (TMyException.cpp, `[[noreturn]]`) throw `TMyException(file, line, "assertion failed", names, values,
  expression)`: the same kind, the same message format, but with the assertion's own file and line
  (std::source_location::current() where the library has it, every product preset; in the oracle's C++17 and with
  PATELLA_SOURCE_LOCATION_STANDIN, tests/unit's stand-in build, an aggregate from `__FILE__`, `__LINE__`,
  `__func__`). The values' names are the preprocessor's text of the values (`#__VA_ARGS__`), split at the top-level
  commas. Nothing is compiled out in any build (the plan's later release-build option waits for M9's fuzzing).
- **The variants** (high). The original's line, TASSERT*'s first argument, is gone (the source location replaces it;
  the lines stay in git history, in the image and in the comments that name a function's lines). TASSERT1 and TASSERT2
  are PATELLA_ASSERT_VALUES, whose values stay in the message, the diagnostic that matters (the developer log writes
  the message at error). The file-local bug variants (Map.cpp's TASSERTB/B1/B2, ContentWindows.cpp's TASSERTB2,
  graphics.cpp's, SurfaceDX.cpp's and surfaceDX9.cpp's TASSERTB1, Creatures.cpp's TASSERT1_BUG/TASSERT2_BUG) appended
  a CipSoft bug number to the expression text ("[bug0000013]" 39 sites, "[bug0000913]" 14, "[bug0000845]" 3,
  "[bug0000038]" 2, "[bug0000290]" 2, "[bug0000289]", "[bug0000611]", "[bug0000996]" one each: 63): an internal
  tracker's number tells a developer of this fork nothing, so they are PATELLA_ASSERT(_VALUES) without it.
- **The conversion** (high). A script outside the repository (build\issue-79 scratch: convert_tassert.py, balanced
  arguments, comments skipped): 802 sites in 30 files, TASSERT 348, TASSERT1 292, TASSERT2 99, TASSERTB 1, TASSERTB1 57,
  TASSERTB2 3, TASSERT1_BUG 1, TASSERT2_BUG 1; PATELLA_ASSERT 349, PATELLA_ASSERT_VALUES 453. The arguments are as
  written apart from Utils.cpp's 16 `NULL` in assertions, now `nullptr` (#76's 16 modernize-use-nullptr findings; the
  baseline shrinks by its entry). The three macros of common.h and the nine local ones are deleted; .clang-format's
  WhitespaceSensitiveMacros names PATELLA_ASSERT and PATELLA_ASSERT_VALUES instead. `git grep TASSERT -- src`: nothing.
- **An MSVC x86 bug the change exposed: TPlayerStates::GetIcon** (high). The first oracle run ended difftest with an
  uncaught C++ exception in ContentWindows' error round: a fake's assertion thrown under TPlayerStates::GetIcon did
  not reach OurThrow's catch. GetIcon's `default: TERROR1(1063, "index out of range", i)` can never run (i is 0-9);
  MSVC 19.51 x86 (/O2, /EHa and /EHsc alike) removes its code but keeps the function's exception frame (five states,
  no unwind actions) and leaves the frame's handler out of the object's .sxdata, so it is missing from the image's
  SafeSEH table and Windows refuses it (STATUS_INVALID_EXCEPTION_HANDLER under cdb): every exception through GetIcon
  ended the program, in difftest and in the oracle Patella.exe alike. Main hid it: TASSERT2's inline throw kept live
  unwind actions in the same frame. The default now does nothing (the original's TERROR1 named in the comment): the
  outcome is the same, as it was never reached. A scan of the x86 images for exception-frame prologues whose handler
  is not in the SafeSEH table (scratch safeseh_scan.py, never committed): on this branch before the fix one each in
  difftest.exe, communicationtest.exe and Patella.exe (GetIcon), after it 0 in difftest, communicationtest, sysinctest,
  vlongtest and Patella.exe; main 0. The x64 images use table-based unwinding and are not affected.
- **The tests** (high). tests/unit/assertion_test.cpp in tests_unit and tests_unit_cxx26_standin (7 cases, with
  TMyException.cpp linked: the location path selected, a true expression evaluated once and nothing thrown, a false
  one throwing TMyException with this file, the line and the expression, the values not evaluated when true and
  evaluated once when false, the names split at top-level commas, the int conversion, a predicate's own exception
  passing unchanged, one statement under if/else). tests_core's Utils and Container tests compared assertion
  messages with the original's lines: they now compare "<file> N: assertion failed..." (TERROR messages keep their
  lines) and `nullptr` in Utils.cpp's texts.
- **The images** (high). Main (168970f) and the branch built at the same path (this worktree), Release, function by
  function through the PDBs (`dumpbin /disasm:nobytes`; scratch funcs.py, never committed: addresses, image-relative
  displacements and the switch tables after a function's code masked). x64 Patella.exe: 13,913 to 13,946 functions;
  579 changed, 162 gone, 195 new. x86 (oracle-x86's Patella.exe): 11,377 to 11,369; 652 changed, 24 gone, 16 new. Of
  the changed, 447 (x64) and 500 (x86) are assertion sites (ours calls patella::AssertionFailed or main constructed a
  TMyException there). The other 132 and 152 were sampled: inlining that follows from smaller assertion code (a
  callee whose inline throw is gone now fits: FindTalkFilter into IsPermanentIgnore, Container.h's constructors into
  their callers, the "gone" list's 162 container constructors and funclets), funclets renumbered by those inlinings,
  TERRORs inlined where their function got smaller (GetRightName), GetIcon's dropped default, and in the x86 image
  library code (MFC, the CRT's float parsing, std::to_chars) whose difference is the bytes after its last instruction
  that the masking does not cut. New: AssertionFailed (three), AssertionFailedValues<int>, <int,int>, <int,TObject>,
  source_location::file_name, functions now out of line. No sampled function changed in its own logic.
- **The gates** (high). `python -I tools/build.py oracle-x86`: difftest 16,459,337, sysinctest 67, communicationtest
  856,621, vlongtest 3,201, 0 failures, CTest 4/4 (unchanged: no check counts a text). windows-x64 14/14,
  windows-x64-debug and windows-x64-asan 13/13 (no ASan finding): golden on main's corpus 15,803,203 replayed +
  1,512,822 retired = 17,316,025, 0 failures (nothing recorded: the corpus has no texts). windows-x64-gcc,
  linux-x64-gcc and linux-x64-clang 11/11. 0 warnings on every preset. tests_unit 65 to 72 cases: MSVC 10,166
  assertions (the stand-in 10,170), mingw-w64 GCC 10,163 / 10,167; on Linux 64 to 71: GCC 10,148 / 10,152, Clang
  10,146 / 10,152 (the Linux numbers from the run before the test's Throws got a condition for MSVC's C4702; the same
  cases). tests_core 42 cases, 390 assertions on Windows, 393 on Linux, unchanged in number. tidy_ci 4 findings in 4
  entries (from 20 in 5: the 16 use-nullptr gone, nothing new; Utils.cpp's `<cstddef>` went with its last NULL, and
  assertion.h includes `<cstdint>` only for the stand-in, both misc-include-cleaner), 0 bugprone; banned_calls 0;
  clang-format clean. `python -I tools/reference.py compare --reference C:/Tibia/Patella-Modern/build/reference`:
  every session matches (error with #74's deliberate differences); the error session's line "[error] Debug
  Assertion 7.72 Player.cpp 383: exception occurred, reason: Control.cpp 1274: unknown packet type during game (Type
  = 255)" (a TERROR, unchanged). Logs: build\logs\issue-79.

## client_state.py's window test on the Debug builds: TWindow::GetFirstChild by its address (Patella-Modern issue #88)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026. Found in #82: with a Debug PatellaTest.exe, testmode_check.py's check e
differed only in "gui" (the client's dump 9 to 50 windows, client_state.py's reading 1 to 3). gui() calls a component
a window when its vtable slot of TComponent::GetFirstChild leads to TWindow's `return FirstChild;`, and it recognised
that function only by its Release code, `mov rax, [rcx+disp8]; ret` (48 8b 41 XX c3; 8b 41 XX c3 on x86). The Debug
build compiles it with /Od, through the stack: `mov [rsp+8], rcx; push rdi; mov rax, [rsp+10h]; mov rax, [rax+38h];
pop rdi; ret` (windows-x64-debug PatellaTest.exe, RVA 0x142b20, 17 bytes). So no component was a window: the walk
listed MainWindow's top-level siblings (and the modal) and never went into a child list. Member offsets, the vtable
slot (0x40) and the RTTI names were right; the Debug layout of the STL plays no part (the tree is TComponent's own
Next/FirstChild pointers). No src/ change.

- **The PDB's address of TWindow::GetFirstChild, then the pattern** (high). Layout gets `functions` (LAYOUT_FUNCTIONS:
  TWindow::GetFirstChild, its RVA from the PDB through Pdb.function_symbol; none when inlined everywhere). is_window()
  follows up to four `jmp rel32` thunks (an incremental link's ILT; the x64 builds link /INCREMENTAL:NO today, the
  oracle-x86 Debug build the same) and compares the target with that address; when it differs, the code pattern
  decides as before. Tibia.exe has no PDB: the pattern alone, unchanged. In a Release image the PDB's function holds
  the pattern's bytes (with /OPT:ICF possibly as the folded copy of another such getter, which the pattern accepted
  anyway), so the address test can only agree with the pattern: Release readings are unchanged by construction.
  Considered: a second, Debug byte pattern (it depends on /Od's register choices, /RTC and /JMC: brittle); RTTI
  (whether a class derives from TWindow: its class hierarchy descriptor gives it, but more reading per component for
  the same answer).
- **The self-test** (high). `--self-test` builds made-up vtables and code in its own process: the Release body is a
  window by the pattern without a PDB address and the Debug body is not; with the address, the Debug body is a window
  directly and through a jmp thunk, a body that is neither (TElement's stand-in) is not, the Release body still is.
  `--layout` lists the function's RVA.
- **Proof** (high). `python -I tools/testmode_check.py --exe build/windows-x64/Debug/PatellaTest.exe --runs 2 --timeout
  600`: exit 0, a-h pass; e equal in all six dumps of both runs (9, 23, 50, 50, 50 and 25 windows). The same with
  build/windows-x64/Release/PatellaTest.exe: exit 0, a-h pass, unchanged (its first attempt stopped before any client
  ran: the test server logged "Server Online" but listened on neither port within 300 s; stopped, the rerun passed). Logs: build\logs\issue-88 of the branch's
  worktree.

## The SafeSEH gate of oracle-x86 (Patella-Modern issue #89)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026. Found in #79 (above, "An MSVC x86 bug the change exposed"): MSVC 19.51 x86
can keep a function's exception frame and leave the frame's handler out of the object's .sxdata, so it is missing
from the image's SafeSEH table, and Windows ends the process when an exception passes the frame. #79's scratch
scanner (build\tools-scratch\safeseh_scan.py, left in place: #80 uses it) is now tools/safeseh_scan.py, and oracle-x86
runs it. No src/ change.

- **What a registration is** (high). Read from the five images' code (dumpbin /disasm of the oracle's Patella.exe and
  difftest.exe, every fs:[0] access sorted by its context) and from each fs:[0] load: the C++ EH prologue of MSVC 14.x
  x86, push -1 (6A FF); push __ehhandler$<function> (68 imm32); mov eax, fs:[0] (64 A1), always adjacent (with or
  without push ebp; mov ebp, esp, and after the aligned frames' lea ebp / sub esp or __chkstk); the inline SEH4
  frame (push -2; push <scope table>; push _except_handler4) and the SEH3 form with -1; push handler; push fs:[0]
  (__SEH_prolog4, __SEH_prolog4_GS, _local_unwind4); the CRT's guard records (mov [ebp+d+4], __CatchGuardHandler or
  __TranslatorGuardHandler, then mov eax, fs:[0]; mov [ebp+d], eax: the record's two fields, so a nearby unrelated
  store is not taken); and mov eax, __ehhandler$...; call <helper>, where the helper is __EH_prolog3, _GS, _catch,
  _catch_GS (push eax; push fs:[0]), __EH_prolog3_align and _GS_align (their aligned frame first) or the old
  __EH_prolog. The handler must lie in an executable section, or the bytes are no registration (a push -1; push
  <data> is skipped). The scratch scanner saw only the first pattern (with a 24-byte window) and would have read an
  SEH3 frame's scope table as its handler; it missed MFC's 1,242 __EH_prolog3 frames in Patella.exe. Counted against
  the listing: Patella.exe 608 C++ EH, 1,242 EH_prolog (841 + 305 + 51 + 6 + 10 + 29 calls, every one), 12 SEH4, 2
  guard, 3 push handler; the 4 fs:[0] loads left (_CallSETranslator's second, _JumpToContinuation,
  _UnwindNestedFrames twice) read or restore the chain. Since the handlers checked are the table's own (the
  CRT's _except_handler4, the guard handlers, every __ehhandler$ thunk, which jumps to __CxxFrameHandler3), they are
  fine when present: membership in the table is the whole check.
- **The table** (high). The load configuration's own Size must reach SEHandlerCount (0x48); SEHandlerTable is a VA,
  its entries RVAs. No load configuration, a short one or no table (/SAFESEH:NO) is reported as such and fails;
  IMAGE_DLLCHARACTERISTICS_NO_SEH fails when a handler is registered (Windows calls none) and passes otherwise. A PE32+
  or non-x86 image is refused (exit 2).
- **Names** (high). From the PDB of the image's CodeView record (its path, then the image's folder), used only when
  its GUID is the image's: the module streams' S_GPROC32/S_LPROC32 ranges name the containing function, the publics
  (S_PUB32) the handler; else `<image>.map`'s publics, else the RVA. A small MSF 7.00 reader with struct (no pefile,
  no new dependency). Patella.exe has Patella.pdb (/DEBUG); the four test programs are linked without one, as the
  former build.cmd linked them, so their findings are RVAs: adding /DEBUG or /MAP to them would change their command
  lines for a name the Patella.exe line already gives. The __ehhandler$ thunks are in neither the publics nor the
  procedures of Patella.pdb, so a handler shows as its RVA.
- **A CTest test, not a post-build step** (high). `safeseh` in cmake/OracleX86.cmake after the four difftests: it
  reads the linked images only, a finding fails `ctest --preset oracle-x86` and build.py like a difftest failure,
  the images stay for a look, and a post-build step would stop the build before the difftests could show the
  crash; and `-R safeseh` runs it alone. CTest 4/4 becomes 5/5. The self-test is not a
  CTest test (it would make six): `python -I tools/safeseh_scan.py --self-test` builds made-up PE32 images (a .text
  and an .rdata with the load configuration, the table and a CodeView record) with each kind of frame, a clean one,
  one whose handler is missing from the table, the same with a made-up PDB (the function named) and with a PDB of
  another GUID (not used), a map, no table, no load configuration, NO_SEH with and without a frame, an x64 image and
  a file that is no PE.
- **The proofs** (high). Branch issue-89 at the same path: `python -I tools/build.py oracle-x86` exit 0, CTest 5/5,
  difftest 16,459,337, sysinctest 67, communicationtest 856,621, vlongtest 3,201, 0 failures; safeseh 0 findings
  (difftest 2,821 registrations, sysinctest 107, communicationtest 1,040, vlongtest 41, Patella.exe 1,867). #79's
  GetIcon fix reverted (`default: TERROR1(1063, "index out of range", i);`, never committed): exit 8, CTest 3/5, the
  gate fails with one finding in each of three images, "TPlayerStates::GetIcon: C++ EH frame at RVA 0x00020503,
  handler RVA 0x001faa30 not in the SafeSEH table" in Patella.exe and the RVAs in difftest.exe (0x001dfa88) and
  communicationtest.exe (0x000a30f8), sysinctest and vlongtest clean, and difftest ends with an uncaught C++
  exception in TestContentWindows, as in #79. Restored: 5/5 again, 0 findings. Logs: build\logs\issue-89.

## The tools wait for the world; the window's place before the exit (Patella-Modern issue #68)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026. tools/testserver.py, tools/compare_traffic.py, tools/compare_files.py,
tools/testmode_check.py; notes/testserver.md ("Start"), notes/testmode.md ("The cold start (issue #25)"). Tools and
docs only, no src/ change.

- **The wait in testserver.py start, for every tool** (high). The issue asks to share testmode_check.py's wait for
  "Server Online!" (issue #25). compare_traffic.start_server, which compare_files.py, testmode_check.py and
  reference.py's live recordings all call, runs `testserver.py start`. So the wait now lives in start itself, and
  `testserver.py start` by hand gives the same guarantee. start returns 0 only when both ports listen (by the
  server's PID, as before) AND server.log says "Server Online!". The case of #25 stays: when the log does not have
  "Starting Login Server" once both ports listen, the output does not reach the file as it is written, and the
  ports alone count, with a line that says so. testmode_check.py's own wait and its `--online-timeout` went (no
  caller passed it); its retry of an unanswered game login stays: the wait cannot see a game server that loaded
  but does not answer.
- **Progress, not a fixed clock, decides a stall** (high). Issue #75's second start took more than the old 300 s on
  a busy machine. Issue #88's run logged "Server Online" and listened on neither port within 300 s. A fixed
  timeout cannot tell those two apart; progress can. An attempt is given up when there is no progress (server.log
  grew, a port began to listen, the process used CPU time: GetProcessTimes, /proc/<pid>/stat on Linux) for
  `--stall` seconds (180); when "Server Online!" is in the log but both ports do not listen `--after-online`
  seconds (60) later (#88); when it has taken `--timeout` seconds (900) in all; or when the server exits. CPU
  time counts as progress because the map's sectors load without a line for many seconds on a busy machine, and
  a loading server always uses CPU, while a deadlocked one does not. The made-up servers of `testserver.py
  self-test` (also run by `testmode_check.py --self-test`) cover each case.
- **Stop the attempt's own server and retry once** (high). A failed attempt's server is the one this start started
  (server.pid, the same executable and creation time), so stop() handles it as always: Ctrl+C, and since it never
  came online and has nothing to save, killed after 30 s. Its server.log is kept as
  build\testserver\server-attempt<N>.log. Then the server starts again, `--retries` times (1). Before every
  attempt the checks of the first run again: a tibia-server from that folder that runs, or a port someone holds,
  ends start with exit code 1 and is never touched. Every step prints a `testserver start:` line, which
  compare_traffic.py copies into the tools' logs.
- **The window placed before the exit, not a mask** (high). The second run of #64 wrote `WindowedMode =
  (-4,6,800,600,no)` from Tibia.exe and `(10,10,800,600,no)` from Patella.exe. Both start at Tibia.cfg's (10,10),
  and the client writes WindowedMode at its exit from GetWindowPlacement's normal rectangle (src/MainFrm.cpp
  OnDestroy). On this branch the shift came back once, in the first `--only options` run, with a build running
  beside it. It did not come back in the later runs: three Tibia.exe and one Patella.exe options sessions with the
  window's place read at every step (always (10,10,810,610), normal), a second `--only options` run, and the
  gate runs below. So Windows moves the window now and then on its own. It is not a difference between the clients. Of the issue's two options, placing the window
  keeps the most comparison. A mask of WindowedMode's position would stop checking, in every run, that a client
  writes the position its window has. Placing the window makes the place an input of the session, like the
  Tibia.cfg it starts with: compare_files.py's close() checks, just before the WM_CLOSE, whether the window's
  normal place is Tibia.cfg's (x, y, width, height), not maximised. If not, it puts the window there with
  SetWindowPlacement (SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE, so no focus moves) and logs where it was. The report lists every window
  it moved ("window placement before the exit"), so a shift stays visible, and WindowedMode, position, size and
  maximised flag, is still compared byte for byte. This applies to every compare_files.py scenario that ends with
  WM_CLOSE (options, walk, the live recording's Tibia.exe run; error ends at its error box). Not done:
  compare_traffic.py's and the reference recordings' closes (sc.Driver.close). They compare or record Tibia.cfg
  too, but the issue saw the shift only in the options session, and changing a recording's session is a matter
  for the reference set. `compare_files.py --self-test` checks the placement on a window of its own: left alone in

## TMyException with a source location, TProgramError, std::expected (Patella-Modern issue #80)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026; M5 (notes/modernization-plan.md, 7 M5: "`TMyException` shrinks to a
message and a `std::source_location`. `PROGRAM_ERROR` becomes an `enum class` carried by its own exception type.
Recoverable failures (a file that does not load, a host that does not resolve) return `std::expected<T, TError>`"),
after #76 (outcome-only comparison), #78 (TBEGIN/TEND deleted) and #79 (PATELLA_ASSERT).

### The split (high)

One branch (issue-80), one commit per part, each built and scanned on its own:

- **80a**: TMyException becomes a message and a source location; TMYEXCEPTION, TERROR* and PATELLA_ASSERT's failure
  functions build it; the line arguments of the sites go.
- **80b**: PROGRAM_ERROR becomes an `enum class` with named values, thrown inside `TProgramError`; every throw and
  catch changes with it; golden_eh's OurThrow maps a TProgramError to the kind the original's bare enum has.
- **80c**: the recoverable failures return `std::expected<T, TError>`, or are documented with a plan when that is
  too risky in this issue.

### 80a: TMyException, a message and a source location (high)

- **The class** (src/TMyException.h): `TMyException(std::string Message, const patella::TSourceLocation &Location)`,
  `GetMessage()`, `GetLocation()`, the virtual destructor kept (RTTI; the thrown type's name stays
  `.?AVTMyException@@`, which golden_eh compares). The old fields are gone: the Origin string ("<file> <line>" of the
  site that first raised the error) had error.txt's report (#74) as its only reader; File, Line, Kind, the two named
  values and the reason are folded into the message, whose format is unchanged: `patella::ErrorText` is the text of
  the original constructor 0x508400 ("<file> <line>: <Kind>[ (<N1> = <V1>)][ (<N2> = <V2>)][, reason:\n<Reason>]", the
  file without its path) and of the wrapping one 0x5086a0 (the inner message always appended), `ErrorOrigin` the old
  origin's text for the tests' comparison and the failure reports. `patella::MakeError(Location, Kind, N1, V1, N2, V2,
  Reason | Inner)` builds the exception for TMYEXCEPTION, the TERROR* macros and PATELLA_ASSERT's failure functions.
- **The layout** (high): nothing compared depends on it. The image's TMyException (vtable, two VC7.1 strings of 0x1c
  bytes, 0x3c bytes) never had our layout (MSVC 19's std::string is 0x18 bytes on x86): the tests keep the two sides'
  exceptions apart (ThrowSideAssertion, ImageSideVtable), imageeh.cpp reads the image's by its own offsets, difftest's
  crash report reads ours as our class. No static_assert names its size. So no same-size replacement is needed.
- **The sites**: TMYEXCEPTION(Kind, N1, V1, N2, V2, Reason) and TERROR, TERROR1, TERROR2, TERROR_REASON,
  TERROR1_REASON and MapWindow.cpp's TERROR1B lose their first argument, the original's line (as TASSERT* did in #79):
  the site's own `PATELLA_SOURCE_LOCATION()` replaces it. A script (scratch, never committed) removed it at 132 sites
  in 22 files (src/ and control_tests.cpp), comments skipped; the lines stay in git history, the image and the
  comments that name a function's lines. The throw stays inline at each site (`throw TMYEXCEPTION(...)`); the text
  parameters are string_views.
- **The box and the log** (tier A unchanged): HandleException still shows TextCriticalError in "Tibia Error - Debug
  Assertion" and logs `[error] Debug Assertion 7.72 <message>`; the message's format is the same, its lines are our
  own now (the error session's line under "The gates").
- **The tests**: errors_tests.cpp's TestMyException compares ErrorText (both forms) and ErrorOrigin with the
  original's constructors for the same 2,000 random arguments, as it compared the constructors (the same checks, the
  same corpus records); its HandleException part builds ours from ErrorText. golden_eh's ThrownOf and OurSideAssertion
  use ErrorOrigin and ErrorText. tests_core's Container and Utils tests compare messages as "<file> N: ..." (their
  TERROR lines are ours now). New: tests/unit/exception_test.cpp (5 cases, both unit builds).

### 80b: PROGRAM_ERROR as an enum class in TProgramError (high)

- `enum class PROGRAM_ERROR : int` with names of ours after GetErrorText's texts and the sites (OBJECTS_FILE 1,
  SPRITES_FILE 2, PICTURES_FILE 3, SPRITES_DATA 4, PICTURES_DATA 5, SOCKET_INIT 6, DIRECTX_INIT 7, COLOR_DEPTH 8,
  CLIPPER 9, COOPERATIVE_LEVEL 10, DISPLAY_MODE 11, SURFACE 12 (the primary surface and the generic code),
  SCREEN_SURFACE 13, TEMP_SURFACE 14, STRETCH_SURFACE 15, CACHE_SURFACE 16, AUTOMAP_SURFACE 17, SPRITE_SURFACE 18), and
  `struct TProgramError { PROGRAM_ERROR Code; }`, 4 bytes, trivially copyable (static_asserts in every build).
- 62 throws became `throw TProgramError{PROGRAM_ERROR::...}` (11 files, SurfaceVulkan.cpp among them), the 7 catches
  `catch (const TProgramError &Error)` (Control.cpp's InitControl, the three ResetDisplays, Player.cpp's InitInstance
  and Run): a rethrow is `throw Error;`, a copy, as before. HandleProgramError(PROGRAM_ERROR) shows the code as an int
  (the same box text; sysinc.cpp's GetErrorText/GetErrorHint keep their int parameter, compared with the original's).
- **The golden_eh mapping**: OurThrow catches `const TProgramError &` first, and ThrownOf(TProgramError) gives it the
  kind PROGRAMERROR, the type name of the original's bare enum (`.?AW4PROGRAM_ERROR@@`) and the value: what
  imageeh.cpp's ImageFilter gives the original's throw. So every check compares what it did (the kind and the value),
  and the corpus records the same. A bare PROGRAM_ERROR of ours (nothing throws one) would be OTHER and fail.
  control_tests.cpp's ControlThrow throws ours in a TProgramError on our side (the image side still throws the image's
  enum through its own _CxxThrowException); MouseMoveAsWrapped catches `const TProgramError &`. No image code catches
  an exception of ours or the reverse (the sides' throws are apart, as for TMyException).
- The tidy baseline loses cppcoreguidelines-use-enum-class's PROGRAM_ERROR entry (4 to 3). New: tests_core's
  core_errors_test.cpp (3 cases: TERROR*, TMYEXCEPTION's wrap, TProgramError caught neither as the enum nor as a
  TMyException).

### 80c: the recoverable failures (high)

`src/compat/expected.h`: `patella::TExpected<T, E>` and `TUnexpected<E>` are std::expected and std::unexpected where
the library has them (every product preset), a C++17 stand-in in the oracle (and with PATELLA_EXPECTED_STANDIN in
tests_unit_cxx26_standin). `TError { std::string Message; TSourceLocation Location; }` (TMyException.h) is what a
TMyException would carry; `TMyException(TError)` throws it after all; `MakeFailure` and common.h's
`TUNEXPECTED_REASON(Message, Reason)` build one. The paths, by how the client recovers:

| Path | Returns now | Comparison boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TReadScriptFile, TWriteScriptFile, TReadBinaryFile, TWriteBinaryFile `TryOpen` (Script.cpp): "file still open", "failed to open file" | `TExpected<void, TError>` | `open`, which the original exposes and errors_tests compares directly, keeps throwing: `if (!TryOpen(...)) throw TMyException(error)`. The checks are unchanged. |
| LoadAutomapBlock (Map.cpp): a map file that does not open, an empty block | tests `TryOpen(...).has_value()` instead of catching open's TMyException | Nothing else in open throws a TMyException (TFile::Open and the copies are noexcept), so the outcome is the same; map_tests compare the function as before. A damaged file (the reads) still throws inside and is caught there: the reads are the original's throwing functions, compared one by one. |
| SaveAutomapBlock (Map.cpp): a map file that does not open, nothing written | the same | The same; the writes' failures stay caught. |
| InitPreferences, SavePreferences (Preferences.cpp): Tibia.cfg missing or malformed, the defaults or nothing | unchanged: catch (TMyException &) | The failure comes from anywhere in the tokenizer (TReadScriptFile::error and the TERRORs of compared functions); the catch is the recovery boundary. |
| ResolveHostname, CreateSocket, ConnectSocket (Network.cpp): a host that does not resolve, a socket that does not connect | unchanged: bool, a WinSock code | They never threw; their returns are the original's, compared directly. |
| The fatal paths (InitObjects, the graphics loaders, the surfaces) | unchanged: TProgramError | Not recoverable: they end the client. |

New: tests/unit/expected_test.cpp (5 cases, both paths). compat/expected.h is in the header checks (core and oracle).

## unique_ptr for the owners blocked by noexcept(false) destructors (Patella-Modern issue #81)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026; M5's last issue (#58's M5 list: notes/ownership.md, section 7), after
#78 (TBEGIN/TEND deleted), #76 (outcome-only comparison), #79 (PATELLA_ASSERT) and #80 (TMyException, TProgramError).
The rules are #58's: every original delete a `reset()` at the same place and in the same order, the allocations
`reset(new ...)`, layouts frozen in oracle-x86 (size and offset asserted under `PATELLA_ORIGINAL_LAYOUT`).

### The question: can the destructors still throw (high)

`std::unique_ptr::reset()` and its destructor are `noexcept` whatever the deleter: an exception from the owned
object's destructor ends in `std::terminate`, where the original let it pass to the caller. So each pointee's
destructor, and what it calls, was read again on main bd08107:

- **`~TTalkBuffer`** (was `noexcept(false)`): `Clear()`, which calls `Remove(first)` until `first` is null. In a
  destructor the virtual calls are TTalkBuffer's own, and Remove of the first line takes its first two branches
  (`line == first && line == last`, `line == first`); the search with its `PATELLA_ASSERT(Search!=NULL)` is only for a
  line in the middle. `free` does not throw. The destructor cannot throw, so it is now implicitly `noexcept`. Its
  derived classes (TPrivateTalkBuffer, TChannelTalkBuffer, TRuleViolationTalkBuffer, TRuleViolationChannel; the tests'
  TConsoleBuffer, TCommBuffer, TTestBuffer) declare no destructor. No check makes it throw (tests/golden and
  tools/difftest searched: no error round fakes Clear or Remove for a destructor).
- **`~TComponent`** stays `noexcept(false)`, and with it every window destructor. `~TTab` keeps
  `PATELLA_ASSERT(PlayerName!=NULL)` (a player's report without a name), calls SendCancelRuleViolation,
  SendCloseRuleViolation and SendLeaveChannel, and DeleteTextBuffer (`PATELLA_ASSERT(Filter!=-1)`);
  `~TConsoleWindow` calls StoreOpenChannels and SetConsoleHeight; `~TContainerWindowBody` SendCloseContainer;
  `~TTradeWindowBody` SendRejectTrade; `~TAutomapWindow` SetAutomapZoom; `~TSubWindow` SetContentWindowSize;
  `~TMainWindow` ClearOpenDialogs and StoreOpenDialogs. The golden ConsoleWindow test throws through `~TTab` on
  purpose ("A player's report without a name: its tab's destructor asserts", tests/golden/consolewindow_tests.cpp,
  two rounds that delete the console and compare the outcome). Making TComponent's destructor `noexcept` would turn
  that round's TMyException into `std::terminate` (the runner would crash), and a real client's assertion there into
  an end without the error box. Proving the throws unreachable is not possible: the golden round reaches one.

### The owners (high)

- **Converted**: `TConsoleWindow::History` (`std::unique_ptr<TTalkBuffer>`: the constructor's `History.reset(new
  TTalkBuffer(0))`, the destructor's `History.reset()` where the original deleted it, before the buttons);
  `TEditLine::Text` (`std::unique_ptr<char[]>`: `reset(new char[_MaxLength + 1])` in both constructors, `reset()` in
  the destructor, `.get()` in every reader of src/ and three golden tests); `TPasswordEditLine::Stars` (the same;
  Draw's two swaps through a local, `Help = Text; Text = Stars; Stars = Help`, are `Text.swap(Stars)`: the same
  values in the same members at every call, and an exception from TEditLine::Draw leaves them swapped, as the
  original did). The TASSERT2 arguments that blocked Text (#58) are PATELLA_ASSERTs whose text is not compared
  (#76, #79). Layouts: TConsoleWindow 0x6c, History +0x48; TEditLine 0x68, Text +0x2c; TPasswordEditLine 0x6c,
  Stars +0x68, and `sizeof`/`alignof` of `std::unique_ptr<TTalkBuffer>` against the raw pointer, in ConsoleWindow.cpp
  and DialogElements.cpp under `PATELLA_ORIGINAL_LAYOUT`.
- **Kept raw**, each in notes/ownership.md section 7 with the milestone:
  - `TTabBar::LeftTabs`, `RightTabs`: their windows hold the tabs that do not fit, so `delete LeftTabs` runs
    `~TTab`. As `unique_ptr`s, `reset()` would terminate, and a throw out of the first delete would destroy
    `RightTabs` (and send its tabs' leave-channel packets) while unwinding, where the original left it. M7 (the GUI
    tree): the destructors' work that can fail moves into an explicit close before the delete, then TComponent's
    destructor can be `noexcept` and these two convert.
  - `ModalWindow`, `MainWindow`: TComponent pointees (the main window's tree holds the console), and a global
    `unique_ptr` would run the window destructors during static destruction after FatalError's `exit(1)`. M7
    (owned by `TClient`).
  - The conditional component members (TSubWindow's parts, TConsoleWindow's buttons, `TListBox::EditLine`): also
    owned by the child list by `IsChild`/`Editing`. M7.
  - The text buffers (`DefaultTextBuffer`, CreateTextBuffer's): `~TTalkBuffer` no longer blocks them, but they are
    allocated with `new (std::nothrow)` and freed with the destructor and `free` (a mismatched release), and owned
    through a tab and the console filter list at once. M7.

### The images (high)

Main's Release images (C:\Tibia\Patella-Modern\build, built from bd08107; copied, read only) against the branch's,
function by function through the PDBs (#78's scratch funcs.py and classify.py, `dumpbin /disasm:nobytes`, addresses
and string-literal symbols masked: main was built in another folder, so every `__FILE__` literal has another name).
x64 Patella.exe: 14,020 to 14,024 functions; 109 changed, 5 gone, 9 new. Of the changed, 91 differ only in the
assertion line constants of ConsoleWindow.cpp, DialogElements.cpp and Talk.cpp (the files gained lines); the other 18
are the converted owners' functions (TConsoleWindow's constructor and destructor, TEditLine's constructors,
destructor, deleting destructors, HandleEvent, InsertChar, InsertText, LeftButtonDoubleClick, TEditText::KeyPress,
TPasswordEditLine's constructor, `~TTalkBuffer`) and their unwind funclets. Gone/new: the constructors' funclets
renumbered and `std::unique_ptr<TTalkBuffer>`'s destructor. x86 (oracle-x86's Patella.exe): 11,410 to 11,411; 106
changed, 83 line constants only, 23 the converted owners' (the same, plus the inlined TEditLine code in TListBox's
constructor, the Draw and GetPosition functions of the edit lines, ExitTalk, which calls `~TTalkBuffer` without an
EH state of its own now, TTalkBuffer's scalar deleting destructor, and the funclet block dumpbin names
`___guard_check_icall_thunk`); 1 new (the `unique_ptr` destructor). No other function changed. Logs:
build\logs\issue-81\list-x64.txt, list-x86.txt.

vlongtest 3,201, 0 failures (unchanged), safeseh 0 findings (difftest 1669 handlers/2785 registrations, sysinctest

## A fatal error before the main window is set (Patella-Modern issue #83)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026, on branch issue-83 (M5, the fatal path of #77). #56 found that a failing
first present (the CPU driver on a hidden desktop) crashed the x64 client with 0xC0000005 instead of ending it with
"Tibia Error", and put the crash in ExitControl after InitControl's catch. That was the wrong place.

- **Where it crashes** (high: seen under cdb). The first present is not in InitControl: InitControl has returned
  (CMainFrame's constructor), and InitInstance's `Redraw(false)` draws the first frame after the surfaces exist and
  before `m_pMainWnd = MainFrame`. TSurfaceVulkan's present catches the TVulkanError and throws PROGRAM_ERROR 12
  (Fail), InitInstance's `catch (const TProgramError &)` calls HandleProgramError, and FatalError calls
  `AfxGetMainWnd()->ShowWindow(SW_HIDE)` with AfxGetMainWnd() null. CWnd::ShowWindow reads `m_pCtrlSite` and
  `m_hWnd` through the null `this`: an access violation. The stack (build\logs\issue-83\cdb-before.txt):
  CWnd::ShowWindow, CPlayerApp::FatalError+0xa1, HandleProgramError, InitInstance's catch funclet, InitInstance,
  AfxWinMain. The log line `[error] Tibia Error: Video surface allocation failed. (Error Code 12)` was already written,
  the box never shown. ExitControl's steps are safe without a main window or with modules not initialised (each
  Exit deletes or frees what may be null; GetSurface creates a surface first), and are not on this path.
- **What Tibia.exe does** (high: the code and its exception tables). FatalError (0x4d7d80) calls CWnd::ShowWindow
  (0x526c14, MFC 7.1's: `if (m_pCtrlSite == NULL) return ::ShowWindow(m_hWnd, nCmdShow)`, reading `this+0x4c` and
  `this+0x1c`) with `this` taken from AfxGetMainWnd (0x527436) and null when it returns null: the same null call.
  The call is in try state 4, whose handler is `catch (...)` at 0x4d7e16 (ehinfo.py: three try blocks, each `catch
  ...`). MSVC 7.1's `catch (...)` catches structured exceptions too, so the access violation is caught and FatalError
  goes on to MessageBoxA and `_exit(1)`. Tibia.exe ends with the box; it does not crash. (A hidden desktop with
  Tibia.exe is not the same path: its DirectX engines fall back to OpenGL there, #56.)
- **The choice** (high). The original does not crash, so ours matches it: FatalError skips ShowWindow when
  AfxGetMainWnd() is null (src/Player.cpp), the one step whose `catch (...)` relied on catching an access violation,
  which /EHsc does not. There is no window to hide then, and the steps after it are unchanged. Every other path is
  unchanged: with a main window the same call. No deliberate difference (tools/deliberate.py unchanged): the
  outcome is Tibia.exe's, the box and exit code 1. Considered: compiling Player.cpp with /EHa (catches every
  structured exception in every handler of the file, a wider change; #67 decides on the SEH-dependent handlers);
  setting m_pMainWnd before the first Redraw (moves the original's order of InitInstance). The same FatalError is the
  oracle's (its /EHsc crashed the same way); difftest fakes FatalError, so no count changes.
- **The test** (high). The test build's hook `PATELLA_TEST_PRESENT_FAILURE(Failure)` (src/TestHooks.h; nothing outside
  PatellaTest.exe) before TRenderer::Present in TSurfaceVulkan's blit throws the TVulkanError of a failing
  vkQueuePresentKHR (VkResult -5) when `PATELLA_TEST_FAIL_PRESENT=1` is in the environment (PresentFails,
  src/testmode/TestModeWin32.cpp, read once). It reproduces #56's path on any desktop and device. Command (from a run
  folder with the data files; build\repro83):
  `PATELLA_VULKAN=cpu PATELLA_TEST_FAIL_PRESENT=1 build/windows-x64/Release/PatellaTest.exe --test-script quit.script
  --test-out out` (quit.script: `wait 2000`, `quit`; with a script the box goes to messages.txt instead of a dialog).
  Before the fix: the `[error]` line, then exit code 0xC0000005 (bash: 139), no messages.txt. After: the same line
  on stderr, messages.txt `{"step":1,"time":0,"caption":"Tibia Error","text":"Video surface allocation failed. (Error
  Code 12)\r\n\r\nPlease choose another video graphics mode.","type":16}`, exit code 1. Without the switch the same
  run exits 0. Not a CTest test: it opens a window on the desktop of the session, as the live checks do.
- **The images** (high). Main (f1be76a) and the branch built in this worktree, Release, function by function through
  the PDBs (scratch funcs2.py, never committed: `dumpbin /disasm:nobytes`, addresses and image-relative displacements
  of 5+ hex digits masked). x64 Patella.exe: 13,947 functions on both sides, none gone or new; FatalError changed;
  InitInstance's and Run's catch funclets and GetWindowClassName differ only in their source-line constants (Player.cpp
  gained five lines above them); the other 22 only in the switch-table bytes after their code (the code after FatalError
  moved). x86 (oracle-x86's Patella.exe): 11,378 on both sides; FatalError changed; InitInstance, Run and
  GetWindowClassName only in the line constants. The hook is empty outside the test build: TSurfaceVulkan's blit is the
  same. Logs: build\logs\issue-83\pecompare-x64.log, pecompare-x86.log.
- **The gates** (high). `python -I tools/build.py oracle-x86`: CTest 5/5, difftest 16,459,337, sysinctest 67,
  communicationtest 856,621, vlongtest 3,201, 0 failures (unchanged), safeseh 0. windows-x64 14/14, windows-x64-debug

## The catch blocks that relied on catching structured exceptions (Patella-Modern issue #67, part 2)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026; M5 (plan 7). #67's first part (a zero-sized patch block) went with the
patcher (#75). The original (MSVC 7.1) gave every `catch (...)` /EHa's meaning: it also caught a structured exception,
an integer division by zero or an access violation. The x64 client and the oracle's Patella.exe build with /EHsc, where
`catch (...)` never sees one: the trap ends the process (exit code 0xC0000094 or 0xC0000005, no box). Only the
difftest programs and the golden runner's comm directory build with /EHa, and the original's code in them keeps its
own meaning, so they already compare the original's error paths; the runner's other directories and every product
build do not.

### The method (high)

`git grep -n "catch *(\.\.\.)" -- src` on f1be76a: 43 handlers (the same 43 on the branch after the merge of
#83, whose FatalError comment adds a 44th line that is not a handler, Player.cpp 154). For each: what its try
block can fault on, whether input (a packet, a file, the environment) can make it fault, and what the original did
then. Two of them, InitInstance's and Run's top-level `catch (...)` ("unknown exception occurred", then
HandleException's "Tibia Error - Debug Assertion" box and exit code 1), have the whole client in their try blocks; for
them every integer division and remainder of src/ whose divisor is not a constant was listed (`git grep -nE` for `/`
and `%` with a name or a call on the right, also `/=` and `%=`, in the .cpp and .h files) and its divisor traced to
its source:

| Division | The divisor's source | Can input make it zero |
|---|---|---|
| Creatures.cpp TCreature::StartMovement, `(Beat - 1 + Duration) / Beat * Beat` | the game login's word (Communication.cpp ReceiveGameLogin, packet 0x0a) | yes: a server's 0, then any step (0x6d, or the player's own walk, DoPlayerStep) |
| Objects.cpp GetCumulativePattern and GetLiquidPattern, `% GetObjectPatternWidth`, `% GetObjectPatternHeight` | Tibia.dat (a pattern size byte) | yes: a damaged or edited Tibia.dat (LoadProperties then allocates no sprites, no error) |
| MapWindow.cpp TMapWindow::DrawObject: the three pattern sizes and the phases | Tibia.dat | yes |
| MapWindow.cpp TMapWindow::DrawCreature, `% GetOutfitPhases` (ANIMATEALWAYS) | Tibia.dat | yes (the other branch's GetAnimationPhase asserts the phases already) |
| graphics.cpp DrawObject, `% GetObjectPhases` and `/ GetObjectExactSize`; DrawOutfit, `/ GetOutfitExactSize` | Tibia.dat (ExactSize is read when the width or height is above 1) | yes |
| Creatures.cpp StartMovement's `/ Speed`, GetAnimationPhase's `% (AvailablePhases - 1)` | a packet, Tibia.dat | no: `Speed > 0` and `AvailablePhases == 1` are tested first |
| ContentWindows.cpp TStatusWindow::Draw, `/ MaxHealth`, `/ MaxMana` | packets (words) | no: only under `Health < MaxHealth`, which a zero maximum never meets |
| DialogElements.cpp the scroll bars' `/ (Max - Min)`, TProgressBar's `/ Maximum` | the ranges; a packet's reconnect time | no: only when Enabled (`Min != Max`); SetMaximum asserts `maximum>0` |
| the skin and font properties (ContentWindows.cpp, ContextMenus.cpp, graphics.cpp's fonts, the `% Skins[n].height` of the backgrounds) | constants of GUI.cpp, Skins.cpp and InitGraphics | no |
| MapWindow.cpp's `/ Width`, `/ Height` (the map's scaling), graphics.cpp's video cache (`/ PerSurface`), the frame timers | the window's and the surfaces' sizes, the clock | no input; the frame timers divide doubles |
| vlong.cpp, TRSA.cpp, TXTEA.cpp | the fixed key and the block sizes | no |

An access violation from input is another matter. The original's checks of input are its assertions and Container.h's
checked indices (TMyExceptions it reports by design), and the reads of packets and files are checked (TReadBuffer,
TReadBinaryFile). An access violation that remains is a memory error (a stale or null pointer, an unchecked index),
which the original "reported" only when it happened to land on an unmapped page and which the sanitizer presets and
the hardening are there to find: the x64 client ending on it is the sane outcome, (c). The null pointers of the
fatal-error path found below are not of that kind: the original's error path made those calls on NULL every time.

### The decisions (high)

(a) not SEH-dependent, nothing to do; (b) SEH-dependent, input reaches it and the original recovered or reported, so
x64 now checks where the trap was and takes the original's path, with a test; (c) SEH-dependent, but the trap is
unreachable from input or a crash is the only sane outcome; #83: left to issue #83's agent (InitControl and
ExitControl, worked on at the same time); settled in #83: fixed there. Lines are the branch's, after the merge of #83.

| Location | What can fault in the try block | The original | x64 on main | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Communication.cpp 124, 184: SendLogin's and SendGameLogin's RSA (after `catch (const char *)`) | TRSA on the fixed public key and a 128-byte block of fixed layout: nothing from input | the message with the block's bytes (TERROR) | the same (only C++ exceptions possible) | (a) |
| Control.cpp 121: CheckSurface, the surface's Init | the graphics driver (x64: the Vulkan loader and driver; the oracle: DirectDraw, Direct3D 9, OpenGL); Tibia.cfg's mode only reaches the driver | PROGRAM_ERROR 12, "Video surface allocation failed" | a driver's trap ends the client | (c): a fault inside a driver is not input's, and a driver that faulted leaves no state to go on with; no input division there (the surfaces' scale factors are doubles) |
| Control.cpp 174, 181, 189, 199, 207: ChangeEngine's five steps | the DirectDraw, Direct3D 9 and OpenGL drivers | a TMyException with the step's message | oracle-x86 only (the x64 ChangeEngine is the Vulkan device choice, with no handler) | (c): oracle only; those engines retire with the oracle (#29) |

In all: 21 (a), 17 (c) (Control.cpp 121, 174, 181, 189, 199, 207; Player.cpp 316; Surface.cpp 204, 254, 274;
SurfaceDX.cpp 591; surfaceDX9.cpp 507; SurfaceGL.cpp 156, 709, 712, 725; SurfaceVulkan.cpp 560), 2 (b) (Player.cpp 359, 389), 1 settled in #83 (Player.cpp 158), 2 #83 (Control.cpp 1170,
Player.cpp 149; #83 fixed neither: its notes list ExitControl's null dereference as found, not done; both settled in #90).

### The changes (high)

- **PATELLA_DIVISOR(Value)** (compat/assertion.h, with PATELLA_ASSERT): the divisor itself, evaluated once; when it is
  zero, the TMyException "<file> <line>: integer division by zero, reason:\n<Value's text>" (TMyException.cpp's
  DivisionByZero, through MakeError) instead of the division. It is the original's outcome by kind, which difftest and
  the golden corpus compare: each of the six functions had a catch wrapper in the original (StartMovement line 142,
  GetCumulativePattern 796-810, GetLiquidPattern 821-826, TMapWindow::DrawObject 1071-1094, DrawCreature 1106-1129,
  graphics.cpp's DrawObject 1100, DrawOutfit 1137), whose `catch (...)` made the trap a TMyException ("unknown
  exception occurred") right there. From there both go up the same way: no handler on the way catches a TMyException
  and recovers (Communication.cpp's cylinder loop's try block holds no step), so a step with Beat 0 or an object with a
  zero pattern ends in Run's handler and HandleException's box, exit code 1, and a draw out of the game in
  MainWindow::Draw's PROGRAM_ERROR 12, as in the original. A divisor that is not zero gives the same quotient and the
  same calls in the same order (the divisor's call was the division's operand already). The divisors: StartMovement's
  Beat; GetCumulativePattern's and GetLiquidPattern's two pattern sizes; DrawObject's (MapWindow.cpp) three pattern
  sizes and phases; DrawCreature's outfit phases; graphics.cpp DrawObject's phases and exact size, DrawOutfit's exact
  size. No check at the load (LoadProperties): the original loads such an entry without an error and fails only when
  the object is drawn, and the error stays where it was.
- **FatalError's main window** (Player.cpp): settled in #83, which tests `AfxGetMainWnd()` for NULL before
  ShowWindow(SW_HIDE) (this branch had the same check; the merge keeps #83's). When it is NULL the original's call
  faulted at once (the first read of `this`), and its handler went on to the box.

### The tests (high)

- **Divisions** (tests/golden/divisions_tests.cpp; difftest.exe's last test, DIFFTEST_ONLY=Divisions alone): ours
  against the original by outcome, StartMovement with Beat 50, 1 and 0 (the step's duration compared when neither
  throws), GetCumulativePattern and GetLiquidPattern on the first cumulative and the first liquid container of the real
  Tibia.dat as it is, with its pattern width 0 and with its height 0 (both sides' property tables; the pattern
  compared when neither throws). 15 checks, 9 exceptions compared, 5 calls that threw. Before the checks (the sites
  reverted, the oracle's /EHa build): 5 failures, each "ours other exception, original TMyException "Creatures.cpp
  142: unknown exception occurred"" (or Objects.cpp 810, 826): the original's wrapper turned the trap into a
  TMyException, our trap passed as another type (build\logs\issue-67b\before-difftest-divisions.log); after: 0
  failures (after-difftest-divisions.log). difftest.cpp's crash report leaves out the original's expected traps again
  (ExpectDivideByZero, gone with #75's patch blocks, set around the original's calls here). In the golden runner it is
  a ported test (registered with `Since = "#67"`, runner.cpp): a corpus recorded before it, as main's, has no
  Divisions test, which the runner notes and accepts instead of calling the corpus stale; the next recording of the
  corpus records it and the runner replays it on x64 (/EHsc: there, before the checks, our trap ended the runner).
- **PATELLA_DIVISOR** (tests/unit/assertion_test.cpp, in tests_unit and the stand-in build on every preset): a divisor
  that is not zero is the value, evaluated once (quotients and remainders of negative and unsigned operands); zero
  throws the TMyException with this file, the line and the divisor's text, the division not done.
- **fatal_error_box** (CTest, for #83's check, windows-x64, windows-x64-debug and windows-x64-asan, wherever PatellaTest.exe is built;
  cmake/RunFatalErrorBox.cmake): PatellaTest.exe in a temporary folder with copies of Tibia.dat, Tibia.spr and
  Tibia.pic (CipSoft's: local, removed afterwards; skipped without them), `VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_DISABLE=*` and

  Before the check (main f1be76a's PatellaTest.exe, the same folder): an access violation in CWnd::ShowWindow, exit

  catch block). No window is shown: the frame is created hidden and the box is the test mode's record.
- Not compared function by function: the drawing sites' zero divisors (MapWindow.cpp's DrawObject and DrawCreature,
  graphics.cpp's DrawObject and DrawOutfit), which need the graphics tests' surfaces and sprites; the macro is the
  same, the original functions' outcome is their wrapper's TMyException as in the compared ones.

## A PROGRAM_ERROR in InitControl (Patella-Modern issue #90)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026, on branch issue-90 (M5; found in #67 part 2, Control.cpp 1170 and
Player.cpp 149 of its table). On x64 a PROGRAM_ERROR from any step of InitControl (a missing Tibia.dat is enough)
ended the client with an access violation instead of the "Tibia Error" box.

- **Where it crashes** (high: seen under cdb, build\logs\issue-90\cdb-before.txt). main 02be035's PatellaTest.exe in
  a folder with Tibia.spr and Tibia.pic but no Tibia.dat: InitObjects throws PROGRAM_ERROR 1, InitControl's `catch
  (const TProgramError &)` calls ExitControl, and `GetSurface()->ExitSurfaces()` calls through NULL (ExitControl+0x2a,
  under InitControl's catch funclet, under CMainFrame's constructor and InitInstance): the x64 GetSurface makes a
  surface only for curEngine 2, which SurfaceInitInstance sets after the frame window exists. Exit code 0xC0000005,
  no `[error]` line, no box. With ExitControl fixed alone (build\logs\issue-90\cdb-exitcontrol-only.txt), the next
  fault is FatalError's SetDisplayMode(1) step (the view mode is still 0): CWnd::ModifyStyle on MainFrame, which
  points to the frame that `new CMainFrame` freed when its constructor threw; after that, Redraw would call
  CheckSurface on the NULL surface and `MainWindow->Draw` on the NULL main window.
- **What Tibia.exe does** (high: the code, its exception tables and a run under cdb). ehinfo.py: InitControl
  (0x44b510) has a `catch (PROGRAM_ERROR)` around its steps whose handler (0x44b5c9) calls ExitControl inside a `catch
  (...)` (0x44b5f0, empty) and rethrows; ExitControl (0x448e30) has its own catch wrapper (PROGRAM_ERROR, TMyException,
  `...` to TERROR at line 1661); FatalError (0x4d7d80) has three `catch (...)` blocks (states 0, 2, 4:
  ShutdownConnection, SetDisplayMode, ShowWindow). Tibia.exe in a folder without Tibia.dat under x86 cdb (access
  violations and C++ exceptions logged, a breakpoint on MessageBoxA that quits before the box opens;
  build\logs\issue-90\cdb-tibia-exe.txt): InitObjects' PROGRAM_ERROR, then an access violation at 0x4ec56d inside
  ExitControl's ExitSurfaces (its GetSurface made a DirectX 5 surface, curEngine 0, whose members were never set:
  0xbaadf00d), turned into a TMyException by ExitControl's wrapper and swallowed by InitControl's `catch (...)`; the
  PROGRAM_ERROR goes on (CMainFrame's constructor, InitInstance) to FatalError. There an access violation in
  CWnd::ModifyStyle (0x526b82, `this` the freed frame, 0xfeeefeee) called from SetDisplayMode (0x4a8bd8), turned into a
  TMyException by SetDisplayMode's wrapper and swallowed by FatalError's `catch (...)`; then #83's access violation in
  CWnd::ShowWindow on NULL (0x526c14), swallowed; then MessageBoxA "Cannot find file "Tibia.dat". (Error Code
  1)\r\n\r\nPlease re-install the program.", "Tibia Error" (and `_exit(1)`). MSVC 7.1's `catch (...)` catches the
  access violations; /EHsc's does not.
- **The choice** (high). The outcome is the original's: the box and exit code 1. Each faulting step is skipped where
  the original's handler swallowed its fault, and only when what it works on does not exist:
  - ExitControl (Control.cpp): `GetSurface()->ExitSurfaces()` only when GetSurface() is not NULL. It is never NULL in
    the oracle (its GetSurface always makes one) or once SurfaceInitInstance has run. Unlike the original, the Exit
    functions after it run too (the original's fault left them out): each deletes or frees what may be null, as #83
    found, and the CTest below runs ExitControl after every step, also under ASan.
  - FatalError (Player.cpp): SetDisplayMode(1) only when `MainWindow != nullptr && GetSurface() != nullptr`.
    MainWindow is set in the frame's OnCreate and cleared only by ExitControl, so it is not NULL exactly when the frame
    window exists, and with it MainFrame is valid; on x64 the surface exists once SurfaceInitInstance has run. On every
    path after the frame's creation (#83's failing first present, the fatal_error_box start without a Vulkan driver, a
    PROGRAM_ERROR in the game) both are set and the step is unchanged. Without them the step is skipped; Tibia.exe's
    made SetViewMode(1) before its fault, which nothing reads before `exit(1)`.
  Not done: clearing MainFrame when CMainFrame's constructor throws (it dangles in the original too, and nothing reads
  it on this path now). No deliberate difference (tools/deliberate.py unchanged). The same code is in the oracle,
  where it changes only this path (difftest fakes FatalError; no count changed).
- **The test** (high). The test build's `PATELLA_TEST_INIT_FAILURE(Step)` (src/TestHooks.h; nothing outside
  PatellaTest.exe: Patella.exe's InitControl is unchanged, below) before each of InitControl's 15 steps and after the
  last throws PROGRAM_ERROR 6 when `PATELLA_TEST_FAIL_INIT=<Step>` (1-16) is in the environment (InitFails,
  src/testmode/TestModeWin32.cpp, read once). The CTest **init_control_failure** (windows-x64, -debug, -asan;
  cmake/RunInitControlFailure.cmake, skipped without the data files) runs PatellaTest.exe 17 times in temporary
  folders without a Vulkan driver (VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_DISABLE=*, PATELLA_VULKAN=cpu): once without Tibia.dat (the box
  "Cannot find file \"Tibia.dat\". (Error Code 1)"), and for each step 1-16 with the data files ("(Error Code 6)");
  each must exit with code 1 and write the "Tibia Error" box to messages.txt. No window is shown (the frame window is
  never created). Before (main 02be035, the same folder layout, build\repro90-before): no Tibia.dat ends with exit
  code 0xC0000005 (bash 139), no messages.txt. After: `[error] Tibia Error: Cannot find file "Tibia.dat". (Error Code
  1)` on stderr, messages.txt `{"step":1,"time":0,"caption":"Tibia Error","text":"Cannot find file \"Tibia.dat\".
  (Error Code 1)\r\n\r\nPlease re-install the program.","type":16}`, exit code 1; the 16 steps the same with "(Error
  Code 6)".
- **The images** (high). Main 02be035's sources and the branch's built in this worktree, Release Patella.exe of
  windows-x64 and oracle-x86, function by function through the PDBs (#78's funcs.py and classify.py on `dumpbin
  /disasm:nobytes`; build\logs\issue-90\pecompare). x64: 14,025 functions on both sides, none gone or new; ExitControl
  and FatalError changed; GetWindowClassName and twelve of InitInstance's and Run's catch funclets only in a line

- **The gates** (high). `python -I tools/build.py oracle-x86`: CTest 5/5, difftest 16,459,352, sysinctest 67,

### The control channel (high)

- **A channel, not more script commands** (high). The drivers decide their clicks from what the client shows at that
  moment (a dialog's place, a check box's state, a creature's name position), so they must read the running client;
  a script written in advance cannot. The reference recordings solve that by recording Tibia.exe's clicks; the live
  comparisons (compare_traffic.py, compare_files.py, compare_rendering.py's replay) compare a running client with
  Tibia.exe and need the reading. So the test build answers the tools while it runs: the tool makes two events
  (`<name>-command`, `<name>-done`) and writes control.txt into --test-out; at an idle call (the driver's step in
  OnIdle, on the client's thread: nothing of the client runs meanwhile) the client does the command and answers in
  control-reply.txt. Considered: a socket (more code; the events are what --test-sync already used); shared memory
  (patcap's way; a probe is JSON of 50 to 200 KB).
- **The probe** (high). `probe` writes probe.json: the state dump's "state" and "gui" (the same code and form, so the
  states compared with Tibia.exe's readings are the state dump's), plus "characters", "skin", "members" (by the gui's
  "ptr"), "names", "device", "frames", "ticks" (src/testmode/StateDump.h, "The probe"). A pointer member is a "ptr" of
  the tree, so the drivers' `node_by_ptr(member(...))` works unchanged. It reads and never writes
  (ClientStateWin32.cpp, as the state dump). One probe per reading: a value is the client's at that call, as a fresh
  ReadProcessMemory was. A probe takes about 10 ms.
- **Without a script: probe only** (high). compare_traffic.py and compare_files.py run the client live against the
  server on the system clock and post their messages to its window, as for Patella.exe: PatellaTest.exe without a
  script takes Windows' input and is the client on the system clock (notes/testmode.md, "Running it"). The channel
  answers `probe` there and refuses anything else.
- **With a script: script lines after the last event** (high). compare_rendering.py needs patcap's time course. The
  test client starts with a script of `clock manual` and `cursor 1020 760` (patcap's clock and cursor); each
  command's lines are parsed as a script of their own (after `clock manual` for a manual clock) and appended after the
  last event at the clock's time (TScheduler::Append, unit-tested), and the command is done once they are handed out,
  the idle calls after each (QuietPasses) have passed and its frames were taken. pace, clock and cursor belong to the
  starting script and are refused, as wait and at are with a manual clock (the parser's rule). Every message goes
  through it as a `post` line, because a scripted client drops Windows' input (DropInput): the messages Tibia.exe
  gets posted, dispatched as the reference compare dispatches them.
- **The frame** (medium). patcap captured after skipping 2 frames; a `frame` line takes the next frame shown. With the
  clock frozen between advances the frames drawn at one moment are the same picture (the reference compare already
  matches Tibia.exe's patcap frames with `frame`), so the scenes compare as before; the gate below shows it.
- **The test build only** (high). Status.cpp's View function and the hook's fifth argument are inside the test
  build's `#if defined(PATELLA_TEST_MODE)` and its empty macro. src/vulkan/SurfaceVulkan.cpp still asks for
  patcap.dll (`GetModuleHandleA("patcap.dll")`), which no tool loads into the x64 client now; removing the lookup
  changes Patella.exe, which this issue keeps the same (found, not done).

### testmode_check.py's check e (high)

Until now e compared each state dump with client_state.py's reading of the same moment from the client's memory (the
client waited at each dump, --test-sync). For the x64 client that reading is gone, and with it the outside half of e.
Decided: e checks each dump on its own, and the values are compared with the original's by the reference compare.

- `--test-sync` stays in the test build; no tool uses it any more.
