## Reproducible golden recordings, no reliance on evaluation order (Patella-Modern issue #55)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026; M6's first issue, before #93 (the final recording). Found in #30. No src/
change: every cause was in the tests. tests/golden (core_tests.cpp, talk_tests.cpp, golden_test.h and the files below),
tools/difftest's three surface tests, cmake/OracleX86.cmake, cmake/CompareGoldenRecordings.cmake.

- **What differed** (high). Two recordings of main (0810767), the same build, into two folders: 40 of 43 files the
  same; Buffers.bin (81,870 bytes), Talk.bin (also in size: 1,189,206 against 1,189,260 records) and difftest's
  manifest.tsv (Talk's record count) not. The records were parsed and the first differing ones named (a scratch
  script, not committed): Buffers' "text bytes" and Talk's "line identity".
- **Buffers: the stack's leftovers** (high). PutBytes takes 7 bytes of a text that may be shorter; the bytes after
  its end were never written (`char Texts[40][32]` uninitialised), and #24 recorded the whole buffer ("text bytes")
  so that the runner used the oracle's. They were whatever the stack held, which differs between runs. Now `Texts` is
  zeroed and the record is gone (both sides write the same zeros; the comparison is unchanged). Buffers: 80,652
  checks as before, 281,282 records to 241,956.
- **Talk: lines by their heap address** (high). OriginalLineId gave an original's line the identity it had before when
  its address was in a map from address to identity and the contents were the same. Whether a new line got a freed
  line's address is the heap's choice, and Windows randomises the low-fragmentation heap's, so the "line identity"
  records (new or known) differed. The runner uses an identity only to find the line's recorded contents. Now the
  map is keyed by the contents (LineKey: the fields, and each text with whether it is NULL and its length), which is
  deterministic and also merges lines of the same contents at different addresses. Talk: 1,214,929 checks as before,
  1,189,206 records to 1,182,231.
- **Proven** (high). After the two fixes, two more recordings of one build: 43 of 43 files byte for byte the same, the
  checks unchanged in every test. With the order fix below a fifth recording, identical to those, and two more through
  the new target (below): 43 of 43. Nothing else in the corpus depends on an address, the time, TEMP or a shared seed:
  every other file was the same in every pair. Looked at, not changed: the tests' maps from the image's or our objects'
  addresses to names (ConsoleWindow's and ContentWindows' Roles, commworld.cpp's Names) name objects by role, so what
  they print does not depend on the address.
- **The check** (high). `python -I tools/build.py --env oracle-x86 cmake --build --preset oracle-x86 --target
  golden_reproducible` runs cmake/CompareGoldenRecordings.cmake's self-test (equal folders, a changed byte, a missing
  file, two empty folders), records the corpus twice from the build into build/oracle-x86/golden-reproducible/1 and /2
  (each test program as golden_corpus runs it, cmake/RunGoldenRecord.cmake), and compares the two file by file: one
  line per file, then "<n> files compared, <k> different". It fails on any difference or missing file and keeps both
  folders then; it removes them when they are the same. About 8 minutes and 1.8 GB while it runs. A target, not a
  CTest test: the oracle-x86 CTest run stays the four comparisons and safeseh (5/5); the check is for a change to the
  recorder or the ported tests, and for #93 before the final recording. Considered: a CTest test kept out of the
  default run by a label (each workflow's test preset would need a filter); a Python tool that also names the first
  differing record (the scratch script did that; CMake alone needs nothing more in this job).
- **Evaluation order** (high). Found with a clang-tidy 22 query-based custom check (`--experimental-custom-checks`; a
  scratch config run through tools/tidy.py with CLANG_TIDY pointing at a wrapper), on windows-x64's
  compile_commands.json for the runner's side and on oracle-x86's (with -m32) for the oracle's side and
  tools/difftest: an expression whose two operands (a binary operator other than && || , << >> and the assignments)
  or two arguments (a call, an overloaded operator, a constructor that is not list-initialisation) each call,
  directly or inside, a function of tests/golden or tools/difftest that reaches Random(), its seed, rand/srand or the
  recorder (1,356 names, a text closure over those files). 55 findings: 53 expressions, and two false ones
  (dialogs_tests.cpp's two Sweep calls, whose lambda arguments do not run where they are passed). Each of the 53 is now
  its calls as temporaries in the order the oracle's MSVC x86 made them: a call's arguments right to left (also
  std::string's operator+ chains, whose last operand is called first), a binary operator's left operand first;
  golden_test.h's `Random32()` is `Random() ^ (Random() << 16)` in that order. Proof: the oracle's recording of the new
  code is byte for byte the one before it (all 43 files, the surface tests' included), and the runner built with the
  new order replays the old order's corpus with 0 failures. So no count and no record changed. The list:
  - tests/golden/communication_tests.cpp: PickID's and Pick32's `Random() ^ (Random() << 16)`;
  - tests/golden/commworld.cpp: the creatures' `(Random() % 3 == 0 ? ... : ...) + Random() % 8`, OpenContainers'
    XOR;
  - tests/golden/core_tests.cpp: XTEA's two plain words, Buffers' values (XOR);
  - tests/golden/gui_tests.cpp: the key's `(0x41 + Random() % 30) | (Random() % 4 << 9)`, TRect Area's four
    arguments;
  - tests/golden/mainfrm_tests.cpp: ResolvedIP's snprintf arguments, the two key messages' `(Chance(50) ? 0x100 : 0)
    | (Random() & ...)`, the error trials' seed (XOR);
  - tests/golden/objects_tests.cpp: the object's Data and the signature (XOR);
  - tests/golden/preferences_tests.cpp: the int options' value (XOR); the generated lines FullscreenMode,
    WindowedMode, ContentWindow, BuddySortmethods, Buddy and the default case's LevelBar/MagLevelBar (operator+
    chains of CfgNumber, CfgString, CfgYes);
  - tests/golden/script_tests.cpp: the list `"[" + RandomNumberText() + ...` and the signed number `(Random() % 2 ?
    "-" : "") + RandomNumberText()`;
  - tests/golden/status_tests.cpp: three values (XOR);
  - tools/difftest/surfacedxtest.cpp: RandomRect's and RandomColor's arguments, StretchTo's `3 * (Random() % 3) +
    (Random() % 2)`, DXMode's four random arguments, the error rounds' Some, Empty and Huge rects;
  - tools/difftest/surfacedx9test.cpp and surfacegltest.cpp: RandomColor and RandomRect, the Source, D, Rects[i],
    Empty, Some (and DX9's Huge) rects of Between() calls; GL's two RandomExtensions(Between(), Chance()).
  Not covered by the query: an order between our side's and the original's calls in one expression that write one
  fake's log (none found: the tests call each side in a statement of its own). Considered: committing the query as a
  tool or a CI check (it needs clang-tidy's experimental option and a name list kept by a script; the order is now
  explicit, and a new test is reviewed against this section); leaving the order implicit and pinning the runner's
  compiler (#91 brings GCC and Clang, which call arguments left to right).
- **The corpus** (high). Recorded again (867 MB): every check count as on main; fewer records in Buffers and Talk only.
  The runner replays it with 0 failures on windows-x64, -debug and -asan.

## TDialogWindow::SetSize and the child its own SetSize deleted (Patella-Modern issue #65)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026, on branch issue-65 (M6; found in #28's second part, "A deleted child
read in TDialogWindow::SetSize"). The owner decided on November 6, 2026 to fix it now.

- **The bug** (high: ASan, build\logs\issue-65\asan-before-run.log). TDialogWindow::SetSize (0x4857b0) sizes each
  child, `Child->SetSize(Width, Child->Height)`, and goes on with `Child->GetNext()`. A sub-window's SetSize ends
  with its column's Rearrange(32) or (2, 4) and then Rearrange(8), whose FitChildren deletes the children that do not
  fit the column's new height (DeleteChild: RemoveChild, then delete), the child being sized among them. The loop
  then calls GetNext on the deleted child: a use after free. RemoveChild had set the child's Next to NULL before the
  delete. The x86 heap and the x64 Release heap leave the freed object as it was, so the original read NULL and its
  loop ended there. The Debug CRT fills freed memory, which is why the Debug golden runner crashed (#28). Only the
  child being sized can be the deleted one the loop reads: a later child deleted by an earlier child's SetSize has
  already been unlinked, so the live child's Next skips it.
- **The fix** (high). After a child's SetSize, the loop goes on to the child's Next only while the child is still in
  the column (`TWindow::IsChild(Child)`, which compares the pointer with the children and does not dereference it).
  Otherwise it ends, as the original's did with the NULL it read. The column's own Rearrange(8) comes after, as
  before. The other option, holding the deleted children until SetSize returns, would have moved their destructors
  (a sub-window's stores its body's height, ContentWindows.cpp's send packets) after the following children's
  SetSize: an order the comparisons can see. The pointer check reads nothing freed, and the order of every call stays
  the same. A freed address cannot come back as a child during the child's SetSize: strategies 2, 4, 8 and 32 delete
  and resize children but never insert one, and only strategy 16 (MakeRoom, a new window) appends. This is a
  deliberate safety difference only in that freed memory is no longer read. The outcome (sizes, layout, the drawing
  order, which children exist afterwards) is the original's, so tools/deliberate.py needs no entry: no comparison can
  see it.
- **The test** (high). CTest **dialogwindow_setsize** (tests/golden/dialogwindow_setsize_test.cpp, doctest; every
  windows-x64 preset). Neither tests_unit nor tests_core can build DialogWindow.cpp (GUI.cpp and the client's other
  files, against the MFC shim). The executable links the golden runner's object libraries with the test in place of
  runner.cpp, and defines runner.cpp's globals. Our columns alone, no corpus, no image. Three cases on a column 176
  wide with sub-windows of a test body of fixed minimum height, the column sized to 180: both children fit (both
  resized); A's SetSize deletes B (A resized, B gone, A's Next NULL); A's own SetSize deletes A and keeps B (A gone,
  B at the top, still 176 wide: the original's loop ended at A). 3 cases, 17 assertions. Before the fix,
  windows-x64-asan: `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free ... READ of size 8` in TDialogWindow::SetSize
  (DialogWindow.cpp:128, the vtable read of GetNext), freed by TWindow::DeleteChild from FitChildren from
  TSubWindow::SetSize; exit code 1. After: 3/3 cases, 17/17 assertions, exit code 0, under ASan and in every
  windows-x64 configuration. difftest has no new check (the test is ours alone), and its counts are unchanged.
- **The runner's workaround removed** (high). dialogwindow_tests.cpp's operator delete (the runner's for every test,
  which held memory freed during DialogWindow's test until its end) is gone. The Debug golden_runner passes without it:
  windows-x64-debug's golden 15,803,218 replayed + 1,512,822 retired = 17,316,040, 0 failures, DialogWindow 24,567 and
  the difftest total 32,526 as the oracle's. That operator delete also took no size, so it had replaced ASan's sized
  delete in the whole runner. Without it, windows-x64-asan's golden found a test instrument (5 reports, one site;
  `ASAN_OPTIONS=continue_on_error=1` listed every report in one run, build\logs\issue-65\asan-golden-continue.log):
  new-delete-type-mismatch in MainWindowTest::TFakeMapFrame's deleting destructor. The test gives our TMapFrames
  (ChangeMode's `new TMapFrame`, 96 bytes) the fake's vtable, so their deleting destructor freed them with the fake's
  size (72). TFakeMapFrame now has a class operator delete without a size (runner only, `#if !GOLDEN_ORACLE`). It is
  a false positive (the block is freed whole; the size is the vtable's), not the client's.
- **The images** (high). Patella.exe of windows-x64 and oracle-x86, Release, built in the worktree with main's
  DialogWindow.cpp and with the branch's, function by function (#78's funcs.py and classify.py on `dumpbin
  /disasm:nobytes`; build\logs\issue-65\pecompare). x64: 14,025 functions on both sides. x86: 11,412. None is gone or
  new. TDialogWindow::SetSize changed (37 to 42 instructions on both; IsChild is a call, not inlined). Six others differ
  only in one or two line constants, +12 (TSubWindow's constructor, Arrange, Minimize, Maximize; TContentWindow::Draw;
  TDialogWindow::Shrink).
- **The gates** (high). `python -I tools/build.py oracle-x86`: CTest 5/5, difftest 16,459,352 (DialogWindow 24,567),
  sysinctest 67, communicationtest 856,621, vlongtest 3,201, 0 failures (unchanged), safeseh 0 (Patella.exe 1093
  handlers, 1808 registrations). windows-x64 17/17, windows-x64-debug 16/16, windows-x64-asan 16/16 (no ASan finding):
  golden on main's corpus 15,803,218 + 1,512,822 = 17,316,040, 0 failures. One test was rerun alone in each of
  windows-x64-debug and windows-x64-asan: fatal_error_box, "A Tibia client is already running!", passed alone. The
  first time my Debug and ASan workflows ran at once. The second time it was CTest's own parallel start of
  fatal_error_box with init_control_failure: both run PatellaTest.exe, and its single-instance check stops the second
  client (main's tests, not this change: neither has a RESOURCE_LOCK). windows-x64-gcc, linux-x64-gcc and
  linux-x64-clang 11/11. 0 warnings on every preset. tidy_ci 3 findings, 0 new (baseline 3), 0 bugprone. tools/tidy.py
  on DialogWindow.cpp and the test (Windows only): no finding on a changed line. banned_calls 0. clang-format clean.

## The test server's bind errors: the server's race, failed at once and retried (Patella-Modern issue #95)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026. tools/testserver.py; notes/testserver.md ("Start", "The bind race"),
notes/reconstruction.md ("Test server"). Tools and docs only, no src/ change; the server's binary, data and config
unchanged (read only).

- **The cause is the server's own start-up race** (high). Read from tibia-server.exe's disassembly (its sources are no
  longer in C:\Tibia\gameserver): StartLoginServer gets a pointer to the global address buffer (0x1401cd960) and the
  login thread builds its std::string from it when it runs (strlen, then a copy; 0x140166690). Meanwhile the main
  thread's InitAll calls ReadConfig a second time, which resets the buffer to "0.0.0.0" and copies bind_address over
  it again, and LoadWorldConfig writes the world's address into it. A copy of "0.0.0.0" binds all interfaces (issue
  #19's 0.0.0.0:7171); a half-written one ("1.0.0.0", "120.0.0", or 7 bytes of "127.0.0.1": "127.0.0") is not a local
  address, and inet_addr plus bind fail with 10049 (each checked with bind on this machine:
  build\logs\issue-95\bind-probe.log). The error line is printed into the middle of the main thread's
  "Initializing database threads & queues..." line, after the second ReadConfig began, as the race needs.
- **Ruled out** (high): Windows' excluded port ranges (netsh: 5357, 13508, 50000-50059, 55777-56463, 61555-61654;
  not 7171 or 7172, and an excluded port fails with 10013); TIME_WAIT or SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE (10048, not 10049; the
  server does not set SO_REUSEADDR and never logged 10048); the WSL, Docker and VirtualBox adapters (the loopback
  pseudo-interface keeps 127.0.0.0/8, and 127.0.0.1 binds; the failing address is not 127.0.0.1).
- **Fail at once, stop once online, retry with its own budget** (high). wait_ready returns ("bind", (server, port,
  code, line)) as soon as server.log has `Failed to bind Login Server on port N (error C)` or the game server's
  `Failed to bind Game Server on port N.`; start prints the line (from its time stamp), the code's meaning (10049: the
  race; 10048: the port taken; 10013: an excluded range or an exclusive holder) and whether netsh lists the port in an
  excluded range (IPv4 and IPv6), whatever the code. The attempt's server is stopped once it says "Server Online!"
  (60 s at most), so its Ctrl+C is the usual shutdown and not one during the map's load, which rewrites data\map at
  the save. A bind failure is cheap (about 5 s) and random, so it has `--bind-retries` (3) of its own before it takes
  from `--retries` (1), which the stalls and exits keep; the issue's "more patient retry". self-test: 17 new cases
  (bind errors, the line's time stamp, the codes' texts, netsh's ranges, the retry budget, wait_online). The other
  outcome of the race, 0.0.0.0:7171, stays compare_traffic.py's restart.
- **The counts** (high). `python -I tools/testserver.py start` / `stop` 10 times in a row: 9 bound at once (3.6 to
  4.1 s), 1 (the 7th) logged 10049 after 0.5 s, its server was stopped and the second attempt bound (19.3 s in all);
  no 0.0.0.0 bind, every stop clean. A made-up tibia-server.exe (scratch, gcc) that writes the error line ran start's
  path end to end: `--bind-retries 1 --retries 1` made 3 attempts, each stopped by Ctrl+C, exit code 1.
- **Not ours to fix**: the server needs to copy the address before the thread starts (or keep the second ReadConfig
  off the buffer). Its binary and code are the user's.

### The gates (high)

`python -I tools/testserver.py self-test`: exit 0, 28 checks (11 of #68, 17 new), 0 failures. The 10 cold starts
above (coldstarts.log, start-NN.log, stop-NN.log, run07-server-attempt1.log). Hosted CI on issue-95. Logs:
build\logs\issue-95 of the branch's worktree.

## The golden corpus on Linux (Patella-Modern issue #91, M6)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026; M6's first item ("the golden corpus is complete and green on x64 Windows
and Linux"). golden_runner, its CTest tests golden and golden_concurrent and #65's dialogwindow_setsize now build in
linux-x64-gcc and linux-x64-clang (Release and Debug) and replay the corpus there. Changed: tests/golden (CMakeLists.txt,
network/CMakeLists.txt, golden_patch.h, golden_test.h, the new linux/ folder and the test files named below),
tools/build.py, and the src/ files below.

### How the code under test compiles on Linux (high)

- **The Windows API: stand-ins of the tests** (tests/golden/linux). The client's files under test include
  src/compat/mfc_shim.h, which includes <winsock2.h> and <windows.h>; on Linux those are linux/'s: the types with the
  Windows x64 sizes (LONG, DWORD and u_long 4 bytes where Linux's long has 8; HOSTENT with its two shorts; the
  handles 8), the SDK's constants (the virtual keys and messages are recorded), and the functions. Each function is
  linux/win32.cpp's and calls through a slot of its own, GoldenSlot_<name>, as the Windows runner's calls go through
  its import table: golden::FindImport (golden_patch.h) finds the slots the tests bind (Sleep, rand, _time64, fwrite,
  the 17 user32 functions and ShellExecuteA of MainFrm's test, MessageBoxA, timeGetTime, GetTempPathA). A slot starts
  at a Linux implementation where the code or the tests need one (the clocks, the temporary folder, the current
  directory, the global memory), else at a stop with the function's name (reached only without a fake: none is). The
  five WinSock functions call through network_tests.cpp's NWSlot_ slots, which are their __imp_ symbols on Windows.
  linux/'s direct.h, io.h, process.h and mmsystem.h are the Microsoft CRT's few names the tests use. No product
  target sees the folder.
- **The C library's functions the tests replace.** time (the Microsoft CRT's _time64) and fwrite are wrapped at the
  link (ld --wrap): every call of the runner's objects goes through a slot that starts at the real function. rand is
  the stand-ins' GoldenRand (a macro in linux/windows.h): glibc declares rand noexcept, and the Network test's fake
  rand throws in its error round, which ends the program in a caller compiled for noexcept.
- **The code patches.** RedirectOwn and RestoreOwn write the jump with mprotect (Windows: VirtualProtect); the tests'
  own patching code uses the stand-ins' VirtualProtect, VirtualQuery (over /proc/self/maps: the images by their file
  mappings, MEM_IMAGE), FlushInstructionCache, HeapCreate/HeapAlloc/HeapFree and NtCurrentTeb (the stack's bounds from
  pthread_getattr_np). The golden objects are compiled with -fsemantic-interposition (they are -fPIC): neither
  compiler inlines a global function into a caller, calls a clone of it or concludes from its body that it cannot
  throw, so that a redirected function is reached and a fake may throw, as across MSVC's object files. GCC and Clang
  both emit a constructor's base-object variant (C2) as the same function as the complete-object one (C1): the tests
  name C1 (checked with nm for all 34).
- **The tests' Windows-only spellings.** Constructors by their Itanium names (golden_test.h GOLDEN_SYMBOL, asm labels;
  elementfakes.cpp, mainwindow_tests.cpp, commworld.cpp) where MSVC's are #pragma comment(linker, "/alternatename");
  a member pointer's code address is its first 8 of 16 bytes (errors_tests.cpp CodeAddress); RaiseException throws a
  C++ TStructuredException, which control_tests.cpp catches where it had __try/__except (a catch (...) catches it, as
  /EHa's catches the structured exception); typeid names demangled (dialogs_tests.cpp, "7TDialog"); the folder
  separator GOLDEN_SLASH (objects_tests.cpp's "tibia-objectstest" with a backslash was a file name on Linux, and
  InitObjects found no Tibia.dat; also map, script, consolewindow and errors_tests.cpp); the runner's own operator new
  (linux/win32.cpp: the tests redirect it, which reaches the runner's image only).
- **The ABI.** Five fakes of functions that return TObject or TRGBColor (12 bytes) by value had the Microsoft form, a
  hidden result pointer (contentwindows_tests.cpp); the System V ABI returns these in registers: GOLDEN_BY_VALUE
  wraps them. Talk.cpp's GetTalkColor and GetTalkboxColor take the pointer themselves and stay. The Itanium ABI puts a
  derived class's first members in the tail padding of its base: TToggleButton's and TMultiStateButton's State after
  TSkinButton's Enabled, TTextToggleButton's after TTextButton's Text; the fakes' bases end where the real members end
  (elementfakes.h GOLDEN_DATA_END), so that the fakes' members are at the real offsets again (elementfakes.cpp's
  static_asserts). No record has a long; the corpus (little-endian, fixed sizes) reads the same on both.
- **Compiler settings for the golden objects** (tests/golden/CMakeLists.txt, golden_linux_options):
  -fno-strict-aliasing (the tests read our objects and member pointers through other types),
  -fno-delete-null-pointer-checks (the shim's GetSafeHwnd compares this with nullptr), -fwrapv (the error rounds give
  INT_MAX sizes, whose sums the original and MSVC's code wrap: TWindow::FitToChild, UBSan's signed overflow), and for
  GCC -fno-lifetime-dse (the tests fill memory with a pattern before a constructor, to compare the bytes it leaves;
  GCC removed the fill as dead: SkinProperties, TTalkBuffer) and -fno-toplevel-reorder (globals in the order of their
  definitions, as MSVC places them).
- **Warnings.** The golden sources build at the baseline level (-Wall, warnings as errors), as MSVC builds most of
  them (/W3), with these off (golden_linux_warnings, after -Wall): invalid-offsetof, overloaded-virtual,
  delete-non-virtual-dtor (Clang delete-non-abstract-non-virtual-dtor), GCC's class-memaccess, stringop-truncation,
  mismatched-new-delete and nonnull-compare, Clang's tautological-undefined-compare and non-pod-varargs (TCallback
  through TMultiStateButton's ...), and DialogElements.cpp's uninitialized (the toggle buttons pass their unset
  Tooltip to the base, as the original). The rest were fixed in the tests ([[maybe_unused]], [[fallthrough]], the
  lambdas' unused parameters, parentheses, an empty format string, "abcdefg" + n as &"abcdefg"[n]). Text.h's table
  and Status.h's LinkPattern say they are unused on purpose (GCC warns about every text a file does not read).

### What the port found in our code (high)

Each fixed in src/, the same behaviour on Windows (the corpus replays it), no layout change:
- **Status.cpp AddMessageFirst read freed memory.** `Messages(i) = Messages(i - 1)`: C++17 evaluates the right side of
  an assignment first, GCC and Clang so, and when Messages(i) grew the vector the copy read the moved-from block
  (glibc's tcache had overwritten its first bytes: a type-0 message at the head, 4 failures of Status). MSVC (and
  the original) evaluate the left side first. The left side is taken first now.
- **Container.h vector<T>'s growth swapped entries member by member.** The Container test compares the entries'
  padding, which the original's block copies carry (and MSVC's): GCC copied TLineFormat's members only and lost it
  (vector<TLineFormat> operator(): entries differ, then a stale corpus). SwapEntries copies a trivially copyable entry
  as bytes.
- **TXTEA read a packet's words unaligned.** EncryptBlock and DecryptBlock cast the block's bytes to uint32 *, at any
  offset of the packet (UBSan: misaligned load). Through an aligned copy now.
- **Objects.cpp indexed Flags[4] past its end** for flags above 31 (inside TProperties, as recorded before; UBSan:
  index out of bounds). FlagByte (Objects.h) reads and writes the entry's bytes.
- **TTabBar::Rearrange read Busy before the constructor set it** (as the original; its value is the memory's, the
  test's pattern 0xbe). A bool that is neither false nor true is undefined, and Clang may test one bit of it (UBSan:
  invalid bool load): its byte is read now, not 0 meaning busy, as the original reads it.
- **graphics.h's TVideoCacheItem had a TRGBColor in an anonymous struct**, which GCC and Clang reject (a member with a
  constructor): a named member now, Item.Tile.TileY and Item.Tile.Color (graphics.cpp, graphics_tests.cpp).
- **Network.cpp's ReceiveData must lie before SendData** (its over-read, #72, reads SendData): Clang emitted SendData
  first (5 Network failures). PATELLA_IN_DEFINITION_ORDER (src/compat/msvc.h, GCC's and Clang's used attribute) emits
  them where they are defined.
- sysinc.cpp's #pragma comment(lib) only for MSVC.

### What the port found in the tests, and the time zone (high)

- contextmenus_tests.cpp and commworld.cpp printed an uninitialised bool (the pattern) as `b ? 1 : 0`: its byte now.
- The window tests' fakes stand where our code expects its classes (a smaller TMenuSkillsStandIn as a
  TSkillsWindowBody, TMapThrower as TMapWindow): UBSan's vptr and object-size checks are off for the golden objects
  (-fno-sanitize=vptr,object-size); the stand-in's cast is a reinterpret_cast.
- Network's rounds call ConnectSocket without a socket, as the original: Socket->Connect on the null pointer, which
  the test's CAsyncSocket takes. UBSan's null check is off for network_tests.cpp only (listed under "Found, not done").
- player_tests.cpp called GetAvailableEngines on a null TSurface: a TTestSurface on Linux. Regexp's allocation sizes:
  _msize is the program walked to its END node on Linux (glibc's malloc_usable_size is not the size asked for).
  ExitCommunication's "single ret" accepts the frame-pointer form (push rbp ... ret) of the sanitizer builds.
- **The time zone.** Talk's and Creatures' fixed clocks print local times, and the corpus has the recording machine's
  (CET): in the image's UTC Talk had 97,883 failures. tools/build.py passes Windows' zone to the container as a POSIX
  TZ (GetTimeZoneInformation: "STD-1DST-2,M3.5.0/2:00,M10.5.0/3:00"), TZ itself when it is set. The corpus does not
  record its zone (listed under "Found, not done").
- **The evaluation order.** Before #55, Clang (a call's arguments left to right) built other inputs than MSVC and
  GCC (right to left) where a test called Random() twice in one expression: Script, PreferencesFile, Talk, GUI,
  ContentWindows, Container, MainFrm and Control failed or went stale on linux-x64-clang only. #55 made 53 of those
  explicit; Clang found the rest, which #55's query (calls that reach Random() or the recorder) does not see: calls
  that reach a logging fake. In the tests: Container's TRGBColor(Rnd(), Rnd(), Rnd()) and ContentWindows' four
  height queries (sprintf of GetInitialHeight, GetMaximumHeight, GetContentHeight and the fourth). In our code,
  where the fakes log the original's order of calls (each now temporaries in that order, right to left):
  Control.cpp's SendLogin and SendGameLogin arguments, ConnectionEstablished's In(GetActiveCharacter(), 0,
  GetAccountCharacters() - 1), TimerEvent's GetMouseX/GetMouseY pairs (MouseHover, SetMouseOverTextPosition,
  MouseWheel) and the nine context menus' (MousePosition); MainFrm.cpp's SetDisplayMode (the two GetSystemMetrics)
  and OnMouseWheel; ContentWindows.cpp's GetOpponentAt(GetMouseX() - x, GetMouseY() - y) and
  TSkillsWindowBody::getMinimumHeight's max of two calls; ContextMenus.cpp's TContextMenuEntry::SetLast (a binary
  operator's left operand first: GCC with -fwrapv took GetFontHeight first, 3,748 ContextMenus failures). The
  Windows images' calls are in the same order as before (MSVC's).
- **The runner's operator delete.** #65 removed dialogwindow_tests.cpp's runner-wide operator delete; Dialogs' test
  redirects operator delete, which on Linux was libstdc++'s, out of a jump's reach: linux/win32.cpp defines it (and
  the sized one) next to operator new, over free.

### The sanitizers (high)

linux-x64-clang (ASan and UBSan, -fno-sanitize-recover=all) over the whole corpus: no finding beyond those fixed
above. Not reported, as MSVC's ASan on Windows reports neither (the golden and dialogwindow_setsize tests'
ENVIRONMENT, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:alloc_dealloc_mismatch=0): the original's mismatched releases (the ownership
map of #58: free of `new (std::nothrow)` memory in Talk.cpp and Preferences.cpp, ClearIgnoreList first) and the leaks
(26.7 MB in 263,286 allocations at the end: the original's and the tests' worlds). The error rounds' signed overflow
is defined (-fwrapv), as above.

### The corpus in the container, the tests (high)

- tools/build.py mounts the corpus read-only at /golden and sets PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR=/golden in the container, mounted
  or not: PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR of the host's environment, else build/golden of the repository when it exists;
  PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR=none mounts nothing. tests/golden/CMakeLists.txt takes the environment's PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR as
  the cache variable's default at the first configure (Windows: build/golden as before, unless the environment names
  another). Without a corpus golden is skipped (77), as in hosted CI, which runs build.py inside the image itself.
- golden_concurrent runs on Linux too, in linux-x64-gcc's Release configuration (no sanitizer, as on Windows since
  #84): the same folder handling (std::filesystem::temp_directory_path reads TMPDIR, TMP, TEMP; the runner sets TEMP
  and TMP, linux/win32.cpp's GetTempPathA reads them).

### Found, not done (high)

- The corpus's local times depend on the recording machine's time zone (Talk, Creatures); a corpus recorded in
  another zone fails both platforms' replay. For #93 (the final recording): record with TZ fixed, or record the zone.
- Network.cpp's ConnectSocket calls Socket->Connect without a socket when ConnectToGameServer comes without one (the
  original's; the real client's CAsyncSocket would crash). M7 (ownership) or a bug issue.
- Some CHECK messages read records in their arguments, so a run with more failures than DIFFTEST_FAILS reads another
  record sequence and later tests go stale (seen only after other failures).

### The gates (high)

On main 499389f merged, over the corpus of 499389f (build\golden-next, recorded by the orchestrator; read only):
`python -I tools/build.py linux-x64-gcc --fresh` and `linux-x64-clang --fresh` with PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR set to it:
golden 15,803,218 replayed + 1,512,822 retired = 17,316,040, 0 failures, every test's count as windows-x64's
(golden_concurrent passes in linux-x64-gcc; Clang under ASan and UBSan without a finding); 14/14 and 13/13. Without
a corpus (PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR=none) linux-x64-gcc, -clang, -gcc-debug, -clang-debug: golden skipped, the rest passes,
0 warnings. windows-x64 17/17, -debug 16/16, -asan 16/16 (golden as above, 0 failures); oracle-x86 5/5 (difftest
16,459,352, sysinctest 67, communicationtest 856,621, vlongtest 3,201, safeseh passed); windows-x64-gcc 11/11.

## The start's window count in the test build (Patella-Modern issue #96)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026, on branch issue-96. CTest fatal_error_box (#67 part 2, #83) failed with
"A Tibia client is already running!" whenever another client was running on the machine (another worktree's test or
reference session, Tibia.exe), seen in #55's and #65's gates. Test build, docs; Patella.exe unchanged.

- **The check is a window count, not a mutex** (high: src/Player.cpp, decisions "Player.cpp"). InitInstance, after the
  frame window and SurfaceInitInstance, runs `EnumWindows(CountTibiaWindows, 0)`: every top-level window of the
  desktop whose title is "Tibia" or whose class is "TibiaClient" (caseless) counts, its own included; none is
  "Application is corrupted!", more than one "A Tibia client is already running!", each ending the start with exit
  code 0. So a window of any client on the desktop stops a test client that gets that far. fatal_error_box gets there
  (its PROGRAM_ERROR 12 comes at the first present, after the check); init_control_failure (#90) never does (its
  error is in CMainFrame's constructor, before the frame window): it neither fails nor stops another client. Reproduced
  (build\logs\issue-96\gate1-before.log): main's PatellaTest.exe kept running with a script of `wait 900000`, then
  `ctest -R "fatal_error_box|init_control_failure"`: fatal_error_box exit code 0, messages.txt the "already running"
  box; init_control_failure passed.
- **The choice: the test build counts only its own windows** (high). The hook `PATELLA_ENUM_WINDOWS(Function,
  Parameter)` (src/TestHooks.h) replaces that EnumWindows call: in Patella.exe and the oracle it is `EnumWindows(Function,
  Parameter)`, word for word; in PatellaTest.exe it is EnumOwnWindows (src/testmode/TestModeWin32.cpp), EnumWindows
  with a filter that hands the callback only the windows of the current process (GetWindowThreadProcessId). The test
  client still runs CountTibiaWindows and both of its outcomes on what it owns (its frame window: 1, the start goes
  on), so it is the issue's "per-run name": each process is its own instance. Always on in the test build, not only
  with --test-out or a script: PatellaTest.exe is never the product, and the comparisons start it without a script
  too. Considered: an environment variable with a per-run name (there is no name to vary: the title and class are the
  client's and visible to the tools); skipping the check (leaves CountTibiaWindows unrun in every test); the scripts
  reporting the box as a skip, exit code 77 (the issue's last choice: the test would not run when it matters).
- **Not covered: the other direction** (high). A test client's frame window still has the title and class, so a
  client without the filter (Patella.exe, Tibia.exe, a PatellaTest.exe built before #96, e.g. another worktree's
  from an older main) still counts it and stops. Once #96 is on main every test build ignores the others.
- **No RESOURCE_LOCK** (high). Within one CTest run the two tests can no longer see each other: each client counts its
  own windows only, and init_control_failure's clients create no frame window. A lock would only serialise them.
  Checked with the holder running: `ctest -R "fatal_error_box|init_control_failure" -j 2 --repeat until-fail:5`, 5
  rounds of both in parallel, all passed (build\logs\issue-96\gate1-after-repeat.log). Nothing else in the x64 presets
  starts PatellaTest.exe (tests_vulkan is headless; testmode_check.py and reference.py are outside CTest).
- **No test of the original's check** (high). None exists, and none is added: Patella.exe's start is unchanged
  (pecompare below), and checking it means two Patella.exe windows at once on the session's desktop, a live check
  for one unchanged call. The test build runs CountTibiaWindows at every start that gets past the surface.
- **The images** (high). x64 Release Patella.exe, main 6cecf91 and the branch, built in this worktree: pecompare.py
  (#8's, build\issue-8\tools of the main checkout): .text, .data, .pdata, .rsrc and .reloc identical; the only
  differences the COFF and debug-directory time stamps and the CodeView record; 0 unexpected
  (build\logs\issue-96\pecompare-x64.log). The oracle compiles the same macro to the same call.
- **The gates** (high). After the fix, with the holder running, `ctest -R "fatal_error_box|init_control_failure"`
  2/2 (gate1-after.log). `python -I tools/build.py windows-x64` 17/17, windows-x64-debug 16/16, windows-x64-asan 16/16;
  golden on main's corpus 15,803,218 replayed + 1,512,822 retired = 17,316,040, 0 failures; 0 warnings. tidy_ci 3
  findings, 0 new (baseline 3), 0 bugprone; tools/tidy.py on the Windows build for TestModeWin32.cpp and Player.cpp: no
  finding on a changed line. banned_calls 0. clang-format clean. Logs: build\logs\issue-96.

## The final oracle recording: the golden corpus and the reference recordings frozen with a manifest (Patella-Modern issue #93, M6)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026. The last recording before #94 removes oracle-x86: after it neither the
corpus nor the reference recordings can be recorded again in the fork. Changed: cmake/OracleX86.cmake,
cmake/RunGoldenRecord.cmake, tests/golden (golden.h, golden.cpp, runner.cpp), tools/data_manifest.py (new),
tools/build.py, tools/reference.py, tools/reference_record.py.

### The manifest (high)

- One format for both data sets, `MANIFEST.tsv` in the set's folder, written and read by tools/data_manifest.py
  (`write`, `verify`, `--self-test`); its module comment is the format. Text, one tab-separated field per line, like
  the corpus's own manifest.tsv files, so that the C++ runner reads it without a library: `format
  patella-data-manifest 1`, `kind` (golden, reference), `commit` and `clean` (the recording's commit and whether its
  tracked files were unchanged), `date` (UTC), `time_zone` (POSIX TZ), `tibia_sha256`, `tool` lines (MSVC's cl
  version, CMake's, the oracle-x86 configuration and folder), `program` lines (size and SHA-256 of difftest.exe,
  sysinctest.exe, communicationtest.exe; the reference set's patcap.dll when a recording writes it), a `manifest` line
  when the manifest was written later than the data (its commit and date), `files <count> <bytes>`, then one `file
  <size> <sha256> <path>` per file, '/'-separated and sorted. The manifest is local data like the set (it lists the
  CipSoft-derived files): never committed; only its format and code are in the repository.
- A folder matches its manifest when every listed file is there with its size and SHA-256, no other file is, and the
  counts are the `files` line's. golden_runner checks this itself (golden::VerifyDataManifest, with golden.cpp's
  SHA-256) before it reads a test; reference.py `compare` and `list` through data_manifest.verify. Either refuses a
  missing or mismatched manifest (exit 1, each problem listed, at most 20). The override: golden_runner `--unverified`
  or `PATELLA_GOLDEN_UNVERIFIED=1` (the environment, so that a CTest run and build.py's image take it; build.py
  forwards it), reference.py compare `--unverified`: the problems are printed and the replay goes on. For local
  experiments only: a corpus recorded again by hand, a changed file. Without any corpus the runner still skips (77),
  as in hosted CI.
- golden_corpus removes the old MANIFEST.tsv before it records and writes the new one after the three programs, so a
  recording that did not finish has none. golden_reproducible writes none (its two recordings must compare equal,
  and the dates would differ).
- A reference set recorded before the manifest gets one from `reference.py manifest` (commit "unknown" unless
  `--commit`, the date from the sessions' meta.json); `record` writes it after a recording.

### The time zone: the recorder fixed to UTC0 (high)

#91 found that the corpus held the recording machine's local times (Talk's and Creatures' fixed clocks go through the
process's localtime on both sides) and replayed only in that zone. Two ways were open: record the machine's zone in
the manifest and replay in it, or fix the recorder's zone. Chosen: the recorder fixed to TZ=UTC0
(cmake/RunGoldenRecord.cmake sets TZ from -DTZ, GOLDEN_TIME_ZONE of OracleX86.cmake; golden_reproducible the same),
the zone recorded in the manifest, and golden_runner setting TZ to the manifest's zone (MsvcPutenv, then _tzset; the
stand-in's tzset on Linux) before the first test. Why:
- The corpus no longer depends on the machine that recorded it: a regeneration from the tag on another machine gives
  the same bytes, which the manifest then confirms.
- A Windows zone with daylight saving time cannot be given to a process through TZ: the UCRT's TZ format is
  `tzn[+|-]hh[:mm[:ss]][dzn]` with the US rules for dzn, and no rule part (`,M3.5.0/2,M10.5.0/3`); so on Windows a
  corpus recorded in CET replays only on a machine set to CET. UTC0 has no rules, and the UCRT, glibc and the image's
  redirected localtime read it the same.
- It is what the rest already does: the reference recordings and their comparison run in TZ=UTC0 (reference.py
  TIME_ZONE), and Errors' HandleException rounds switch to UTC0 on both sides (errors_tests.cpp TUtcZone).
- The oracle's own comparisons are unaffected: in the recording both sides of each Talk and Creatures comparison read
  the same process zone, and the recordings under UTC0 had 0 failures.
A TZ in the runner's environment that names another zone than the manifest's is refused (the corpus's times would
not be the replay's); with --unverified the environment's TZ is kept, so that a corpus recorded before #93 in the
machine's zone can still be replayed. tools/build.py passes the manifest's zone into the image (the host's zone, as
before, only for a corpus without a manifest).

## The oracle retired (Patella-Modern issue #94, M6)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026 (plan M6, items 3 and 4; the owner's go and decisions of that day). The
32-bit oracle left the fork: there is no 32-bit client build any more, and tier A, the golden corpus and the unit tests
pass without it ("The gates"). upstream/main (55e97f1) was already merged, so there was nothing to merge. The tag
`layout-frozen-final` is on ee1705c, main's head with the oracle, pushed before the removal; the oracle stays there and
in upstream Patella.

### The asserts (high)

The plan (M6, item 3) moves the size asserts that matter for wire and file formats to the serialisers as checks of
the format, and drops the x86 layout asserts. Every assert of the removed `#if PATELLA_ORIGINAL_LAYOUT` blocks was
looked at for a format it protects:

- **Moved: the automap file** (src/Map.cpp, next to LoadAutomapBlock and SaveAutomapBlock). The `.map` file is the
  block's Color and Speed layers, each read and written in one piece (`readBytes`/`writeBytes` of `sizeof(Block.Color)`
  and `sizeof(Block.Speed)`), then the marks field by field. TAutomapBlock's x86 assert (size 0x200a8, Color at 0x14,
  Speed at 0x10014, each 0x10000) is now `sizeof(TAutomapBlock::Color) == AUTOMAP_FILE_LAYER_BYTES` and the same for
  Speed, AUTOMAP_FILE_LAYER_BYTES = 256 * 256: the format, on every target. The block's offsets and size are no part
  of the file and are not checked.
- **Already checks of the format, kept as they are** (unconditional, every target): Network.cpp's `sizeof(ReceiveData)
  == 0x4000` and `sizeof(SendData) == 0x800` (the largest packets each way), MainFrm.cpp's PacketHeader (16 bytes of the
  last packet), Control.cpp's LastPacketTypes (10). They were never x86-only.
- **No format behind them: Tibia.cfg, Tibia.dat, .spr, .pic, the packets' fields.** Tibia.cfg is text (TWriteScriptFile
  and TReadScriptFile, key by key); Tibia.dat's entries are read field by field into TProperties (Objects.cpp's
  readByte/readWord per flag), Tibia.spr's and Tibia.pic's records field by field into TSprite and TPicture
  (graphics.cpp), the packets by TReadBuffer/TWriteBuffer's typed reads; no structure is read or written as memory.
  None of them had an x86 assert, and the unconditional asserts on those structures (TProperties' flags in
  FlagByte, TCharacter, TServer, TBuddy) stay: they hold on every target and are no layout freeze of the oracle.
- **Dropped with the oracle** (x86 layout, no format; 73 in src/, the file's structures and their offsets): Communication.cpp
  (TTalkBuffer first and cursor, TTalkLine Addressee: 3); ConsoleWindow.cpp (unique_ptr<char[]>, TTextWindow,
  TTab, unique_ptr<TTalkBuffer>, TConsoleWindow: 5); ContentWindows.cpp (TBattleWindowBody, the unique_ptrs,

  TGraphicsOptionsDialog, TNewChannelDialog, TAdvancedGraphicsDialog: 20); GUI.cpp (TComponent: 1); Inventory.cpp
  (TContainer, TOffer, the object lists: 3); MainFrm.cpp (CMainFrame's KeyStates and KeyFlags: 1); Map.cpp
  (TAutomapBlock: 1, its format part moved, above); MapWindow.cpp (TMapWindow: 1); Player.h (CPlayerApp's size: 1);
  Script.h (TReadScriptFile twice, TWriteScriptFile, TReadBinaryFile, TWriteBinaryFile: 5); TXTEA.cpp (TXTEA: 1);
  Talk.cpp (the eight talk classes' sizes, TTalkLine's WithoutTime, Time and the addressees: 11); vlong.cpp (flex_unit:

## Patella.exe without the patcap.dll lookup, PatellaTest.exe without --test-sync (Patella-Modern issue #97)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026 (#92's and #94's found-not-done points, after #94: Patella.exe may change
freely). Files: src/vulkan/SurfaceVulkan.cpp, SurfaceVulkan.h, src/TestHooks.h, src/testmode/TestModeWin32.cpp,
src/compat/msvc.h (a comment); notes/testmode.md, notes/vulkan.md, notes/progress.md.

### The lookup removed (high)

TSurfaceVulkan::CreateSurfaces (InitDisplay's device set-up) asked `GetModuleHandleA("patcap.dll")` for every device
and took its four exports PatcapVulkanDevice, PatcapVulkanFrame, PatcapVulkanPixels and PatcapVulkanMask as the
engine's observers. No tool has loaded patcap.dll into the x64 client since #92 (compare_rendering.py reads the frames
through the test mode's control channel; patcap.c does not build for x64), so the lookup always failed. It is gone with
its four strings and the GetModuleHandleA call site (GetModuleHandleA and GetProcAddress stay imported for other
callers). The observer members and their calls in FinishFrame and the device set-up stay: the test build's frame dump
is the only observer, installed by PATELLA_TEST_FRAME_OBSERVERS, whose first argument (the patcap module, which made
the test mode stand back when patcap.dll was there) is gone. Patella.exe's observers stay null, so the engine calls
nothing and keeps no masks, as before without patcap.dll. The observer types keep PATELLA_CDECL (nothing on x64 and
Linux; the unit test that asserts so is unchanged).

- Considered: removing the observer members from Patella.exe too (behind the test build's `#if`): it would move the
  class layout and FinishFrame's code apart between the two builds, which the test build is meant to share; the null
  checks cost nothing measurable.
- tools/capture/patcap.c keeps its Vulkan exports and its header comment that describes the engine's lookup: the file
  is capture-x86's, which this issue leaves unchanged (found, not done).

### --test-sync removed (high)

`--test-sync <name>` made the test client set `<name>-ready` after each state dump and wait up to 300 s for
`<name>-continue`, so that testmode_check.py's client_state.py reading saw the same moment. That reading left with
#92 (check e checks each dump on its own), and no tool passes the argument. Gone: the argument, TState's two event
handles, OpenSync, SyncTimeout and the wait in WriteStateDump. The client takes the words as unknown ones now (its
parser skips them), so an old command line still runs, without the wait.

### Found, not done (high)

- tools/capture/patcap.c still exports PatcapVulkanDevice, PatcapVulkanFrame, PatcapVulkanMask and PatcapVulkanPixels,
  and its header comment and compare_rendering.py's Capture (the `.mask` file next to a capture) still describe the
  engine's lookup. No client calls them now; removing them changes capture-x86's patcap.dll, which the reference
  recordings' record step loads into Tibia.exe: a change of its own.
- notes/testmode.md's opening still names "the oracle's 32-bit Patella.exe" beside Tibia.exe as client_state.py's and
  patcap.c's clients (#94's wording missed there).

## Patella.ini as the only settings file (Patella-Modern issue #45, M6)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026, on the owner's decision of November 3, 2026: Tibia.cfg kept the
original's format until the oracle retired (#94), then Patella.ini becomes the x64 client's only settings file. Plan
D12 and section 3 (tier A) say so now.

### The keys (high)

Every option Tibia.cfg holds (Preferences.cpp's reader and writer, 0x4ddc00 and 0x4de890) is a key of Patella.ini under
Tibia.cfg's own name, ASCII case-insensitive like every key there (src/settings/PreferenceKeys.h lists them with an
example each): the flags as `yes`/`no` (`TestServer`, `WindowsMousepointer`, `LightEffects`, `TextualEffects`,
`NoStretching`, `BuddyHideOffline`, the console filters `InfoMessages`, `EventMessages`, `StatusMessages`, `TimeStamps`,
`PrivateMessages`, `ClassicControl`, `AutoChaseOff`, `SecureMode` (a number in Tibia.cfg), `ShowNewHints`, `LevelBar`,
`MagLevelBar`), the numbers (`CreatureInfo`, `ConfineFramerate`, `Engine`, `ConsoleHeight`, `AutomapZoom`, `LastMotD`,
`AttackMode`, `ChaseMode`), the tuples as comma lists (`FullscreenMode=640,480,32`, no line while none was chosen;
`WindowedMode=10,10,800,600,no`; `BuddySortmethods=2,1,0`), the lists (`OpenDialogs=1,4`, `OpenChannel=5,7`,
`KnownHints=1,2,3`, `SkillBars=0,1,2,3,4,5,6`, `White="name",...`, `Ignore="name",...`), and the entries that repeat a
key in Tibia.cfg as numbered keys: `Hotkey<N>="text",<sent at once>` with Tibia.cfg's number N (0-35, F1 is 0; a line
only for a hotkey with a text), `ContentWindow<n>=ID,Size` and `Buddy<n>=CharacterID,Icon,"description",notify` with
n 1, 2, ... in the list's order. `PreferencesVersion=1` marks a file that has the options. ServerAddress, ServerPort and
LoginMessages, which the original reads and drops, are not kept. Why Tibia.cfg's names: a user (and the comparisons)
can find each option by the name they know; the numbered keys keep one option per line, as the format asks.

A save sets the keys where they are and appends the missing ones; the numbered keys of entries that are gone, and
FullscreenMode while none is chosen, are removed (TSettingsFile::Remove, new; also Keys). Every other line (comments,
Device, LogLevel, LogFile, unknown keys) stays as it was. A new file starts with `# Patella-Modern's settings`, CR LF
(Settings.h NewFileComment, NewFileNewline, now shared with DeviceSettings.cpp through settings::LoadForUpdate).

### The escaping and the 8-bit bytes (high)

A value is a list of fields separated by `,`: a decimal number (32 bits), `yes`/`no`, or a text in double quotes, in
which `\\`, `\"`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t` and `\xHH` are escapes and the writer escapes every other byte below 0x20 and 0x7f
as `\xHH` (`\x00` is refused: the client's texts end there). So a text keeps its spaces at both ends, a `,`, an `=`
(only the first `=` of a line ends the key) and line breaks, and no line of the file ever holds a line end or a NUL.
Bytes from 0x80 on are written and read as they are: the client's texts are Latin-1 bytes (a buddy's description, a
name in the ignore list, a hotkey's text), and plan D4 (UTF-8 at the platform boundary) is undecided, so the file is
Latin-1 where a text has such a byte, not UTF-8. The conservative choice: no conversion now that D4 could have to undo;
an editor must keep those bytes. When D4 is decided, the format can say so (PreferencesVersion 2, or UTF-8 at this
boundary).

Superseded by issue #117 (the owner's decision of November 6, 2026; "#117: Patella.ini in UTF-8" below): the file is
UTF-8 with `PreferencesVersion=2`, a file of version 1 (these raw bytes) is read as Windows-1252 and converted once, at
the next save. The escapes stay, and the five bytes Windows-1252 leaves undefined are escaped as well.

### The import (high)

InitPreferences (the name the client calls, Control.cpp InitControl) sets the defaults and reads Patella.ini; when it
has `PreferencesVersion`, the options are read from it and Tibia.cfg is not opened. Without it (no Patella.ini, or one
with only issue #31's or #77's keys), the original's reader runs on Tibia.cfg (ReadTibiaCfg, unchanged: a missing or
unreadable Tibia.cfg gives the defaults, as in the original), and the options go into Patella.ini at once, so the
import happens once. SavePreferences and ExitPreferences write Patella.ini where the original wrote Tibia.cfg (closing
the options or hotkey dialog, a logout, the exit); nothing in the client writes Tibia.cfg. The log says which way the
options came (`[info] Patella.ini: the options imported from Tibia.cfg ...`); a value that cannot be read is a warning.

The reading gives the client the options the original's reader would give it from the Tibia.cfg its writer wrote with
the same values: ChaseMode 2 reads as 0; a hotkey's text with its sent-at-once flag gets the original's line-break
handling (a final break: sent at once; the others: spaces) and is cut to 255 bytes; an OpenDialogs number is added
only when the original's duplicate check would add it (SetPreferenceValues keeps that check as ReadTibiaCfg has it,
on the vector's fields, entries an earlier load left included; the client loads once); NoStretching's "not set yet"
(2) is written as no, as the original wrote it; a deleted buddy (CharacterID 0) is not written; a description is read
as the original's writer read it, up to its NUL within the entry (#85's bytes). One deliberate difference, for a
hand-edited file only: a value Patella.ini's reader cannot read keeps that option's default and is reported, where the
original's reader dropped every option on any error. The client never writes such a value.

### The original's reader and writer kept, the golden checks unchanged (high)

Preferences.cpp's InitPreferences and SavePreferences of the original are ReadTibiaCfg and WriteTibiaCfg now (their
comments give the original's names and addresses). ReadTibiaCfg is the import. WriteTibiaCfg is not called by the
client; it stays because the golden corpus's Preferences tests read ReadTibiaCfg's results through it (CompareSaved
compares the Tibia.cfg it writes with the original's, byte for byte, after each of the 400 random files and the
long-description case), so removing it would retire the checks of the import path too. The tests call the new names;
the original's ExitPreferences (free the message of the day, save) is ours followed by WriteTibiaCfg. No check is
retired and the counts are the same: 15,803,218 replayed + 1,512,822 retired = 17,316,040, 0 failures. The tests that
fake the three entry points (commworld.cpp's InitPreferences, SavePreferences and ExitPreferences, dialogs_tests.cpp's
SavePreferences) fake the names the client calls, so they are unchanged.

New tests: tests_core's core_preferences_test.cpp (every preset: the escaping of every byte, the fields, the round trip
of every option, the removal of entries that are gone with the other keys kept, the reading as the original's reader,
the values it cannot read) and preferences_file (tests/golden/preferences_file_test.cpp: the client's own Preferences.cpp
and Talk.cpp, no corpus, as dialogwindow_setsize; on Windows and both Linux presets): the import of a Tibia.cfg with
every kind of option into Patella.ini; the options read back from it equal to the original's reader's; a later start
does not import a changed Tibia.cfg; no Tibia.cfg: the defaults, and no Tibia.cfg made; a Patella.ini with only Device
and LogLevel keeps them; a Tibia.cfg the reader refuses imports the defaults; Tibia.cfg's bytes and time unchanged
after the saves and the exit.

### The comparisons (high)

Tibia.exe still writes Tibia.cfg; the x64 client writes Patella.ini. tools/settings_file.py reads both as values
(cfg_values: Tibia.exe's reader's semantics; ini_values: PreferenceKeys.cpp's) and compare_options compares Tibia.exe's
Tibia.cfg (the one it wrote, else the run's start file: the x64 client imported it) with the x64 client's Patella.ini,
which it must have written (its start imports the run folder's Tibia.cfg). tools/deliberate.py drops Tibia.cfg from
Tibia.exe's written files (files) and lists the difference (expected_lines); each tool drops Patella.ini from the x64
client's and compares the options instead:

- reference.py compare: d. files compares the options of files\Tibia.cfg (or Tibia.cfg.start) with the client's
  Patella.ini, and the options session's saved Tibia.cfg (after-options) with the client's saved Patella.ini: the run's
  script is the reference's with `save Tibia.cfg` as `save Patella.ini` (the frozen recordings are not touched).
- compare_files.py: the written files as before without Tibia.cfg and Patella.ini, the options by value; the options
  scenario also compares the copies after the options dialog.
- compare_traffic.py d.: the options each client wrote on exit, equal across the runs of a kind, by value.
- testmode_check.py d.: Patella.ini identical across the runs and with the options; the run's Tibia.cfg never written.
- compare_network.py: "options" (the values) in place of "Tibia.cfg"'s text; Patella.ini not one of the files.

Not through the state dump or the probe: the frozen reference states (Tibia.exe's, #93) have no options, the dump's
keys are client_state.py's (testmode_check.py's check h), and the files are written at the same checkpoints (the
options dialog's OK, the exit), so the written files are the comparison's source on both sides. The issue's "through
the state dump" is met this way; a probe key for the options can come when a tool needs the options of a running
client.

### Deliberate tier A differences (high)

Added to the table of "Deliberate tier A differences" (issue #74's section):

| Issue | Difference | Where Tibia.exe differs |
|---|---|---|
| #45 (D12) | No Tibia.cfg written; the options in Patella.ini, compared with Tibia.exe's Tibia.cfg by value | SavePreferences writes Tibia.cfg (the options and hotkey dialogs, a logout, the exit) |
| #45 (D12) | Patella.ini written at the first start without the options in it (the import of Tibia.cfg, or the defaults) | Tibia.exe writes nothing at its start |

### Found, not done (high)

- Plan D4's row still says "Tibia.cfg next to the data files": D4 is undecided and the owner's; the settings file's
  place is Patella.ini's now (D12, section 7's file layer).
- The probe has no options; a tool that needs the options of a running client can add them (StateDump.h, "The probe").
- names.tsv (the decompilation workspace, not in the repository) still names 0x4ddc00 and 0x4de890 InitPreferences and
  SavePreferences, the original's names; the source's comments give both.
- compare_rendering.py seeds Tibia.cfg for each engine run; the x64 client imports it (the run folders are emptied
  first), so it works unchanged. Not run here (#98).

### The gates (high)

## compare_rendering.py's failed starts and runs explained, patcap.dll without its Vulkan exports (Patella-Modern issue #98)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026 (#92's, #94's and #97's failed compare_rendering.py passes). Files:
tools/capture/patcap.c, tools/compare_rendering.py, tools/reference_record.py; notes/rendering.md ("When a run
fails"), notes/vulkan.md, notes/progress.md. No src/ change. Logs: build\logs\issue-98 of the branch's worktree.

### Tibia.exe's first capture without a frame: a CreateDevice that did not return (high)

patcap.dll now records Direct3D 9's course in its shared memory (version 4: Direct3DCreate9's calls, CreateDevice's
calls, result, time, back buffer and window, whether a call is still inside the driver, TestCooperativeLevel's last
result and its failures, Present's first and last time, last result and failures) and its rare events in patcap.log
(the run folder; the tool keeps it). A start of Tibia.exe makes the device twice: Direct3DCreate9 and CreateDevice at
about 80 ms, both again at about 480 ms, the first Present at about 560 ms.

The repro (a script of this issue's, not committed: Tibia.exe under patcap.dll started again and again, its first
frame, an advance, the "start" capture, WM_CLOSE; logs repro-01 to repro-04): 15 starts, 14 with the first frame
within 0.6 s; one (repro-01's first, 17:17, the display on, the window visible and not minimized, Chrome in the
foreground, the input desktop Default) ran the second Direct3DCreate9 and nothing after it: no CreateDevice result,
no TestCooperativeLevel, no Present for 30 s (patcap.log: "Direct3DCreate9(32): an object" at 484 ms, then nothing;
CreateDevice's result is logged when the call returns; the line before the call came later in this issue). That is
#92's, #94's and #97's "command 2 not done within 30 s (frames 0)": the first capture waits for a Present that never
comes. #97's first compare_traffic.py run (the helper Tibia.exe got no game connection within 10 s, then passed) fits
the same start, without patcap.dll. Not caught again: 8 starts in a row with fresh copies of the client, 2 starts
after 6 minutes without GPU work, and the gate runs below all worked; no stack of the hung thread was taken (the
repro's non-invasive cdb attach was ready but never needed). So it is in the driver's start-up (NVIDIA RTX 5080, the
Direct3D 9 runtime) or the machine's state, rare, and a second start works.

- Fixed in the tool: Driver.start waits for the first frame (FIRST_FRAME_TIMEOUT, 30 s) instead of sleeping 2 s, and a
  client that shows none is ended and started once more (START_ATTEMPTS, 2), logged as "start 1 of 2 failed,
  starting the client again: <the diagnosis>". Nothing has been sent to the client before its first frame (the first
  command, the advance, comes after), so the run is the same as one whose first start worked; a second failure fails
  the run with the diagnosis. reference_record.py's record step gets the same (it uses this Driver).
- Considered: a longer capture timeout (the hang did not end within 30 s, nor #94's within 34 s: a longer wait is no
  fix); patcap.dll making the device itself or skipping the second one (it would change what the client does).

### The x64 client's trade window "late": its window was minimized (medium)

#94's log (C:\Tibia\Patella-Modern\build\logs\main-94-rendering.log): the GPU pass's PatellaTest.exe frames were
780x557 until "walk east" and 0x0 from "walk south" on (15:22:08). The frame dump's size is SCREEN_SURFACE's
rectangle, the window's client area, so the window was minimized; with no client area the map window has none, the
click on the trade partner hit nothing, the client sent no trade request (the proxy: "recorded 7dffff05...; client
sent closed"), and "no window of class TTradeOffers (#0) within 5 s" followed. So the window was not late and the
trade is not ordered differently from compare_traffic.py's: it was never asked for. What minimized the window is
inferred: the monitor is a DisplayPort one (WmiMonitorConnectionParams: VideoOutputTechnology 10); asleep it is gone
for Windows (the desktop falls back to 1024x768, notes/rendering.md "How the pixels are read without a display");
Windows 11 minimizes the windows of a monitor that went away (MonitorRemovalRecalcBehavior unset: the default, on);
the power scheme turns the display off after 900 s without input on AC; posted window messages are not input. No log
records the display's state at 15:22; at 17:10 the display was on after 1705 s without input (something held it on),
so the timeout does not always fire.

- Fixed in the tool: SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS | ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED | ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED) while the runs
  last (a display already off comes on again; no input is sent); a scene whose window is minimized, and a 0x0 frame
  dump, fail the run at once with the diagnosis, instead of a later step with a misleading message.
- Not done: restoring a minimized window (SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE would not take the input, but the client would get window
  messages the other run did not: the scenes would not come from the same session); bringing the window to the
  foreground (every passing run of this issue had another program in the foreground: the clients do not need it, and
  taking it would take the user's keyboard).

### The diagnosis (high)

Every failed start, capture timeout, minimized scene, 0x0 frame and failed session step ends its message with the
window's state (visible, minimized, the client area, the foreground window and whether it covers its monitor), the
display's (GUID_CONSOLE_DISPLAY_STATE, the idle time against the display timeout, the input desktop: Winlogon when
locked, the monitors, the mode) and, for Tibia.exe, patcap.dll's Direct3D 9 course. Each run's log starts with a
`display:` line, and run.json's facts have patcap.dll's `d3d9`. `--self-test` (new) checks the offsets against
patcap.c's struct Shared and the diagnosis texts on made-up data.

### patcap.dll's Vulkan exports removed (high)

PatcapVulkanDevice, PatcapVulkanFrame, PatcapVulkanMask and PatcapVulkanPixels (issue #19) had no caller since #97.
Removed with the shared memory's Vulkan fields (VulkanFrames, VulkanType, VulkanCpuDriver, VulkanDevice, MaskPixels;
version 4 has Direct3D 9's course from offset 876), API_VULKAN, compare_rendering.py's `.mask` reading and
vulkan_device(), and reference_record.py's `.mask` removal. dumpbin /exports (build\logs\issue-98\exports.txt):
before PatcapLoaded, PatcapVulkanDevice, PatcapVulkanFrame, PatcapVulkanMask, PatcapVulkanPixels; after PatcapLoaded
only. The tool refuses a patcap.dll of another version ("rebuild it"); it builds the DLL itself when patcap.c is
newer.

The reference recordings (build\reference) were recorded with the old patcap.dll. `reference.py compare` loads none
(PatellaTest.exe replays each session's script), so it is not affected. A future `reference.py record` runs
Tibia.exe under the new one: the same hooks, the same clock and the same captures; the differences are patcap.log in
the record step's run folder (not one of the saved files) and the restart of a client without a first frame, before
any line of the script is written. So a recording made with it is the same.

### Found, not done (high)

- `python -I tools/testmode_check.py --self-test` and `python -I tools/testmode_dumps.py --self-test` fail on main
  c0aad52 too (their "identical runs" case: "Tibia.cfg was written"; log gate4-main-comparison.log): since #45

  aborted-gate2-other-client-running.log).

## import std (Patella-Modern issue #113, M7)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026 (CMake 4.1.2 and Ninja 1.13.2 on Windows, CMake 4.4.5 on the hosted
Windows runner; MSVC 14.51 / cl 19.51.36260; mingw-w64 GCC 16.2.0; in the Linux image GCC 16.2.0, Debian's Clang
22.1.8, CMake 3.31.6 before and 4.1.2 after this issue, Ninja 1.12.1). Files: cmake/ImportStd.cmake (new),
CMakeLists.txt, CMakePresets.json, tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt, tests/unit/import_std_test.cpp (new),
docker/linux-x64/Dockerfile; CLAUDE.md, notes/reconstruction.md, notes/progress.md.

### What CMake needs (high)

`import std;` under CMake is experimental in every version up to 4.4 at least: the target property CXX_MODULE_STD
(variable CMAKE_CXX_MODULE_STD) acts only when CMAKE_EXPERIMENTAL_CXX_IMPORT_STD holds the gate's UUID before the CXX
language is enabled (before project()), and the UUID changes with CMake's minor version: 3.31
`0e5b6991-d74f-4b3d-a41c-cf096e0b2508`, 4.1 `d0edc3af-4c50-42ea-a356-e2862fe7a444`, 4.4
`f35a9ac6-8463-4d38-8eec-5d6008153e7d` (each read from its cmake executable: `grep -ao "CxxImportStd.\{40\}"`). It
also needs a Ninja generator (the presets' Ninja Multi-Config scans modules; Ninja 1.11 or newer: 1.13.2 on Windows,
1.12.1 in the image) and a library that ships its std module: MSVC's `modules/std.ixx`, libstdc++'s
`libstdc++.modules.json` (GCC 15 and newer, `bits/std.cc`), libc++'s `libc++.modules.json`. CMake adds the std
module's target only to a target with the compile feature cxx_std_23 or newer. CMake 3.31 supports MSVC and Clang
with libc++ only; 4.1 adds GCC 15+ and Clang with libstdc++.

### Per compiler (high)

A minimal project (build\logs\issue-113\minimal: `import std;`, a vector, std::ranges::fold_left, std::println),
Ninja Multi-Config, Release:

| Compiler | CMake | Result |
|---|---|---|
| MSVC 14.51 (cl 19.51) x64 | 4.1.2, 4.4.5 | works: CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_IMPORT_STD is `23` (/std:c++latest; no 26); prints 6 |
| mingw-w64 GCC 16.2 | 4.1.2 | works: `23;26`; links with libstdc++exp (std::print's terminal helpers, as cmake/Warnings.cmake links it); runs with the compiler's runtime DLLs next to it (exit 127 without them: another libstdc++-6.dll on PATH, what Warnings.cmake's copy solves) |
| GCC 16.2 (Linux image) | 3.31.6 | fails: "Toolchain does not support discovering `import std` support" (3.31 has no GNU-CXX-CXXImportStd.cmake) |
| GCC 16.2 (Linux image) | 4.1.2 | works: `23;26`; prints 6 |
| Clang 22.1.8 (Linux image) | 3.31.6 | fails: "Only `libc++` is supported" |
| Clang 22.1.8 (Linux image) | 4.1.2 | fails: "`libstdc++.modules.json` resource does not exist": Clang uses Debian's GCC 14 installation, and libstdc++ 14 has no std module |

What would unblock Clang (both tried; build\logs\issue-113\minimal-linux-clang-unblock.log and -byhand.log):

- GCC 16's libstdc++ for Clang (`--gcc-install-dir=/usr/local/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/16.2.0`): by hand Clang 22
  precompiles libstdc++ 16's bits/std.cc without an error and the program runs (prints 6). Under CMake the flag in
  CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS does not reach CMake's `-print-file-name=libstdc++.modules.json` probe, which still finds nothing;
  the flag would have to be part of the compiler (a Clang configuration file, or CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER with the
  argument). It moves linux-x64-clang from libstdc++ 14 to 16: everything that preset checks (the unit tests, golden
  under ASan and UBSan, and the clang-tidy job and its baseline, which read its compile_commands.json) would run on
  another library. The owner's decision (Needs the user).
- libc++ 22 (Debian's libc++-22-dev and libc++abi-22-dev 1:22.1.8-1~deb13u4): CMake finds `libc++.modules.json`
  (`23;26`), but it is reached through /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu, and its relative `../share/libc++/v1/std.cppm` resolves
  to /lib/share/libc++/v1/std.cppm, which does not exist ("Cannot find source file"): a packaging defect. And libc++
  is another library than the one the preset tests: the same decision, with a second dependency.

### What is enabled where (high)

The option PATELLA_IMPORT_STD (cmake/ImportStd.cmake, default OFF) is set ON by the presets windows-x64 (so
windows-x64-asan too, which inherits it), windows-x64-gcc and linux-x64-gcc; not by linux-x64-clang (above) and not by
capture-x86 (returns before the product build). With it the configure sets the gate for the CMake versions above
(4.1 and 4.4: the ones verified) and, after project(), requires the toolchain's std module for the targets' standard
(MSVC 23, GCC 26), or fails ("PATELLA_IMPORT_STD: ... has no std module ..."): the option on where it does not work is
an error. On a CMake version with no known gate it warns at configure and turns itself off, so a hosted runner's CMake
update does not fail every build (Found, not done). CMake prints its own "experimental" developer warning at
configure; build.py's warning check is the compilers' and linkers', so it passes.

The one user is tests_import_std (tests/unit/import_std_test.cpp, a CTest test of its own): only `import std;`, no
#include and no doctest (whose header would put the library's headers and the module into one translation unit; the
module exports no macros, so the result is the return value). It checks std::format, std::ranges (fold_left, sort,
views::filter), std::map with a transparent comparator, std::span and std::expected, with the product settings
(patella_target_language, _warnings, _hardening: /W4 or -Wall -Wextra ..., warnings as errors). No existing code
converted (the issue: new code only).

### The std module's options (high)

CMake compiles the std module with the directory's flags (CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_<CONFIG> and its own standard flag), not
with the importing target's options. With MSVC that gave C5050 in tests_import_std, "Possible incompatible environment
while importing module 'std': _CONTROL_FLOW_GUARD=1 is defined in current command line and not in module command
line" (/guard:cf) and the same for _UTF8 (/utf-8); GCC compiled bits/std.cc as `-std=gnu++26` without the importer's
-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3, -fstack-protector-strong, -D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS (Debug) and sanitizers, silently. So
patella_target_import_std, called after the three settings functions, gives the module the target's own
COMPILE_OPTIONS: for MSVC the module is a static library of the build (`__cmake_cxx23`, aliased as `__CMAKE::CXX23`),
its COMPILE_OPTIONS; for GCC an imported INTERFACE target (`__CMAKE::CXX26`) that CMake compiles for each importer,
its INTERFACE_COMPILE_OPTIONS (the importer gets them again; they are its own already). Checked in the generated Ninja
files: std.ixx with /std:c++latest /permissive- /Zc:__cplusplus /utf-8 /Zc:preprocessor /Zc:inline ... /guard:cf,
bits/std.cc with -std=c++26 -fstack-protector-strong -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3. The warning level is a
source property (patella_target_warnings), so the module keeps the compiler's default level; its code is the
library's. A second user of import std would need the same options, so the function refuses a second target; with
more users the options move to one place they share.

CMake 4.4 (the hosted Windows runner's 4.4.5) does it differently: it creates the std module's target only at
generate time (`@cmake_cxx_std`, its objects compiled as `-std:c++20` with the directory's flags) and compiles the BMI
that an importer reads for each importer with that importer's options (`@cmake_cxx_std@synth_<n>`: /guard:cf /utf-8
... /WX), so there is no C5050 and nothing to copy; `__CMAKE::CXX23` does not exist at configure. The first hosted run
of the branch failed there ("get_target_property() called with non-existent target "__CMAKE::CXX23"", the three
Windows jobs); the function copies only when the target exists. Checked locally with CMake 4.4.5 on the repository
(windows-x64-cmake4.4.5.log: windows-x64 without the client, Release and Debug, tests_import_std passed).

- Considered: CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS for the options: they would reach every target, the third-party code too (the regexp,
  doctest).
- Considered: C5050 left as a warning: /WX and tools/build.py fail it, rightly.

### The Linux image (high)

docker/linux-x64/Dockerfile: CMake 3.31.6 (Debian's cmake and cmake-data packages) replaced by Kitware's release
4.1.2 for Linux x86_64, downloaded from its GitHub release, checked against its SHA-256
(773cc679c3a7395413bd096523f8e5d6c39f8718af4e12eb4e4195f72f35e4ab, from the release's cmake-4.1.2-SHA-256.txt),
unpacked to /opt/cmake, with cmake, ctest and cpack linked into /usr/local/bin. Why: 3.31 has no import std for GCC,
and 4.1.2 is the Windows builds' version, whose gate the build knows (Debian's trixie-backports has 4.3.4: a third
version, a third gate). GCC 16.2's std module was in the image already (the gcc image installs
`libstdc++.modules.json` and bits/std.cc); no other package changed. The tag stays
`patella-modern/linux-x64:gcc16.2-clang22.1` (it names the compilers, which are the same); a local image must be
built again with CLAUDE.md's command. With the old image linux-x64-gcc still builds: CMake 3.31 has no gate the build
knows, so it warns and leaves tests_import_std out. The branch's gates ran on the new image built as
`patella-modern/linux-x64:issue-113` (PATELLA_DOCKER_IMAGE), so other branches kept the old one meanwhile.
