## #104: TClient and the subsystem objects (Patella-Modern issue #104, M7)

Designed by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026 (plan M7, "Globals into subsystems"). This section is the plan the
later M7 issues follow (#105 TNetwork and TCommunication, #106 TMapState, #107 TGUI, #108 the noexcept destructors,
#109 the platform interfaces, #110 and #111 into patella_core); each move appends its own subsection here. The first
move, TPreferences, is #104's ("The first move: TPreferences", below).

### The objects (high)

TClient (src/Client.h, Client.cpp) is the composition root: it owns the subsystems as members, made in the order
below, each given the earlier ones it needs in its constructor (references, never owners). A subsystem never holds
a later one; a call "upwards" goes through a small interface the lower subsystem declares in its own header and the
upper one implements (TTalkLists, below, is the first). The original's files stay the module map (plan M7): a file's
functions become the members of its subsystem under the same names, with their address comments, in the same file.

| Object | Made | Files (their globals) | Issue |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TPreferences | 1 | Preferences.cpp (43: the options, the lists, the hotkeys, MotD, PreferencesLoaded) | #104, done |
| TNetwork | 2 | Network.cpp (17: Socket, the send and receive buffers, Servers, CurrentServer, TestServer, the host name request, SymmetricKey, the timeouts, NetworkWindow, RecursionProtection); MainFrm.h's PacketHeader (the last packet's first bytes); Control.cpp's Reconnect and ReconnectTimeout | #105, done |
| TMapState | 3 | the game state, as five smaller objects it owns (below): Objects.cpp, Map.cpp, Creatures.cpp, Inventory.cpp | #106, done |
| TCommunication | 4 | Communication.cpp (6: SkipFields, OutfitRequested, CancelCount, LastCancelX/Y/Z); Control.cpp's LastPacketType, LastPacketIndex, LastPacketTypes; Status.cpp's session (ConnectionState, Progress, AccountNumber, AccountNumberString, AccountPassword, Characters, AccountCharacters, ActiveCharacter, PremiumDays, Gamemaster, Rights) | #105, done (the session as TSession, below) |
| TGraphics (recommended) | 5 | graphics.cpp (21: the sprite, picture and font tables, the two caches and their lists), Surface.cpp (18: the engine choice, the screen, the blit counters, the surfaces), Skins.cpp (Skins, NumberOfSkins): the client's side of TSurface | #116, done (with GUI.cpp's SkinProperties: "#116") |
| TGUI | 6 | MainWindow.cpp (ModalWindow, MainWindow); GUI.cpp (SkinProperties, NumberOfHotkeys, the LastTime static of its timer); Help.cpp (8); Talk.cpp (11 and its LastTime static, as a TTalk inside TGUI); ContentWindows.cpp (the two mouse-over texts); Status.cpp's user interaction (the action, drag, use and trade fields and objects, PendingAction*, the message queue Messages and NumberOfMessages, MouseX/Y, WindowWidth/Height, MouseCursor, the blink, the mouse-over text, LinkRegexp, TaintedClipboardText, LinkWarningEventHandler); Control.cpp's LastMouseMove, WindowHandle, ShowFPS | #107, part 1 done (not yet: SkinProperties, the functions of Control.cpp and MainWindow.cpp) |
| the platform objects | outside TClient | MainFrm.cpp (MainFrame, the cursors, the buttons, Closing, DisplayChanged, ClassName, WheelDelta), Player.cpp (theApp, TitleKey, ClassNameKey, LastMouseCursor, NumberOfTibiaWindows, LastMousePosition), sysinc.cpp (the clipboard buffer; TitleCode and ClassNameCode are constants), src/vulkan (SurfaceVulkan.cpp, DeviceSettings.cpp) | #109 |

TMapState's finer split (#106), each an object TMapState owns and passes to the others:

- TObjectTypes: Objects.cpp (ObjectProperties, OutfitProperties, EffectProperties, MissileProperties, DatSignature,
  NoObject): Tibia.dat, read once, then read-only. First, because the others read it.
- TMap: Map.cpp (16: the map points and their position MapX/Y/Z, the effect table and the two iterators, the automap
  blocks and their cache list, the ambient light).
- TCreatures: Creatures.cpp's creature table (Creatures, FirstOpponent, LastOpponent, Beat), the battle and follow
  targets (AttackID, FollowID, HighlightID) and the buddy window's list (Buddies, NumberOfBuddies,
  NumberOfOnlineBuddies, BuddySortMethods: Creatures.cpp's, not Preferences').
- TPlayerState: Creatures.cpp's Player* values (PlayerID, the health, mana, level, skills, capacity, soul, state) and
  the walk (PlayerSteps, NumberOfPlayerSteps, CurrentPlayerStep, PlayerStepDX/DY/Direction, the destination,
  NewPlayerDestination).
- TInventory: Inventory.cpp (Body, Containers, OwnOffer, CounterOffer).

Why this split: Creatures.cpp holds three unrelated tables (the plan's "Player" state is its Player* globals; there
is no game-state player file, Player.cpp is the application object); TPlayerState is what the packets of the
player's stats write and the walk reads, TCreatures what the battle window reads. The five are the units #110 moves
into patella_core.

What stays outside TClient: the developer log (src/log's TLog, a process-wide service like stderr), the test mode's
TState (the test build's own), constants and tables (Text.h, TitleCode, ClassNameCode), and the CRT shims'
function-local caches. The platform objects (#109: IWindow, IInput, IClock, IClipboard, ISocket, IFileSystem,
TSurface) are made by the platform's entry point (CTibiaApp today, M8's SDL3 main later), and TClient takes them as
references in its constructor and passes them on: TNetwork ISocket and IClock, TPreferences IFileSystem, TGraphics
TSurface, TGUI IWindow, IInput and IClipboard.

### Which object owns each global (high)

The table above is the map. The inventory it comes from (November 6, 2026, main c0aad52): `git grep -E "^extern "
-- 'src/*.h'` (Communication.h 1, GUI.h 1, MainFrm.h 3, MainWindow.h 2, Objects.h 6, Player.h 1, Skins.h 2,
Surface.h 15, Talk.h 1, graphics.h 21, sysinc.h 2, log/Log.h 2) and the file-scope data of each .cpp
(Preferences.cpp 43, Status.cpp 48, Creatures.cpp 38, graphics.cpp 21, Surface.cpp 18, Network.cpp 17, Map.cpp 16,
MainFrm.cpp 13, Talk.cpp 11, Control.cpp 8, Help.cpp 8, SurfaceVulkan.cpp 8, Communication.cpp 6, Objects.cpp 6,
Player.cpp 6, Inventory.cpp 4, sysinc.cpp 4, DeviceSettings.cpp 4, ContentWindows.cpp 2, GUI.cpp 2, MainWindow.cpp 2,
Skins.cpp 2), and two function-local statics (GUI.cpp's and Talk.cpp's LastTime). The other files (the window and
dialog files, Script.cpp, Utils.cpp, the crypto) have no data of their own. A global the table does not name goes
with the file it is defined in; one whose file is split (Status.cpp, Control.cpp, Creatures.cpp) goes with the
object that writes it, and the issue that moves it says so in its subsection.

The rules for a move, the same in every issue:

1. The file's data becomes its object's members, in the original's .data/.bss order with the address comments; each
   member has the initial value the static had (an explicit `{}` for the zero of .bss, so that an object a test
   makes on the stack starts the same).
2. Data that was file-local (an anonymous namespace) is private. Data that was `extern` is a public member, and its
   `extern` declaration goes; its users write `patella::bridge::<Object>().<Name>` (a mechanical rewrite), or the
   member through the object they hold. A member that a golden test or the test mode reads is public, with a comment
   naming the reader.
3. The file's functions become the object's member functions of the same names; a parameter that hides a member is
   renamed (Value; MSVC's C4458 and GCC's -Wshadow catch them); the getters are const where they can be
   (readability-make-member-function-const).
4. The original's free functions stay, each calling its member on the bridge (below), while anything calls them by
   name: the other files, the golden tests (which also fake them by symbol: commworld.cpp's F(), the redirects of
   golden_patch.h; a forwarder is a real function in its file's own object, so the fakes still land), the test mode.
5. A dependency on an earlier subsystem is a constructor reference; on a later one, an interface the lower header
   declares, implemented by the later object (until that object exists, by an adapter in Client.cpp that calls the
   other file's free functions: from another object file, so the golden tests' fakes of those functions still land).

### The order of the moves (high)

1. #104: TClient, TPreferences, the bridge (done here).
2. #105: TNetwork, then TCommunication (one pull request each if the diff is large). TCommunication's packet handlers
   write TMapState's and TGUI's state: through the bridge until #106 and #107, then through the references.
3. #106: TMapState with its five objects (TObjectTypes first).
4. #107: TGUI, with TTalk implementing TTalkLists (Client.cpp's adapter goes) and Status.cpp's interaction state;
   ModalWindow and MainWindow become TGUI's members (#81's two raw owners, notes/ownership.md section 7).
5. #108: the noexcept destructors (the window destructors' work into an explicit close), on TGUI's owners.
6. TGraphics (graphics.cpp, Surface.cpp, Skins.cpp), with or right before #109's TSurface.
7. #109: the platform interfaces, passed to TClient's constructor; MainFrm.cpp, Player.cpp and sysinc.cpp become
   the Win32 implementations.
8. #110, #111: the subsystems' files into patella_core; the bridge goes at the end of #111 (below).

The order follows the dependencies: each object needs only the ones moved before it (TPreferences none, TNetwork
TPreferences' TestServerLogin, TCommunication TNetwork and the state it writes), so every pull request builds, and
the bridge carries the calls that still go the other way until their callee has moved.

### TClient during the transition: one instance and the bridge (high)

- **One TClient**, made on first use by `patella::bridge::Client()` (Client.cpp: a function-local static). Its
  members start as the original's statics did (an object of static storage is zero-initialised before its
  constructor runs, and the members' initialisers are the statics' own), and it is destroyed at the exit as they
  were. Why not made by an entry point now: InitControl, golden_runner, the unit tests and the test mode all reach
  the state before (or without) any one entry point; a lazy instance keeps their order of initialisation the
  original's.
- **One accessor per subsystem**, `patella::bridge::<Object>()`, declared in the subsystem's own header and defined
  in Client.cpp (`TPreferences &bridge::Preferences()`). Only Client.cpp includes Client.h, so no subsystem depends
  on TClient's header (or, through it, on every other subsystem). `git grep -n "bridge::"` lists every use.
- **The free functions of the original's names** are the bridge's callers: each is one line that calls its member on
  the accessor.
- **How it disappears.** A file stops using the bridge when its functions are members of an object that holds what
  they need (its own members, the constructor references, the interfaces). The callers of a free function move to
  the member as their own file moves; a free function with no callers left goes (the golden tests then call the
  member, and fake it by its member address, commworld.h's MemberAddress, as FM() does today). When `git grep
  "bridge::"` is empty (the end of #111, the M7 exit), Client.cpp's accessors and bridge::Client() go, and the entry
  points own their TClient: the platform's main (CTibiaApp::InitInstance; M8's main) makes it before InitControl's
  work and destroys it after ExitInstance's, where the statics' first use and their atexit release are today.

### golden_runner and the test mode (high)

- **golden_runner** links Client.cpp (golden_client's objects) and calls the free functions as today, so the tests
  replay the frozen corpus unchanged: one TClient for the whole run, as the original's statics were one set for the
  whole recording (later tests start from the state earlier ones left). The tests that compile a file into
  themselves to read its statics (mainfrm_tests.cpp, network_tests.cpp) read the members through the bridge
  (`bridge::Network().ReceiveData`, public by rule 2). When the bridge goes, the runner makes one TClient for the run
  and the tests call its members; the checks stay as they are (plan: adapt the runner's calls, never the checks).
- **The test mode**: the state dump and the probe (src/testmode/ClientStateWin32.cpp, StateDump, TestModeWin32.cpp)
  read through each file's View functions (ClientView.h: ViewCreatures, ViewMap, ViewInventory, ViewConnectionState,
  ViewCharacters, Status.cpp's View) and the free getters. The View functions stay each file's window onto its data:
  they read their object through the bridge, later through a `const TClient &` that TestModeWin32.cpp's TState gets
  from the entry point. The dump's keys and values do not change (testmode_check.py's check h compares them with
  client_state.py's).

### The include cycles (high)

Measured on main c0aad52 with a short script over the `#include "..."` lines of src/ (November 6, 2026): the headers
have no include cycle (compat/msvc.h and msvc_portable.h include each other on purpose: one interface in two
files). The cycles are between modules, a module being a .cpp with its header, an edge a .cpp that includes another
module's header:

- {Preferences, Talk, graphics, Surface}: Preferences -> Talk (the White and Ignore lists), Talk -> Preferences (the
  console filters, TimeStamps), Talk -> graphics -> Surface -> Preferences (the engine), Surface <-> graphics.
- {Communication, ConsoleWindow, ContentWindows, ContextMenus, Control, DialogWindow, Dialogs, MainFrm, MainWindow,
  MapWindow, Network, Player}: the windows call Communication's Send functions (down), Communication calls the
  windows on packets (up); Control (the controller) calls the windows and is called by them; Network -> MainFrm (the
  network window's messages); MainFrm -> Control, Network, Player; Player -> MainFrm, Control, MainWindow, Network.

The objects' layering breaks them: the platform (MainFrm, Player, sysinc, src/vulkan) -> TClient -> TGUI -> TGraphics
-> TCommunication -> TMapState, TNetwork -> TPreferences -> the libraries (Script, Utils, Container, the crypto). A
call down is a constructor reference; a call up an interface the lower module declares (rule 5), so its .cpp no
longer includes the upper module's header:

- #104: Preferences -> Talk is gone (TTalkLists); the first cycle is {Surface, graphics} now, which TGraphics with
  #109's TSurface breaks (graphics.cpp's caches call the surface; Surface.cpp's engine switch resets graphics').
- #105: Network -> MainFrm becomes ISocket's events (#109) or a TNetwork interface the platform implements;
  Communication -> the windows becomes an interface TCommunication declares (the game events: a packet changed the
  map, a container, the console...) that TGUI implements.
- #107: Control's calls into the windows become TGUI's own; the windows' calls into Control go through TClient's
  references; ContentWindows, ContextMenus and ConsoleWindow are TGUI's members calling each other through TGUI.
- #109: MainFrm and Player become the platform layer, which calls TClient and is called back only through IWindow,
  IInput and the others.

Each issue reruns the measurement (every `#include "X.h"` of a src/*.cpp is an edge to X's module; Tarjan's
strongly connected components) and notes the cycles left in its subsection.

### The first move: TPreferences (high)

- **Moved**: Preferences.cpp's 43 globals (0x5c2558-0x5c255f, 0x719e70-0x71c44f) are TPreferences' private members
  (Preferences.h), in the same order with the same comments; WindowedWidth 600 and WindowedHeight 400 as before,
  every other member `{}` (the .bss zero), the five vectors with their (0, 9, 10) and (0, 9, 10, -1). The 87
  functions are its members of the same names with their address comments, the 30 pure getters const; SetViewMode's
  parameter is Value (it hid the member); the arrays' static_assert is in the class.
- **The callers**: unchanged. Preferences.h keeps the original's free functions, and each (at the end of
  Preferences.cpp) calls its member on `patella::bridge::Preferences()`, the one TClient's TPreferences. So the 18
  files that call them (17 .cpp and Talk.h), the golden tests, their fakes of InitPreferences, SavePreferences and
  ExitPreferences (commworld.cpp, dialogs_tests.cpp) and the test mode's reads are as before. TClient owns
  TPreferences (Client.h).
- **Talk's lists**: TPreferences reaches the White and Ignore lists (ClearIgnoreList, GetBuddyIgnoreText,
  AddBuddyIgnore, IsPermanentBuddyIgnore, GetIgnoreListText, IgnoreName, IsPermanentIgnore) through TTalkLists
  (Preferences.h), a parameter of the eight members that use them (SetDefaultPreferences, ReadTibiaCfg,
  WriteTibiaCfg, GetPreferenceValues, SetPreferenceValues, InitPreferences, SavePreferences, ExitPreferences). A
  parameter, not a member, because Talk's state is TGUI's (#107), made after TPreferences: a stored reference would
  point up. Until #107 `bridge::TalkLists()` is an adapter in Client.cpp that calls Talk.cpp's functions (the golden
  tests that fake them, dialogs_tests.cpp and contextmenus_tests.cpp, still reach their fakes: Client.cpp is its own
  object). Preferences.cpp no longer includes Talk.h.
- **Behaviour**: the same code on the same data. Patella.ini is read and written the same, the import of Tibia.cfg
  the same; what runs differs only by the call through the accessor and, for the eight, the lists' virtual calls.
  The vectors are allocated at the first use of the options instead of before main (nothing observes when). The
  mismatched release of MotD (new[] in SetMotD, free in ExitPreferences; notes/ownership.md) is kept.
- **Container.h**: the vector members keep CipSoft's `vector<T>` (now in Preferences.h, which includes Container.h);
  #99 (TIndexedVector) renames them with its other users, a one-line rebase there.

### The second move: TNetwork and TCommunication (issue #105)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026 (branch issue-105, two commits: TNetwork, then TCommunication). TClient
makes TPreferences, TNetwork, TCommunication, in that order (Client.h).

- **TNetwork** (Network.h; high): Network.cpp's 17 globals, MainFrm.cpp's PacketHeader (0x5d1644) and Control.cpp's

## TIndexedVector over std::vector (Patella-Modern issue #99, M7)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026. Plan M7, containers: CipSoft's `vector<T>` of Container.h is
`TIndexedVector<T>` of `src/types/IndexedVector.h`, over a std::vector, with the original's semantics. Container.h's
vector is gone (no alias); array, matrix and matrix3d stay there. #100 moves the call sites that need neither min..max
nor growth to standard containers.

### The interface (high)

- `TIndexedVector(int Min, int Max, int Block, T Init)` and `TIndexedVector(int Min, int Max, int Block)`: the two
  constructors, with the original's two assertions (`space > 0`, `block >= 0`, PATELLA_ASSERT_VALUES; their messages
  name IndexedVector.h now, the golden corpus compares the outcome only).
- `T &operator()(int i)`: the original's growth, unchanged: below `start` or past `start + space` the storage grows by
  `block` entries at a time (by `space`, doubling, when `block` is 0), the entries min..max swapped into the new storage
  (SwapIndexedEntries, Container.h's SwapEntries of #91 moved with it: a trivially copyable entry copied as bytes, its
  padding with it); then `min`/`max` move to `i`, each entry taken in set to `init` when `initialized`.
- The members are the original's names in its order, public as before: `min`, `max`, `start`, `space`, `block`,
  `initialized`, `init`, then `entry`, the storage (`std::vector<T, TArrayNewAllocator<T>>`, `entry.size() == space`)
  where the original had `T *entry`. Call sites keep reading `min`/`max` and `entry[...]`; no accessor layer was added,
  since #100 rewrites most of those loops anyway. Copy and move are deleted, as before.
- The members are initialised with braces: `<windows.h>`'s min and max macros take `max(` in an initialiser list.

### The storage's allocator (high)

std::vector's own allocator value-initialises (an int entry is 0); the original's `new T[n]` default-initialises (an
int keeps the memory's bytes, a class runs its constructor), and the golden corpus's Container test compares every
allocated entry with the bytes the image's `new[]` left (the runner's operator new[] fills with a pattern). So the
storage's allocator, TArrayNewAllocator, allocates through `operator new[]` and frees through `operator delete[]`, and
its `construct(p)` without arguments default-initialises. With it the Container test's 192,832 checks pass unchanged.
The alternative, std::allocator with the runner also replacing the global operator new, would have changed the runner's
allocation for every test; rejected. Over-aligned types are refused (static_assert): none is stored.

### The golden tests' calls (high)

Adapted, no check changed (17,316,040, the same counts): container_tests.cpp's header layout ends at the storage
(`offsetof(TIndexedVector<T>, entry) + sizeof(void *)` as our size; the compared bytes are min ... init with their
padding, as before) and its "entry is the last member" check uses the storage's size; `entry.get()` is `entry.data()`
there and in dialogs_tests.cpp (`entry == NULL` is `entry.empty()`); talk_tests.cpp frees the filter vector's storage
with `entry = {}` where it reset the pointer. talk_tests.cpp's 21-byte header comparison is unchanged (the same
members, offsets and padding).

## #102: fixed-capacity lists (Patella-Modern issue #102, M7)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026. Plan M7, "Fixed-capacity lists": the effect table is a
`TSlotTable<TEffect, EFFECTS>` (src/types/SlotTable.h) over `patella::TStaticVector` (compat/cxx26.h: std::inplace_vector
with GCC 16's libstdc++, the stand-in with MSVC and Clang 22 against libstdc++ 14). `TMapPoint::Objects` +
`ObjectCount` is **not** converted: the golden corpus has a check that a vector would fail (below; the owner decides).

### What the original does when a list is full (high)

- **A map point** (OBJECTS_PER_POINT, 10): InsertObject (0x4b8310) shifts the objects above Position up by one, but
  from index 9 at most (`if (8 < count) i = 9`), so on a full point the top object falls off, and the count goes up
  only while it is below 10 (decompilation `0x4b8310.c`, lines 156-171). AddObject (0x4b88f0) inserts only when the
  position it found is below 10, so on a full point an object that belongs on top is dropped; AppendObject (0x4b8ec0)
  throws "too many objects on map point" on a full point; DeleteObject (0x4b9420) returns true when the point was
  full (its objects that fell off have to be requested again). Map.cpp does all of this, unchanged by #102. The
  golden corpus's Map test replays random AddObject, AppendObject (below 10 only), DeleteObject and ChangeObject on
  the points against the original, and its Errors test AppendObject's error path.
- **The effect table** (EFFECTS, 200): NewEffect (0x4ba6e0) searches the array for the first entry with Status 0 and
  returns -1 when there is none; AddGraphicalEffect, AddTextualEffect and AddMissileEffect then do nothing: the new
  effect is dropped, every other entry unchanged. Kept: TSlotTable::New() returns -1, and Map.cpp's NewEffect too.

### The effect table (high)

- An entry's number is its index, held by TMapPoint::EffectNumber and the entries' Field, Previous and Next links
  (#103 makes them typed handles), so the numbers must stay. TSlotTable's TStaticVector only grows: New() gives the
  first entry below Size() with Status 0, else appends one (try_emplace_back, value-initialised, left at Status 0 for
  the caller to fill), else -1. Clear (ClearMap) empties it. So the entries from Size() to EFFECTS are exactly the
  ones the original had free and had not taken since its last ClearMap or the start, and New() gives the original's
  number in every state; a freed entry below Size() keeps its other members until it is taken again, as the
  original's did.
- Reads: `Get(Number)` returns an entry beyond Size() as a free one (all zero), so GetEffectStatus and the getters'
  Status assertions read 0 there, as the original read Status 0. What differs: the original's free entries beyond
  our Size() kept the members of their use before the last ClearMap; every reader asserts the Status first or follows
  a link, and no link reaches an entry freed by ClearMap (it sets every point's EffectNumber to -1), so nothing reads
  them. Writes (`operator[]`) go to entries below Size() only: the entry New() gave, and the linked ones.
- ProcessEffects and ProcessMissileEffects loop to Size() instead of EFFECTS: the entries beyond are free, which
  both skip.
- TEffect stays in Map.h (its anonymous structs are a Microsoft extension that MFC's headers switch on, C4201, and
  -Wpedantic rejects outside the client's files), so TSlotTable is a template over an entry type with a Status;
  Map.cpp is its one user.
- Tests: tests/unit/slot_table_test.cpp in tests_unit and tests_unit_cxx26_standin (5 test cases): an empty table, a
  full table (-1, nothing changed), freed entries taken again lowest first with their old members, the free entries
  beyond Size() and Clear, and 20,000 random takes, frees and clears against the original's array and search (the
  run meets a full table). The golden corpus's Map test (random effects of the three kinds, ProcessEffects,
  ProcessMissileEffects, ClearField and ClearMap against the original, every entry's status and fields compared)
  and Errors test (the getters on every entry, out-of-range numbers) replay unchanged.

### TMapPoint::Objects: why not converted in #102 (high; the owner chose option 2, done in #102b below)

The golden corpus's Container test (container_tests.cpp, TestArray) checks `array<TMapPoint>` (0x4b0bc0) against the
original: after `new TMapPoint[d]` on memory both sides filled with the same pattern, every byte of every entry must
equal the original's (the check of 192,832 that #99 kept unchanged). The original's TMapPoint has a
compiler-generated constructor (0x4b0b40) that only zeroes the TObjects (their constructor); ObjectCount, Order,
EffectNumber and RefreshRequested keep the pattern. A TStaticVector<TObject, 10> (std::inplace_vector or the
stand-in) has a constructor that sets its size to 0 and constructs no element: the count's bytes would be 0 where
the original's are the pattern, and the objects' the pattern where the original's are 0. No projection of our
entry onto the original's layout (the test's TLayout) gives the original's bytes, so the Container test would fail
for every round of array<TMapPoint> (and skip the operator() comparisons after it). The rule (plan M7: adapt the
runner's calls, never the checks) leaves the conversion to the owner. The options:

1. Keep TMapPoint as it is (std::array + ObjectCount, what #102 does). Its overflow behaviour is the original's,
   checked by the golden Map test.
2. Convert it, and give the Container test's array<TMapPoint> round an element type with the original TMapPoint's
   members (the test then checks array<T>'s code for that instance, not the client's TMapPoint's construction).
3. Convert it, and leave the count's and the objects' bytes out of the byte comparison for TMapPoint (a weaker
   check: they become indeterminate in the original only).

Same precedent: notes/ownership.md keeps TProperties and TPicture without a constructor for the same comparison.

### Found, not done (high)

- #103 (the effect table's typed handles and the iterator) builds on TSlotTable: Get, operator[] and New take and
  give the numbers it types.

## #112: text encoding at the platform boundary (Patella-Modern issue #112, M7)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026. D4 (plan section 9): the client's 8-bit code page inside, as the
original; Unicode only where its text meets the platform. The code page is Windows-1252 (Latin-1 with the printable
characters of 0x80-0x9f): what the protocol, Tibia.dat, Tibia.cfg and Patella.ini carry, and what Tibia.exe's ANSI
calls meant on the Western Windows it was made for.

### The conversion (high)

`src/types/Cp1252.h` (header only, no platform header; patella_core's, and types/File.h's in tests_unit):
`Cp1252ToUtf8`, `Utf8ToCp1252`, `Cp1252ToUtf16`, `Utf16ToCp1252`, on Windows `Cp1252ToWide` and `WideToCp1252`
(wchar_t), and for single characters `Cp1252ToCodePoint` and `CodePointToCp1252`.

- **The five undefined bytes** (0x81, 0x8d, 0x8f, 0x90, 0x9d) are the C1 controls of their value (U+0081, U+008D,
  U+008F, U+0090, U+009D), as Windows' own code page 1252 maps them (MultiByteToWideChar; the unit test compares all
  256 bytes with it) and as the WHATWG encoding standard does. Every byte has a character and each of those characters
  its byte, so the client's text goes out and comes back unchanged: no byte is lost on the clipboard or in a file name.
- **A character with no Windows-1252 byte** becomes `?` (`patella::text::Replacement`; the functions take another),
  one per character whatever its length; so does each ill-formed part of the input: a maximal subpart of ill-formed
  UTF-8 (Unicode 15, section 3.9, the practice WHATWG and Windows follow), a lone UTF-16 surrogate. Nothing is
  dropped; NUL and the C0 controls convert as themselves. `?` is the default character of Windows' WideCharToMultiByte
  without best fit (WC_NO_BEST_FIT_CHARS); the unit test compares every BMP character with it. Best fit (U+0100 as
  `A`, U+221E as `8`) was rejected: it is Windows' own table, not portable, and silently turns text into other text.

### The boundaries (high)

Every place where the client's text meets the platform, with its decision. On this machine (ANSI code page 1252)
nothing tier A compares changes: the texts there are ASCII, or 8-bit bytes whose Windows-1252 characters are the ones
the ANSI calls produced.

| Boundary | Before | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| The clipboard: SetClipboardText (CopyToClipboard, CheckClipboardText, CopyTaintedClipboardText), GetClipboardText and IsClipboardEmpty (the paste), sysinc.cpp | CF_TEXT: the bytes in the system's ANSI code page; Windows makes the Unicode text of a copy from the code page of the input language active then (a Russian layout: 1251) | **Converted**: CF_UNICODETEXT, to and from Windows-1252. A real mismatch wherever the ANSI or the input language's code page is not 1252 (a copied "Jörg" pasted elsewhere as "J?rg" or "Jцrg"). Here the same for every character the client has; a pasted character outside Windows-1252 is `?` now where Windows' CF_TEXT made a best-fit one (Needs the user, below). The original's odd CR removal (one byte past the data) is kept; its Size is the converted text's with the NUL |
| File names, TFile::Open(const char *) (types/File.h): the data files (Tibia.dat, .spr, .pic), Tibia.cfg's import, the map files, "Save Window" (`<channel>.txt`: the caption is the server's text, a private channel the partner's name), Patella.ini's LogFile | `_fsopen` (ANSI) on Windows, the bytes as they are elsewhere | **Converted**: a name is the client's text; on Windows `_wfsopen` with its UTF-16 name (the same sharing, _SH_DENYNO), elsewhere `fopen`/`open` with its UTF-8 name. Here the same file for every name; on another ANSI code page and on Linux (M8) "Jörg.txt" is that file, not mojibake. The test mode's UTF-16 overload is unchanged |
| The developer log's output (log/Log.h): stderr and LogFile | the message's bytes | **Converted**: every line goes out in UTF-8 (FormatLine). The messages are the client's text (exception texts with the server's or a file's bytes, Patella.ini's values); a terminal, an editor and M8's Linux console read UTF-8. An ASCII line is unchanged. golden's errors_tests.cpp expects HandleException's line in UTF-8 now (its random messages have ä and ß): that expected text is ours, made from our exception; the check is as strict as before |
| The Vulkan device names (Renderer.cpp TDeviceInfo::Name: the advanced options' device buttons and label, GetDeviceName, the test mode's device observer) | Vulkan's UTF-8 shown as 8-bit text | **Converted**: Utf8ToCp1252 when a device is listed, so the GUI draws a driver's ® or ü as itself. The names here (lavapipe's, the GPUs') are ASCII: unchanged |
| Window titles and the window class (Player.cpp GetWindowTitle, GetWindowClassName, CMainFrame::Create, PreCreateWindow; CountTibiaWindows' GetWindowTextA and GetClassNameA of other windows) | ANSI calls | **Unchanged**: the texts are ASCII constants ("Tibia", "TibiaClient"); another window's non-ASCII title is not "Tibia" in any code page. M8: SDL_CreateWindow's UTF-8 title |
| Message boxes (PATELLA_MESSAGE_BOX: FatalError's, the start's two; the test mode's ShowMessageBox) | MessageBoxA | **Unchanged**: every caption and text is ASCII (the PROGRAM_ERROR texts, TextCriticalError, the two start messages); the exception's message goes to the log, not into the box. The golden corpus has MessageBoxA's slot. M8: SDL_ShowSimpleMessageBox with Cp1252ToUtf8 |
| URLs (MainFrm.cpp OpenURL: ShellExecuteA) | ANSI | **Unchanged**: the client's links are ASCII constants and LinkPattern's characters (Status.h) are ASCII; golden's mainfrm test fakes ShellExecuteA. M8: SDL_OpenURL with UTF-8 |
| Keyboard input (CMainFrame::OnChar: WM_CHAR of the ANSI window class) | Windows converts a typed character to the code page of the active input language | **Deferred to M8**: a real mismatch for a layout whose code page is not 1252 (a Polish ł arrives as 0xb3, shown as ³). The fix needs a Unicode window (RegisterClassW and MFC's message handling, which the test mode's scripted WM_CHAR bytes go through) or SDL_EVENT_TEXT_INPUT's UTF-8 through Utf8ToCp1252, which M8's table names. Here (1252) correct |
| The command line (Player.cpp InitInstance: m_lpCmdLine's gamemaster, host, port, engine) | ANSI | **Unchanged**: ASCII keywords (host's and port's values are dropped, the original's) |
| Patella.ini's name and contents (settings/Settings.cpp) | the bytes as they are (#45) | **Unchanged**, as decided in #45: the name is an ASCII constant, the values stay Windows-1252 bytes (a value typed in a UTF-8 editor arrives as its UTF-8 bytes; Needs the user, below). **Converted since #117** (the owner's decision): UTF-8, PreferencesVersion 2; "#117" below |
| The environment (PATELLA_VULKAN, PATELLA_VULKAN_VALIDATION, the test mode's variables) | ANSI | **Unchanged**: ASCII names and values |
| The CPU driver's manifest (vulkan/DeviceSettings.cpp FindCpuDriverManifest: GetModuleFileNameA, GetFileAttributesA; Renderer.cpp TDriverFiles: _putenv_s of VK_DRIVER_FILES) | ANSI | **Deferred to M8** (Found, not done): not the client's text but the executable's folder; a folder name outside the ANSI code page loses the CPU fallback. The fix is std::filesystem paths and the wide environment end to end (the path also goes into error texts, the client's text): M8's "Files and paths" |
| sysinc.cpp FileExists and RemoveFile (_access, remove) | ANSI | **Unchanged**: no caller |
| The test mode's dumps (packets.log, messages.txt, the state dump, the frames' index) | the client's bytes | **Unchanged**: test data compared byte for byte with the frozen reference recordings, not a platform boundary |

### Tests (high)

tests/unit/cp1252_test.cpp in tests_unit and tests_unit_cxx26_standin (every compiler): every byte's character, the
round trips of all 256 bytes through UTF-8 and UTF-16, every code point 0-0x10FFFF against the table, the characters

## #102b: TMapPoint's objects as TStaticVector (Patella-Modern issue #102, M7)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026, after the owner chose option 2 of "#102: fixed-capacity lists" ("TMapPoint::
Objects: why not converted"). `TMapPoint` is in src/MapPoint.h (Map.h includes it): `Objects` is a
`patella::TStaticVector<TObject, OBJECTS_PER_POINT>` (std::inplace_vector with GCC 16's libstdc++, the stand-in with MSVC
and Clang 22 against libstdc++ 14), its size the original's ObjectCount; `Order`, `EffectNumber` and `RefreshRequested` as
before, and `Vacated` (below). The layout is free (M6): Map.cpp's TMapPoint static_assert is gone.

### The golden Container test's round (high)

The round of `array<TMapPoint>` (0x4b0bc0, 0x4b5900) tests Container.h's `array<T>`: its header (min, d), the entries
`new T[d]` leaves (every byte against the original's, on memory both sides fill with the same pattern) and
operator()'s addresses. What it checks of T is T's default initialisation, the original point's compiler-generated
constructor (0x4b0b40: the ten TObjects zeroed, the rest the pattern). Since #102b the client's point is another type
with another construction (the vector's constructor sets its size and constructs no object), not part of what
array<T> does. So the round's T is `TOriginalMapPoint` (container_tests.cpp, beside TErrorReport, the same kind of
record kept for a vector instance): the original's members in its order (ObjectCount, std::array<TObject, 10>, the
order, EffectNumber, RefreshRequested; 0xac bytes, static_assert), PLAIN_LAYOUT as before (the same "c172@4"). Every
check is unchanged: 192,832 checks, 0 failures; the round's name stays "array<TMapPoint>".

### The original's behaviour, kept (high)

src/MapPoint.h has the stack operations Map.cpp's functions make of a point, each the original's:

- `InsertPointObject` (InsertObject, 0x4b8310): the original shifts from index 9 at most, so on a full point the top
  object falls off and the count stays 10: `pop_back` first when full, then `insert`. Map.cpp's InsertObject keeps its
  assertions and SortObjects.
- `AddPosition` (AddObject, 0x4b88f0): the original's search for the position (ground, borders, bottom, top objects,
  creatures), GetObjectFlag passed in (Map.cpp passes a lambda over it; the overload for a TObject makes the name
  ambiguous). AddObject inserts only below OBJECTS_PER_POINT: on a full point an object that belongs above every
  object is dropped.
- `CheckPointRoom` (AppendObject, 0x4b8ec0): "too many objects on map point" on a full point, the same
  TMYEXCEPTION and reason text (the error's source location is MapPoint.h now; golden compares the outcome).
- `DeletePointObject` (DeleteObject, 0x4b9420): true when the point was full.
- `ClearPointObjects` (ClearField, ClearMap).
- `PointObject(Point, Position)`: the original's `Objects[Position]`. The original's array kept the objects beyond
  ObjectCount, and one of them is read: GetTopMoveObject, GetTopLookObject, GetTopUseObject and
  GetTopMultiUseObject return `Objects[0]` of an empty point (Position 0, the loops not entered), which the golden Map
  test compares on every point (ComparePoint). A vector has no object beyond its size, so the point keeps
  `Vacated`, the object the original's slot 0 still held: the last object deleted from a point of one (the original
  moves nothing then), or the bottom object when ClearField or ClearMap empties a point; a new point's is the cleared
  TObject (`new TMapPoint[n]`'s zeroed objects). No other slot beyond the count is read (GetMapObject checks the count,
  InsertObject reads below it, SortObjects and the loops stay below it).

### golden_runner and the test mode (high)

- The Map, Objects, MapWindow and Errors tests reach the points only through Map.cpp's functions (mapwindow_tests.cpp
  fakes them with its own fields): no read changed, the counts are the same (Map 639,877, MapWindow 122,324).
- The test mode's state dump (ClientStateWin32.cpp) reads `Objects.data()` and `PointObjectCount` where it read the
  array and the count clamped to 10 (the size is never beyond 10).

### Tests (high)

tests/unit/core_map_point_test.cpp in tests_core (MapPoint.h needs common.h, patella_core's): 6 test cases, one per
behaviour (InsertObject's cap, AddObject's drop, AppendObject's throw and its message, DeleteObject's true when full,
an empty point's Objects[0]) and 20,000 random inserts, deletes and clears against the original's point (ObjectCount
and the array, changed as 0x4b8310, 0x4b9420 and 0x4bc720 change them): the objects, the count, DeleteObject's
results and Objects[0] after every step; the run meets full points. MapPoint.h is on cmake/HeaderCheck.cmake's core
list.

## #115: an empty function's code at every optimisation level (Patella-Modern issue #115, M7)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026 (branch issue-115). Only tests/golden/communication_tests.cpp changed.

### Why the check exists (high)

ExitCommunication is empty in the original: the linker folded it with four other empty Exit functions into one
`ret` at 0x496160 (GUI.obj; Communication.cpp's comment). The golden Communication and Control tests replace it with a
fake on both sides (ExitControl's calls of it are compared by controltest.cpp), so no comparison ever runs our body.
The byte check in TestCommunication, before the fakes are installed, is the only proof that ours has none: it reads the
first bytes of `patella::TCommunication::ExitCommunication` (the member since #105; the free function forwards to it)
and the original's byte at 0x496160 (the corpus' recorded value, a `ret`, C3).

### What changed (high)

The check accepted three codes for an empty function: `ret`, `ret 0` (C2 00 00) and Clang's frame-pointer frame
`push rbp; mov rbp, rsp; pop rbp; ret` (55 48 89 E5 5D C3, #91: the sanitizers' -fno-omit-frame-pointer; linux-x64-clang-debug
passes with these). GCC at -O0 (linux-x64-gcc-debug) puts a `nop` for the empty body inside the frame: 55 48 89 E5 90 5D C3,
read from the Debug golden_runner with objdump. The check now accepts that sequence as a fourth exact shape, and nothing
looser: no other instruction, no call, no store. A body with any code still fails on every preset. Not chosen: skipping
the check in Debug builds (it would prove nothing there) or a behaviour test (an empty function has no behaviour that the
fakes leave visible). The failure message now prints the first seven bytes instead of one.

### The gates (high)

(PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR=C:/Tibia/Patella-Modern/build/golden), its manifest verified. Each golden run: 15,803,218 replayed +
1,512,822 retired = 17,316,040, 0 failures.

- After: linux-x64-gcc-debug exit 0, 15/15; linux-x64-clang-debug exit 0, 14/14, no sanitizer report; linux-x64-gcc

## #117: Patella.ini in UTF-8 (Patella-Modern issue #117, M7)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026, on the owner's decision of the same day: Patella.ini is read and written
as UTF-8, not as the client's raw Windows-1252 bytes (#45 kept the bytes, #112 left the choice open).

### The format (high)

- `PreferencesVersion=2` marks a UTF-8 file (src/settings/PreferenceKeys.h `PreferencesVersion`). A text field's
  characters are the UTF-8 of the client's Windows-1252 bytes (types/Cp1252.h Cp1252ToUtf8); when read, each run of
  characters between escapes goes through Utf8ToCp1252, so a character Windows-1252 does not have (typed in an editor)
  is `?`, one per character, and so is each ill-formed part of the UTF-8, as #112 chose.
- The escapes of #45 stay: `\`, `\"`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\xHH` for the other bytes below 0x20 and 0x7f, `\x00`
  refused. New: the five bytes Windows-1252 leaves undefined (0x81, 0x8d, 0x8f, 0x90, 0x9d) are written as `\xHH`
  too. They are C1 controls (U+0081 ...), invisible in an editor, like the C0 ones; written raw they would read back
  the same (the reader takes U+0081 as 0x81), the escape only keeps them visible. `\xHH` is always the client's byte
  HH, never a byte of the UTF-8 (an escape ends the run that is converted), in both versions.
- The encoding is the file's (Settings.h `EncodingOf`, `ClientText`): Windows-1252 where PreferencesVersion is `1`,
  UTF-8 otherwise: version 2, a later one (read as 2 and reported, ReadPreferences' problems), and a file without the
  key (one with only Device, LogLevel, LogFile: an editor's file). `LogFile`'s name is converted the same way
  (LogSettings.cpp, `ClientText`), so a log file named in a UTF-8 editor is that file (TFile opens the client's text by
  its Unicode name, #112). Device and LogLevel are ASCII. A problem line reports the value as the client's text (the
  log writes it as UTF-8 again, #112).

### The import of version 1 (high)

InitPreferences reads a version-1 file as Windows-1252 (the values are the bytes #45's client wrote) and says so in the
log (`[info] Patella.ini: PreferencesVersion 1 (Windows-1252) read; written as version 2 (UTF-8) at the next save`).
The next save (SavePreferences, ExitPreferences) converts the whole file first (PreferenceKeys.cpp `ConvertToUtf8`:
every line's text through Cp1252ToUtf8, comments, LogFile and unknown keys included; a UTF-8 byte order mark kept as
it is), then writes the options as version 2. So the file is converted once, every line of it, and its options are
unchanged by value; a crash before the save leaves version 1, read the same way next time. Converting the whole file
rather than only the options' texts: a version-1 comment or LogFile with é would otherwise be ill-formed UTF-8 in a
version-2 file (LogFile then `?`).

### tools/settings_file.py (high)

`ini_values` reads both versions (version 2's texts through the same conversion: Python's UTF-8 decoder with
`errors="replace"` replaces maximal subparts, then each character's Windows-1252 byte or `?`; the five undefined bytes
as their C1 controls), and the values stay Latin-1 str of the client's bytes, so the comparison with Tibia.exe's
Tibia.cfg is by value and the comparisons' verdicts are unchanged. `parse_fields(value, utf8=True)` mirrors ParseFields'
default. The self test covers both versions, every Windows-1252 character, `?` and the escapes.

### Tests (high)

tests/unit/core_preferences_test.cpp (tests_core, every preset): every byte 1-255 quoted in UTF-8 and read back (the
UTF-8 of its character or its escape; its raw character and its `\xHH` read as the byte, in both encodings); `?` for
Ł, ź, 日, an emoji and ill-formed parts; a version-1 file with ö, € and 0x81 in a hotkey, a buddy's description and
the lists, a comment and LogFile with é, read by value, written as version 2 in UTF-8 (every line), read back equal and
written again unchanged; a byte order mark; EncodingOf, ClientText, an unknown version. tests/golden/preferences_file_test.cpp
(the client's Preferences.cpp): the same version-1 file through InitPreferences and ExitPreferences, the getters'
values, the file rewritten as version 2, the next start equal by value; its import test expects the UTF-8 of Ärger now.

### Found, not done (high)

- tests/golden/preferences_file_test.cpp's test cases share the client's talk lists (TTalkLists outlives
  SetDefaultPreferences there: an earlier case's White name stays in a later one's file); the new case checks only its
  own name. Not a client issue: the client loads the options once.

### The gates (high)

Logs: build\logs\issue-117 of the branch's worktree; golden replayed main's frozen corpus read only
(PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR=C:/Tibia/Patella-Modern/build/golden), its manifest verified.

  golden the same, no ASan report. windows-x64-gcc: exit 0, 12/12. linux-x64-gcc: exit 0, 16/16; linux-x64-clang (ASan,
  UBSan): exit 0, 14/14; golden the same on both. 0 warnings on every preset.
- First runs that failed: MSVC's C7744 (a hex escape running into the next letter, `\xb3d`) and preferences_file's new

## #114: reflection for the state dump and the serialisers (Patella-Modern issue #114, M7)

Evaluated by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026. Decision: **adopt later**. No product code changed. The experiment is
tests/reflection/state_dump_reflection.cpp, outside every build: no preset compiles it, and its header says how to run it.

### The experiment (high)

The state dump's creature entry (StateDump.h TCreatureValue, 13 members) and container entry (TContainerValue, 6
members, with a nested TObjectValue and a vector of them) were each written three ways and compared byte for byte with
what the product writes (StateDumpJson's "creatures" and "containers", from WriteCreature and WriteContainer of
StateDump.cpp):

1. the product's hand-written writer;
2. the fallback that MSVC and Clang would need: per structure, a table of member pointers (`PATELLA_FIELD(Type, Member)`,
   C++23: the member's name stringized and its pointer), written by one generic function (std::apply over the table);
3. C++26 reflection (P2996, GCC `-freflection`): `nonstatic_data_members_of(^^T, access_context::unchecked())` in an
   expansion statement (`template for`, P1306). The key is the member's identifier in snake_case
   (`std::define_static_string`, HasParent: has_parent), and the value is `Value.[:Member:]`.

Both generic paths share one overload per member type: signed, unsigned, std::string, std::array, std::vector, and
TObjectValue. The dump writes a TObjectValue as an array [Type, Data, Data2], not as an object, so that type has a
format rule of its own in either path. The data: three creatures (the largest unsigned id, INT_MIN, negative values,
a Latin-1 name with a quote, a backslash, a line feed and 0x7f) and two containers, 546 + 197 bytes.

With reflection the program also checks at compile time (static_assert) that each fallback table names every member
of its structure, in the structure's order, and that the derived keys are StateDump.h's CreatureKeys and
ContainerKeys (the lists that step h of tools/testmode_check.py compares with client_state.py). If a member is added,
renamed or reordered without its table entry, the GCC build fails. That is the sync check, and it needs no generated
file.

Results (logs: build\logs\issue-114\experiment-*.log of the worktree):

| Compiler | Paths | Result |
|---|---|---|
| GCC 16.2 (image), `-std=c++26 -freflection -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror` | product, table, reflection | same bytes, exit 0, 0 warnings |
| GCC 16.2 (image), the same at -O0 with `-fsanitize=address,undefined` | the same | same bytes, no report |
| GCC 16.2 (image), without `-freflection` | product, table | same bytes |
| Clang 22.1.8 (image), the same flags (`-freflection` unknown to it) | product, table | same bytes |
| mingw-w64 GCC 16.2 (this machine, windows-x64-gcc's compiler), `-freflection` | product, table, reflection | same bytes |
| MSVC 19.51, `/std:c++latest /EHsc /W4 /WX /O2` | product, table | same bytes |

### GCC 16.2's reflection (high)

- What works: `__cpp_impl_reflection` and `__cpp_lib_reflection` 202603, `__cpp_expansion_statements` 202506,
  `__cpp_lib_define_static` 202506, `<meta>`, splices, `define_static_array` and `define_static_string`, and
  annotations (P3394: `[[=Key{"has_parent"}]]` and `annotations_of_with_type`; GCC 16.2 defines no `__cpp_annotations`
  macro). They behave the same on the mingw-w64 build (Windows) and in the image (Linux).
- No ICE in the experiment. The two mistakes made along the way gave clear errors: a `std::vector<info>` used as a
  constant (it is the result of `operator new`; `define_static_array` fixes it), and an annotation with a
  `const char *` member (reflect_constant fails; an annotation's type must be structural, e.g. with a `char[N]` member).
- Build time: the experiment's file (two reflected structures) compiles in 1.6-1.7 s at -O2 with reflection and in
  1.4 s with the table alone, so reflection adds 0.2-0.3 s (about 15 %). `-freflection` on a file that does not use it
  costs nothing measurable (StateDump.cpp takes 1.1-1.2 s with and without; 5 runs each). The object has 34.6 KB of
  text with reflection and 30.5 KB with the table (the compiler inlines differently; the output is the same).
- Tooling: Clang 22 has no `-freflection`, so clang-tidy (tidy_ci, which uses the image's linux-x64-clang database)
  never sees the reflection code. clang-format 22 parses splices and `^^` but not `template for`: it puts the loop's
  brace on a line of its own. MSVC 19.51 has no reflection at all.

### What it would save (high)

- The state dump (StateDump.cpp): 56 of its 404 lines are a key and a value per member, for the 28 members of
  TCreatureValue, TContainerValue, TOfferValue and TGuiNode. With reflection alone they become one generic writer.
  StateDump.h's key arrays stay (testmode_check.py reads them) and are checked against the members. The irregular parts
  stay hand-written: TGuiNode's three-state "text", TObjectValue as an array, the player's values as an array under
  PlayerFields, the console's [mode, text or null], and the probe's maps keyed by pointer.
- The settings (PreferenceKeys.cpp): 25 options are a flag or a number whose key is the member's name, written by 25
  Put lines and read by 25 Read lines (50 of 543). The other 14 members are not regular:
  - Hotkeys and HotkeyAutoSend share one indexed key;
  - WindowedMode and WindowedMaximized share one key;
  - FullscreenMode is optional;
  - ContentWindows and Buddies are numbered keys;
  - OpenChannels is written as `OpenChannel`;
  - SkillBars is a list of indices;
  - ChaseMode 2 reads as 0;
  - OpenDialogs drops repeats.

  The members' order is also not the file's: Engine is written last, a new Patella.ini's lines follow the order of the
  writes, and compare_files reads them. A reflected writer would therefore need each member's order or key as an
  annotation.
- The golden records: nothing. The tests record values by name, one call each (248 names such as "FindPath steps"),
  not the members of structures. The names are frozen with the corpus (#93), so a derived name would make it stale.
- With the fallback that MSVC (windows-x64, the client's compiler) and Clang (linux-x64-clang, clang-tidy) need, a
  table entry replaces each key-and-value pair one for one. No line is saved while the fallback exists, and the change
  adds one more path and the sync check. The gain comes only when every compiler has reflection and the tables can go.

### What it would add (high)

Adopting it now would add:

- `PATELLA_HAS_REFLECTION` in src/compat/cxx26.h and `-freflection` for GCC in cmake/Warnings.cmake;
- the generic writers and the tables;
- reflection code that only GCC compiles: clang-tidy cannot see it, and clang-format needs an exception for
  `template for`;
- a second path that hosted CI tests only on linux-x64-gcc and windows-x64-gcc;
- a test per serialiser that the two paths give the same bytes.

That is more to maintain than the 28 dump members and 25 options it covers. They change rarely and are already
compared: the dumps by testmode_check.py and the reference compare, the options by compare_files and tests_core.

### Decision and when to revisit (high)

Adopt later, not now. GCC 16.2's implementation was reliable here, but the required fallback makes reflection a net
addition of code and of tooling gaps, and it gains no behaviour. Revisit when MSVC ships P2996 (MSVC compiles the
windows-x64 client) and when upstream Clang does (`-freflection` for linux-x64-clang and clang-tidy). The first target
then is StateDump.cpp's member writers: one generic writer, with the key arrays checked against the members as the
experiment does. After that come the 25 regular options, with annotations for their keys and order. If MSVC catches up
and Clang does not, adopt it with the experiment's pattern (tables checked by the GCC build's static_assert), starting
from the experiment's file.

### The gates (high)

Only the notes and the experiment outside the build changed. No preset compiles tests/reflection, so the builds,
golden and the live checks are not affected and were not run. The experiment was formatted with Visual Studio's
clang-format 22.1.3 (`-i`); `--dry-run --Werror` exits 0 afterwards. banned_calls and tidy_ci: exit 0 (logs
banned_calls.log, tidy_ci.log).

## #103: the effect table's links as TEffectId (Patella-Modern issue #103, M7)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026. Plan M7, "The effect table's index links": the effect numbers that the
map points and the effects hold are `enum class TEffectId : int` (src/MapPoint.h), and a point's effects are a range.

### The handle (high)

- `TEffectId`'s value is the original's effect number, the entry's index 0 to EFFECTS - 1; `TEffectId::None` is the
  original's -1, its only sentinel: NewEffect returns -1 for a full table, ClearMap sets every point's EffectNumber to
  -1, the end of a point's list is a Next of -1 and GetFirstEffect/GetNextEffect return -1 after the last (the golden
  Map test compares those returns with the original's, so -1 is the original's value, not ours). No 0 sentinel: 0 is
  the first entry. `EffectNumberOf` and `EffectIdOf` convert, nothing else does.
- Typed: TMapPoint::EffectNumber (the first effect of the point), TEffect::Previous and Next, the table
  (`TEffectTable` = `TSlotTable<TEffect, EFFECTS, TEffectId>`: TSlotTable has a third parameter, the key, int by
  default; New() gives Key(-1) when full), and TMap's effect members (GetFirstEffect, GetNextEffect and
  GetEffectIteratorNumber give a TEffectId, the getters, NewEffect and DeleteEffect take or give one). TEffect's layout
  is unchanged (an enumeration over int: the static_assert holds).
- Not typed: **TEffect::Field** is a map point's number (an index into Fields, FieldNumber's value), not an effect's;
  a TEffectId there would be wrong, so it stays an int (the issue lists it among the links; a point handle would be a
  change of the map, not of the effect table). **The original's free functions** (GetFirstEffect ... GetMissileEffectY
  of Map.h's global part) keep their int numbers: they are the original's interface, which the golden tests call with
  numbers (in range and not: the Errors test) and fake by address (the MapWindow test's fakes replace them in our
  code); they convert at the bridge. MapWindow's TTextualEffectPosition::EffectNumber is MapWindow's own state from
  those functions and stays an int. ProcessEffects and ProcessMissileEffects walk the table by index (their loop
  counter is the original's i, which ProcessMissileEffects' assertion reports) and convert it where they link.
- The assertions report the number (`EffectNumberOf`), as before; their outcome is unchanged (golden compares the
  error paths by outcome).

### The iterator (high)

- `TSlotTable::Chain(First)` (TPointEffects in Map.h, `TMap::PointEffects(Point)`): the numbers from First by the
  entries' Next, a range with `std::default_sentinel_t` as its end (Key(-1)). Its step reads the Next of the entry it
  leaves after the loop's body, which is what the original's loops do, and lets a body delete that entry because
  DeleteEffect keeps a deleted entry's links.
- GetEffectIteratorNumber (0x4b9e30) walks it n steps: the same entries, the head's assertion first as before.
- ClearField (0x4bc720): the original deletes the point's first effect until there is none; the range gives the same
  effects in the same order (each deleted one was the point's first, and its Next, which DeleteEffect made the
  point's first, is the range's next), with the same Status assertion before each delete. The unit test checks this
  against the original's loop.
- TMapWindow::DrawField's effect loop (0x4c5520) called GetFirstEffect and GetNextEffect by hand; it is a range-for
  over `TMapEffects(x, y, z)` (Map.h), whose begin() calls GetFirstEffect and whose step GetNextEffect, the original's
  free functions in the original loop's order, so the MapWindow test's fakes still replace them and its "effect number
  out of range [bug0000913]" check still sees any number they give. It yields int (above).
- NewEffect's and ProcessMissileEffects' linking and DeleteEffect's and ProcessMissileEffects' unlinking are not
  loops over a point and stay as they were, typed.

### Tests (high)

- tests/unit/slot_table_test.cpp (tests_unit and tests_unit_cxx26_standin): two new test cases, a table keyed by an
  enumeration (its full table gives Key(-1)), and Chain against the original's loop over Next on four lists under 5,000
  random pushes (NewEffect's linking), deletes of the n-th effect found through the range (GetEffectIteratorNumber)
  and clears that delete while walking (ClearField's order checked). The five #102 cases are unchanged.
- The golden corpus replays unchanged: no runner call changed (the tests use the original's int functions).

### The gates (high)

Logs: build\logs\issue-103 of the branch's worktree; golden replayed main's frozen corpus read only
(PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR=C:/Tibia/Patella-Modern/build/golden), its manifest verified.

- `python -I tools/build.py windows-x64`: exit 0, 19/19, golden 15,803,218 replayed + 1,512,822 retired =
  17,316,040, 0 failures (golden_concurrent the same; Map 639,877, MapWindow 122,324, Errors 17,076 checks, as
  before), 0 warnings. windows-x64-debug: exit 0, 18/18; windows-x64-asan: exit 0, 18/18, no ASan report; golden the
  same on both. windows-x64-gcc: exit 0, 12/12. linux-x64-gcc: exit 0, 16/16; linux-x64-clang (ASan, UBSan): exit 0,
  14/14, no sanitizer report; golden the same on both. 0 warnings on every preset (a first linux-x64-gcc run failed
  on -Wshadow in the new ranges' constructors, fixed in the second commit; every preset above ran on the fix).
- slot_table_test.cpp: 7 test cases, 43,216 assertions, in tests_unit and tests_unit_cxx26_standin on every compiler.
- Live: `python -I tools/reference.py compare --reference C:/Tibia/Patella-Modern/build/reference` exit 0, every

## #109: the platform interfaces (Patella-Modern issue #109, M7, part 1)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026 (branch issue-109). Part 1 of the issue, as the brief allowed: IClock,
IFileSystem and ISocket, with the core code calling them instead of the system for those services. IClipboard,
IInput, IWindow and TSurface are not done (below, "Unfinished").

### The interfaces and their implementations (high)

The interfaces are portable headers in src/platform (no platform header, on patella_core's header list):

| Interface | Header | Win32 implementation (Patella.exe, golden runner) | Test implementation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| IClock: Milliseconds, WallSeconds, FrameWait | platform/Clock.h | TWin32Clock: timeGetTime, time, Sleep (platform/Win32Platform.cpp) | TVirtualClock (testmode/Clock.h), PatellaTest.exe's with --test-script; without a script the test build uses TWin32Clock |
| IFileSystem: Open (a TFile by name), Exists | platform/FileSystem.h | TSystemFileSystem: TFile::Open, std::filesystem::exists (portable, header only) | TFolderFileSystem: the names of a folder, every open listed, names made missing (tests_core, core_file_system_test.cpp) |
| ISocket: Startup, LastError, New, Delete, Create, Connect, Send, Receive, Shutdown, Close, ResolveHostname, CancelResolve, ResolvedAddress; ISocketEvents: OnConnect, OnReceive, OnClose | platform/Socket.h | TWin32Socket: AfxSocketInit, WSAGetLastError, CAsyncSocket, shutdown, WSAAsyncGetHostByName, WSACancelAsyncRequest, inet_ntoa; the connection TSocket is the original's CAsyncSocket class (vtable 0x56d388), moved from Network.cpp | none yet (below) |

- **TPlatform and Platform()** (platform/Platform.h): the three references. Platform() is defined once per executable:
  Win32Platform.cpp's for Patella.exe and the golden runner (`#if !defined(PATELLA_TEST_MODE)`), TestModeWin32.cpp's
  for PatellaTest.exe (the test mode's clock as Initialize chose it, the Win32 file system and socket). The Win32
  objects are constant-initialised (stateless, trivial destructors), so they are there for sysinc.cpp's StartTime
  initialiser before main and after the static destructors; the interfaces' destructors are protected and not
  virtual (nothing is deleted through them), as TNetworkSession's.
- **How the code reaches them** (high). #104's design: the entry point makes the platform objects and passes them
  to TClient's constructor. During the transition TClient is bridge::Client()'s, made on first use, so the
  executable's Platform() stands for the entry point: `bridge::Client()` makes `TClient(platform::Platform())`, and
  TClient passes TPreferences its IFileSystem (Tibia.cfg's Exists in InitPreferences) and TNetwork its ISocket
  (constructor references). The callers that are not an object's member, or whose object TClient does not make, use
  `platform::Platform()` as the free functions use the bridge: sysinc.cpp (GetMilliseconds, StartTime, the seed of
  srand; platform side), the wall clock of Talk.cpp, Creatures.cpp, ConsoleWindow.cpp and ContentWindows.cpp, the
  frame timer of vulkan/SurfaceVulkan.cpp, Control.cpp's Redraw (its Sleep(10) for an unavailable surface is the
  clock's FrameWait now), Script.cpp's four opens and ConsoleWindow.cpp's saved channel. When the entry point owns
  TClient (#111) it makes the platform and the objects take references from TClient.
- **TNetwork** (high): every WinSock and CAsyncSocket call of Network.cpp is an ISocket call, in the same order with the
  same arguments (two LastError calls in ConnectSocket, as the two WSAGetLastError; Delete where it deleted;
  ConnectSocket without a socket calls Connect with a null connection, which TWin32Socket passes to
  CAsyncSocket::Connect as the original did). TNetwork is the connection's ISocketEvents (final; its OnConnect,
  OnReceive and OnClose are the overrides), so it has a vptr now; its members keep their order. `Socket` is a
  `platform::TSocket *`. Network.cpp no longer names WinSock but its error codes (GetErrorMessage's table,
  WSAEWOULDBLOCK, SOCKET_ERROR), which are the protocol's error numbers here; MainFrm.cpp's WSAGETASYNCERROR is the
  platform side's.
- **The test mode** (high): TSystemClock went (TWin32Clock is the same three calls); TimeGetTime, WallTime and
  FrameSleep went with the hooks PATELLA_TIME_GET_TIME, PATELLA_TIME and PATELLA_FRAME_SLEEP. The only behaviour of
  the test build that changes: Redraw's wait for an unavailable surface is the virtual clock's FrameWait with a script
  (a real millisecond instead of 10; the virtual time moved by neither). Patella.exe makes the same calls.

### Why the test build keeps the Win32 file system and socket (high)

- Files: compare_files.py and the reference compare read the files the client writes in its working folder (the
  options, the automap, the saved channels), and the test build must write them as Patella.exe does. A folder of its
  own (TFolderFileSystem) would be a test mode switch; none is needed yet.
- Sockets: the server replay (--test-replay) was a server on the loopback ports in the client's own process, which the
  client reached through real sockets. Done in #120: with --test-replay the test build's ISocket is the replay's
  inside the process, no ports ("#120: the server replay's socket inside the process"); without it Win32's.

### The hooks that remain (high)

TestHooks.h keeps 14 hooks. The services of the interfaces still to come: PATELLA_GET_CURSOR_POS, PATELLA_SET_MAIN_TIMER,
PATELLA_TEST_IDLE, PATELLA_TEST_CAPTURE_CHANGED and CPlayerApp::PreTranslateMessage's DropInput (IInput: the scripted
cursor, the main timer's ticks, the driver's step, the dropped desktop input), PATELLA_MESSAGE_BOX, PATELLA_ENUM_WINDOWS
and PATELLA_ENUM_DISPLAY_SETTINGS (IWindow: the boxes not shown, the own windows' count, the fixed display modes). They
live in MainFrm.cpp, Player.cpp and the Vulkan engine, the platform side, and become IInput's and IWindow's test
implementations with them. The rest are the test mode's observers and failure injections, not a platform's service:
PATELLA_TEST_RSA_BLOCK, PATELLA_TEST_PACKET_SENT, PATELLA_TEST_PACKET_RECEIVED (the packet log), PATELLA_TEST_FRAME_OBSERVERS
(the frame dump, TSurface's), PATELLA_TEST_PRESENT_FAILURE and PATELLA_TEST_INIT_FAILURE; they stay hooks (an observer
interface would be a test-only interface in the product).

### The golden tests' calls (high)

No check changed. network_tests.cpp includes platform/Win32Platform.h for TSocket and fires the events through
`patella::platform::TSocket`'s vtable (FireEvent); Win32Platform.cpp is compiled in tests/golden/network, with the
Network test's exception model (/EHs: the error round's WinSock fakes throw through TWin32Socket now) and, on Linux with
UBSan, its -fno-sanitize=null (the null connection's Connect). The other tests' fakes land as before: the clock's
timeGetTime, _time64 and Sleep are the same imports (the runner's import slots, Linux's --wrap and slots), the files the
same TFile calls.

### Player.cpp (high)

Not touched (#108 works there): the interfaces needed nothing of it.

### Unfinished (high)

- IClipboard (sysinc.cpp's clipboard and its buffer), IInput and IWindow (MainFrm.cpp, Player.cpp: the hooks above),
  and TSurface as the platform's (the Vulkan engine's seam; with TGraphics, #104's step 6).
- A test implementation of ISocket: the server replay inside the process (above). Done in #120.
- IFileSystem for the fork's own files: Settings.cpp's Patella.ini (std::fstream) and the log's LogFile (TFile) open
  themselves; they are patella_core's and portable already.
- sysinc.cpp's FileExists and RemoveFile (no caller in the client since issues #74 and #75; the golden tests' only)
  stay the C library's.

### The image (high)

Main aa4444c and the branch, the x64 Release Patella.exe built from the same source path (main into build/pe-main),
compared function by function through their PDBs (dumpbin's disassembly with the PDB's labels; absolute and
image-relative addresses masked, each function cut at its first jump table, the padding after it dropped; the script

123 with only assertion line numbers changed (the include lines moved them in Creatures.cpp, Talk.cpp, Script.cpp,
ConsoleWindow.cpp, ContentWindows.cpp, Control.cpp, Preferences.cpp, sysinc.cpp). Every change is one of:
