## #108: noexcept destructors, the windows' close (Patella-Modern issue #108, M7)

### The close (high)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 6, 2026, on branch issue-108 (M7, after #107's TGUI part 1). #81 kept
`TComponent`'s destructor `noexcept(false)` (notes/ownership.md, section 7): the window destructors sent packets, wrote
the preferences, removed hotkeys and asserted, and the golden ConsoleWindow test throws through `~TTab` on purpose.

- **The close.** `TComponent::Close()` (GUI.h; not in the original) runs a component's close once (`Closed`, set
  first: a close that throws is not run again, as the original's destructor was not), through the protected virtual
  `OnClose()`. `Closed` is the byte after `DrawingListLength`, in the x64 padding there, so no class's size or offsets
  change (static_assert in GUI.cpp: 56 bytes, Parent at 24); at the end of TComponent, GCC and Clang (the Itanium ABI)
  put derived members into its tail padding, and the golden tests' fake elements (elementfakes.cpp, which assert
  their layout against the real classes) did not compile there. The classes whose destructors did such work override it with that work, in the destructor's order, and
  end with their base's, as a destructor ends with its base's: `TTab` (the rule violation and channel sends, the
  nameless report's `PATELLA_ASSERT(PlayerName!=NULL)`, DeleteTextBuffer), `TTabBar` (the left and right windows'
  tabs, where it deleted them), `TConsoleWindow` (StoreOpenChannels, SetConsoleHeight, the buttons that are not
  children, six RemoveHotkey), `TAutomapWindow` (SetAutomapZoom, eight RemoveHotkey), `TContainerWindowBody`
  (SendCloseContainer), `TBattleWindowBody` (SetHighlightID(0)), `TTradeWindowBody` (SendRejectTrade, ClearOffers),
  `TSubWindow` (SetContentWindowSize, the parts that are not children), `TMainWindow` (ClearOpenDialogs,
  StoreOpenDialogs), `TMapWindow` (two RemoveHotkey). `TWindow::OnClose` closes the children first to last (~TWindow's
  order). The hotkeys and SetHighlightID moved too, though they cannot fail: the golden tests log them among the sends
  (FakeRemoveHotkey, FakeSetHighlightID), so their order with the closes is compared.
- **What stays in the destructors**: freeing memory (the captions, the history, the drawing lists, the label texts),
  the deletes of the parts that are not children (the close closed them first), the timers' RemoveTimer (`~TTimer`,
  noexcept before), the skill window's and its context menu's pointers to each other. So every free happens where and
  in the order it did (ASan, windows-x64-asan and linux-x64-clang, checks the order); only the work before the frees
  moved ahead of them. `TComponent`'s destructor is implicitly `noexcept` now, and with it every window destructor
  (static_asserts in GUI.cpp and ConsoleWindow.cpp).
- **Where the close runs**: before each delete of a component. `DeleteComponent(C)` (GUI.h) is the original's `delete
  C`: Close, then delete; `TWindow::DeleteChild` removes the child and then deletes it so. The original's deletes of
  components in src/ (CloseChannel's tab, TSubWindow's five setters, Control.cpp's nine of ModalWindow and MouseMove's
  help bubble, ExitMainWindow's two) call it. `~TWindow` still deletes its children through DeleteChild: after the
  window's close they are closed and only freed; a window destroyed without a close is one whose constructor threw
  (TMainWindow's ChangeMode, a sub-window's): then DeleteChild closes each child there, as the original's destructors
  did their work during that unwinding, and an exception of it ends the program, as the original's second exception
  did. A class with a close of its own that is destroyed without one writes `<class> destroyed without Close` to the
  developer log (error level; CheckClosed): a missed close is visible in every test run (the gates' logs have none).
- **An exception of a close** (the faked Send functions of the golden error rounds, the nameless report): the
  original's destructor body stopped, its bases' destructors ran while the exception passed (~TWindow deleted the
  children, which sent), and a throw out of a child's delete left the siblings after it undeleted. Each OnClose
  keeps that: its own part in a try block, the base's close in the handler (CloseWhileUnwinding: noexcept, a second
  exception terminates as the original's did) and the rethrow; TWindow::OnClose stops at the child that threw, so the
  later ones are not closed. DeleteComponent then does not delete: the component stays allocated and closed as far as
  it came (the original had freed it as far as its destructors had come; nothing reads it after: the golden tests drop
  it, the client ends at FatalError). Considered: deleting it anyway (then ~TWindow would close the children the
  original never reached, sending their packets).
- **The golden ConsoleWindow test's throw** ("A player's report without a name: its tab's destructor asserts"):
  the assertion now throws in `TTab::OnClose`, reached from `DeleteComponent(C(s))` through `TConsoleWindow::OnClose`,
  `TWindow::OnClose`, the tab bar's (or its left or right window's) close; before the delete, so nothing is freed while
  it passes. The outcome per call is the same (a TMyException), the round keeps its name ("TConsoleWindow::
  ~TConsoleWindow nameless report"), and the fake calls' log before it is the same.

### The owners (high)

notes/ownership.md, sections 6 and 7.


- **Converted**: `TTabBar::LeftTabs`, `RightTabs` (`std::unique_ptr<TWindow>`: the bar is their only owner, they are
  not its children; `reset(new TWindow)` in the constructor, `reset()` in the destructor in the original's order, after
  OnClose closed them), `TGUI::MainWindow` (`std::unique_ptr<TMainWindow>`: InitMainWindow stores the new window as
  the original did, over a pointer it never had set (`release()`, then the move), ExitMainWindow closes and frees it).
  TGUI's constructor and destructor are in MainWindow.cpp, where TMainWindow is complete.
- **Kept raw, with the reason**: `TGUI::ModalWindow`: one owner, but MouseMove's help bubble (issue #36) leaves it
  pointing to the bubble it deleted when `new THelpBubble` or Place throws, and the golden Control test compares that
  ("modal deleted ..." in its world dump, from TCtlWindow's names); an owner cannot hold a freed window. Its deletes
  are DeleteComponent and the original's `= NULL`. The conditional members (TSubWindow's eight parts,
  TConsoleWindow's five buttons, `TListBox::EditLine`): owned by the child list while they are children and by the
  member while they are not (IsChild, Editing), so neither alone is the owner. The text buffers (`DefaultTextBuffer`,
  CreateTextBuffer's, a tab's `TextBuffer`): owned by a tab and the console's filter list at once (DeleteTextBuffer
  frees both), allocated with `new (std::nothrow)` and freed with the destructor and `free`.
### The static destruction (high)

TGUI owns the main window now, and TClient is a function-local static, so a
  window still set at the exit would be destroyed by static destruction: after FatalError's `exit(1)` the main window
  unclosed, ~TWindow closing its children (the console's leave-channel packets, the content windows' closes, the
  preferences). The original's globals had no destructor. The choice: an explicit teardown before the exit,
  `TGUI::AbandonWindows()` (noexcept) in CPlayerApp::FatalError right before `exit(1)`: MainWindow released, the window
  left allocated and unclosed as the original left it. The normal end (ExitControl's ExitMainWindow) closes and frees it
  before, and ModalWindow is raw. Not the entry point owning TClient: #104's reason holds (InitControl, golden_runner,
  the unit tests and the test mode reach the state before any one entry point), and a TClient of the entry point
  would still have to leave the windows alone at `exit(1)`, so the same release would be needed there. The golden
  tests release the main window they set (`SetSideMainWindow`, the MainWindow tests' `release()`), as their raw
  assignments left it before.

### The golden tests (high)

The calls adapted, no check changed: every delete of a component in the window tests is
`DeleteComponent` (94, incl. the ConsoleWindow test's nameless report rounds and the content windows' error rounds,
whose faked closes throw: a plain delete would reach them inside ~TWindow, noexcept); commworld's `SideMainWindow`
is a getter with `SetSideMainWindow`; the MainWindow test reads and releases `MainWindow` through `.get()` and
`release()`; the console test reads `LeftTabs`/`RightTabs` through `.get()`; the MapWindow test, which runs
`~TMapWindow` by hand on its own block, calls `Close()` first.

## #101: the matrices and the automap layers as mdspan views (Patella-Modern issue #101, M7)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026. Plan M7, "Containers": `matrix3d<T>` and the automap's `uint8
Color[256][256]` and `Speed[256][256]` become std::mdspan views over owned storage.

### std::mdspan and its stand-in (high)

- `src/compat/mdspan.h` gives `patella::TMdspan<T, Extents, Layout>`, `TExtents`, `TDynamicExtents`, `TLayoutRight` and
  `TLayoutLeft`: std's where the library has `__cpp_lib_mdspan` (checked November 7, 2026: MSVC 19.51 /std:c++latest
  202207; GCC 16.2's libstdc++, mingw-w64 and the image's, 202406), a stand-in elsewhere: the image's Clang 22 with
  Debian's libstdc++ 14 has no `<mdspan>` (linux-x64-clang). All four compilers have C++23's multidimensional
  subscript (`__cpp_multidimensional_subscript` 202211), so the stand-in's `operator[]` takes the indices as std's
  does and the code is the same on both paths. `PATELLA_MDSPAN_STANDIN` selects the stand-in for a whole target, as
  span.h's and expected.h's do: tests_unit_cxx26_standin and header_check_cxx26_standin.
- The stand-in has the part of the interface the code uses (the header lists it): the extents, layout_right and
  layout_left with their mappings, construction from a pointer and the dynamic extents, the const conversion,
  `operator[]`, `data_handle`, `extent`, `size`, `stride`. It checks no precondition, like std::mdspan without
  hardening: the containers check their indices first.
- A view is made where the storage is indexed and never stored in a structure (it would be a second pointer to keep
  in step with the owner).

### The containers (high)

- `matrix<T>` and `matrix3d<T>` (src/Container.h) keep their members and their storage (`std::unique_ptr<T[]> entry`,
  issue #58): the golden Container test compares the members before entry with the original's bytes and reads
  `entry.get()` for the entries and the element addresses, so nothing there changed and no golden call changed.
  `view()` (and a const one) make a `TMdspan<T, TDynamicExtents<int, N>, TLayoutLeft>` over entry with dx, dy (and
  dz); layout_left because x is the fastest index: `view()[x, y]` is entry[y * dx + x], `view()[x, y, z]` entry[(z *
  dy + y) * dx + x], the original's formulas, now in the mapping. operator() checks the indices and builds the same
  error as before, then returns the view's element.
- `matrix<T>` is included, though the issue names matrix3d only: the issue's exit is "no raw 2-D/3-D array indexing
  of these remains", and matrix's `entry[y * dx + x]` is the same raw 2-D indexing in the same header (FindPath's
  nodes); the same two lines as matrix3d's. `array<T>` stays as it is: it is one-dimensional (an mdspan of rank 1
  would be a span), so it has no multi-dimensional indexing to replace.
- The index type is int, the original's arithmetic: the extents are the containers' int dx, dy, dz, and the offsets
  fit (FieldNumber 18 x 14 x 8, FindPath's nodes 223 x 223).

### The automap layers (high)

- `TAutomapLayer` (src/AutomapLayer.h, new, header only, in patella_core's header list): a layer owns its 256 x 256
  bytes (`std::array<uint8, 65536> Bytes`) and `view()` gives `TMdspan<uint8, TExtents<int, 256, 256>>`
  (layout_right): `view()[x, y]` is `Bytes[x * 256 + y]`, the byte order of the original's `Color[x][y]` and of the
  automap file. TAutomapBlock's Color and Speed are TAutomapLayer: the same size (0x10000 each), at the same offsets
  (not frozen since M6, but unchanged). Its own header so tests_core can test it without Map.h, which is the client's.
- Map.cpp: UpdateAutomap, GetAutomapColor, IsAutomapBlocked and GetAutomapSpeed index `Color.view()[x % 256, y %
  256]`; LoadAutomapBlock and SaveAutomapBlock read and write `Bytes` in one piece as before (a TSpan of the array:
  the same 65,536 bytes each, in the same order) and empty a block with `Bytes.fill(0)` / `fill(250)`, which were
  memset of the same bytes.
- The file format check stays a check of the file layout (#94): `sizeof(TAutomapLayer::Bytes)` is the file layer's
  256 x 256 bytes, and a second static_assert checks the view's mapping against the file's offset x * 256 + y (0,1;
  1,0; 255,255; the span size). A change of the layer's order or size fails to compile instead of writing another
  file.

### Tests (high)

- tests/unit/mdspan_test.cpp (tests_unit and tests_unit_cxx26_standin): the extents (static, mixed, dynamic), both
  mappings at compile time, indexing and strides of both layouts, the const view, an empty view; and in tests_unit
  that the names are std's where the library has std::mdspan. The automap layer's mapping at compile time.
- tests/unit/core_container_test.cpp (tests_core): matrix's and matrix3d's views against operator() and against the
  original's offsets of entry, over every element of a matrix and a matrix3d with negative bounds, and the const views.
- tests/unit/core_automap_layer_test.cpp (tests_core): TAutomapLayer's view against the bytes at x * 256 + y, both
  ways, and its const view.
- The golden Container test (matrix3d<int>'s and matrix<TPathNode>'s headers, entries and operator() addresses
  against the original) and the Map test (GetAutomapColor and the automap's other calls) replay unchanged; the
  automap files: compare_files.

### The gates (high)

(PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR=C:/Tibia/Patella-Modern/build/golden), its manifest verified.

## #120: the server replay's socket inside the process (Patella-Modern issue #120, M7)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-120). Until now PatellaTest.exe's server replay
(`--test-replay`, the reference compare's sessions) was a server on the loopback ports 7271 and 7272 inside the
client's process, which the client reached through real sockets; two replays at the same time, or a replay and
another agent's live run, collided on those ports, the most common cause of failed live runs during M7.

### The design (high)

- **TPipeNetwork** (src/testmode/PipeNetwork.h, portable, patella_testmode, tests_testmode's testmode_pipe_test.cpp):
  the loopback network without ports. The replay's listen lines are listeners on 127.0.0.1 and a port; a client
  connection is two byte queues with TCP's ends (each side's shutdown for sending, its close, a close with unread
  bytes as a reset). Its events for the client follow WinSock's WSAAsyncSelect rules: a connect never completes in
  the call (Connect, then Write, are posted; a port nothing listens on posts Connect refused), Read is posted when
  bytes come and none is posted and again after a receive that leaves bytes (WinSock's re-enabling recv), Close once
  at the server's shutdown or close. The server's side polls (Accept, ServerReceive, ServerSend, ServerShutdown,
  ServerClose), as the driver polled accept, recv, send, shutdown and closesocket.
- **TPipeSocketWin32** (src/testmode/PipeSocketWin32.h, the test build only): the ISocket of #109 over TPipeNetwork.
  The connection stays Win32's TSocket (a CAsyncSocket that never gets a handle), so TNetwork and its events are
  untouched. The events are posted to a message-only window of the client's thread (made when the replay opens) and
  its window procedure calls the TSocket's OnConnect, OnSend, OnReceive or OnClose: from the message loop, or a modal
  loop's (the message boxes' hook), as MFC's socket window's WM_SOCKET_NOTIFY. OnReceive only when the connection is
  readable at that time (MFC's CAsyncSocket::DoCallBack selects first); an event of a connection closed since it was
  posted is dropped (MFC's handle map has it no more). The error codes are WinSock's (WSAEWOULDBLOCK, WSAENOTCONN,
  WSAESHUTDOWN, WSAECONNRESET, WSAECONNREFUSED). Startup (AfxSocketInit) and the name resolution go to TWin32Socket:
  no recording resolves a name (the client is patched to 127.0.0.1).
- **Which socket** (high): the test build's Platform() (TestModeWin32.cpp) gives TNetwork TPipeSocketWin32 with
  --test-replay and TWin32Socket without it. The live runs against the test server (compare_traffic.py,
  compare_files.py, compare_rendering.py, compare_network.py, testmode_check.py) run without --test-replay and keep
  the real sockets; Patella.exe and the golden runner are not touched (Win32Platform.cpp unchanged).
- **The driver** (TestModeWin32.cpp): PumpReplay, ReplayDeliver and CloseReplaySocket call the network's server side
  instead of accept, recv, send, shutdown and closesocket; the out queue went (a pipe takes the whole frame). The
  schedule, the holds, the keys and the logs are as before; the log adds a line per listener ("listens on
  127.0.0.1:7271 in the process (no port)").
- **The loopback replay went** (high): no tool needs it (only reference.py passes --test-replay), and keeping both
  would be a test mode switch with nothing to choose it. reference.py no longer checks that 7271 and 7272 are free.
- **An address other than 127.0.0.1** is refused (OnConnect with WSAECONNREFUSED), as a loopback listener bound to
  127.0.0.1 refuses 127.0.0.2; a host name is refused too, where CAsyncSocket::Connect would have resolved it. The
  recordings name 127.0.0.1 only (the proxy's character list).

## #128: vlong as a portable, tested component; the protocol's unpadded RSA (Patella-Modern issue #128, M8)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-128, from main e8e1602). Plan section 7, M8, "Crypto".

### vlongtest's cases as unit tests (high)

- What was there: tests_core (tests/unit/core_vlong_test.cpp, issue #7) already ran all of the retired vlongtest's
  3,201 cases (tools/difftest/vlongtest.cpp at the tag `layout-frozen-final`: 200 RSA blocks, 600 each of `+ - * / %`,
  one decimal conversion; seed 4242, none skipped for a zero divisor) in every preset, but as one check: the FNV-1a
  digest of all the result bytes against the one tests/unit/core_expected.py computes with Python's integers
  (`pow(m, 65537, n)`, `+ - * // %`), the way vlongcheck.py checked vlongtest.exe. A wrong case failed that one
  check, without saying which case or what vlong gave.
- Now each case is checked on its own: tests/unit/core_vlong_cases.inc is one row per case in vlongtest's order (the
  operation and the 64-bit FNV-1a digest of the expected result bytes), written by
  `python -I tests/unit/core_expected.py --vlong-cases tests/unit/core_vlong_cases.inc` from Python's exact integers
  only; vlong never computes an expected value. tests_core has a test case per operation (`r`, `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`,
  `%`, `d`) that compares each of its cases with its row and names, on a failure, the case's number, its operands and
  vlong's result in hex (the full expected value is Python's for the same case, core_expected.py's vlong_cases()).
  The test also checks the row's operation and the count, so a change of the generator fails; the old combined
  digest stays as a test of its own (the same constant, 0x4850195d8e8c8047).
- A digest per case, not the expected bytes (medium): the results alone would be about 0.8 MB of hex in the
  repository; 64 bits per case catch any wrong result with certainty in practice, and the RSA rows are no more
  than the digest committed since #7 is (the modulus is the client's public key, a literal in src/Communication.cpp).
- One more test, "TRSA: raw RSA without padding": the same block encrypts to the same cipher text, and
  E(a)·E(b) mod n = E(a·b) for three pairs, which holds only for textbook RSA.
- The cases run in every preset that builds tests_core: windows-x64 (-debug), windows-x64-asan (AddressSanitizer),
  windows-x64-gcc, linux-x64-gcc and linux-x64-clang (AddressSanitizer and UBSan). They found no portability fault, so
  src/vlong.cpp is unchanged (its 32-bit units are `unsigned`, 32 bits on every target; `long` is cast where it has 8
  bytes on Linux since issue #7). Golden's replay of vlong is unchanged.

### The protocol's RSA has no padding (high)

- The login packets (Communication.cpp SendLogin and SendGameLogin) encrypt one 128-byte block with TRSA::Encrypt:
  the block, big-endian, is the number m, and the client sends m^65537 mod n (n: the 1024-bit public key, first byte
  0xb1). The block is a zero byte, the 16-byte XTEA key, the login data (game login: the gamemaster flag, account,
  name, password; login server: account, password) and rand()'s bytes after them. There is no PKCS #1 v1.5 or OAEP
  padding: the leading zero byte only keeps m below n (Encrypt refuses a first byte above 127, and m >= n). The server
  decrypts with the raw private exponent and reads the block at fixed offsets, so this is a property of the 7.72
  protocol, not of the client's code, and it stays (plan section 7, M8: XTEA and raw RSA are protocol requirements).
- What follows from it (documented, not changed): textbook RSA is deterministic and malleable; what keeps two logins
  apart is the XTEA key and the filler, both from rand() (seeded from timeGetTime, so guessable), and nothing protects
  the block's integrity. A client that padded the block would not log in to a 7.72 server.
- Comments at the call site (Communication.cpp, both Encrypt calls) and at TRSA::Encrypt point here; comment-only
  changes, so no live client run was needed for them.

## #72 and #86: the original's reads past their data, bounded (Patella-Modern issues #72 and #86, M7)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-72, from main e8e1602), after the owner's decision of
November 7: bound these over-reads of Tibia.exe now, as deliberate differences. Behaviour changes only for these
inputs; every other check stays as it was.

### #72: a frame whose inner length runs past it (high)

Changed by #139 (the owner's decision of November 7, "#139" below): such a frame is now dropped and logged, and the
connection goes on with the next frame; it no longer throws. The rest of this section is #72's outcome until then.

- **The read.** PrepareNextPacket set ReceiveBuffer's size from the frame's inner length as it was (`GetWord() + 4`).
  A length larger than the frame made every later read of the packet go on past the frame: into the next frames, and
  for a long one past ReceiveData into SendData (the read #70's ASan run found; since #105 the buffers are TNetwork's
  members, inside one object, so ASan no longer saw it). A frame of size 0 has no inner length at all: Tibia.exe read
  it from the two bytes after the frame.
- **What a short packet does now** (high; the issue's suggestion). The payload, `[u16 length][length bytes]`, must
  lie inside the frame (the length at most the frame's size minus 2; a length that runs into the frame's XTEA padding
  is still inside it and read as before). Otherwise the frame is dropped (ReceiveRead past it, PacketHeader and the
  test hook as before, the read buffer empty: Size = Position) and PrepareNextPacket throws the TMyException "packet
  length exceeds the received data" (TERROR2: the length + 4 and the frame's end). That is what a read past a packet's
  end already does (TReadBuffer's assertion): the exception leaves the receive handler and ends the client through
  HandleException and FatalError. Considered: cutting the size to the frame's end (the reads past it would then throw
  at the read, later, after commands read from a packet whose length lied); dropping the frame silently (hides a
  broken or hostile server, and differs from the short read). Because the frame is dropped first, the buffer stays
  consistent: a caller that catches the exception reads the next frame normally (bounded_reads checks it).
- **The suppressions.** #70's PATELLA_NO_SANITIZE_ADDRESS on ReceiveData and SendData went with #105 already (the
  globals became members); its one use left is TRGBColor::operator== (graphics.h, #70's other row). Gone now, their
  reason being this read: PATELLA_IN_DEFINITION_ORDER (src/compat/msvc.h, no user since #105) and golden_linux's GCC
  option -fno-toplevel-reorder (tests/golden/CMakeLists.txt: ReceiveData before SendData for the replayed over-read).
  Linux golden replays without it (gates below).

### #86: names of 30 and descriptions of 128 characters without a NUL (high)

- **The reads.** #85 kept the original's bytes: a 30-character ignore or white list name fills TIgnoreEntry::Name and
  its NUL lands in Permanent, which the caller sets next; a 128-character buddy description fills TBuddy::Description,
  its NUL in Notify. The readers read the field as a C string and went on into Permanent (with it set, "\x01" and the
  next entry's name in the rebuilt list line), and past the description into Notify, the padding and further.
- **Bounded** (the writes unchanged, #85's bytes): `TIgnoreEntry::NameText()` (Dialogs.h) and
  `TBuddy::DescriptionText()` (Preferences.h) give the field's characters up to its NUL or its end, as a
  TFixedString<31> or <129> with a NUL. Their users: TIgnoreListDialog::HandleEvent's two list rebuilds (Delete, 710
  and 713: `Name.Length()` for the empty test, NameText for the line); TPreferences::GetBuddyDescription (the text in
  a member of its own, `BuddyDescription`, not the original's: valid until the next call, which is how its callers use
  it; the edit buddy dialog's SetText copies it); WriteTibiaCfg's description; GetPreferenceValues' description for
  Patella.ini (#85 read up to the NUL within the entry's last 132 bytes; now at most 128). No layout change
  (non-virtual members; TPreferences' new member follows the original's data, no layout is asserted for it).
  Considered: writing a NUL into the field (cuts the name to 29 and the description to 127: #57's regression that #85
  fixed, and the saved files lose a character).

### The golden corpus: deliberate parts (high)

The corpus is frozen (#93), so a difference cannot be recorded, and a retired part (golden::RetiredBegin) needs the
oracle's records around it, which these places do not have. New, the narrowest mechanism that fits:
`golden::BeginDeliberate(Issue)` and `EndDeliberate()` (golden.h, golden.cpp). Between them the runner still runs our
side and reads every value of the corpus (the inputs still compared, so a test that generates other inputs is still
stale), and every check still counts in Checks (the test's total is still the oracle's); a check that differs is
counted as the issue's (golden::Deliberates: the parts, their checks, those that differed), not as a failure. CHECK
(golden_test.h) and the Network test's log check ask golden::CheckFailed. The runner prints each issue's numbers.

- **#72** (network_tests.cpp, the only user). Our side's GetNextCommand and PrepareNextPacket are called through
  OurGetNextCommand and OurPrepareNextPacket, which open a part for #72 exactly when ours throws "packet length exceeds
  the received data". From there the sides' receive buffers differ (the original's size is the frame's length, ours
  the frame's end; the original goes on reading commands past the frame), so nothing of the round compares until
  ResetSides, where both sides start the next round from the same cleared statics: the part ends there. In the main
  rounds Both catches our side's throw while a part is open (the error rounds' OurThrow catches it anyway). The frozen
  corpus has such frames (MakeFrame's modes 2 and 3: a length past the frame, a frame of size 0) in 196 of the 300
  main rounds and in 84 iterations of the error round's failure injection: **280 parts, 37,052 checks (of the Network
  test's 111,893), 14,165 of them differ**; the other 22,887 checks in the parts still agree. Every other check of the
  corpus is compared as before.
- **#86: 0 checks affected, no part.** The Dialogs test's rounds of #85 (LongIgnoreNames, 80 checks) never set
  Permanent on the 30-character entry: the dumps show its Permanent byte 0 in all four rounds, the permanent box set
  or not, when the list is rebuilt after "Delete the first line" (DG_LOGS). So the original's line there ends at
  Permanent's 0, as ours does; #85's note that the rebuilt line had "\x01" and "new entry" is not what the corpus
  holds. PreferencesFile's 179 checks of #85 have Notify "no" for the descriptions of 128 characters or more, whose
  read stops at Notify's 0 in the original too. Both replay with 0 failures, unchanged.
- **Counts**: 15,803,218 replayed + 1,512,822 retired = 17,316,040, 0 failures, as on main; of the replayed, 37,052 in
  #72's parts.

### The tests (high)

- **bounded_reads** (tests/golden/bounded_reads_test.cpp; a CTest test of every preset that builds the golden
  objects: windows-x64, -debug, -asan, linux-x64-gcc, linux-x64-clang): the golden runner's objects with doctest, no
  corpus, as preferences_file. #72: a TNetwork of its own (a fake session and sockets), XTEA frames through OnReceive:
  a length into the padding read as before; lengths 7, 8, 100, 0x3ff0 and 0xffff in a frame of 8 (dropped, the throw,
  the buffer empty, the next frame read); a frame of size 0; a frame that fills ReceiveData with the length 0xffff.

## #121: linux-x64-clang on GCC 16's libstdc++ (Patella-Modern issue #121, M7)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-121). The owner decided on November 7 that linux-x64-clang
moves from Debian's libstdc++ 14 to GCC 16's libstdc++ (in the image already), so `import std;` (#113) builds in all
four presets that know it, and std::mdspan (#101) is std's there. Files: docker/linux-x64/Dockerfile,
CMakePresets.json, cmake/ImportStd.cmake, src/compat/cxx26.h, the comments of src/compat/mdspan.h,
tests/unit/mdspan_test.cpp, tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt and cmake/Warnings.cmake; the image's tag in tools/build.py,
both workflows, CLAUDE.md, README.md and notes/reconstruction.md.

### How Clang gets GCC 16's library (high)

- Clang's default configuration files, `/usr/lib/llvm-22/bin/clang++.cfg` and `clang.cfg` in the image, each one line
  `--gcc-install-dir=/usr/local/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/16.2.0` (the directory of `gcc -print-libgcc-file-name`; the
  Dockerfile's RUN checks the path, that `clang++ -v` and `clang -v` say "Selected GCC installation:" that directory,
  and that `clang++ -print-file-name=libstdc++.modules.json` exists). Clang reads `<driver>.cfg` from its executable's
  directory (`clang++ -v`: "Configuration file: /usr/lib/llvm-22/bin/clang++.cfg"), so every caller has it.
- Why not the preset's flags: CMake 4.1's probe for the std module (Modules/Compiler/Clang-CXX-CXXImportStd.cmake)
  runs `${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER} ${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID_ARG1} -print-file-name=libstdc++.modules.json`, without
  CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS, so a `--gcc-install-dir` there leaves the probe on libstdc++ 14 (#113 tried it). A configuration
  file is part of the compiler; it also reaches clang-tidy, whose driver reads the same file (checked: `<mdspan>`,
  which libstdc++ 14 lacks, compiles under clang-tidy with a compile_commands.json that names only `clang++`). The C
  driver gets the same installation, so C and C++ objects link against one libgcc and its start files.
- `--gcc-install-dir` rather than `--gcc-toolchain`: the install dir names the one installation (GCC 16.2.0's
  directory, checked by the RUN), a toolchain names a prefix in which Clang picks a version itself; the gcc image has
  GCC 16 in /usr/local next to Debian's GCC 14 in /usr.
- The image's tag is new, `patella-modern/linux-x64:gcc16.2-clang22.1-libstdcxx16` (was `gcc16.2-clang22.1`, which
  #113 kept because the compilers did not change): Clang's library changed, and a local image under the old tag keeps
  serving the branches that still have the old Dockerfile (#116 and #72/#86 run meanwhile). After the merge a local
  image is built once with CLAUDE.md's command; the old tag can then be removed (`docker rmi`).
- PATELLA_IMPORT_STD is ON in linux-x64-clang (CMakePresets.json). An image without the configuration files fails its
  configure ("PATELLA_IMPORT_STD: Clang 22.1.8 has no std module ...", ImportStd.cmake), which names the cause.

### What the library switch changed in the build (high)

- The std module under _FORTIFY_SOURCE: glibc 2.41 declares its checked printf family (fprintf, printf, snprintf,
  sprintf, swprintf) for Clang as static overloads (`__fortify_clang_overload_arg`, bits/stdio2.h, bits/wchar2.h), and
  bits/std.cc's `export using std::printf;` cannot export a name with internal linkage ("using declaration referring
  to 'printf' with internal linkage cannot be exported", 5 errors in Release, where Hardening.cmake defines
  _FORTIFY_SOURCE=3). GCC's wrappers are extern inline and export. So on Clang patella_target_import_std gives the
  target (and with it the module, which takes the target's options) `-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE` after the hardening options.
  It is `SHELL:-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE`: CMake removes a repeated option, and the hardening already says
  `-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`, so a plain `-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE` was dropped (checked in the Ninja files:
  both std.cc and import_std_test.cpp end with -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE). tests_import_std includes no header, so it has no
  call fortify would check; every other target keeps _FORTIFY_SOURCE=3.
  - Considered: the module without fortify and the importer with it: the module and its importer would differ in a
    macro of the library again (#113's reason to give the module the target's options).
- std::inplace_vector: libstdc++ 16 says `__cpp_lib_inplace_vector` 202603 under Clang too, so cxx26.h selected it,
  and it fails there: its `_M_init` names `is_trivial_v` (deprecated in C++26) in a template the code instantiates,
  which Clang reports at the instantiation (-Wdeprecated-declarations, an error under -Werror: tests_unit's
  cxx26_contracts_test, slot_table_test, cxx26_static_vector_test), and its constexpr copy is not a constant
  expression under Clang ("subobject '_M_elems' is not initialized", cxx26_static_vector_test.cpp:122). cxx26.h keeps
  the stand-in for Clang with libstdc++ (`__clang__` and `__GLIBCXX__`), what linux-x64-clang had: TStaticVector
  (TMapPoint::Objects, the effect table's TSlotTable) is the same type there as before. tests_unit's path check
  expects nothing on Clang (PATELLA_EXPECT_CXX26 is empty), so no test changed. The stand-in goes when libstdc++'s
  inplace_vector builds under Clang (Found, not done).
- What else Clang now takes from libstdc++ 16: std::mdspan (`__cpp_lib_mdspan` 202406; below), and the newer
  library's headers everywhere; contracts stay off (Clang 22 has no `__cpp_contracts`). std::stacktrace through
  libstdc++exp (Warnings.cmake's check) passes as before.

### The mdspan stand-in (high)

Every preset's library has std::mdspan now (MSVC 202207, GCC 16's libstdc++ 202406 in windows-x64-gcc, linux-x64-gcc
and linux-x64-clang), so no preset compiles the stand-in in its product code. It stays, as the test switch
PATELLA_MDSPAN_STANDIN only (tests_unit_cxx26_standin, header_check_cxx26_standin), like span.h's and expected.h's
stand-ins: removing it would be a change of src/compat/mdspan.h's interface for no gain, and the header still serves a
library without `<mdspan>`. mdspan_test's static_assert branches are unchanged (the "library without std::mdspan"
branch is now reached by no preset). Only comments changed.

### clang-tidy (high)

tidy_ci runs clang-tidy in the image on linux-x64-clang's compile commands, so it now reads GCC 16's headers:
3 findings, the baseline's 3 (cppcoreguidelines-owning-memory in Utils.cpp and vlong.cpp), 0 new, 0 gone. No
finding moved.

### Found, not done (high)

- cxx26.h's Clang exception for std::inplace_vector: when libstdc++ (or Clang) fixes the deprecated is_trivial_v use
  and the constexpr copy, Clang can take std::inplace_vector as GCC does.
- tests_import_std on Clang is built without _FORTIFY_SOURCE while glibc's Clang wrappers are internal; a glibc or
  libstdc++ that exports them (or a std.cc that skips them under fortify) would let it keep the hardening.
- The old image tag `patella-modern/linux-x64:gcc16.2-clang22.1` stays on this machine until the branches that use it
  are merged.

## #116: TGraphics (Patella-Modern issue #116, M7)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-116, from main e8e1602). #104's step 6: graphics.cpp,
Surface.cpp and Skins.cpp, with GUI.cpp's SkinProperties (the issue's scope addition from #107, settled by the
orchestrator). TClient makes TPreferences, TNetwork, TMapState, TCommunication, TGraphics, TGUI, in that order
(Client.h).

### The objects (high)

- **TGraphics** (graphics.h): graphics.cpp's 21 globals (0x5cc430-0x5ccf94, .bss order, `{}` for the zero, the
  original's comments) and its 57 functions are its members of the same names, with their address comments. All
  its data is public (rule 2: it was extern; Communication.cpp sends the two signatures, the golden Graphics and
  Errors tests read and set the tables and the caches). The thirteen members that only read are const (the Find
  functions, the font and text measures, GetTextPosition). It owns the two objects below as `Engine` and `Skins`.
- **TGraphicsEngine** (Surface.h, defined in Surface.cpp; TGraphics' `Engine`): Surface.cpp's 18 globals, in .data
  and .bss order with their initial values (CommandLineEngine -1, the cache surfaces' 256 x 256), and its four
  functions (GetCurrentEngine const, GetSurface, SurfaceExitInstance, SurfaceInitInstance). An object of its own in
  Surface.h, as #105's TSession is Status.cpp's inside TCommunication: the file stays the module map. Public: the
  engine choice and the shared engine data (the Vulkan engine, Control.cpp, Dialogs.cpp, MainFrm.cpp, Player.cpp
  and the golden tests use them); private: the three file-local values (SurfaceWindow, AvailableEngines, Surface),
  read by TSurface's TestEngine and GetAvailableEngines, which reach them through `bridge::GraphicsEngine()` (TSurface
  is a friend). TSurface is unchanged: the same interface, layout and vtable (#119's).
- **TSkins** (Skins.h, defined in Skins.cpp; TGraphics' `Skins`): NumberOfSkins and the table (0x71c450, 0x71c454)
  and InitSkins and ExitSkins as members, and SkinProperties (0x5ccfc8) as its third member. SkinProperties' types
  (TGUIPoint, the TSkinProperties blocks) moved from GUI.h to Skins.h with it, unchanged; GUI.cpp keeps their layout
  asserts and InitSkinProperties, which fills it. GUI.h includes Skins.h (exported), so the windows see the types as
  before.
- **TRect, TRGBColor, TFont and the alignments** moved from graphics.h to types/GraphicsTypes.h (header only,
  portable, on patella_core's header list), which graphics.h exports: Surface.cpp (TSurface's default slots take
  them by value) and Skins.h (SkinProperties holds them) need them without graphics.cpp's module.

### The free functions and the bridge (high)

- The original's free functions stay and forward (rule 4): graphics.cpp's 57 to `bridge::Graphics()` (at the end of
  graphics.cpp), Surface.cpp's four to `bridge::GraphicsEngine()`. InitSkins and ExitSkins forward to `bridge::Skins()`
  from graphics.cpp, not from Skins.cpp: Skins.cpp is patella_core's, which has no TClient (the golden runner and the
  unit tests link Skins.cpp from the library), and graphics.cpp is the client's file of TGraphics. Control.cpp calls
  them; the golden Communication world fakes them by these symbols (commworld.cpp's F()).
- Calls between graphics.cpp's functions are member calls (the cache lookups, the draws, the text measures); its calls
  into the other files stay their free functions (GetSurface, which the golden Graphics test redirects to its recording
  surface and the window tests fake; GetActionNumber; the object table's accessors; Script.cpp's file class). The
  golden window tests fake the drawing functions by their free symbols, which the windows call, so no member fake was
  needed.
- **SkinProperties and the skin table** (high; a deviation from rule 2's `bridge::<Object>().<Name>` at each use):
  Skins.h has two inline accessors of the globals' names, `SkinProperties()` and `Skins()`, returning the one TClient's
  TSkins members, and the users write `SkinProperties().TooltipBorder` and `Skins()[skin].width` where they wrote
  `SkinProperties.TooltipBorder` and `Skins[skin].width` (about 2,000 and 245 uses in src/: the window files, GUI.cpp,
  Control.cpp, MapWindow.cpp, the test mode's dump; and the golden window tests: a script added `()` in the code, not
  in comments; the string literals it also changed at first were restored, below). Why: #107 left SkinProperties because
  the bridge path at each use would rewrite every expression of every window file; the accessor is the same object
  through the same bridge, with one call per use, and the windows' text stays the original's. NumberOfSkins (four
  assertions and the tests) is `bridge::Skins().NumberOfSkins`. They go when the windows hold TGraphics (below).
- The other users of the moved globals write the bridge path (rule 2): Communication.cpp's two signatures
  (`bridge::Graphics()`: TGraphics is made after TCommunication), the Vulkan engine's shared counters, the screen and
  the cache surfaces' size, Player.cpp's CommandLineEngine, and curEngine in Control.cpp, Dialogs.cpp and MainFrm.cpp
  (`bridge::GraphicsEngine()`); inside TGraphics' members curEngine is `Engine.curEngine`.
- TGraphics takes no constructor reference: everything it calls in an earlier subsystem (the object table) is a free
  function the golden tests fake, as #118 kept Control.cpp's calls.

### Behaviour (high)

The same code on the same data. What differs: the calls through the accessors (one more call per use of a moved
global, a guarded static's check in bridge::Client()), and the storage: one object inside TClient instead of each
file's .data and .bss, made at the first use of the client's state instead of before main (SkinProperties'
initialiser 0x559e50 ran its constructor before main; TClient is zero-initialised first, as a static, and its
member's `{}` gives the same zeros, so InitSkinProperties finds what it found). The unique_ptr tables are freed in
TClient's static destruction as before in the globals'; TGraphicsEngine's Surface stays a raw pointer, freed only by
SurfaceExitInstance, as the global was. The golden GUI test's placement construction of SkinProperties (and its
byte comparison with the original's constructor and InitSkinProperties) runs on the member unchanged.

### The include cycles (high)

Measured as #104 and #118 did (every `#include "X.h"` of a src/*.cpp naming another src/*.cpp's module is an edge;
Tarjan's strongly connected components; build\logs\issue-116\cycles-*.txt): main e8e1602 has 33 modules, 205 edges
and 2 cycles, {Surface, graphics} and {MainFrm, Player}. The branch has 33 modules, 207 edges and 1 cycle,
{MainFrm, Player}. Surface -> graphics went (Surface.cpp includes types/GraphicsTypes.h, a header without a module);
Client -> graphics, Skins and Surface came (the accessors). graphics -> Surface stays (graphics.h holds
TGraphicsEngine, graphics.cpp calls GetSurface); Surface now reaches only Preferences.

### The golden tests' and the unit test's calls (high)

Adapted, no check changed: the moved data through the bridge (graphics_tests.cpp through a local `Ours()`,
errors_tests.cpp's static table, commworld.cpp's signatures, the curEngine of the Control, Dialogs, Errors, Graphics,
MainFrm, MapWindow and Player tests), SkinProperties and the skin table through the accessors (the window tests, the
GUI test, core_tests.cpp's Skins test). dialogelements_tests.cpp's own `int Skins[9]` member is untouched.
The first golden run replayed 10,530,710 checks and stopped at the GUI test: the rewrite had changed the string
literal "SkinProperties constructor" (an output name of the corpus; the runner refused it as a stale corpus) and three
other literals; restored, the next run replayed everything. tests/unit/core_skins_test.cpp makes a TSkins of its own in each case and calls its members (patella_core has no
bridge); its checks are the same.

### Found, not done (high)

- The windows reach SkinProperties and the skin table through the accessors (the bridge); when the windows hold their
  TGUI and TGUI holds TGraphics (rule 5's constructor reference: TGraphics is earlier), the accessors go.
- Communication.cpp's two signatures and Control.cpp's, Dialogs.cpp's and MainFrm.cpp's curEngine use the bridge:
  TCommunication is made before TGraphics (an interface, or the signatures passed in), Control.cpp is TGUI's (a

- The image comparison #109 made (the x64 Patella.exe function by function against main's) was not made here.
### The core header's checks (high)

- TRect's and TRGBColor's constructor parameters were named as their members (x, y, width, height; R, G, B):

## #129: the regexp as C17 behind TRegexp (Patella-Modern issue #129, M8)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-129, from main 8d9cd2c). Plan section 7, M8, "regexp".

### What was there (high)

- src/Extern/regexp/regexp.c (Henry Spencer's regexp of 1986, the client's version, issue #15) was in patella_core and
  the client's own sources. It was C17 on GCC and Clang only (`-std=c17`, issue #7); MSVC compiled it in its default
  C dialect (C89 with extensions). It was on all three warning baselines (MSVC /W3, GCC and Clang -Wall) and Clang's
  `-Wdeprecated-non-prototype` was off for every C source, both because of its K&R definitions; regexp.c also turned
  off MSVC's C4018 and /analyze's C28278 and C6001.
- Status.cpp, the one user, held the program as `regexp *LinkRegexp` (InitStatus: regcomp; CheckClipboardText:
  regexec; ExitStatus: free, by hand). tests/unit's core_regexp_test.cpp freed its programs by hand too.

### regexp.c as C17, 0 warnings at the full level (high)

- C17 on every compiler: patella_target_language gives C sources `/std:c17` on MSVC too (cmake/Warnings.cmake).
- The K&R function definitions and the forward declarations without parameters are prototypes, with the same
  parameter types (`register` kept where it was). K&R definitions are obsolescent in C17 and gone in C23; MSVC warns
  about them at /W4 (C4131, 16) and Clang in every mode. The calls were all to definitions in the same file, so the
  values passed do not change; the char parameters of regnode, regc and reginsert now get their conversion at the
  call instead of in the callee, the same value. GCC 16.2 -O2's code for the old and the new file differs only in
  instruction order and register choice in reg and regatom (120 of 1,762 lines of objdump).
- The implicit conversions that the prototypes and the full levels show are casts to the type they already
  converted to: regnode's and regc's char arguments (MAGIC through unsigned char: MSVC's C4310 on a constant cast
  that does not fit; the byte stays 0x9c), regtail's offset bytes, and the int lengths given to strncmp and compared
  with strlen (unsigned, as the binary compares; the pragma off C4018 is gone). reg's parno keeps its 1986 form
  (set and read only when paren is set): GCC's -Wmaybe-uninitialized was already off for that function, MSVC's
  C4701 now is too (push/pop around it).
- The /analyze suppressions C28278 and C6001 are gone: with prototypes MSVC /analyze reports nothing in the file
  (Release and Debug), so the static analysis table ("Static analysis of the core library") marks those two rows.
  GCC -fanalyzer's -Wanalyzer-null-dereference suppression stays (regmatch's regnext, unrelated to the K&R form).
- regexp.c is off the three warning baselines, and Clang's `-Wno-deprecated-non-prototype` is gone: the file builds
  at /W4, and at -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wshadow with GCC 16.2 and Clang 22.1, with no warning
  (measured by hand for each compiler at -O0 and -O2 before the presets ran).
- Everything else is the 1986 text and the client's changes; each change is described in the file's own header,
  marked "Patella-Modern change (issue #129)". The file stays out of clang-format (`.clang-format-ignore`).

### TRegexp (high)

- src/types/Regexp.h, header only, in patella_core's header list (cmake/HeaderCheck.cmake, a separate
  `list(APPEND ...)`): `patella::TRegexp` holds regcomp's program in a `std::unique_ptr` whose deleter is free (the
  allocation is regcomp's malloc). Construct from a pattern (regcomp; empty when it fails or the pattern is
  nullptr), IsCompiled / `explicit operator bool`, Execute (regexec, 1 or 0), Subexpression(n) (a string_view of
  startp/endp, empty when that group did not take part), Reset, Get (the program, for tests). Movable, not copyable.
- Every call is regcomp's or regexec's own, with the same errors through regerrorhandler: Execute on an empty
  TRegexp is regexec(NULL, ...), which returns 0 ("NULL parameter"), as Status.cpp's call did when LinkRegexp was
  NULL. The const_cast to char * of the K&R interface is the wrapper's (neither function writes to the text).
- Status.h's `regexp *LinkRegexp` is `TRegexp LinkRegexp` (the forward declaration of struct regexp is gone; Status.h
  includes types/Regexp.h). Status.cpp: InitStatus assigns `TRegexp(LinkPattern)`, CheckClipboardText calls Execute,
  ExitStatus calls Reset. No caller frees a program by hand; the only direct regcomp/regexec calls left are
  regexp.c's own, the wrapper's, golden's regexp_tests.cpp (the differential test of the C code itself against the
  original's, frozen corpus) and core_regexp_test.cpp's checks of the error texts through the header's names.
- Two differences, both outside what the client does (conservative choice, owner's to revisit): ExitStatus now
  clears LinkRegexp (the original left it dangling until the next InitStatus, so a link check between the two was a
  use after free; now it is regexec(NULL), 0, and the text is copied), and a second InitStatus without ExitStatus
  frees the old program instead of leaking it. The client calls InitStatus once at start-up and ExitStatus once at
  exit, and golden's status test runs Init, the checks, Exit, twice; neither path is reached otherwise.

### Unit tests (high)

- tests/unit/core_regexp_test.cpp (tests_core, every preset with tests_core; ASan on windows-x64-asan and
  linux-x64-clang, where LeakSanitizer would see a program not freed) goes through TRegexp: matching and the
  subexpressions (pointing into the text), leftmost-first alternation (`(a|ab)(c|bcd)` on "abcd": a, bcd; one reason
  std::regex is no drop-in), a group that takes no part, Latin-1 classes, the program's fields (reganch, regstart,
  regmust/regmlen, the magic byte), every error text regcomp gives for a syntax error and regexec's "NULL
  parameter" (on an empty TRegexp and a NULL text), the ownership (move, assignment, Reset), and the client's own
  pattern, Status.h's LinkPattern, on more texts (a URL, a parenthesised host, a long top-level domain, four numbers
  that are not an address, upper case, the empty text).

### The gates (high)

Logs in build\logs\issue-129 of the branch's worktree, all on f2057e4's tree; golden replayed main's frozen corpus read
only (PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR=C:/Tibia/Patella-Modern/build/golden), its manifest verified. Every golden run: 15,803,218
replayed + 1,512,822 retired = 17,316,040, 0 failures; 0 compiler warnings on every preset, regexp.c at the full level.

## #133: hardened standard library modes (Patella-Modern issue #133, M9)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-133). Files: cmake/Hardening.cmake (the settings), the
comments of cmake/ImportStd.cmake, notes/reconstruction.md ("Building", patella_target_hardening). Every product
target gets them through patella_target_hardening; capture-x86's patcap.dll still uses none of it.

### What each library offers in this toolchain (high)

- **MSVC STL** (MSVC 14.51.36231, cl 19.51, `_MSVC_STL_UPDATE` 202604; 14.44, also installed, has it too):
  `_MSVC_STL_HARDENING` (yvals.h, since VS 2022 17.14 / MSVC 14.44; it replaced `_CONTAINER_DEBUG_LEVEL`, which is now
  an error, STL1006). 1 turns on the precondition checks of array, basic_string, basic_string_view, bitset, deque,
  vector, list, forward_list, span, mdspan, optional, expected, valarray, shared_ptr<T[]>, basic_stacktrace,
  common_iterator, counted_iterator and ranges::view_interface (each also its own `_MSVC_STL_HARDENING_<NAME>`). A
  violation calls the "doom function", `__fastfail(5)` (FAST_FAIL_INVALID_ARG): no exception, no handler, the process
  ends (a Debug build reports it through _RPTF0 first). ABI-neutral: no `detect_mismatch`, unlike
  `_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL`. Not used: `_MSVC_STL_DESTRUCTOR_TOMBSTONES` (writes a bad pointer into destroyed objects;
  not named by the plan, Found, not done).
- **libstdc++ 16** (GCC 16.2.0's, in the image, windows-x64-gcc's mingw-w64 GCC 16 and, since #121, linux-x64-clang):
  `_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS` is the hardened mode. It turns on `__glibcxx_assert`, the library's precondition checks
  (operator[], front/back of the containers, string and string_view, span's and mdspan's indices and extents,
  optional's and expected's access, marked "hardened precondition"); a violation calls `std::__glibcxx_assert_fail`
  (the file, line, function and condition on stderr, then abort). It keeps the ABI. GCC's `-fhardened` defines exactly
  it (checked: `g++ -fhardened -O2 -dM -E` gives `_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS 1` and `_FORTIFY_SOURCE 3`); libstdc++ 16 has
  no other hardened mode. `_GLIBCXX_DEBUG` (the debug mode, checked iterators) changes the containers' layout and
  ABI: not for release, and not taken. libstdc++ defines `_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS` itself in an unoptimised build since
  GCC 15 (c++config.h: `! defined(__OPTIMIZE__)`), so Debug had it twice already.
- **libc++**: not used by any preset (Clang uses libstdc++ 16 since #121), so `_LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE` is not set.

### What is on now (high)

- MSVC (windows-x64, windows-x64-debug, windows-x64-asan and their -debug): `/D_MSVC_STL_HARDENING=1` for C++ in every
  configuration. In Debug `_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL` 2 (/MTd's `_DEBUG`) checks the same preconditions and more, so
  hardening adds nothing there; it is on everywhere for one rule.
- GCC and Clang (windows-x64-gcc, linux-x64-gcc, linux-x64-clang and their -debug): `-D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS` for C++ in
  every configuration (Debug only until now). Bounds-checked std::span and std::mdspan in Debug, as the plan asks,
  come from these two (std's span and mdspan on every preset; span.h's and mdspan.h's stand-ins check nothing, test
  switches only).
- They are compile options, not compile definitions: patella_target_import_std gives the std module the importer's
  COMPILE_OPTIONS (CMake 4.1), so tests_import_std's module is built with the same mode; MSVC would warn C5050 for a
  macro of the importer that the module lacks (none: 0 warnings).
- A violation is not a TMyException: golden's error paths (compared by outcome) would see a dead runner, not a
  different exception, so a firing check fails golden visibly.

### Findings (high)

None. No hardening check fired in golden (every Windows and Linux preset, also under ASan and UBSan), the reference
compare, compare_traffic's sessions and replays, or the unit tests.

### The gates (high)

- windows-x64, windows-x64-debug, windows-x64-asan: exit 0, golden 15,803,218 + 1,512,822 = 17,316,040, 0 failures,
  0 compiler warnings (CMake's own "import std is experimental" notice as on main). windows-x64-gcc, linux-x64-gcc,
  linux-x64-clang (ASan, UBSan): exit 0, golden the same on both Linux presets.
- `reference.py compare`: exit 0, every session matches (twice: the baseline and the hardened build).
- `compare_traffic.py`: three runs. 1: exit 1, Tibia.exe's helper got no game connection (the original's live
  session, before the x64 client ran). 2: exit 1, Tibia.exe's replay window did not appear in 30 s while another
  session's PatellaTest.exe was on the desktop. 3 (the machine clear): exit 1, one live client packet different,
  the known live-world race of #101's gates: at "look north" Tibia.exe looked at a creature (0x63) that had walked
  onto the field, Patella.exe at the field's top item (0x19a); the four replays identical, the 15 states of each
  replay identical, the options equal. Not run a fourth time.
- `banned_calls.py`: exit 0. clang-format (CLAUDE.md's command): exit 0. `tidy_ci.py`: exit 0, 3 findings, the
  baseline's 3, 0 new, 0 gone.

### The cost (medium: each run once, on this machine, as the issue asked)

Before: main 30a934a; after: this branch; the same build folders, rebuilt; each command alone on the machine.

| Run | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| golden, windows-x64 Release (`ctest -C Release -R ^golden$`) | 100.3 s | 116.1 s | +16% |

One run each is noisy: the workflow's own golden on Windows (next to golden_concurrent) took 137.6 s before and

The reference compare is the frame-time run (the client's cycle with the Vulkan CPU driver under the virtual clock);

## #119: the platform interfaces, part 2 (Patella-Modern issue #119, M7, part 1 of the issue)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-119, from main 025376f). The issue's IClipboard, IInput and
IWindow with their Win32 and test implementations, the test hooks they replace, Patella.ini and LogFile through
IFileSystem, and the {MainFrm, Player} module cycle. TSurface as the platform's interface is not done: part 2
("Unfinished", below), as the brief allowed.

### The interfaces (high)

Portable headers in src/platform (no platform header, on patella_core's header list; cmake/HeaderCheck.cmake), in
#109's form (no copies, a protected non-virtual destructor, the process's objects through `platform::Platform()`,
whose TPlatform holds them after the clock, the files and the socket). No Win32 type in a signature, so M8's SDL3
implementations (#122, #123, #124) sit behind them as they are: a window is `TWindowHandle` (`void *`: an HWND, an
SDL_Window), a point `TPoint`, a display mode `TDisplayMode`, an icon `TMessageBoxIcon`, the text the client's
(Windows-1252, #112; each implementation converts).

| Interface | Header | Calls | Win32 implementation (Patella.exe, the golden runner) | Test implementation (PatellaTest.exe) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| IClipboard: HasText, Text, SetText | platform/Clipboard.h | sysinc.cpp IsClipboardEmpty, GetClipboardText, SetClipboardText | TWin32Clipboard: IsClipboardFormatAvailable, OpenClipboard ... CloseClipboard with CF_UNICODETEXT and #112's conversion, the calls sysinc.cpp made | TMemoryClipboard (portable, in the header; tests_core's core_platform_input_test.cpp): with a script; without one Win32's |
| IInput: CursorPosition, StartTimer, StopTimer, BeginIdle, IgnoreCaptureChange | platform/Input.h | MainFrm.cpp OnCreate, OnDestroy, OnSetCursor, OnCaptureChanged; Player.cpp InitInstance, OnIdle | TWin32Input: GetCursorPos, SetTimer, KillTimer; BeginIdle nothing, IgnoreCaptureChange false | TTestInput (TestModeWin32.cpp): the hooks' code (the script's cursor, the driver's ticks, the driver's step, #52's dropped capture changes); KillTimer always |
| IWindow: ShowMessageBox, VisitWindows, DisplayMode | platform/Window.h | Player.cpp FatalError, InitInstance (the two boxes, CountTibiaWindows); vulkan/SurfaceVulkan.cpp GetFullscreenModes | TWin32Window: MessageBoxA (MB_ICONHAND, MB_ICONEXCLAMATION), EnumWindows with GetWindowTextA and GetClassNameA (30), EnumDisplaySettingsA | TTestWindow: the boxes not shown with a script (messages.txt's type stays MessageBoxA's flags), the process's own windows only (#96), `--test-display-modes` (#48) |

- **The cursor into a POINT** (high): the callers keep their POINTs (ScreenToClient takes them);
  `ReadCursorPosition(IInput &, POINT &)` (Win32Platform.h) writes the point only when the cursor was read, as
  GetCursorPos left it unchanged.
- **CountTibiaWindows** (high): a visitor of the window's title and class (`TWindowVisitor`), called by VisitWindows;
  the Win32 side reads them as the callback did (GetWindowTextA, GetClassNameA with 30, in that order, before the
  decoders), so the count is the same. SDL3 has no other process's windows: M8's single-instance check is another
  implementation of this one call.
- **The clipboard's text** (high): the interface carries the client's text, so the implementation converts (Win32:
  UTF-16, '?' for a character Windows-1252 does not have, #112, the owner's decision; SDL3: UTF-8). GetClipboardText keeps its buffer and the original's
  odd CR removal (one byte past the data); two changes of order, no change of result: the clipboard is closed before
  the buffer is filled (the original closed it after the copy; only an exception there, a std::bad_alloc, left it
  open), and a clipboard without text data is an empty text, Size 1 (the original's Size 0 and a NUL in the buffer:
  the same buffer, ResizeClipboardBuffer of 0 or 1 does nothing).
- **TMemoryClipboard with a script** (high, a change of the test build only): a scripted run (the reference compare,
  compare_rendering) neither reads the desktop's clipboard (another program's, a parallel test client's) nor
  changes it. No recording pastes text it did not copy; the reference compare is the check. Without a script (the
  live runs against the test server) Win32's, as Patella.exe.
- **The display modes** (high): through IWindow, so the hook went. The desktop's own mode (CreateSurfaces'
  ENUM_CURRENT_SETTINGS) stays the Vulkan engine's own EnumDisplaySettingsA: the engine's call, part 2 (TSurface).

### The hooks (high)

Gone from src/TestHooks.h: PATELLA_GET_CURSOR_POS, PATELLA_SET_MAIN_TIMER, PATELLA_TEST_IDLE,
PATELLA_TEST_CAPTURE_CHANGED (IInput), PATELLA_MESSAGE_BOX, PATELLA_ENUM_WINDOWS, PATELLA_ENUM_DISPLAY_SETTINGS
(IWindow). Remaining: PATELLA_TEST_RSA_BLOCK, PATELLA_TEST_PACKET_SENT, PATELLA_TEST_PACKET_RECEIVED,
PATELLA_TEST_FRAME_OBSERVERS, PATELLA_TEST_PRESENT_FAILURE, PATELLA_TEST_INIT_FAILURE (the test mode's observers
and failures, as #109 decided: an observer interface would be a test-only interface in the product), and
CPlayerApp::PreTranslateMessage's DropInput (the test build's override): a filter of Win32 window messages (MSG),
which no portable IInput call can carry; M8's SDL3 input has events of its own, and the test mode's input then comes
from its own IInput. notes/testmode.md, "The hooks".

### Patella.ini and LogFile through IFileSystem (high)

- settings::Load, LoadForUpdate and Save take an IFileSystem and open Patella.ini through it as a binary TFile
  (TFile::Open, _wfsopen with _SH_DENYNO: what std::ifstream and std::ofstream opened on Windows; on Linux fopen with
  the UTF-8 name). Callers: Preferences.cpp (TPreferences' IFileSystem of #109), the Vulkan engine's device choice and
  the developer log's settings (Platform()'s). The name is the client's text, as every TFile name; "Patella.ini" is
  ASCII, so the same file.
- LoadForUpdate's "no file" is the open's ENOENT (until now std::filesystem::exists after a failed read). The same
  outcome in every case: not there (or its folder not there) a new file; there but not readable (EACCES, a folder)
  nothing; read but larger than MaxFileSize or a read error nothing. Load's read error is TFile::Failed (ferror;
  new, in types/File.h), where it was the stream's bad().
- The log: TLog::OpenFile, log::Configure and log::LoadSettings take the IFileSystem; Player.cpp passes Platform()'s.
  OpenFile stays noexcept (an implementation's std::bad_alloc is a failed open).
- The unit tests (core_settings_test, core_log_settings_test, log_test) pass a TSystemFileSystem; golden's
  preferences_file and bounded_reads tests Platform()'s. No check changed.

### The {MainFrm, Player} cycle (high)

MainFrm.cpp included Player.h for one call: PreCreateWindow decoded the window class (GetWindowClassName, Player.cpp's
0x4d92b0). CMainFrame's constructor takes the class InitInstance registered (`CMainFrame(bool Gamemaster, const char
*WindowClass)`, a TFixedString<32> member WindowClass, not the original's), and PreCreateWindow copies it into
ClassName, the same 32 bytes the decoder wrote. Player.cpp still includes MainFrm.h (the application makes its frame
window). Measured as #118 and #116 did (every `#include "X.h"` of a src/*.cpp naming another src/*.cpp's module is an
edge; Tarjan's strongly connected components; build\logs\issue-119\cycles-main-025376f.txt, cycles-branch.txt):
main 025376f 33 modules, 207 edges, 1 cycle {MainFrm, Player}; the branch 33 modules, 206 edges, 0 cycles (the edge
MainFrm -> Player went). The client has no module cycle any more.

### The golden tests' calls (high)

No check changed. mainfrm_tests.cpp constructs ours with "TibiaClient" (the class InitInstance registers) and
includes Player.h itself (it lays out a CPlayerApp; MainFrm.cpp no longer brings it). The MainFrm test's user32 fakes
(GetCursorPos, SetTimer, KillTimer) land as before: TWin32Input calls the same imports, in the runner's image
(Win32Platform.cpp, compiled in tests/golden/network with /EHs, so the error round's throwing fakes pass through it).

### The image (high)

Main 025376f and the branch, the x64 Release Patella.exe built from the same source path (main's into build/pe-main
before the first change, the branch's into build/pe-branch), compared function by function through their PDBs
(dumpbin /disasm:nobytes with the PDB's labels; absolute addresses and image-relative table offsets masked, each
function cut at its first jump table or padding; the script is not committed: build\logs\issue-119\pecompare.txt):
14,393 and 14,335 functions; 101 gone, 43 new, 24 changed, 44 whose only change is a called symbol's name (identical
COMDATs the linker folded under another name, e.g. `_Myptr` for `c_str`), 13 whose only change is an immediate (the
assertion line numbers of InitInstance's and Run's catch funclets, Player.cpp's lines moved; CMainFrame's deleting
destructor, its size). The 24 changed (build\logs\issue-119\pecompare-changed.txt):

- the call sites: MainFrm.cpp's OnCaptureChanged, OnCreate, OnDestroy, OnSetCursor, PreCreateWindow (and the
  constructor's unwind funclet); Player.cpp's CountTibiaWindows, FatalError, InitInstance, OnIdle; sysinc.cpp's
  GetClipboardText, IsClipboardEmpty, SetClipboardText; the Vulkan engine's GetFullscreenModes, LoadDeviceChoice,
  SaveDeviceChoice; Preferences.cpp's InitPreferences and SavePreferences (Patella.ini through IFileSystem);
- four functions the call sites' new code changed through the optimiser, with the same calls but for inlined
  std::string members (LTCG: the new code uses the same templates): FindCpuDriverManifest (DeviceSettings.cpp,

  (Cp1252ToWide's conversion a call now: Settings.cpp and the log open files through it too).

Gone: std::ifstream and std::ofstream with their filebuf, codecvt and CRT parts (_fsopen, _sopen_s, fsetpos ...:
Patella.ini's streams, now TFile), the old Load, LoadForUpdate, Save, Configure, LoadSettings and CMainFrame
constructor signatures, GetWindowClassName (inlined into its two callers now that MainFrm.cpp no longer calls it), and
funclets and folded names the linker numbered or chose differently (TTalkBuffer::IsPrivateChannel is folded with
TPrivateChannel's). New: the Win32 implementations (TWin32Clipboard, TWin32Input, TWin32Window, VisitWindow), the
new signatures, Settings.cpp's ReadFile, ferror, and the same kind of funclets and folded names. No other function
changed.

## #100: the vectors that need neither min..max nor growth by indexing (Patella-Modern issue #100, M7)

Settled by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026. Plan M7, containers, second half: each use of TIndexedVector (#99) was
classified; the lists that append at their count and read below it, and the keyed lookups, are standard containers,
one subsystem per commit, each commit with the golden replay. "Growth by indexing" here is an index past the end
other than the append at the count, an index below 0, or a read past the count (entries the range or the init fill
holds). An index that comes from a file or a packet counts as unbounded unless the code bounds it.

### Converted (high)

- **Help** (7b4c4c8): THelp::EventHelps + NumberOfEventHelps is `std::vector<int>` (the count is its size): a queue,
  appended at the count (AddEventHelp, Number asserted 1..EVENTHELPS), popped at 0 (the original shifts the entries
  down), read only below the count.
- **Preferences** (73e96a9): TPreferences' ContentWindows, OpenChannels, Buddies and KnownHints with their counts are
  `std::vector`s; the counts are their sizes (cleared where the original set the count to 0: SetDefaultPreferences,
  ClearOpenChannels). Every reader stops at the count; WriteTibiaCfg's shared counter `i` still ends the Buddy loop at
  the number of entries, deleted ones included, so the White list's commas are the original's. ReadTibiaCfg wrote an
  entry in place and counted it after its last token; now the entry is read into a local and appended then. The
  difference is an entry left half-written by a read error, past the count: the error resets the options
  (SetDefaultPreferences), so it was never read. `std::flat_map` was not used for ContentWindows (ID to size): the
  saver writes the entries in insertion order (compare_files, Patella.ini's ContentWindow list), and a Tibia.cfg may
  hold the same ID twice (the reader appends without a check; GetContentWindowSize returns the first).
- **GUI** (724388e): TGUI::Timers is `std::vector<TTimer *>`: AddTimer takes the first null entry from 0 or appends
  (the original's `while (Timers(i) != NULL) i++` grows by one at max + 1, init NULL), RemoveTimer nulls the entry,
  UpdateTimers goes by index with the size read each time (a callback may add or remove timers); min stays 0, so
  max + 1 is the size. TGUI::Hotkeys + NumberOfHotkeys is `std::flat_map<int, TCallback>` (MSVC's STL and libstdc++
  16 have it on every preset, `__cpp_lib_flat_map` 202511 checked; no stand-in): AddHotkey replaces the callback of a
  key that is there, so each key is there once, and the order is never read (RemoveHotkey moved the last entry into
  the gap). CheckHotkey sends a copy of the callback, as the original's Send read the entry's two members before it
  called the receiver. THotkey stays in GUI.h: the golden Container test's vector<THotkey> round uses it.
- **Map** (ce8f5f6): GetAutomapMarks' out parameter is `std::vector<TMark> *` (the callers' local vector<TMark>(0, 0,
  10), ContentWindows.cpp's two): it sets the entries 0 to the count - 1, appended past the vector's size, as the
  original's operator() did from 0 up; the null pointer of the golden Errors test is still not dereferenced without
  marks. golden's calls adapted (map_tests.cpp's locals, contentwindows_tests.cpp's FakeGetAutomapMarks,
  errors_tests.cpp's null pointer's type); no check changed.
- **Status** (after #129's merge, which had Status.cpp): TInteraction::Messages + NumberOfMessages is
  `std::vector<TMessage>`: AddMessage appends at the count, AddMessageFirst inserts at 0 (the original moved the entries
  up from the count, the first growth at the count), FetchMessage pops at 0, ClearMessages frees the parameters of
  the entries below the count, InitStatus empties it without freeing them, as the original. The golden Status test
  reads only the original's NumberOfMessages (recorded) against its own count.

### Kept as TIndexedVector, with why (high)

- **TPreferences::OpenDialogs** (0, 9, 10, init -1): ReadTibiaCfg's and SetPreferenceValues' duplicate check reads
  `entry[min .. max - 1]`, past NumberOfOpenDialogs: the init fill and the entries ClearOpenDialogs left count as
  present.
- **TAutomapBlock::Marks**: MarkCount comes from the block's file (LoadAutomapBlock's readQuad) and can be negative;
  AddAutomapMark then indexes below 0 and the vector grows downwards; the reload clears min to max.
- **TTextWindow::Lines** (ConsoleWindow.h): GetTalkLine and GetLineFormat test `min <= LineNumber <= max`,
  FormatLines empties the entries up to max, and the golden ConsoleWindow test's dump compares Lines.min, Lines.max
  and the entries min..max with the original's.
- **DialogElements.h**: TRadioButtonGroup::Buttons, TEditText::LineStart (PageUp reads LineStart(-1): growth below
  0), TFocusGroup::MemberList, TListBox::LineText, TFontListBox::FontLines; and **Dialogs.h** TIgnoreListDialog's
  IgnoreEntries and WhiteEntries: the golden Dialogs test's dumps compare each vector's min, max, start, space and
  block, and the DialogElements test reads the entries by min..max (a std::vector has no start, space or block:
  converting them would change those checks).
- **Talk.h**: BuddyExemptionList, TemporaryIgnoreList, IgnoreList and ConsoleFilterList, and the parameters of
  FindTalkFilter, FindTextBuffer and AddTalkFilter: the golden Talk test compares the vector's 21-byte header (min ...
  init, the original's block growth) after each of 65 AddTalkFilter calls; the lists are searched from min to max.
- The golden tests' own TIndexedVectors (container_tests.cpp, talk_tests.cpp, dialogs_tests.cpp, ...) test the type
  itself or the original's instances.

So the CipSoft vector is left only where its min..max, its block growth or its growth below 0 is part of the
behaviour, or a golden check compares its header.

### The gates (high)

Logs: build\logs\issue-100 of the branch's worktree; golden replayed main's frozen corpus read only
(PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR=C:/Tibia/Patella-Modern/build/golden), its manifest verified.

## #137: compare_traffic's look step at the player's own field (Patella-Modern issue #137, M7)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-137). Files: tools/session_client.py (run_session's `look`,
LOOK_NORTH, LOOK_OWN_FIELD), tools/compare_traffic.py (play passes LOOK_OWN_FIELD), notes/traffic.md (the step table).

### The race (high)

The live part a. of compare_traffic failed now and then at "look north" (#101's gates, three of #133's, main after
#133): one client's look packet named a creature (type 0x63, stack position 1), the other the field's top item
(0x19a, stack position 0). The recorded states of main's failing run (build/traffic/result, a8ccca5) name the
creature: Cipfried, the temple NPC, stood on [32098, 32218, 7], the field north of the player, in Tibia.exe's live
session at "say" and "look north", and on [32096, 32217, 7] in Patella.exe's. The NPC wanders around the start
fields of the test server's world; the clients behaved alike (the four replays identical, every replayed step's state
equal).

### The fix (high)

The scenario, not the tool: compare_traffic's sessions (live and replays) look at the player's own field (map field
(8,6)) instead of the one north of it; the step is named "look at own field". No creature can stand on a player's
field, so both clients send the look at the player, with the same position and stack position. Nothing of the client
packets is masked or excused; a. compares as before. The test server's world and files are unchanged.

The frozen reference recordings (build/reference, recorded through compare_rendering.py's session, which calls the
same run_session) have "look north" at field (8,5): run_session keeps it as its default (LOOK_NORTH), so
reference_record.py and compare_rendering.py are unchanged, and `reference.py compare` replays its recorded window
messages anyway (it never calls run_session). So compare_traffic's live session now differs from the recorded
"traffic" session in that one step: its name and the field clicked (the player's own field there, north of it in the
recordings). A `--skip-live` run on recordings made before this change replays them with the new step, and the proxy
reports the look packet as different: record them again.

### A kill in the middle of the server's save (high)

The fourth live run of the first series (07:16) met the server's bind race (#95) in its first start: testserver.py
waited for "Server Online!", sent Ctrl+C and killed the server 30 s later (STALLED_STOP). A server whose world is
loaded saves all 9,873 map sectors on Ctrl+C, and with the fuzzers of #132 and two builds on the machine that took
longer: the kill at 07:17:35 cut `C:\Tibia\gameserver\data\map\1040-1009-10.sec` off at 4096 bytes, in the
middle of a line, and every later start failed with "Game initialization failed: Cannot load sector" (the fifth run
and the five of the second series, in seconds each; for the other agents' live runs as well). The truncated file was
the only sector not ending in a newline.

- testserver.py: a failed attempt's server whose server.log says "Server Online!" gets SAVING_STOP, 600 s, for its
  Ctrl+C (stop_timeout; both of start's stop paths, the bind error's and the stall's); one that never came online
  keeps the 30 s. Two self-test checks. notes/testserver.md, "Start".
- The sector, rebuilt (a repair of what the run broke, not a change of the world): the server writes a sector as
  origmap's lines with the coordinates without leading zeros under its own header ("# Data for sector x/y/z"); that
  rebuild from data\origmap gives 6,975 of the 9,872 other sectors byte for byte (the rest have changed in play), its
  z=10 neighbours among them, and the cut-off file's 4096 bytes are an exact prefix of the rebuild of
  1040-1009-10.sec (21,586 bytes). Written back; the server then loaded the world (17.3 s) and stopped cleanly. The
  cut-off file and the rebuild are kept in build\logs\issue-137 (1040-1009-10.sec.truncated-0717, .rebuilt).

### The gates (high)

On this branch's client (main a8ccca5's windows-x64 build, the same sources), the machine shared with the agents of
#119, #100 and #132; logs in build\logs\issue-137 (summary.txt lists every run).

- `python -I tools/compare_traffic.py --patella build/windows-x64/Release/Patella.exe`: 18 runs. Every run that
  played both live sessions passed: 1, 2, 3, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, each exit 0, "RESULT: no differences", a. 18 and
  18 client packets identical, the look packet `8c 627d db7d 07 6300 01` (the player's field [32098, 32219, 7], type
  0x63, stack position 1) in both clients. **14 to 18: five in a row**, with testserver.py's fix. The others never
  compared anything: 4 (the bind race, then the kill in the middle of the save, above) and 5 to 10 (the cut-off
  sector: no server); 11 (another agent's server came up between the check and the start: refused); 13 (the replay
  of patella-live: Tibia.exe's window not there in 30 s while another agent's PatellaTest.exe was on the desktop,
  #133's run 2).
- `python -I tools/reference.py compare --reference C:/Tibia/Patella-Modern/build/reference`: exit 0, every session
  matches its reference (07:21, and 08:09 on the final tools).
- `python -I tools/testserver.py self-test`: 0 failures (the two new checks among them). The changed tools compile
  (`python -I -m py_compile`).
- No C++ preset, banned_calls or clang-format: src/ and CMake are unchanged.

### Found, not done (medium)

- The walk steps share the race in principle: "walk north" steps onto the field Cipfried stood on in main's failing
  run; a creature there blocks the step and the sessions part. Not seen in 18 runs; a field no creature can reach
