## #138: TSurface as a platform interface (Patella-Modern issue #138, M7; part 2 of #119)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-138, from main 9ffbb50). #119's "Unfinished: part 2" and
#116's leftovers: TSurface is the platform's interface, the engine's shared data no longer goes through
`bridge::GraphicsEngine()`, and the window handle is a `TWindowHandle` where the client held an HWND.

### TSurface in src/platform (high)

- **platform/Surface.h** (portable, no platform header; patella_core's header list, cmake/HeaderCheck.cmake, a separate
  `list(APPEND ...)`): TSurface with its slots in the original's order and their comments, and the view mode and
  surface index constants (WINDOWED_MODE ..., PRIMARY_SURFACE ... NUMBER_OF_SURFACES), moved from src/Surface.h, which
  exports it (every user includes Surface.h as before). The default bodies (the constructor, the destructor,
  SetColorKey, TestEngine, GetAvailableEngines and the empty slots) stay Surface.cpp's, at their addresses: the
  original's code, as #109's TSocket stayed the original's class. TSurface keeps its global name (the engines, the
  window files and the golden tests name it). The two unnamed enums keep a NOLINT with GraphicsTypes.h's reason
  ("The other ten stay unscoped"): Visual Studio's clang-tidy reports them in the new header.
- **No Win32 type in it** (the issue's condition, for M8: #126 puts SDL_Vulkan_CreateSurface behind it, #122 replaces
  the MFC window): `Init(TWindowHandle *Window, ...)` (a pointer, as the slot's: Control.cpp's CheckSurface passes
  `&WindowHandle`, the engine reads it during the call), `hWindow` a TWindowHandle, `DeviceContext` (SurfaceGL.cpp's
  HDC, unused since #94) a `void *`, ClipRect's two rectangles and `ScreenRect` a `platform::TEdgeRect` (RECT's four
  edges as ints, the same members in the same order: the engine's code reads `.left` ... as before), the bytes
  `std::uint8_t` (`uint8` is the same type, common.h). The engine's local rectangles that go to ClipRect and its
  ColorFill are TEdgeRects; its surface rectangles stay RECTs (GetClientRect writes them).
- **The shared data** (high): `platform::TSurfaceShared` holds what the engines and the client share (the cache
  surfaces' size, InitStep, the blit statistics, the screen's size, NumberOfSurfaces, the two SurfaceGL.cpp values,
  and Surface.cpp's file-local SurfaceWindow and AvailableEngines, protected, TSurface a friend). TGraphicsEngine
  derives from it (users write `bridge::GraphicsEngine().BlitCount`, `Engine.curEngine` as before) and keeps
  CommandLineEngine, curEngine and the surface pointer. TSurface's constructor takes a `TSurfaceShared &` (its
  member `Shared`, protected, after the original's members): GetSurface passes `*this` to CreateSurfaceVulkan, so
  the Vulkan engine writes `Shared.BlitCount++` where it wrote `patella::bridge::GraphicsEngine().BlitCount++`, and
  TestEngine and GetAvailableEngines read `Shared.SurfaceWindow` and `Shared.AvailableEngines`. No accessor of the
  client is left in the engine code (src/vulkan and TSurface's bodies); the free functions of Surface.cpp keep
  theirs (rule 4: GetSurface, GetCurrentEngine, SurfaceExitInstance, SurfaceInitInstance).
- **Its layout** (high): the pointer first, the thirteen ints in the original's relative order, the byte last, so
  TGraphicsEngine is 80 bytes on x64 as before and TGraphics' and TClient's later members keep their offsets. A
  first version in the original's .data/.bss order (the byte in the middle) made it 88 and changed every function
  that reads a later member of TGraphics or TClient (91 changed in the image comparison; 50 with this order).
- **Why a base, not an interface the engine calls** (medium): the data is plain fields the engine increments in its
  drawing loops (as the original's globals); a virtual call per blit would change the drawing code, and a pointer to
  TGraphicsEngine would make the platform side depend on the client's class. TSurfaceShared is portable data that
  the client owns and lends to the engine for the surface's life (SurfaceExitInstance deletes the surface before
  TClient goes).

### TWindowHandle for the HWND uses (high)

`SurfaceInitInstance(TWindowHandle)` (by value: the x64 client's own function; Player.cpp passes `MainFrame->m_hWnd`
where it passed its address, and the function read it at once), TGUI's `WindowHandle` and `InitWindow(TWindowHandle,
...)` (GUI.h, Control.h, Control.cpp), TNetwork's `NetworkWindow` and `SetNetworkWindow(TWindowHandle)` (Network.h,
Network.cpp; ISocket::ResolveHostname took a `void *` already). MainFrm.cpp passes its m_hWnd (an HWND converts to
`void *`); the Vulkan engine converts back where it calls Win32 (GetClientRect, ClientToScreen, its present and test
windows: `TSurfaceVulkan::MainWindow()`, a static_cast). Control.h, GUI.h and Network.h include platform/Window.h and
need no HWND any more.

### The desktop's mode through IWindow (high)

`IWindow::DesktopMode(TDisplayMode &)` (platform/Window.h): EnumDisplaySettingsA(nullptr, ENUM_CURRENT_SETTINGS) in
TWin32Window (Win32Platform.cpp; DisplayMode and DesktopMode share ReadDisplaySettings, the code DisplayMode had), and
Win32's in TTestWindow too (the machine's, with or without `--test-display-modes`, as the engine's own call was).
CreateSurfaces reads its depth: `if (!Initialized || !DesktopMode(Desktop)) Depth = 0; if (Depth < 16)` PROGRAM_ERROR 8,
the same order and outcome as with the DEVMODEA it filled (it read only dmBitsPerPel).

### The golden tests' calls (high)

No check changed. The recording surfaces pass the client's TGraphicsEngine to TSurface's constructor
(testsurface.h's TTestSurface, defined in graphics_tests.cpp; commworld.cpp's TCtlSurface) and take the new ClipRect
and Init signatures; client_stubs.cpp's CreateSurfaceVulkan stub takes the shared data; network_tests.cpp's view and
function table and commworld.cpp's SetNetworkWindow fake take a TWindowHandle. player_tests.cpp's GetAvailableEngines
check called the member on a null surface on Windows (the original's member does not read `this`); ours reads the
shared data through the surface now, so it uses a real TTestSurface on every platform, as Linux has since #91 (the
same check: 0 on both sides).

### The image (high)

Main 9ffbb50 and the branch, the x64 Release Patella.exe of the same build folder (main's copied to build/pe-main
before the first change, the branch's to build/pe-branch), compared function by function through their PDBs as #109
and #119 did (dumpbin /disasm:nobytes with the PDB's labels, absolute and image-relative addresses masked, each
function cut at its first jump table or padding; the script is not committed: build\logs\issue-138\pecompare.txt, and
pecompare-classified.txt with the memory displacements masked too): 14,344 and 14,346 functions; 10 gone, 12 new, 50
changed, 4 whose only change is a called symbol's name, 21 whose only change is an immediate (the folded
GetFirstChild/GetLastChild's offset, TSurface's deleting destructor's size, and the assertion line numbers of 18
Network.cpp functions and funclets: its include of platform/Window.h moved its lines by one). The 50 changed:

- 30 only in memory displacements: the engine's members moved by the 8 bytes of TSurface's `Shared` (TSurfaceVulkan's
  CanShadeRectangles, ExitSurfaces, FlushVertices, GetFullscreenModes, GetSurfaceRect, Masked, SetPixel,
  SetRenderTarget, SetSurfaceRect, ShadeRectangles, StretchBlit, StretchBlitUnclipped, SurfaceRecreated, Track,
  UpdateWindowRect, WriteImage, WriteMaskedImage, a CreateSurfaces funclet, GetDeviceName), and TGraphicsEngine's own
  members at other offsets (curEngine, the cache surfaces' size: TGraphics' GetVideoFontChar, GetVideoMaskedSprite,
  GetVideoPicture, GetVideoSprite, TGUI::Redraw, the graphics and advanced graphics dialogs, MainFrm.cpp's
  SetDisplayMode, GetCurrentEngine, SurfaceExitInstance);
- the call sites: TSurface's TestEngine (reads its Shared), GetSurface (passes the engine), CreateSurfaceVulkan's
  funclet, the engine's functions that wrote the shared data (a load of `Shared` where the bridge was called:
  BlitRectClipped, CreateSurfaces and its catch funclet, DrawHorizontalLine, DrawVerticalLine, ExitDisplay,
  FillRectangle, FillRectangleClipped, FinishFrame, InitSurfaces, StretchBlitRect, the deleting destructor),
  CPlayerApp's InitInstance (SurfaceInitInstance's argument; CommandLineEngine's offset), TClient's constructor
  (TGraphicsEngine's initial values at their new offsets), TWin32Window::DisplayMode (calls ReadDisplaySettings);
- two std templates the optimiser compiled differently (LTCG), with the same calls: std::_Integer_to_chars<unsigned
  char> (`mov ecx,eax` for `mov rcx,rax`, twice) and a lambda of std::format's _Write_escaped matched under another
  name.

Gone: the old signatures (InitWindow, SetNetworkWindow, both SurfaceInitInstance, TSurface's constructor,
CreateSurfaceVulkan, TSurfaceVulkan's Init, ClipRect and ColorFill with HWND and RECT) and a FindCpuDriverManifest
funclet the linker numbered differently. New: the same functions with the new signatures, TWin32Window::DesktopMode,
ReadDisplaySettings, and a WritePreferences funclet. No other function changed (measured on the head b2fe7ae).

### Found, not done (high)

- TSurfaceVulkan keeps its Win32 side inside the engine (the RECT arrays, GetClientRect, vkCreateWin32SurfaceKHR, the
  present windows): #126 (SDL_Vulkan_CreateSurface) replaces it behind TSurface.
- MainFrm.cpp and Player.cpp (MFC) still hold the HWND they pass on; #122 replaces them.
- Control.cpp's, Dialogs.cpp's and MainFrm.cpp's curEngine and Surface.cpp's free functions still use
  `bridge::GraphicsEngine()` (#116's note: the windows reach TGraphics when TGUI holds it).
- Visual Studio's clang-tidy reports two findings on lines this change touched that it reported on main too:
  GetCurrentEngine without [[nodiscard]] (Surface.h) and CreateSurfaceVulkan's `new` (cppcoreguidelines-owning-memory).

### The gates (high)

Logs in build\logs\issue-138 of the branch's worktree (final\ for the head b2fe7ae); golden replayed main's frozen
corpus read only (PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR=C:/Tibia/Patella-Modern/build/golden), its manifest verified. Every golden run:
15,803,218 replayed + 1,512,822 retired = 17,316,040, 0 failures; 0 compiler warnings on every preset.

## #110: packet parsing and building and the game state into patella_core (Patella-Modern issue #110, M7)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-110, from main 8006002, with #138's main 4b94b69 merged). Half
of M7's exit (#111 is the other): Network.cpp, Communication.cpp, Objects.cpp, Map.cpp, Creatures.cpp and Inventory.cpp
are patella_core's sources (cmake/Core.cmake), compiled with PATELLA_CORE (no MFC, no Windows header) on every product
preset, under MSVC /analyze and GCC -fanalyzer, and linux-x64-gcc and linux-x64-clang compile them without
tests/golden/linux.

### What patella_core is now (high)

| | Sources | Lines of the sources | Headers on the core list (cmake/HeaderCheck.cmake) |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main 8006002 (and 4b94b69) | 10 | 3,671 | 40 |
| issue-110 | 16 | 12,278 (the six: 8,607) | 56 |

The 16 headers that joined the core list: the six files' (Communication.h, Creatures.h, Inventory.h, Map.h,
MapState.h, Network.h, Objects.h), what they include of the client's (Help.h, Preferences.h, Script.h, Status.h,
Talk.h, TestHooks.h, Text.h, sysinc.h), and the new types/Callback.h. They leave the client's list in a block of their
own (`patella_headers_core_110`); the client's header checks still compile them with its settings. Status.cpp,
Talk.cpp, Help.cpp, Preferences.cpp, Script.cpp, sysinc.cpp, graphics.cpp and Client.cpp (the bridge) are not in the
library: the six objects call them, the client links them (it compiles every source itself, as before: the library is
not linked into it yet), and their move is #111's. The unit tests (tests_core) use only the library's self-contained
objects, so nothing links the six from the library yet.

### What the six needed of Windows, and what they use now (high)

- **INT_PTR** (the message queue's parameters: Status.h, the TCreaturesGUI and TNetworkSession interfaces, their
  callers and Client.cpp's adapters): `std::intptr_t`, the same type (MSVC x64's `__int64`, the stand-ins'
  `std::intptr_t`), so no signature, mangled name or golden fake changes. The client's other files (Control.cpp, the
  windows, MainFrm.cpp) keep INT_PTR.
- **WinSock's numbers** in Network.cpp (GetErrorMessage's table, WSAETIMEDOUT, WSAEWOULDBLOCK, SOCKET_ERROR,
  MAXGETHOSTSTRUCT): constants of ISocket in platform/Socket.h (`socket_error::TimedOut` ..., `SocketFailed`,
  `HostEntrySize`) with WinSock's values, which every implementation reports (#109: the protocol's numbers here);
  Win32Platform.cpp asserts them against WinSock. HostnameRequest is a `void *` (ISocket's ResolveHostname returned one
  already); the lookup's message WM_USER + 1 is Network.h's HOSTNAME_RESOLVED_MESSAGE, which MainFrm.cpp's message map
  uses and asserts. NetworkWindow and SetNetworkWindow are #138's TWindowHandle.
- **The test hooks** (PATELLA_TEST_PACKET_SENT, _RECEIVED, _RSA_BLOCK): common.h includes TestHooks.h with
  PATELLA_CORE too; the library is never the test build, so they are empty there. The test build compiles the files
  itself with PATELLA_TEST_MODE, as before.
- **graphics.h** (whose engine part was the platform's surface until #138, and which defines PATH_MAX, a macro of the
  Linux headers): Map.h and Creatures.h needed only TRGBColor and include types/GraphicsTypes.h; Creatures.cpp needed
  GUI.h only for NoCallback's TCallback, which is types/Callback.h's now (GUI.h exports it; its two functions stay
  GUI.cpp's). Communication.cpp read TGraphics' two signatures for the login packet through the bridge; now through
  TLoginSignatures (Communication.h; #104's rule 5, TGraphics being made after TCommunication), which Client.cpp's
  stateless TGraphicsSignatures implements by reading the one TClient's TGraphics, as TStatusCppSession does for
  TNetwork. The golden Communication world sets bridge::Graphics()'s signatures, which the adapter reads.

Behaviour: the same code on the same data. What differs: the two signatures through a virtual call, and the code of
the bugprone fixes below, which takes the same paths.

### The compilers' checks (high)

- **Warnings.** At GCC's and Clang's full level (-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wshadow) the six files were
  measured when they joined (cmake/Warnings.cmake's rule; in the image, Release, without -Werror): GCC
  Communication.cpp 69 -Wconversion; Clang Communication.cpp 69 -Wimplicit-int-conversion and 17 -Wsign-conversion,
  Creatures.cpp 69, Inventory.cpp 63, Network.cpp 24, Map.cpp 18 and Objects.cpp 2 -Wsign-conversion (and Container.h's
  6, in Map.cpp's and Objects.cpp's units). Those files are on the GCC and Clang baselines (-Wall), in a list(APPEND) of
  their own. Fixed: two -Wshadow (ReceiveOpenContainer's inner Type is ObjectType, TCreature::SetMark's parameter
  Value). MSVC's baseline is unchanged (Communication.cpp and Creatures.cpp were on it); Map.cpp builds at /W4.
- **TEffect's anonymous structs** (Map.h): a Microsoft extension that MFC's headers allowed for their includers (C4201)
  and -Wpedantic names; allowed for TEffect alone (warning push, disable, pop for MSVC; `#pragma GCC diagnostic` for
  GCC and Clang). Naming the structs would rewrite every effect access of Map.cpp and the windows.
- **Static analysis**, rows for the table of "Static analysis of the core library" (high):

  | Analyzer | Finding | Where | Kind | Suppression | Reason |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | MSVC /analyze | C6011 (dereferencing NULL 'Player') | Creatures.cpp, TCreatures::CheckMonsterHint | false positive | PATELLA_MSVC_WARNING(suppress : 6011) on the line | the else branch reads Player only after IsOpponent returned true, which asserts the player creature |
  | MSVC /analyze | C28020 (`_Param_(1)<10`) | Map.cpp, TMap::GetAutomapBlock | false positive | PATELLA_MSVC_WARNING(suppress : 28020) on the return | the cache list links all AUTOMAP_BLOCKS entries (InitMap), so Position is one of them; the analysis takes LeastRecentBlock as any int |

  GCC -fanalyzer found nothing in the six (Release and Debug).

### clang-tidy (high)

The image's clang-tidy (tools/tidy_ci.py: linux-x64-clang's compile commands, `--all --headers`) saw the six files
and the headers they include for the first time: 296 new findings at the first run (build\logs\tidy-ci\a92eadd.log),
0 after (the baseline stays at its 3 findings; bugprone- at 0):

- modernize-use-nodiscard 182 and modernize-use-nullptr 34: clang-tidy's own fixes (run in the image, copied out).
  The `NULL` they replaced inside assertions changes those assertions' text only (#76: the golden corpus compares the
  error paths by outcome). The golden Errors test discarded TReadBinaryFile::eof()'s result: a `(void)` call now (its

## #132: fuzzing the packet parser and the file loaders (Patella-Modern issue #132, M9)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-132, from main e4b67d7). Plan section 7, M9, "Fuzzing".

### The targets (high)

tests/fuzz, added by the top-level CMakeLists.txt after tests/golden (one line); each target an LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput
and an LLVMFuzzerInitialize (tests/fuzz/fuzz.h):

| Target | Input | Code under test | Reached how |
|---|---|---|---|
| fuzz_settings | Patella.ini's text | settings/Settings.cpp, settings/PreferenceKeys.cpp, log/LogSettings.cpp | patella_core alone |
| fuzz_network | the server's stream, frames in the clear (the harness encrypts each whole 8-byte block with the session key); byte 0 picks the receive size, 1 to 0x4000 | Network.cpp: OnReceive, PrepareNextPacket, GetNextCommand, the readers | a TNetwork of its own, a fake session and sockets, as bounded_reads (#72) |
| fuzz_packets | [connection state][u16 size][frame]... (payloads as PrepareNextPacket leaves them) | Control.cpp's ReceivePackets, Communication.cpp's Receive* | the golden Communication test's world (commworld.h): every callee a fake, the readers on a buffer of the frame's own size |
| fuzz_tibia_cfg | Tibia.cfg | Preferences.cpp's ReadTibiaCfg (Script.cpp), the import into Patella.ini (#45), the next start | the client's TPreferences (the golden objects' TClient) |
| fuzz_map | 00000000.map (byte 0: as it is, or after 128 KiB of layers; bit 1: add a mark and save) | Map.cpp's LoadAutomapBlock, SaveAutomapBlock through the block cache | a TMap of its own |
| fuzz_dat | Tibia.dat | Objects.cpp's LoadObjects, LoadProperties | a TObjectTypes of its own |
| fuzz_sprites | Tibia.spr | graphics.cpp's LoadSprites, LoadSprite (the first 16 sprites) | a TGraphics of its own |
| fuzz_pictures | Tibia.pic | graphics.cpp's LoadPictures, LoadPictureTile (16 tiles, one past each picture's edge) | a TGraphics of its own |

- **Outside patella_core** (the issue's question): only fuzz_settings is patella_core's. The others need the client's
  code, which is not in patella_core yet; they link the golden runner's objects (the client's code against the MFC
  shim, on Linux the Windows stand-ins) with tests/fuzz/client.cpp in place of runner.cpp, as bounded_reads does
  (`patella_fuzz_client`; the golden directory's settings read through get_directory_property). So they are built
  where golden_runner is (windows-x64, -debug, -asan, linux-x64-gcc, linux-x64-clang), not on windows-x64-gcc.
  ReceivePackets with the real game state and windows is not reachable outside the full client: fuzz_packets runs
  every handler's own code with the comm world's fakes below it (map, creatures, windows, events), so a finding in
  the handlers' parsing shows, one in the game state they feed does not.
- **Outcomes** (client.h Guard): a TMyException, a TProgramError and std::bad_alloc are the client's own errors (it
  ends through HandleException and FatalError on each), not findings; any other exception, a sanitizer report, a
  hang (libFuzzer's -timeout=25) and a property that does not hold (fuzz.h Fail: abort) are.
- **Properties** (the fork's code only, never the original's): fuzz_settings: Parse(Text()) is Text(); Set/Get/Remove;
  ReadPreferences of what WritePreferences wrote gives the options again, without a problem, into a new file and into
  the file itself, and a second write changes nothing. fuzz_tibia_cfg: the Patella.ini the import wrote reads the
  options the client held after the import, the next start holds them again, and a third start holds what the second
  did. "The options" are as the client can hold them (tests/fuzz/values.h Held: a text ends at its first NUL; a hotkey
  without a text has no "sent at once", Tibia.cfg's writer skips it as well). Not compared with the import: OpenDialogs
  (SetPreferenceValues keeps ReadTibiaCfg's duplicate check, which reads the vector's entries of the first load in the
  same process; the client loads once per process), White and Ignore (a name longer than the list keeps is kept cut,
  so the import can hold it twice; saved, both are the same cut name, which the next load adds once, as Tibia.exe's
  next start does). The white list is cleared before each start (SetDefaultPreferences clears the ignore list only).

### Builds, seeds and runs (high)

- **PATELLA_FUZZ=OFF** (every preset): each target is linked with tests/fuzz/driver.cpp, which replays its inputs and a
  fixed number of its own mutations (bits, bytes, 8- and 16-bit edges, insertions, removals, repeats, splices; seed
  1, the same on every platform). CTest's `fuzz_<name>` (label `fuzz`) runs it on tests/fuzz/seeds/<name>: the smoke
  run, under each preset's sanitizers; the hosted CI runs them so (synthetic seeds only). Mutations: settings 5,000,
  network 20,000, packets 5,000, tibia_cfg, dat, sprites, pictures 1,000, map 200.
- **PATELLA_FUZZ=ON** (a tree of its own; the presets are #133's, so no new preset): on top of linux-x64-clang (Clang
  22's -fsanitize=fuzzer-no-link on patella_core, the golden objects and the targets, -fsanitize=fuzzer on the link,
  with ASan and UBSan) or windows-x64-asan (MSVC's /fsanitize=fuzzer; refused without PATELLA_SANITIZE=address).
  CTest's `fuzz_<name>` then runs libFuzzer for 10 s on the synthetic seeds. `python -I tools/fuzz.py build --platform
  linux|windows` makes build/linux-x64-clang-fuzz (in the image, through build.py's Docker command) or
  build/windows-x64-fuzz (-DPATELLA_CLIENT=OFF); `run` runs each target for --time seconds with the options the
  targets need (-max_len per target, fuzz_dat's -rss_limit_mb and -malloc_limit_mb 8192, -timeout=25; on Linux the
  corpus on the container's own file system, copied back after the run, and addr2line as the symbolizer: the image
  has no llvm-symbolizer) and writes summary.tsv.
- **Seeds**: tests/fuzz/seeds (106 files, 143 KB, `python -I tools/fuzz.py synthetic`) are written from the formats the
  code reads, nothing taken from CipSoft's files or recordings; .gitattributes keeps their bytes (`binary`). Among
  them #72's short packets (#72's "Found, not done"): inner lengths 7, 8, 100, 0x3ff0 and 0xffff in a frame of 8, a
  frame of size 0, a frame filling ReceiveData with the length 0xffff. `python -I tools/fuzz.py seeds` writes the

- **The harness, not the code**: the inputs the original's code cannot take without corrupting memory or hanging are
  left out by the harness, so the fuzzer goes on past them; each is a finding below. decode.h: sprites and tiles
  whose runs pass the 1024th pixel; fuzz_dat and fuzz_pictures free what a failed load allocated and clear what it
  did not (the original deletes indeterminate pointers there); fuzz_map adds no mark to a block whose file has a count
  below -64; fuzz_network reads a string that does not fit with the non-allocating reader, and stops after 32 throws
  per input and 4 in a row; fuzz_dat under ASan skips files with a sprite table of a negative or more than 2^30
  entries (ASan reports a new[] it cannot satisfy instead of throwing std::bad_alloc or std::bad_array_new_length,
  which is what the client gets: PROGRAM_ERROR 1); fuzz_tibia_cfg clears the white list before each input (below).

### Found and fixed (ours) (high)

- **TSettingsFile::Parse lost a CR** (src/settings/Settings.cpp, #31/#45's): in a file with CRLF line ends, the last
  line, when it has no line end, lost a CR it ended with ("A=1\r\nB=2\r": B's line text "B=2", so Text(), which Save
  writes, dropped the CR, one more at every save). The CR belongs to a line end only when a LF follows; now it stays.
  Values never changed (Trim takes CR as a blank). Found by fuzz_settings' Parse(Text()) property on Linux after
  224,882 executions (artifact crash-f68e2ec2...). tests_core: a subcase of "Settings: line ends". Behaviour of the
  client: only the bytes Save writes for such a file.
- **A renumbered entry lost to a numbered key written otherwise** (src/settings/PreferenceKeys.cpp RemoveIndexed, #45's):
  Indexed takes the first line of a number, and IndexOf reads Buddy01 as entry 1. A file with Buddy01 (say, one that
  cannot be read) and Buddy2: the buddy of Buddy2 is written as Buddy1, appended after Buddy01, which RemoveIndexed
  kept (its number is written), so the next read took Buddy01 again: the buddy was gone and every start reported the
  line. Now RemoveIndexed also removes the Hotkey<n>, ContentWindow<n> and Buddy<n> lines whose key is not spelled as
  the writer spells it (`Prefix` + std::to_string(n), any case). Found by fuzz_settings' round trip into the file itself
  (143,483 executions, crash-ac9b15c9...). tests_core: "Preferences: a numbered key written otherwise goes when the
  entries are written (issue #132)".
- **Set with a key that starts with a byte order mark** (src/settings/Settings.cpp TSettingsFile::Set): on the first
  line (after spaces, or appended to an empty file) the next parse took the mark as the file's, so Get did not find the
  key Set had just written. Set refuses such a key now, as it refuses a key that starts with '#' or ';' (the client
  sets only its own keys). Found by fuzz_settings' Set/Get property (610,436 executions, crash-8ad1f856...).
  tests_core: "Settings: keys and values Set refuses".

The slow ones write their file for every input (Windows' file system and its scanner for the MSVC runs).

### Found, filed: the original's code paths (high)

None is changed (the original's behaviour; the owner's to decide, as #72 was).

1. **A failed load of Tibia.dat deletes indeterminate pointers** (Objects.cpp LoadObjects, ReleaseObjects; Container.h
   array's `new T[d]`): the tables are allocated first, then LoadProperties fills entry after entry; a file that ends
   early leaves the later entries' Sprites unset, and ExitObjects (InitControl's catch calls ExitControl) deletes them.
   Shown in the client: build\windows-x64-asan\Release\PatellaTest.exe in a folder with the first 300 bytes of
   Tibia.dat (and Tibia.spr, Tibia.pic): AddressSanitizer "attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed:
   0xbebebebebebebebe" in ReleaseObjects from ExitControl from InitControl's catch
   (build\logs\issue-132\dat-finding.log). The Release client without ASan shows the box "Cannot find file "Tibia.dat".
   (Error Code 1)", exit 1, because that memory happened to be zero: undefined, latent. A fix would value-initialise
   the tables (`new T[d]()`), a deliberate difference.
2. **The same for Tibia.pic** (graphics.cpp LoadPictures, ExitGraphics): `new TPicture[n]`; a file that ends early
   leaves later pictures' Offsets unset, ExitGraphics deletes them (InitGraphics is InitControl's step 10).
3. **Sprite and tile runs write past the buffer** (graphics.cpp LoadSprite, LoadPictureTile; its comment says so):
   Pixel grows with each run's skip and count without a bound, so a Tibia.spr or Tibia.pic whose runs pass the
   1024th pixel writes past the 32 x 32 x 3 bytes the caches pass.
4. **TReadBuffer::GetString leaks a string that does not fit** (Utils.cpp): it allocates Length + 1 bytes before its
   assertion that the text fits; the assertion throws and the allocation is lost. The client ends at that assertion,
   so only a caller that goes on (the fuzzer: out of memory after 109,455 executions on Linux, 83,738 with MSVC)
   accumulates it.
5. **A negative mark count in a .map file** (Map.cpp LoadAutomapBlock keeps it and reads no mark; AddAutomapMark then
   writes Marks(MarkCount)): TIndexedVector grows down to that index, 10 entries at a time, which for a count far below
   0 runs for minutes and takes the memory it needs (libFuzzer's timeout after 37 s on a 19-byte input).
6. **A frame larger than ReceiveData never completes** (Network.cpp OnReceive): a frame size above 0x3ffe leaves
   ReceiveData full, Receive gets no room and returns 0, and the client waits for the frame forever: a server can stall
   the client so.
7. **A frame whose size is no multiple of 8 is refused before it is dropped** (PrepareNextPacket): every later
   GetNextCommand throws the same error. The client ends at the first, so nothing more follows from it.
8. **LoadProperties' sprite count is the int product of seven bytes**: on x64 up to 2^31 - 1 entries (a 4 GB
   allocation before the reads fail); a negative product throws std::bad_array_new_length. Both end as PROGRAM_ERROR 1,
   as the original's (whose 32-bit new[] did not check the size); noted, nothing to fix.

Also seen, not findings: the white list (Talk.cpp's BuddyExemptionList) is not cleared by SetDefaultPreferences, and
OpenDialogs' duplicate check reads earlier entries, so a second InitPreferences in one process differs from the
first (the client runs it once).

### Not done (high)

- **fuzz_packets under MSVC's /fsanitize=fuzzer**: every input ends in a heap report inside the comm world's own
  strings (commworld.cpp's log: use after free, double free, container overflow, in the first inputs). The same target

## #47: final on the classes nothing derives from (Patella-Modern issue #47, M7)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-47, from main 8006002). #33 added `override` and left `final`
for after the oracle (`final` changes the generated code: devirtualized calls, other inlining); with the oracle gone
(#94) the proof is behaviour: the golden corpus, the reference compare and the live comparisons.

### The count (high)

Recounted on main 8006002 (a scan of src/ and tests/ without src/Extern: every class or struct definition, its bases,
whether its body says `override`): 100 classes of src/ override and have no subclass in src/ or tests/ (#33 counted
107 on November 2; the subsystem moves and the oracle's departure removed and added classes: TSurfaceDX and the other
engines went with #94, the platform classes of #109/#119, TClient's adapters of #118 are new and already `final`). 20
classes were `final` already (Client.cpp's three adapters, TMapState, TNetwork, TTalk, the platform and test-mode
classes). Classes without an override (TXTEA, the cipher and exception bases, the interfaces) are not in the issue's
scope.

### Marked (high)

70 classes, one keyword each: ConsoleWindow.h's TTextWindow, TConsole, TTab, TTabBar; ContentWindows.h's
TAutomapView, TCompassRose, TCapacityLabel, TSoulLabel, TPlayerStates, TSmallInventoryWindow, TInventoryView,
TCombatControls, TBattleWindowBody, TTradeOffers, TTradeNames, TTradeButtons, TTradeWindowBody, TBuddylistWindowBody;
ContextMenus.h's TContextMenuEntry; DialogElements.h's TLink, TOutfitIcon, TObjectIcon, TColorButton, TIconButton,
TCheckBox, TPasswordEditLine, TEditText, THorizontalScrollBarRange, THorizontalScrollBar, TFontListBox, TProgressBar;
DialogWindow.h's TSubWindow, TDialogWindow; Dialogs.h's 28 (TQuestionLabel, TLogoutLabel, TWaitLabel,
TReconnectWindow and every dialog class but TDialog); MainWindow.h's TStartWindow, TSplitter; Player.h's CPlayerApp;
Talk.h's TPrivateTalkBuffer, TRuleViolationTalkBuffer, TRuleViolationChannel, TPrivateChannel; Win32Platform.h's
TSocket; SurfaceVulkan.h's TSurfaceVulkan.

### Left without final: the golden tests' seams (high)

Nothing in src/ or tests/ derives from these 30, but the golden window tests use them as seams that `final` closes. With all
100 marked, golden failed (DialogWindow: an Inventory.cpp assertion with a garbage container, then "windows differ"
in five operations).
- **The tests build objects of their own where our code expects the class** (29). They redirect our constructors
  (`/alternatename` to the decorated names, elementfakes.cpp's PatchElementFakes, commworld.cpp's GOLDEN_SYMBOLs), so
  `new TResizer(...)` in our code builds a mirror fake (elementfakes.h) or a TCtlWindow; or they hand a stand-in to
  our code as the class (casts). A virtual call through a pointer of a `final` class is direct, so our code would run
  our function on the fake instead of the fake's override. Constructors redirected: TAutomapWindow, TButtonsWindow,
  TStatusWindow (mainwindow_tests' TMainSide*), TConsoleWindow (TFakeConsole), THelpBubble and the nine context menus
  (TObjectContextMenu, TCreatureContextMenu, TBuddyContextMenu, TTextContextMenu, TChannelContextMenu,
  TRequestContextMenu, TEditContextMenu, TMarkContextMenu, TSkillContextMenu: commworld's TCtlWindow),
  TBlinkingButton, TBorder, TFormattedText, TMultiStateButton, TResizer, TScrollBar, TSkinIcon, TTextToggleButton,
  TToggleButton (elementfakes.h). Stand-ins as the class: TScrollBarRange (TFakeScrollBarRange), TSkillsWindowBody
  (contextmenus_tests' TMenuSkillsStandIn), TMapFrame (TFakeMapFrame), TMapWindow (mapwindow_tests' TMapThrower),
  TMainWindow (commworld's TCtlMainWindow), TDialog (commworld's DIALOG_RESULT: every creator returns a TCtlWindow).
- **A member function the tests redirect that `final` lets the compiler inline** (1): TContainerWindowBody. golden
  patches TContainerWindowBody::UpdateUpButton's first bytes (FakeUpdateUpButton); as `final`, its `GetParent()` is
  direct and inline, the function small enough that MSVC inlines it into UpdateContainerUpButton (same file), and the
  patch is not reached (the first failure). The tests' TFakeBody also stands in for the container body.
- **Checked, not only run**: golden_client's Release objects (dumpbin) of main and of the branch compared call by
  call: every function of ours that some function calls less often in the branch, and whether the tests redirect
  it. Redirected ones: CreateTextBuffer and GetTextBuffer (main had TConsoleWindow::OpenChannel inline in
  ReportRuleViolation; the branch calls OpenChannel, which calls them), TConsoleWindow::AddChannel (now inline in
  OpenChannel; commworld redirects both), GetNumberOfBuddies and TScrollBarRange::SetRange (more calls in all). Not
  redirected: TTradeButtons::SetCancelButton, TWaitLabel::SetTimer, TMainWindow::CloseContentWindow,
  THorizontalScrollBarRange::SetValue, TTalkBuffer::Append, TTradeWindowBody::getMinimumHeight, TIndexedVector's
  Grow, the subsystem destructors in TClient's unwinding.
- The tests' own classes (fakes, probes, surfaces) are not marked: the issue is src/'s classes, and the fakes are
  the tests' to change.
- When a test stops using one of these seams, its class can get `final`; a new stand-in or redirect of a `final`
  class removes the keyword (golden fails first, as here).

#34 kept `virtual ~TXTEA() {}` (with a NOLINT) because `= default` changed the oracle's image; it is `= default`

{}`, #34's other case, left with the DirectDraw engine in #94.

## #140: compare_rendering's look step and the recordings' scenario check (Patella-Modern issue #140, M7)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-140, from main 2898a44). Files: tools/session_client.py
(LOOKS, recorded_look, check_recorded_look), tools/compare_rendering.py (LOOK, scenes(), session's `look`, main's
check, the self-test's recording checks), tools/compare_traffic.py (LOOK, replay_run's check), tools/reference_record.py
(passes LOOK_NORTH), notes/rendering.md, notes/traffic.md.

### The same scenario, and a check of the recording (high)

compare_rendering.py replays compare_traffic.py's orig-live.jsonl, but its session kept run_session's default look
step, "look north" (field (8,5)), while compare_traffic's has looked at the player's own field (8,6) since #137: a
fresh recording replayed one client packet off, and the proxy reported it as a client difference. Both fixes of the
issue, together:

- compare_rendering.py's session has compare_traffic.py's look step (LOOK = LOOK_OWN_FIELD in both); its scene names
  follow it (scenes(look): "look at own field").
- Both tools read the recording's look step before they replay it and refuse another one with its name and field
  (compare_rendering's main: SystemExit, before any client starts, also with --compare-only; compare_traffic's
  replay_run: a RunError, which matters for --skip-live on recordings from before #137). session_client.recorded_look
  reads it from the recording itself, not from a side file, so recordings made before this change are classified too:
  the client's first look packet (0x8c x y z; "look in container" and "look at offer" come later and look at a
  container slot, x 0xffff) against the player's position in the game server's first packet (0x0a player, beat, bug
  reports, 0x64 x y z). The four walks bring the player back to that field before the look, so the difference is the
  look field's offset from the player's field (8,6): (0,-1) is "look north", (0,0) "look at own field"; anything else,
  no look or no game login answer is refused too.
- On the real files: the fresh orig-live.jsonl and patella-live.jsonl (and their replays) are "look at own field",
  the frozen reference session traffic (reference.jsonl, server.jsonl) "look north". The other reference sessions
  (walk, report, error, error-login, patch, patch-exe) have no look or no game connection: the check is never run on them.

The frozen reference recordings stay as they are: tools/reference_record.py passes LOOK_NORTH to compare_rendering's
session (it records from a live server, and never again since #93), and `reference.py compare` replays its recorded
window messages without run_session or this check.

## #139: the original's failures on corrupt data files and hostile frames, fixed; #72's frames dropped (Patella-Modern issue #139, M9, and #72's outcome)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-139, from main b24483a), after the owner's decisions of
November 7: fix all seven findings of #132 ("#132", "Found, filed: the original's code paths", items 1 to 7) as
deliberate differences; and change #72's outcome: a frame whose inner length runs past it is no longer an error that
ends the client, it is dropped, a line goes to the developer log at warn, and the connection goes on with the next
frame, the same "drop and log" for #139's frames (items 6, 7) where it fits, so that every bad frame behaves alike.
Each difference is a row of the table of deliberate tier A differences (#74's section). #132's eighth note (the sprite
count's int product) is unchanged: no fix was asked for.

### The bad frames: one rule (high)

TNetwork drops a server frame the client cannot use, writes one warn line (`[warn] server frame dropped: ...`, the
frame's numbers; src/log, #77), counts it (DroppedFrames, and LastDrop: a TFrameDrop, Network.h, which says which of
the three it was; the members follow the original's data, not the original's) and goes on with the next complete frame
in the same call, so a caller that asked for a command gets the next frame's. Network.cpp's DropFrame is the one
place that drops in PrepareNextPacket (ReceiveRead past the frame, the read buffer empty); PrepareNextPacket is a loop
that prepares the next frame after a drop.

- **#72, the change** (high; the owner's): a frame of size 0, or one whose payload `[u16 length][length bytes]` runs
  past it, was dropped and threw "packet length exceeds the received data" (#72's outcome, which ended the client
  through HandleException). Now dropped and logged ("it has no length (size 0)", "its length L runs past its size
  S"), no throw. The frame's test hook (PATELLA_TEST_PACKET_RECEIVED) and PacketHeader are set as before, since the
  frame was decrypted.
- **#139, item 7** (high): a frame whose size is no multiple of 8 (XTEA's block) threw "packet size does not fit to
  symmetric encryption" before the frame was dropped, so every later call threw the same (the client ended at the
  first). Now dropped before decryption ("its size S is no multiple of 8"): no test hook, PacketHeader unchanged (the
  frame was never decrypted, so it has no packet). Considered: decrypting its whole blocks (bytes the server cannot
  have meant); keeping the throw but dropping first (the client still ends on a frame it can skip: not "alike").
- **#139, item 6** (high): a frame larger than ReceiveData (a size above 0x3ffe) can never be complete there. The
  original kept its first bytes and waited: ReceiveData filled up, Receive got no room and returned 0, and no later
  byte came through, forever. (Since #133 the hardened library would also have stopped the x64 client at the next
  receive event: `&ReceiveData[ReceiveDataSize]` at a full buffer is operator[] at the array's end. OnReceive now
  takes the free part's start as a pointer, so a full buffer, still possible while the handler has not read the
  frames in it, gives Receive no room as the original's did.) Now OnReceive drops it as soon as its size is read:
  the bytes of it already received are cut off (ReceiveDataSize back to the frame's start) and the rest is dropped as
  it comes (ReceiveSkip: the bytes still to come; a receive's bytes after them are moved down and read as the next
  frames), with one warn line ("its size S does not fit the receive buffer of 16384 bytes"). The complete frames
  before it are kept and read. ConnectSocket and InitNetwork clear ReceiveSkip with the other receive state.
  Considered: closing the connection (a hostile server could then end the session with one frame; not "alike").
- **What a caller sees**: the connection never ends because of a frame's shape; ReceivePackets (Control.cpp) gets
  the next frame's commands. A frame's commands that are wrong in themselves (a read past the packet's end) still
  throw at the read, as before.

### The data files and GetString (high)

- **Item 1, Tibia.dat** (Objects.cpp LoadObjects): each table's entries get a null sprite table as soon as the table
  is allocated (before the next table's constructor, which can refuse its count: a header with 0 outfits), so
  ReleaseObjects after a file that ends early deletes only the tables LoadProperties allocated. The original left the
  entries' Sprites indeterminate (array's `new T[d]`) and InitControl's error path deleted them (ASan: a free of
  0xbebebebebebebebe; the plain client showed the error box only because that memory happened to be zero). Considered:
  value-initialising every array of Container.h (`new T[d]()`: changes every user of the template, which needs none of
  it). The outcome (PROGRAM_ERROR 1, the box) is the original's.
- **Item 2, Tibia.pic** (graphics.cpp LoadPictures): every picture's Offsets is null before the first picture is read,
  so ExitGraphics and ReloadPictures delete only the tables LoadPictures allocated. Outcome as before
  (PROGRAM_ERROR 3).
- **Item 3, the runs** (graphics.cpp LoadSprite, LoadPictureTile): a pixel past the 1024th is a data error (a
  PATELLA_ASSERT inside the functions' try blocks: PROGRAM_ERROR 4 for Tibia.spr, 5 for Tibia.pic, as a short sprite
  or tile already was). The order is the original's: each byte is read, then the pixel checked, then written, so a
  sprite or tile the original decoded without writing past the buffer decodes to the same pixels, and a read past the
  file's end is still the error it was; the pixels before the 1024th are written as before. Considered: clipping (a
  silently wrong picture from a corrupt file, where a short file is already an error).
- **Item 4, GetString** (Utils.cpp TReadBuffer::GetString, the allocating one): the check that the text fits comes
  before the allocation, so a text that does not fit throws with nothing allocated. Same outcome (the TMyException);
  "free before the throw" without a free.
- **Item 5, the .map files** (Map.cpp LoadAutomapBlock): a negative mark count throws "negative mark count" inside the
  marks' try block, so the file is a corrupted one, as a file that ends early is: "Map file '...' was corrupted!" in
  the default console, the block cleared (no marks, the colours 0 and the speeds 250). The original kept the count,
  read no mark, and AddAutomapMark then wrote Marks(count): TIndexedVector grew down to that index (minutes and much
  memory for a count far below 0). Considered: taking the count as 0 and keeping the layers (a file whose count is
  impossible is not trusted elsewhere either). The block is saved again only when a mark is added (Changed), as for
  any corrupted file.

### The golden corpus (high)

The frozen corpus (#93) is replayed unchanged; the golden Network test's deliberate parts (golden::BeginDeliberate,
"#72 and #86") follow the new outcome. A part now opens in the call of our side that dropped a frame (Both:
TNetwork's DroppedFrames before and after our side's call, normal and error rounds alike; network_tests.cpp
OpenDropPart), named "#72" for a length drop and "#139" for the others, and still ends at the round's ResetSides: after
the drop our side reads the next frame's commands while the original reads on past the frame (#72) or keeps waiting
(item 6), so the two sides do not agree again within the round. Until #139 the part opened at our side's #72 throw
(OurGetNextCommand, OurPrepareNextPacket, now gone).

- **Item 6 is in the corpus.** MakeFrame's frames are at most 58 bytes, yet some OnReceive calls of the corpus read a
  "frame size" above 0x3ffe: bytes of a stream that are out of step with its frames (the fake world's queued bytes

- **The counts** (windows-x64; the same on every preset that replays the corpus): 15,803,218 replayed + 1,512,822

  27 rounds with only an item-6 drop have a part they did not have (until #139 both sides waited there alike). More of

- **Items 1 to 5: 0 checks affected.** The Objects, Graphics, Map, Communication and Network tests replay with 0

- The Network test's log level is error while it runs (our side's warn lines are not the test's output).

### The tests (high)

- **bounded_reads** (tests/golden/bounded_reads_test.cpp, now #72, #86 and #139; every preset that builds the golden

  every byte taken (item 6), and the largest frame that fits still read; a Tibia.dat that ends after one entry and

  bytes (item 3); GetString's throw with no allocation (container_tests.cpp's operator new[], the runner's, counts

- **The fuzz targets** (tests/fuzz): the harness's guards around the original's findings are gone, so the fuzzers now

### Found, not done (high)

- **A packet of length 0 leaves the frames after it waiting** (the original's, not one of #139's): a frame whose

## #141: CMake 4.4.5 everywhere (Patella-Modern issue #141, M7)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-141, from main b24483a; CMake 4.4.5, MSVC 14.51, mingw-w64 GCC
16.2, GCC 16.2 and Clang 22.1.8 in the image). Files: tools/build.py (pinned_cmake, install_cmake, CMAKE_VERSION,
CMAKE_SHA256, the image tag), tools/compare_rendering.py and tools/fuzz.py (the pinned CMake for their own cmake
calls), docker/linux-x64/Dockerfile, cmake/ImportStd.cmake, .github/workflows/hosted.yml and self-hosted.yml, CLAUDE.md,
README.md, notes/reconstruction.md.

### One version, pinned in three places (high)

The owner's decision: CMake 4.4.5 (the newest stable release, October 27, 2026) for every build. Before: 4.1.2 locally
(C:\Program Files\CMake, first on the machine PATH; and vcvarsall.bat puts Visual Studio's 4.3.1 first in the MSVC
presets' environment), 4.1.2 in the image, whatever the hosted Windows runner had (4.4.5, unpinned).

- This machine: Kitware's cmake-4.4.5-windows-x86_64.zip in C:\Servers\Software\cmake (the owner's rule for portable
  tools), its bin folder on the user PATH, the zip's SHA-256 checked against the release's cmake-4.4.5-SHA-256.txt
  (326c8264...f004). C:\Program Files\CMake, mingw64's 4.4.2 and Visual Studio's copy are untouched.
- tools/build.py: on Windows a bare cmake, ctest or cpack becomes the pinned executable (PATELLA_CMAKE_DIR, default
  C:\Servers\Software\cmake), checked once per run with `--version`; a missing one or another version is a BuildError
  that says how to install it. A path stays as it is; Linux (in the image, or a Linux host) uses PATH. The machine
  PATH comes before the user PATH, so PATH alone could not pick it. compare_rendering.py (patcap's build) and fuzz.py
  (the Windows fuzz tree) call cmake themselves with build.py's environment; they now go through pinned_cmake too.
- `python -I tools/build.py --install-cmake <folder>`: downloads the zip, checks it against build.py's CMAKE_SHA256,
  unpacks it into a new folder. Hosted CI's three Windows jobs run it into $RUNNER_TEMP\cmake and set
  PATELLA_CMAKE_DIR, so the runner's own CMake is never used; one copy of the hash serves CI and a new machine.
- The image: CMAKE_VERSION 4.4.5, CMAKE_SHA256 ed85135c...0be0 (the release's Linux x86_64 tarball), a new tag
  `patella-modern/linux-x64:gcc16.2-clang22.1-libstdcxx16-cmake4.4.5` (in build.py, both workflows and the docs):
  branches still on the old Dockerfile keep the old image, which is not removed.
- Hosted CI prints the version in every job that runs CMake: the Windows jobs' install step (and windows-msvc's Tool
  versions through build.py), and a `cmake --version` step in each job that builds the image (linux, clang-format,
  clang-tidy). The banned-calls job runs no CMake.

A build folder configured by 4.1.2 needs one `python -I tools/build.py <preset> --fresh` (or a new folder): its cache
names the old cmake and 4.1's std module target. Said in CLAUDE.md and notes/reconstruction.md, "Building".

### ImportStd.cmake: the 4.4 path, and kept the 4.1 path (high)

Every build takes the 4.4 gate now. Kept: the 4.1 gate and code path, and cmake_minimum_required 3.30 (and the
presets' 3.30): they cost a few lines, and a distribution build with its own CMake (4.1, or 3.30 without import std,
where the option is off with a warning) still configures. Removing them would gain nothing the pin does not already
give.

Clang under 4.4 failed two ways, both fixed in patella_target_import_std (Clang only):

- The fortify exception (#121) stays, but differently. 4.4 compiles the std BMI per importer with the importer's
  options (@cmake_cxx_std@synth_0), de-duplicated: #121's second `-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE` after Hardening.cmake's
  `-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3` was dropped, the BMI was compiled with -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3, and bits/std.cc
  failed as in #121 ("using declaration referring to 'printf' with internal linkage cannot be exported"). 4.4's
  per-importer module does not remove the exception: the module is compiled with the importer's options, so it needs
  the importer without fortify. The target's COMPILE_OPTIONS now lose the hardening's _FORTIFY_SOURCE item (list
  FILTER) instead; the target and its BMI compile without it, as before. It works on 4.1 as well (its module copies
  the filtered options).
- 4.4 also compiles bits/std.cc and std.compat.cc into the objects of a target @cmake_cxx_std with the directory's
  flags only, and Clang warns "'std' is a reserved name for a module [-Wreserved-module-identifier]"; 4.1 gave its
  module target -Wno-reserved-module-identifier (Modules/Compiler/Clang-CXX-CXXImportStd.cmake), 4.4 does not and
  has no property for it. The function sets it in the caller's CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS (PARENT_SCOPE: tests/unit, whose only
  module is std) on CMake 4.4 and newer. build.py fails any warning, so this was a build failure.

Found, not changed: 4.4.5's synthesized BMI evaluates the importer's configuration-dependent options for the first
configuration (Release): in Debug, GCC's std BMI gets `-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`, which the Debug
importer does not have (compile_commands.json of linux-x64-gcc). GCC accepts it without a warning and
linux-x64-gcc-debug passes; MSVC's options have no configuration-dependent item (its runtime flag comes from CMake's
own per-configuration flags, correct in both). A CMake bug to report upstream; nothing here depends on it.

MSVC and GCC needed no change: windows-x64 (and -debug, -asan) and windows-x64-gcc, linux-x64-gcc build tests_import_std
on 4.4.5 as they did on 4.1.2.

### The gates (high)

## #122: the SDL3 window and its event loop (Patella-Modern issue #122, M8)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-122, from main 2898a44). Plan section 7, M8, first step: SDL3
as the pinned dependency, the client's main window and event loop on SDL3, the game timer in the loop. Input (#123),
the display, clipboard, URLs and message boxes (#124), the socket (#125), the Vulkan surface (#126) and the MFC removal
(#127) come after it.

### SDL3, pinned (high)

cmake/Sdl3.cmake, included by cmake/WindowsX64.cmake: SDL **3.4.18** (released October 2, 2026), the release archive
SDL3-3.4.18.tar.gz by URL and SHA256 (9c75cf16...334a3, the digest GitHub publishes for the asset, checked against the
download), built by FetchContent with SDL's own CMakeLists into build/<preset>/_deps, as cmake/Vulkan.cmake builds
glslang. Nothing is installed on the system. Why 3.4.18: the newest 3.4 release with a month in the field (3.4.20 came
out four days before this change); 3.4 is SDL's current stable series. Settings:

- the static library only (SDL3-static), the client's static CRT (CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY in the function that adds
  it), no test library, tests, examples or install rules;
- only the subsystems the client uses: video and events. Audio, camera, joystick, haptic, HIDAPI, sensor, power, GPU,
  render, dialog, tray, OpenGL and OpenGL ES are off. Vulkan support stays on (#126 needs SDL_Vulkan_CreateSurface);
- SDL's /W3 replaced by /W0 on its target (third-party code: build.py fails a build on any warning; a /W0 in
  CMAKE_C_FLAGS would print D9025 against SDL's /W3). The build log has no SDL warning;
- the client targets link SDL3::SDL3-static; the compile-only targets (Patella_compile, PatellaTest_compile, the hosted
  CI) and the header checks only SDL3::Headers, so they do not build the library;
- plan section 5's `find_package` first: FetchContent's FIND_PACKAGE_ARGS (3.4.18 or newer, CONFIG) on platforms other
  than Windows; on Windows always the pinned archive. No Linux preset includes the file yet: the Linux presets build
  patella_core, the unit tests and the golden runner, none of which uses SDL3, so **the Linux image does not get
  SDL3** in this change (patella_core does not depend on it).

### The two paths: a run-time switch (high)

`PATELLA_WINDOW` in the environment (platform/WindowChoice.h, read once, before main): `mfc` (any case) MFC's frame
window and message loop, as before; `sdl`, unset or empty the SDL3 window, **the default**; any other value the SDL3
window with a warning in the log. A run-time switch, not a build option: one build's Patella.exe and PatellaTest.exe
run either way, so every comparison checks both paths from the same binaries (the tools pass the environment on:
`PATELLA_WINDOW=mfc python -I tools/reference.py compare ...`), the MFC path is compiled and linked by every client
build (the issue's "the MFC path still builds"), and #127 removes the switch with MFC. MFC stays linked on the SDL3
path in any case: the sockets are MFC's CAsyncSocket until #125. The start-up log names the path (`[info] window:
SDL3`).

### What the SDL3 window does (high)

src/SdlFrame.cpp (namespace patella::sdlframe; SdlFrame.h has no SDL header: the golden tests compile Player.cpp,
which includes it, and stub its functions in client_stubs.cpp) stands for CMainFrame and CWinApp::Run, function for
function, with the client calls in their order:

- **Start** (Player.cpp InitInstance; its SDL3 branch InitSdlWindow takes the same steps after the command line): SDL's
  hints, `SDL_RegisterApp(ClassName, CS_OWNDC | CS_DBLCLKS | CS_HREDRAW | CS_VREDRAW)` (the class InitInstance registers
  for the MFC frame, so CountTibiaWindows finds the window by its class, and Windows makes the double clicks the client
  handles; the icon is resource 128 through SDL_HINT_WINDOWS_INTRESOURCE_ICON, the MFC path's class icon and
  WM_SETICON), SDL_Init(VIDEO), then CMainFrame's constructor's steps (InitControl ...), SDL_CreateWindow hidden and
  resizable (WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW's styles), OnCreate's steps (InitMainWindow with the client size, InitWindow with the
  HWND, the placement from Patella.ini or the default 600x450 centred, the main timer, the size once more as
  CreateWindowEx's WM_SIZE), the surfaces, the count of the Tibia windows and its boxes, the first Redraw, the window
  shown (maximized if stored so), the first mouse position.
- **SDL's hints**: its message pump off (below); **no DPI awareness** (`SDL_WINDOWS_DPI_AWARENESS=unaware`: SDL3 would
  declare per-monitor awareness, and the original's process is not DPI aware: no manifest); no SDL mouse capture (the
  client takes the capture itself); a fullscreen window not minimized on focus loss (the client leaves fullscreen
  instead); Alt+F4 the client's key.
- **The frame**: MFC's frame windows have WS_EX_CLIENTEDGE (CFrameWnd::PreCreateWindow), SDL's window has not. The SDL
  window gets it (and SetDisplayMode takes it away with WS_EX_APPWINDOW for fullscreen and gives both back, as the
  original's ModifyStyleEx). SDL3 reads the window's extended style when it computes the outer rectangle, so the same
  Patella.ini gives the same outer rectangle and the same client area as the MFC frame. A first version computed the
  edge into the stored numbers instead: the reference compare matched, but compare_files' placement check (#68) reads
  the HWND's GetWindowPlacement, found the window 2 pixels inside Tibia.cfg's rectangle on each side and moved it, and
  the client then stored [8, 8, 804, 604] for [10, 10, 800, 600] (build\logs\issue-122\compare_files-try1.log).
- **Placement**: GetWindowRect is SDL's position and size plus SDL_GetWindowBordersSize (GetWindowRect against
  GetClientRect, as AddFrameSize); MoveWindow the same backwards; GetWindowPlacement's normal rectangle is the last
  rectangle seen while the window was neither maximized, minimized nor fullscreen, in workspace coordinates (minus the
  primary display's work-area offset, as rcNormalPosition: with the taskbar at the top or the left the window moves by
  it at each start, as Tibia.exe's does); SM_CXSCREEN is the primary display's bounds.
- **Events through an event watch** (SDL_AddEventWatch): SDL calls it as it sends the event, inside its window
  procedure, so the client sees a size change within the call that made it, as with MFC's WM_SIZE (SetDisplayMode's
  Resize(0, 0) comes after the fullscreen size's Resize, as in the original). Resized and restored: OnSize (Resize,
  the client area at least 550x450; SDL_SetWindowMinimumSize is OnGetMinMaxInfo). Focus gained or lost: OnActivateApp
  (KeyFlags 0; leaving fullscreen is done after the message). Close requested: OnClose after the message
  (CloseRequest, then DestroyWindow's and OnDestroy's steps: fullscreen left, the placement saved for Patella.ini, the
  timer stopped, the cursors destroyed; the window destroyed, the frame's destructor's ExitControl, the loop ends,
  ExitInstance). The display's mode changed: OnDisplayChange after the message. What would change the window from
  inside SDL's window procedure is only noted there and done right after the message that caused it.
- **The loop** (Run, CWinApp::Run's place): on Windows the thread's messages are pumped as MFC's PumpMessage did
  (PeekMessageA, the test build's DropInput filter with a script, TranslateMessage, DispatchMessageA), each message
  followed by what it noted, until the queue is empty; then SDL_PumpEvents (its own message loop off:
  SDL_HINT_WINDOWS_ENABLE_MESSAGELOOP=0) with its queue flushed (the watch has seen every event), the main timer, and
  CPlayerApp::OnIdle with MFC's idle count. Why not SDL's own pump: it breaks off after a few new messages per call
  (SDL_windowsevents.c WIN_PumpEvents), so the idle step could run between messages MFC dispatched together (the test
  mode's replay socket and the MFC sockets post them), and it has no place for the test build's filter but a hook. The
  order of messages, idle steps and ticks is MFC's; the reference compare's sessions match on it.
- **The main timer in the loop** (platform/LoopTimer.h; TSdlLoopInput, platform/Win32Platform.h): IInput's StartTimer
  arms a TLoopTimer (no SetTimer); the loop asks it once per pass with IClock::Milliseconds and calls TimerEvent when
  100 ms have passed since the last tick: one tick at a time, none queued while the loop was held up, as WM_TIMER.
  SetTimer's ticks came at the system timer's granularity (100 ms rounded up to 15.6 ms steps, about 109 ms); the
  loop's at 100 ms (at the next pass). The test build with a script has no timer on either path (the driver dispatches
  WM_TIMER 1, which the SDL window's subclass handles as OnTimer); without a script TTestInput passes the timer on to the
  path's input (platform::WindowInput()). Patella.exe's Platform() gives WindowInput() (compiled with PATELLA_SDL3; the
  golden runner, without it, keeps TWin32Input).

### Win32 until its own issue (high)

On the SDL3 path these stay Win32, each named in SdlFrame.cpp: the keys, buttons and wheel come as window messages
through a subclass of the SDL window (SetWindowSubclass), whose handlers are MainFrm.cpp's (TranslateKey, KeyDown,
KeyUp, OnChar, the button handlers with SetCapture/ReleaseCapture, OnCaptureChanged, OnMouseWheel, OnSetCursor,
OnTimer; their Default() is DefWindowProc, the MFC frame's default, so SDL never sees them and makes no key or mouse
events): #123 replaces them with SDL's events. This is also what keeps the test mode working unchanged: its driver
dispatches the script's Win32 messages to the main window (TestModeWin32.cpp's MainWindow() names the SDL window's
HWND), and the reference recordings' `post` lines are Win32 messages. Also Win32: the Windows cursors and SetCursor
(#123), WM_USER + 1 of the host lookup (#125), ShellExecute for OpenURL (#124), the message boxes, the windows' count
and the display modes (IWindow's Win32 implementation, #124), the Vulkan surface on the HWND (vkCreateWin32SurfaceKHR,
#126), ExitProgram's posted WM_CLOSE (after the messages already queued, as MFC's), the client edge's extended style
and the message pump (#127).

The handlers are copies of MainFrm.cpp's, not calls: MainFrm.cpp is unchanged (the golden MainFrm test compares
CMainFrame's handlers and layout against the original), and #123 and #127 replace both.

### Behaviour changes of the SDL3 path (medium)

None the gates see. Known, by construction: the timer's ticks at 100 ms instead of about 109 ms (above); the window
class's small icon is resource 128 too (the MFC frame's class had none: Windows took it from the large one); the IME
messages go to SDL's window procedure instead of DefWindowProc (#123's input); fullscreen is SDL's fullscreen-desktop
window (borderless, the display's size; the original's a topmost popup of the screen's size), and compare_rendering's
fullscreen scenes (they need a 1024x768 desktop) were not run (#98's windowed set). The MFC path is unchanged.

### The golden tests (high)

No check changed. Player.cpp includes SdlFrame.h and platform/WindowChoice.h; the runner's stubs (client_stubs.cpp)
stand in for the nine sdlframe functions and CWinThread::ExitInstance, which the shim (src/compat/mfc_shim.h) now
declares (Player.cpp's Run calls it after the SDL3 loop, as CWinThread::Run does at WM_QUIT). MainFrm.cpp is not
touched.

### The image (high)

Not compared: Patella.exe's default path changed (SDL3), so #109's function-by-function image comparison does not
apply. The MFC path's code is MainFrm.cpp's, unchanged, and Player.cpp's branches.

### Unit tests (high)

tests_core's core_window_loop_test.cpp: TLoopTimer (nothing due before Start or after Stop, the tick once the interval

## #142: an empty packet no longer stalls the reading (Patella-Modern issue #142, M9)

Done by Claude Opus 5.5, November 7, 2026 (branch issue-142, from main 260f066), after the owner's decision of
November 7: fix #139's last fuzzing case ("#139", "Found, not done") as a deliberate difference, with #139's rule for
bad frames (go on to the next frame; a warn line in the developer log where it is a drop). A row of the table of
deliberate tier A differences (#74's section).

### The fix (high)

- **What the original did.** PrepareNextPacket prepared a packet of inner length 0 (a frame of 8 bytes, Size 4, no
  command in it) like any other, so GetNextCommand returned -1 at once: ReceivePackets (Control.cpp) and
  Communication.cpp's loop stopped with the complete frames behind it unread, until a later receive completed another
  frame. Its own frame stayed in ReceiveData (ReceiveRead past it) until the next PrepareNextPacket, so a following
  frame that fit ReceiveData only without those 10 bytes (up to 16 KB) never completed, and with ReceiveData full the
  connection stalled as #139's item 6 had.
- **Now** (Network.cpp PrepareNextPacket): an empty packet has nothing left to read, so the loop that #139 made goes
  on to the next frame in the same call, as after a dropped frame, and the empty packet's frame leaves ReceiveData at
  once. TNetwork counts it in EmptyPackets (the tests'). The test hook (PATELLA_TEST_PACKET_RECEIVED) and PacketHeader
  are set for it as before (it was decrypted), then by the next frame.
- **Not a drop, no log line** (high; the owner's rule: "a warn line where it is a drop"): an empty packet is a
  well-formed packet whose length is inside its frame; it is read, to its end, and has no command. So it is not
  counted in DroppedFrames, LastDrop is unchanged, and the developer log gets no line. Considered: dropping it as a
  bad frame with a warn line (TFrameDrop would gain a fourth reason for a packet nothing is wrong with; a server that
  sent them as keep-alives would fill the log). If the owner wants a line, it is one `patella::log::Debug` or `Warn`
  call in the new branch.

### The golden corpus (high)

The frozen corpus is replayed unchanged. Its generated frames (network_tests.cpp's MakeFrame) include empty packets,
and where our side now reads on past one, the round's checks differ from the original's until the round's ResetSides
(our side reads the next frame's commands and has moved the frame out; the original returned -1 with the frame still
in ReceiveData). Recorded as #139's parts are: a deliberate part named "#142" opens in our side's call that went on
past an empty packet (Both: TNetwork's EmptyPackets before and after the call, normal and error rounds alike;
OpenDropPart), unless a drop in the same call opened a "#72" or "#139" part first, and ends at ResetSides. Every other
check is compared as before.

- **The counts** (windows-x64 and linux-x64-gcc alike, every preset that replays the corpus the same): 15,803,218
  replayed + 1,512,822 retired = 17,316,040, 0 failures, as on main. Deliberate parts: **#72: 269 parts, 35,460
  checks, 16,386 differ; #139: 32 parts, 3,303 checks, 1,167 differ; #142 (new): 36 parts, 3,688 checks, 1,037
  differ**; together 337 parts, 42,451 checks, 18,590 differ. Before (#139): #72 274 parts, 36,104 checks, 16,588
  differ; #139 33, 3,343, 1,178; together 307 parts, 39,447 checks, 17,766 differ. Six rounds or error-round
  iterations whose part #139 opened at a later drop now open it earlier at an empty packet (5 of #72's, 1 of #139's),
  and 30 have a part they did not have (both sides stopped at the empty packet alike until now).
- The Communication tests (Communication.cpp's GetNextCommand loop in the golden world) replay with 0 failures and no
  part, unchanged.

### The tests (high)

- **bounded_reads** (3 new cases, 19 in all): empty packets before, between and after frames, all read in one call,
  EmptyPackets counted, nothing dropped or logged; an empty packet alone, its frame out of ReceiveData after the call
  (ReceiveDataSize, ReceivePacketEnd and ReceiveRead 0; nothing past it read under ASan's poison) and the next frame
  read; #139's fuzzing case, an empty packet then a frame of 0x3ff8 bytes (0x4004 together, more than ReceiveData) and
  another frame, received 1, 2, 7 and 0x4000 bytes at a time: every receive takes bytes and both frames are read (with
  the original's behaviour Receive gets no room after the empty packet: the REQUIRE fails).
- **fuzz_network**: the stall property in full: the exclusion of an input once an empty packet stayed in ReceiveData
  (`Waiting`) is gone, and a new property fails when GetNextCommand returns -1 with a frame left in ReceiveData
  (ReceiveRead or ReceivePacketEnd not 0). New synthetic seeds (`python -I tools/fuzz.py synthetic`, hand-made):
  142-empty-packets, 142-empty-then-largest (#139's case, 2-byte receives).

### Found, not done (high)

- The MSVC libFuzzer tree (`python -I tools/fuzz.py run --platform windows`) was not run; Linux's was (below), and
  every preset's fuzz_network smoke run (the synthetic seeds and fixed mutations) passes, windows-x64-asan's among them.

### The gates (high)

Logs in build\logs\issue-142 of the branch's worktree; golden replayed main's frozen corpus read only
(PATELLA_GOLDEN_DIR=C:/Tibia/Patella-Modern/build/golden), its manifest verified. Every golden run: 15,803,218 replayed
+ 1,512,822 retired = 17,316,040, 0 failures, with the parts above; 0 compiler warnings.

- `python -I tools/build.py windows-x64` exit 0, 28/28; windows-x64-debug exit 0, 27/27; windows-x64-asan exit 0,
  27/27, no ASan report; windows-x64-gcc exit 0, 13/13; linux-x64-gcc exit 0, 25/25 (golden); linux-x64-clang (ASan,
  UBSan) exit 0, 24/24 (golden), no sanitizer report.
- Live: `python -I tools/reference.py compare --reference C:/Tibia/Patella-Modern/build/reference` exit 0, every
  session matches its reference (the known deliberate differences of #45 and #74); `python -I tools/compare_traffic.py`
  exit 0, no differences.
- Fuzzing: `python -I tools/fuzz.py run --platform linux --time 180 fuzz_network` (Clang 22, ASan and UBSan; the
  synthetic seeds and the local ones of `fuzz.py seeds`) exit 0: 233,177 executions (1,288 per s), cov 487, ft 2,698,
